“The Princess of Vikistv” / Eldest of the Three Sisters

ー

Worked alongside her father on the agricultural farm from a young age.

growing up sheltered from the horrors of the outside world by her father

Magic (if applicable):

ARC & DEVELOPMENT
Where They Start: A happy, modest princess-figure preparing for her wedding, the
stable center of her family
Key Turning Points: Solis conquers Vikistv; father is executed; Natav (who sold the
country out) is also executed; Enyokia is spared but sold into slavery — Solis says
she was “probably just used by her father and fiancé”
Where They End: Dies in slavery in Gherci  months after arrival, likely burned.
Her body is dumped in an unmarked mass grave with other Vikistv people.
Vandrea later finds her grave after 7 months of searching, reburries her
individually, and buries pieces of her own skin and hair with her sister.
∼3
A  T ALE OF THREE SISTERS
3
Theme They Embody: The forgotten victim - the sister no one remembers, who
died unmourned in a strangerʼs land. The first casualty of the Patton dynastyʼs
expansion.
ROLE IN STORY
Narrative Function: Represents the cost of colonization on the most innocent; her
death is the wound that never heals for Vandrea
Key Scenes: Wedding preparations; Solisʼs conquest of Vikistv; being separated
from her sisters and sold into slavery
Relationships That Drive Plot: Her death is the core of Vandreaʼs guilt Vandrea
chose to run with Apharia instead of rescuing Enyokia) and fuels Vandreaʼs
10,000-year vengeance
Impact on Other Characters: Her loss breaks Vandrea fundamentally - Vandrea
never forgives herself for hesitating

Memorable Lines:

A  T ALE OF THREE SISTERS
4
Details of her time in slavery before death
Was she definitely burned, or is that Vandreaʼs assumption? Vandrea reasons
that illness/disease wouldnʼt be able to kill her)
Connections to Track:
Vandreaʼs guilt arc (chose to flee with Apharia instead of rescuing Enyokia
immediately)
Vandreaʼs speech about Enyokia during Crown of Glory confrontation with
Minara
Unmarked grave location in Gherci
Enyokia was sold into debt slavery after her father Cevalʼs execution. She died in
slavery before Vandrea could rescue her. The timeline of events: after Vandrea
and Apharia escaped, while Apharia was with Soli, and before Aphariaʼs death -
Enyokia died without her sisters ever reaching her.
Enyokiaʼs death was the first wound that never healed for Vandrea. It is the
foundation of Vandreaʼs transformation into a vengeance-obsessed figure.
Vandrea carries the specific guilt of having chosen to run with Apharia instead of
immediately going back for Enyokia. This choice - survival over rescue haunts
every decision Vandrea makes for the next ten thousand years.

FAMILY & RELATIONSHIPS

BACKGROUND
Childhood: Second daughter of the City Lord. Had tremendous magical power
from a young age, which surprised people because she was not full Vikistian. Very
sheltered - never learned much about the outside world. Hot-headed with anger
management issues. Regularly took a drug called Haitak.
Formative Events: Motherʼs death; being engaged to Heian Orana (loveless
match); the fall of Vikistv; her fatherʼs execution; fleeing with Apharia; discovering

PERSONALITY
ー
⼀
Core Traits: Hot-headed, brash, feminine but with an edge, fiercely protective,
angry
Greatest Fear:
Greatest Desire: Revenge - against Solis, the gods, the humans. Everyone who
contributed to her sistersʼ deaths.
Fatal Flaw: Feeds grief with hatred; unable to let go
Secret They Keep:
What They Want vs What They Need: WANTS vengeance and suffering for the
Patton bloodline. NEEDS to grieve and forgive herself for failing Enyokia.
BELIEFS & VALUES
Religious Affiliation: Turns against all the gods of new after Aphariaʼs death
Political Stance:
Moral Code: Evolves from protective older sister to “make everyone who
contributed suffer”
What They Would Kill For: Her sisters (and eventually, their memory)
What They Would Die For: Her sisters
ABILITIES & SKILLS
Magic (if applicable):
Division: Life magic initially; taps into Death magic Chaos, Destruction, the
Peculiar) — the taboo side
A  T ALE OF THREE SISTERS
7
Level: Tremendous power from a young age (surprising given sheʼs half-Vikistian)
Specific Abilities: First shown choking a man unconsciously (death magic); uses
magic to shield herself and Apharia while fleeing; disguise magic; later receives
massive power boost from Renedin, including immortality and
shapeshifting/illusion
Combat Skills:
Other Talents: Selling flowers, herbs, and wood (survival skills learned in exile)
Weaknesses: Haitak dependency (at story start); grief and guilt over Enyokia
ARC & DEVELOPMENT
Where They Start: A sheltered, hot-headed young woman standing in a rose
garden, preparing for her sisterʼs wedding, referring to Solis as “the one with
golden hair” because sheʼs never learned about the outside world
Key Turning Points:
Fleeing Vikistv with Apharia after Solisʼs conquest
First use of death magic (choking the Equateiy townsman who insults her
family)
Letting Apharia go with Soli - trusting a god to protect her sister better than
she could
Discovering Enyokiaʼs unmarked grave in Gherci (  months of searching)
Soli arriving with Apharia and her nieceʼs corpses - the breaking point
Hearing Renedinʼs whisper asking if she wants revenge
Where They End (in Three Sisters): Standing in a rose garden in Vikistv, grasping a
dirty dahlia, hearing Renedinʼs voice. Sets her on the 10,000-year path to Crown of
Glory.
Theme They Embody: The mindset of those who experienced colonization. A
broken woman feeding grief with hatred for millennia. Not a villain - a victim
whose pain became monstrous.
ROLE IN STORY
∼7
A  T ALE OF THREE SISTERS
8
Narrative Function: Central protagonist of A Tale of Three Sisters. The reader
should never see her as a villain - she represents the colonized perspective.
Key Scenes: Rose garden (opening); fleeing through Silora forest; the choking
scene in Equateiy; settling in Nedi Forest; letting Apharia go with Soli; finding
Enyokiaʼs grave in Gherci (cutting her own skin and hair to bury with her sister);
receiving the bodies from Soli; burying Apharia and her niece; returning to Vikistv;
rose garden (closing — Renedinʼs whisper)
Relationships That Drive Plot: Enyokia (guilt), Apharia (loss), Soli (betrayal of trust),
Renedin (corruption), the Patton bloodline 10,000-year vengeance)
Impact on Other Characters: Her deal with Renedin shapes the entire future of the
world through Crown of Glory

VANDREAʼS IMMORTALITY  ORIGIN
VANDREAʼS IMMORTALITY
ORIGIN
Approximately 7,100 BR, after burying Apharia, Vandrea made a deal with Renedin
(the Old God of dreams and the eternal plane) for immortality.
COST
-
The deal corrupted Vandreaʼs soul. She is damned to the Pertari Stairs upon death
and has traded away the natural rebirth cycle in exchange for eternal life. By
Minaraʼs era, Vandrea has been alive for approximately 10,000 years.
POWERS GAINED
-
Through the deal with Renedin, Vandrea gained shapeshifting and illusion abilities.
These are the powers she uses to assume the identity of Macenja Lorafonmenti
and maintain the deception for millennia.
EXISTING NOTES FROM HUB  ALREADY IN DOC, DO NOT DUPLICATE
Plans: Demon attacks destabilize faith to weaken gods for Renedinʼs barrierbreaking plan
Motivation: Wants suffering, not just death. After 10,000 years of hatred, quick
assassination would be unsatisfying. Wants Pattons to watch empire crumble,
understand loss as she has.
Macenja replacement: Killed real Macenja Lorafonmenti before imperial marriage,
assumed identity using shapeshifting/illusion from Renedinʼs power.
Cover maintenance: Attempts to produce male heir with other men (knights killed
afterward) were to maintain cover as legitimate empress desperate for succession.

BACKGROUND
Childhood: Youngest daughter/“princess” of the City Lord — heavily protected
from birth. Born a little sick, so extra care was always directed toward her. Mother
died giving birth to her. Named after her maternal grandmother who also had
blonde hair. Never met her birth mother. Close with stepmother Madame Saiye
(who had the same blonde hair). When both Apharia and Madame Saiye fell sick
with a deadly disease, Saiye nursed Apharia instead of herself. Vandrea and
Enyokia disliked Madame Saiye but tolerated her for Aphariaʼs sake.
Formative Events: Birth motherʼs death; Madame Saiyeʼs selfless care during
illness; fall of Vikistv; fleeing with Vandrea
Education/Training:
Before the Story Begins: Living the most sheltered life of the three sisters in Torad

Where They End: Killed by Vapaz alongside her daughter, as punishment for

Theme They Embody: Innocence destroyed by forces beyond comprehension.
The person who “started” the War of the Gods through no malice of her own -
through love.
ROLE IN STORY
Narrative Function: Her relationship with Soli triggers the Second War of the Gods
and the chain of events that creates Vandreaʼs vengeance. Represents innocence
caught between divine politics.
Key Scenes: Being chased by a bear and saved by Soli; waiting in the forest for
Soli day after day; Soliʼs divine confession (bird scene); revealing the truth to
Vandrea; departure from Vandrea
Relationships That Drive Plot: Soli (her pregnancy violates the First Divine Law);
Vandrea (her death is the final blow that sends Vandrea to Renedin)
Impact on Other Characters: Her daughterʼs soul is reincarnated as Minara Gonia
in Crown of Glory

Having no one left to be human for
When Renedin whispers to her after she buries Apharia and her niece, she has
nothing left but grief and rage. Her answer begins the corruption of her soul.

DATES & ERA
Born: 8,779 BR
Died: 8,709 BR
Era: Warriorsʼ Age ]
Years Active: 8,779 BR  8,709 BR
IDENTITY
Full Name: Before marrying King HaliourLayern Patton I, Walica Kevena Patton was
known as Walica Banain, the only daughter of Dures the Great, also called Dures
Banain.
Historical Figures
5
House/Family: House Patton Through Marriage), The Banainʼs Maiden
Family/Pre-Marriage) Ethnicity: Aicruaean-Barie People with typically light to fair
skin tones, sometimes with pink or cool undertones. Their noses are often narrow
or straight-bridged; the tip may be pointed or softly rounded. Their eyes are
usually deep-set with defined eyelid creases in colors like blue, green, grey, hazel,
or light brown. Their hair texture is usually straight or wavy and the colors range
anywhere from blonde to brown to black to red. With an angular or softly squared
jawline, thinner lips that can sometimes be moderately full, cheekbones range
from high to mid-set.)
Appearance: Walica had a soft, symmetrical oval face with light skin and delicate
features. Walicaʼs eyes were clear, pale blue,and slightly almond-shaped with a
visible upper eyelid crease and gently rounded lower lids. She had slightly bushy
eyebrows that were moderately defined to frame her eyes. Walicaʼs nose was
small and straight, she had full gently curved lips. Her hair was light brown with a
warm undertone. Her hair was slightly wavy and long falling all the way to her
waist. She was roughly 5ʼ6” with a slender build, she had narrow shoulders and a
lean frame.
Nation: Aicruae
HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE
Known For: Walica Kevena Patton is known for being the wife of King Haliour
Layern Patton I, Known for being the daughter of Dures the Great, and the mother
of Prince Benjaien Nefest Patton (who would go on to become King Benjaien
Nefest Patton), Princess Aliedea Cawiloan Patton,and Princess Narseai Bekan
Patton.
Major Accomplishments: Besides giving birth to three Patton heirs; Prince Benjaien
Nefest Patton, Princess Aliedea Cawiloan Patton, and Princess Narseai Bekan
Patton. Queen Walica stabilized House Patton at a time when everyone wanted it
to fail, so they could claim the title for themselves; she helped secure the most
successful line to ever exist. She securely placed her son Prince Benjaien Nefest
Patton and he became King Benjaien Nefest Patton of Aicruae.
Major Failures:Queen Walicaʼs greatest personal failure was her inability to earn
the respect of the Aicruaean court during her husbandʼs lifetime. Despite being the
only daughter and heir of the most powerful warlord in the region, her father
Duresʼs brutal reputation preceded her, and she inherited the hatred and distrust
that others felt toward the Banainʼs. She was also unable to compete with Lenkitta
Historical Figures
6
Arvento for her husbandʼs attention and affection. Additionally, she lost her
youngest daughter Princess Narseai Bekan Patton in infancy ( 8,748 BR  8,747 BR
), and despite her efforts to guide her son Benjaien, he grew to resent and openly
hate her, wishing her dead and blaming her for controlling his life.
How History Remembers Them: At the time of Warriors age her family The
Benainʼs) was the most powerful in the region in what was to become the country
of Aicruae. When she was born her mother Tehesti Benain had succumbed to the
illness from childbirth. But, since her birth, she was loved by her father and
constantly protected by him during one of the most turbulent times in history. But,
when she reached age twenty, a new man, King Haliour Layern Patton I, arose to
claim the region/land as his. Walica for the first time in her life watched her father,
Dures the Great, bow to another man, King Haliour Layern Patton I, and call him
king. Dures the Great offered the newly twenty year old Walica as King Haliour
Layern Patton Iʼs bride. Walica married King Haliour Layern Patton I but her life
was far from perfect, from afar she watched as her husband King Haliour Layern
Patton) doted on Lenkitta Arvento and while everyone publicly claimed Walica as
their queen they held little respect for her because her father Dures, had besigned
the region for quite some time and had earned a nasty reputation, because of that
Walica took on hate because of her connection to him and the The Banainʼs.It
wasnʼt until her husbandʼs death in 8,736 BR that Walica was fully able to prove
that she was Dureʼs daughter by coming out of the shadow and acting as her son
Prince Benjaien Nefest Pattonʼs regent. Since her son was still “young” she acted
as his regent for six years until he officially took full power at the age of 24 .
Queen Walica Kevena Patton is often referred to as The Mother of the great
Aicruaean Dynasty but among other members of the house, she is often
outshadowed as well.
POWER & POSITION
Highest Title Held: Queen of Aicruae
Political Faction:As the first queen, Walica worked to legitimize and stabilize the
newly founded Patton dynasty. She maintained connections to her maiden family
the Banainʼs through her cousin Vala and leveraged those relationships to
strengthen Patton rule.
Key Allies:Queen Vala Uinara Patton (distant cousin whom she trusted enough to
Historical Figures
7
place at her sonʼs side as his wife to monitor his behavior), the Banain family
loyalists who remained after her fatherʼs defeat, and the court factions who
supported a stable regency during Benjaienʼs minority.
Key Enemies:Lenkitta Arvento (founder of House Arvento, her husbandʼs close
friend and advisor whom he openly favored over Walica), King Benjaien Nefest
Patton (her own son, who hated her and wished her dead), and the noble factions
who wanted House Patton to fail so they could claim the throne for themselves.
LEGACY
Immediate Impact:Walicaʼs regency (  ) preserved House
Patton during its most vulnerable period. After King Haliour Iʼs death, many
powerful factions saw an opportunity to seize power from the young heir Benjaien.
Walicaʼs firm hand prevented civil war and ensured a smooth succession. Her
arrangement of Benjaienʼs marriage to her trusted cousin Vala was an attempt to
maintain influence and stability even after she relinquished the regency.
Long-Term Impact:Walica established the precedent that Patton queens could and
would rule as regents when necessary, a tradition that would be invoked multiple
times throughout the dynastyʼs history. Her bloodline through both her son
Benjaien and her daughter Aliedea (who married into House Mena) created the
interconnected web of royal and noble lineages that would eventually produce
figures like Queen Isalian Liazen and, ultimately, Emperor Solis Elias Patton. Every
subsequent Patton ruler traces their lineage back to Walica. Additionally, a later
king, King Sayero Walica Patton ( 8,615 BR  8,540 BR, was named after her in
tribute to her legacy as the mother of the dynasty.
How Later Generations View Them:Queen Walica is viewed with a mixture of
reverence and pity. She is honored as “The Mother of the Great Aicruaean
Dynasty” and acknowledged as the woman who stabilized House Patton when
everyone wanted it to fail. But, she remains somewhat overshadowed by the more
dramatic figures who came after her, particularly the great love story of King
Haliour II and Queen Isalian, and the later imperial accomplishments of Solis. Later
generations recognize that without her sacrifice and steady governance, there
would have been no dynasty to inherit.
8,736BR−8,731BR
Historical Figures
8
Monuments/Memorials:King Sayero Walica Patton was named in her honor. As one
of the founding figures of House Patton, she is included in royal genealogies,
histories, and the official records of the dynasty. As the first queen she is
commemorated in the royal familyʼs ancestral halls and records.
CONNECTIONS TO NARRATIVE
Descendant Characters:Every member of House Patton after her, including
Emperor Solis Elias Patton (the protagonist of A Tale of A Thousand Songs),
descends from Walica. Her son King Benjaien Nefest Patton continued the direct
royal line, while her daughter Princess Aliedea Cawiloan Patton married Duke
Nayiler Mena and produced the lineage that would eventually lead to Queen Isalian
Liazen. Solis is her direct descendant through approximately 1516 generations.

House/Family: House Patton Through Marriage), The Casustʼs Maiden

or straight-bridged; the tip may be pointed or softly rounded. Their eyes are
usually deep-set with defined eyelid creases in colors like blue, green, grey, hazel,
or light brown. Their hair texture is usually straight or wavy and the colors range

jawline, thinner lips that can sometimes be moderately full, cheekbones range
from high to mid-set.)
Appearance: Vala had a fair, light toned complexion with smooth and even skin.
Her eyes were soft blue and fairly wide-set, almond shaped with a slight upward
tilt at the outer corners. Valaʼs eyebrows were well defined, and more cleanly
shaped with an arch framing around her eyes that gave her an intimidating and
almost masculine look. Her nose was narrow and straight with a subtle bridge and
refined tip. Her lips were full and evenly proportioned, with a slight downward
curve and natural
volume. Her hair was light blonde wavy and fell past her shoulders, her face shape
was oval and her face was balanced in width and length, she had a gently tapered
jawline and high cheekbones. She was  and had a slender build, and a notable
graceful frame.
Nation: Aicruae
HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE
Known For: Vala is known for being the distant cousin of Queen Walica Kevena
Patton.Vala is also known for being the Wife of King Benjaien Nefest Patton of
Aicruae, Also known for being the 2nd queen of Aicruae. And the mother of Prince
Ilaem Nefest Patton and Princess Cawiloan Heka Patton who would go on to
become King Ilaem Nefest Patton I and Queen Cawiloan Heka Patton of Aicruae.
Major Accomplishments:
Major Failures:Queen Vala was unable to win her husbandʼs affection or respect.
King Benjaien despised her from the beginning of their marriage, calling her “an
58′ ′′
Historical Figures
10
old prude” and resenting that she was older than him and (in his words) “looked
more like a king than him.” She could not protect herself from his jealousy or his
many affairs, and she suffered constant ill health from the strain of bearing his
children. Ultimately, she was unable to escape her fate and was most likely
murdered by the man she was forced to marry.
How History Remembers Them: Queen Vala was a distant cousin of Queen Walica.
Valaʼs father was Pavim Casust, her mother was Malejia Casust,and she had a
younger brother Kaseieke Casust who died in infamcy. One of Queen Walicaʼs
wishes was that her son, King Benjaien Nefest Patton of Aicruae marry Vala,
because Vala was one of her favorite cousins, and she felt as though to control
King Benjaien Nefest Patton after giving up her regency that it would be best to
appoint someone she trusted by his side to watch over her son who Queen Walica
personally called a reckless, irresponsible, bastard. So in 8,732 BR the two Vala
and Benjaien) married each other. King Benjaien Nefest Patton of Aicruae was
very childish and was said to have detested and more so loathed Valaʼs entire
existence. He was very aware of his motherʼs intention of putting Vala by his side
leading him to take out his frustration on Vala, calling her an old prude, a worthless
bitch and the bane of his existence because Benjaien also hated the fact that Vala
was older than him and how as he put it “looked more like a king than him”. So
because of these facts Vala led a very sad life, she was always the target of
jealousy from her husband and at the same time very sickly from giving him
children and heirs.Not much is known about her life other than the fact that she
was most likely poisoned by her husband.
POWER & POSITION
Highest Title Held: Queen of Aicruae
Political Faction:Vala served as a continuation of Queen Walicaʼs political strategy,
representing the Banain familyʼs interests within the royal household and
theoretically acting as a check on King Benjaienʼs worst impulses.
Key Allies:Queen Walica Kevena Patton (her cousin and mother-in-law, who
arranged the marriage to monitor her son), Princess Cawiloan Heka Patton (her
daughter, who remained fiercely loyal to her motherʼs memory throughout her life),
and the Banain family loyalists at court.
Key Enemies:King Benjaien Nefest Patton (her husband, who openly hated her and
Historical Figures
11
likely murdered her), Araner and Jelkita (the kingʼs lovers who replaced her
influence after her death and became his chief advisors), and the many other men
and women Benjaien took to his bed while Vala was still alive.
LEGACY
Immediate Impact:Valaʼs death (most likely by poisoning) freed King Benjaien from
what he considered the controlling influences of both his mother and his wife.
Ironically, after her death, Benjaienʼs lovers Araner and Jelkita became his
advisors and he finally matured into an effective ruler, accomplishing feats that
matched his fatherʼs legacy. Some interpret this as proof that Vala was never the
problem, Benjaien simply blamed her for his own inadequacies until she was gone.
Long-Term Impact:Valaʼs children carried her gentle nature and sense of duty into
the next generations. Her son Ilaem inherited her sickly constitution but also her
diplomatic abilities. Her daughter Cawiloan became one of the most beloved
figures in House Pattonʼs history, and Cawiloanʼs fierce hatred of her father
(stemming from his treatment of Vala) influenced court dynamics for decades.
When Benjaien died, Cawiloan wore white to his funeral, went to her motherʼs
grave, expelled all of his lovers from court, and forbade anyone from tending to his
burial site. This act of filial vengeance ensured that Valaʼs suffering would not be
forgotten.
How Later Generations View Them:. Her story is often contrasted with that of
Queen Isalian Liazen, who would later marry into a genuine love match with King
Haliour II, a relationship that was everything Valaʼs marriage was not.
Monuments/Memorials:Valaʼs grave was maintained and visited by her daughter
until Cawiloanʼs own death.
CONNECTIONS TO NARRATIVE
Descendant Characters:Through her son King Ilaem Nefest Patton I and daughter
Princess Cawiloan Heka Patton (who married ilaem in a consanguineous union
typical of early Patton practice), Vala is an ancestor of the entire subsequent
Patton line. This includes King Haliour Layern Patton II, King Viake Recreadion
Patton, King Sayero Walica Patton, and eventually Emperor Solis Elias Patton.
Every Patton after her carries her blood.

extraordinary craftsmanship and loose stones reserved for future settings.

Born to Queen Naila Deyua Patton and King Consort Teravian Geraser Patton,
Viake was the grandson of the legendary King Haliour Layern Patton II and Queen
Isalian Liazen, whose love story had inspired twelve songs and whose reign had
ushered in the Second Golden Age. The contrast between Viake and his
grandparents could not have been more stark. Where Haliour II had been devoted
and hardworking, Viake was lazy and indifferent. Where Isalian had enriched the
treasury and introduced countless innovations, Viakeʼs wife Queen Mari depleted it
through reckless spending and crushing taxes.
Viake married Mari Liazen, a woman from a distant branch of the Liazen family.

attended official business, preferring instead to indulge in whatever idle pleasures
caught his attention while his wife made all decisions. The people suffered under
Mariʼs inflated taxes, watching the royal treasury their grandparentsʼ generation
had built be drained for frivolous expenditure. Viake earned the epithet “The
Skunk King” because he was considered foul and repulsive, and “The Weak King”

pacifist religious sect that rejected worship of the gods and instead venerated the

communal charity. Their pacifism made them easy targets, and King Viakeʼs forces
killed men, women, and children alike. The massacre was committed for no
justifiable reason beyond royal paranoia and fanaticism, likely because the sectʼs
growing influence challenged traditional religious authority. The surviving Pure

Aryanara  (approximate)
Aryanara was one of the twin prophets who co-founded the Circle of Eternal Light
in 14,271 BR. She and her sister Vekta were the first to articulate that death was
merely a pause in a longer song, that souls carried traces of past lives into new
bodies, and that corruption was the only true ending. They were not saints-they
carried no fraction of a godʼs power-but they lived close enough to the age of
saints to witness miracles firsthand. Aryanara was the more contemplative twin,
drawn to the philosophical and metaphysical aspects of the soulʼs journey. She
recorded Vektaʼs speeches, and these writings became the foundational texts of
the Circle. She established a teaching center in what became the eastern
heartland of Gherci, in fertile river valleys that attracted scholars and thinkers. She
emphasized memory, the way souls carry echoes of past lives, and the eternal
nature of the spirit. After her death, her territory became a place of pilgrimage.
The lands were incorporated into Gherci by Saint Duri in 8,763 BR and are
protected by House Catern.

purification and protection. She emphasized action-how to live in harmony with

Known For: His crusade for social justice - economic equality, womenʼs rights, and
freedom of speech. Earned the title “The Sacred Knight” for his chivalrous
dedication to these causes. His assassination at 18 made him a martyr whose
ideas spread even more widely after his death.
Major Accomplishments: Led a crusade for economic equality - at one point,
drank only salt water for days to draw attention to the plight of the poor. Boldly
promoted women to high positions of power, strengthening and updating Saint
Siriandeʼs Yerian Laws. Became a staunch defender of free speech and freedom
of the press, even inviting criticism of himself. Famously declared: “If you have no
enemies, then you have no friends.”
Major Failures: His progressive stances made him fierce enemies. He was
ultimately ambushed and slain by those threatened by his reforms. His beloved
sister died defending him in the attack.
How History Remembers Them: Malign is remembered as a martyr and reformer
whose brief life inspired generations. Even the god Finore, who blessed him, is
said to have chosen him because they shared values. His assassination shocked
the world and made his ideas spread even further than they had during his
lifetime. The month of Baer October) was created after his death. His
Zodiac/Eternal Sign is Baerin Welcoming, Individualistic).
POWER & POSITION
Highest Title Held: Tenth Saint (blessed by Finore, God of the Forge)
Key Allies: Finore (patron god - shared his values); his sister (died defending him)
Key Enemies: Those threatened by his reforms - political enemies who arranged
his assassination
LEGACY
⼀
Historical Figures
96
Immediate Impact: His assassination made him a martyr. His ideas about economic
equality, womenʼs rights, and free speech spread even more widely after his
death. Many continued to champion his causes.
Long-Term Impact: Saint Duri, the greatest of all Saints, was personally obsessed
with Malign. She worshipped him like an idol, believed he was “taken before his
time,” and spent her entire life trying to spread his beliefs. This one-woman
crusade to honor Malignʼs legacy was a driving force behind many of Duriʼs own
reforms. Malignʼs brief life cemented the principle that moral leadership can
challenge even entrenched social norms.
How Later Generations View Them: Deeply revered. His quote about enemies and
friends remains well-known. He represents the ideal of a principled reformer who
stood by his convictions even when it cost him everything.
Monuments/Memorials: Statue erected in Gherciʼs capital by Saint Duri (given
particular prominence due to Duriʼs devotion). Month of Baer named in his honor.
CONNECTIONS TO NARRATIVE
Descendant Characters: None noted - died at 18
Events Referenced in Books: His reforms and assassination are referenced as
formative events in the development of gender equality and free speech traditions
How Characters View Them: TBD

Where This Figure Appears in Canon: Timeline, Canon document Saints list #10 -
implied), Era 5 synopsis
Contradictory Accounts (if any): None noted.
NOTES
Malignʼs death during “a holy celebration” (per the Era 5 synopsis) adds extra
horror - he was killed at what should have been a sacred, protected event. His
sisterʼs unnamed sacrifice (dying to defend him) is a powerful detail that deserves
further development. At 18, Malign achieved more for social reform than many who
Historical Figures
97
lived decades longer. His influence on Duri - who became arguably the most
accomplished Saint of all - means his legacy was multiplied exponentially through
her devotion to his cause.

HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE
Known For: Being the most accomplished Saint in history. The only Saint to found,
rule, and die as monarch of a nation Gherci. The longest-lived Saint at 77 years.
Never lost a single battle. Blessed by Allan, Goddess of Nature, who believed Duri
was destined for greatness.
Major Accomplishments: Founded the Kingdom of Gherci (“The Land of Eternal
Silence”) in 8,763 BR. Created the first formal judicial court system to ensure laws
like the Code of Esa were upheld impartially. Authored military strategies that
became classics of warfare, studied by generals for centuries. Constructed an
international trade route linking Gherciʼs markets with distant lands. Established
8,747BR
8,670BR
8,900−7,945BR
8,747−8,670
Historical Figures
98
“Tanyaʼs” - the worldʼs first free public hospitals for common folk. Erected
monuments to all ten Saints before her in Gherciʼs capital, placing their statues as
protective sentinels around the city while humbly making her own statue the
smallest. Spent her life spreading the beliefs of Saint Malign, whom she idolized.
Major Failures: Many historical texts describe Duri as cold and standoffish. Her
personal relationships appear to have suffered for her public achievements. Her
diaries reveal a woman carrying immense guilt over the lives she took in battle.
How History Remembers Them: Duri has more titles than any other Saint: “Queen
of the People,” “The True Saint,” “Duri the Wise,” “The Mother of Gherci.” She was
the most powerful and wisest of the Saints. She is the fourth and final Saint buried
in the kingdom of the gods, honored for her unparalleled accomplishments. The
month of Niserfa November) was created after her death. Her Zodiac/Eternal Sign
is Sinfa Outspoken, Pompous, Illogical).
POWER & POSITION
Highest Title Held: Queen of Gherci / Eleventh Saint (blessed by Allan, Goddess of
Nature) Key Allies: Allan (patron goddess); the memory of Saint Malign (her idol)
Key Enemies: All who opposed Gherciʼs founding and expansion - though none
ever defeated her in battle
LEGACY
Immediate Impact: Gherci established as a unified, powerful kingdom. Judicial
courts, military academies, trade routes, and public hospitals created. The ten
Saints memorialized in Gherciʼs capital.
Long-Term Impact: Gherci stood as a beacon of enlightened rule for centuries.
Duriʼs judicial courts, military strategies, trade routes, and hospitals improved
common life across the world. Her decision to make her own statue the smallest of
the eleven saintly monuments in Gherci became a famous symbol of humility and
service. She is the last of four Saints buried among the gods - after her, no Saint
would receive that honor.
How Later Generations View Them: Revered as the greatest Saint. Her diaries - in
which she wrote the name of every enemy soldier she killed, penning “I am sorry”
beside each name - revealed a compassionate heart beneath her cold exterior.
Historical Figures
99
Monuments/Memorials: Buried in the kingdom of the gods (fourth and final Saint
to receive this honor). Her own statue (the smallest) among the eleven saintly
monuments in Gherciʼs capital. Month of Niserfa named in her honor. “Tanyaʼs”
public hospitals. International trade routes. Judicial court system.
CONNECTIONS TO NARRATIVE
Descendant Characters: Gherciʼs royal House Mava descends from or is
established by Duriʼs political legacy
Events Referenced in Books: The founding of Gherci; the Warriorsʼ Age
How Characters View Them: TBD
SOURCES
Where This Figure Appears in Canon: Timeline (multiple entries), Canon document
Saints list #11 Warriorsʼ Age synopsis, Location entries for Gherci
Contradictory Accounts (if any): Historical texts describe her as cold and
standoffish; her diaries reveal deep compassion and guilt. These arenʼt
contradictions so much as different layers of the same person.
NOTES
Duriʼs obsession with Saint Malign is one of her most defining traits - she
“worshipped him like an idol” and “thought that Malign was taken before his time.”
This devotion drove much of her lifeʼs work. Her famous quote: “To have existed
for as long as I have, one must ultimately reconcile with those who once stood as
their adversaries, even if they remain oblivious to such gestures of peace. For it is
the divine, in their omniscience, who observes the full spectrum of our deeds and
moral failings.” The detail about her diary - recording every kill with “I am sorry” -
is one of the most emotionally powerful details in the entire worldbuilding canon.
SAINT RERON
Name Meaning: TBD
Ender of Worlds, The Twelfth Saint, The Taboo Saint]
DATES & ERA

Historical Figures

IDENTITY
Full Name: Reron (no surname noted)
House/Family: Son of a mortal woman named Mevi (who was falsely accused of
seducing Vapaz). Had a wife (name unknown, murdered), an eldest daughter
(murdered), and a youngest child whom he hid in Equateiy.
Ethnicity: TBD
Appearance: TBD
Nation: TBD - operated across multiple territories; hid his youngest child in
Equateiy]
HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE
Known For: Being the most controversial Saint in history. A “taboo Saint” -
depending on who tells the story, he was or was not truly a Saint. Blessed by
Vapaz (the second of only two Saints to receive Vapazʼs gift, alongside Bura),
Reron used his powers not for peace but for vengeance after the murder of his
wife and eldest daughter. He destroyed villages and killed many people at will,
earning the nickname “Ender of Worlds.”
Major Accomplishments: None in the traditional sense - Reronʼs “achievements”
were acts of destruction driven by grief and vengeance]
Major Failures: Reronʼs entire story is one of tragedy and moral failure - not his
own, but the worldʼs failure toward him, and then his failure to channel his grief
into anything but violence. He abused his saintly powers for revenge, killing
indiscriminately and destroying communities. His campaign of vengeance made
him a figure of terror.
How History Remembers Them: Reron is deeply divisive. Many sympathize with
him, saying he only killed and destroyed to avenge his family. Others say he
abused his power as a Saint for petty revenge. His mother Mevi was hanged after
being labeled “a witch and a temptress who seduced the god Vapaz” - the
recurring theme of mortals accusing others of breaking divine rules. Young Reron
was left as a beggar. When he manifested his abilities at 24 , the people used his
wife and children as hostages to force him to perform his duties as a Saint.
Historical Figures
101
Eventually, his captors killed his wife and eldest daughter. He rescued his
youngest child and hid her in Equateiy, never seeing her again. The month of
Agariso December) was created after his death. His Zodiac/Eternal Sign is Gariso
Carefree, Friendly, Charming) - another sharp irony given his violent life.
POWER & POSITION
Highest Title Held: Twelfth Saint (blessed by Vapaz, King of the Gods)
Key Allies: Vapaz (patron god); his youngest child (hidden in Equateiy)
Key Enemies: Those who hanged his mother, held his family hostage, and
murdered his wife and eldest daughter
LEGACY
Immediate Impact: His campaign of destruction devastated villages and killed
untold numbers. The Battle of Relirian - his final stand - was apocalyptic: Reron
ensured no enemy left the battlefield alive, unleashing the full fury of Vapazʼs
power before dying himself at age 48 amid a pile of his slaughtered foes.
Long-Term Impact: Reronʼs story made the concept of sainthood permanently
complicated. He proved that divine power in the hands of a broken person could
be catastrophically destructive. His infamy is second only to Saint Harnua (the
13th Saint). Debates about whether Reron was “truly” a Saint persist into the
present era of the narrative. His youngest child, hidden somewhere in Equateiy,
may have descendants — but their identities are unknown.
How Later Generations View Them: Deeply divided. Some view him as a tragic
hero driven to madness by injustice. Others view him as proof that the godsʼ
choices were fallible. His story is considered taboo to discuss openly.
Monuments/Memorials: No known monuments (given his controversial status).
Statue erected in Gherciʼs capital by Saint Duri (as part of her memorial to all
Saints before her). Month of Agariso named in his honor. The Battle of Relirian site.
CONNECTIONS TO NARRATIVE
Historical Figures
102
Descendant Characters: His youngest child was hidden in Equateiy - potential
descendants unknown Events Referenced in Books: The Battle of Relirian;
referenced throughout as the prime example of a “failed” or “dark” Saint
How Characters View Them: TBD
SOURCES
Where This Figure Appears in Canon: Timeline Battle of Relirian entry), Canon
document Saints list #12
Contradictory Accounts (if any): Whether Reron was “truly” a Saint is actively
debated. Whether his mother actually had an affair with Vapaz or was falsely
accused is unclear. Whether his vengeance was justified is a matter of
perspective.
NOTES
Reronʼs story contains a recurring theme from the canon: “mortals will always
accuse other mortals and even saints of breaking some divine rule.” His motherʼs
execution on charges of seducing Vapaz mirrors the false accusations that killed
Saint Galamma. The detail that Reron manifested his abilities at 24 and was
immediately enslaved through hostage-taking shows that even divine power
couldnʼt protect him from mortal cruelty when his loved ones were leveraged
against him. His youngest child, hidden in Equateiy and never seen again, is a
loose thread with significant narrative potential.

Born a mortal prince of Aicruae, third child of King Benjamin and his concubine
Lady Emillea Hige. After the deaths of his father and mother Lady Emillea was
forced to drink poison during his half-siblingsʼ coup), Solis waged a civil war

entries.title: House Aedria
entries.text:
House Aedria
House Aedria
“HONOR TO THE LESSER”
Quick Facts
Status: Count/Countess
Origin: Aicruae Eastern), ties to House Liazen
Founded: 8,516 BR (shortly after Kaernio and Cairyiaʼs wedding)
Official Founder: Kaernio Aedria
“Real” Founder: Atiane Aedria (created the house motto, designed the crest,
lifelong charity work)
Name Meaning: Servant of the Gods
Seat: Haleker, Eastern Aicruae (opposite side of town from House Vika)
Faction: Neutral (despite ties to the Divine Faction, thanks to Atiane)
Spirit Animal: Ram (a knight riding a ram with sword and shield)
Colors:
Wealth: 138,000 Rern (from The Aedria, Kanus Company / TAKC
Military: Merchant family that also operates as a knight family; one of the noble
houses that produce the most knights for the crown
Religion: Barqeten
Theme Song: “Breath of Life” by Florence + The Machine
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Count/Countess. Founded in 8,516 BR as a wedding gift from the
king. One of the most publicly loved houses in Aicruae, built on charity,
commerce, and knightly service to the crown.
Solisʼs Era: Count/Countess. Head of house: Janileandora Aedria. House Aedria
survives the civil war between Solis and the twins, with the familyʼs line continuing
through Lady Alizieya Aedria.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
House Aedria
1
Why They Matter
House Aedria was born from something ugly. A 32-year-old man married a 17
year-old exile whoʼd already been abused by her own family, and the king signed
off because the groom was his friend. Cairyia Liazen endured countless
miscarriages, a husband who cheated on her with even younger girls, and died at
27 giving birth to her second child. Kaernio was so despised by his own children
that they called him “the enemy” and refused him a proper burial.
But from that rotten foundation, the Aedria children built something extraordinary.
Zolair became one of the most powerful magic users in Aicruaeʼs history, earning
the title “nationʼs treasure” and changing the countryʼs position in global trade.
Elsenthe restructured the house into a dual matriarchal-patriarchal power system
and reformed divorce laws to protect women. Atiane gave the house its
conscience, its motto, and its crest. Kanus turned the Aedria name into a
household staple through commerce. They co-founded the Council of the
Forsaken, a feared alliance that cut the kingdomʼs crime rate to 30%.
House Aedria is the proof that a familyʼs legacy doesnʼt have to be defined by the
man who started it. Everything good about this house came after Kaernio, and
most of it came from the women.
Heraldry
The Crest: Azure, a knight in full silver armor mounted upon a white ram passant
with brown horns, the knight bearing a sword raised in dexter and a blue shield in
sinister, plumed azure. The shield is bordered brown. Below, a tilted silver helm
with blue and white oak leaf mantling.
Symbolism: The knight riding a ram is the soul of House Aedria, service and
humility fused into a single image. A knight is the highest expression of duty to the
crown, and House Aedria produces more knights for the king than nearly any
other noble family. But Atiane Aedria, the woman who designed this crest, didnʼt
put the knight on a warhorse. She put him on a ram. The ram is a creature of the
common pasture, of shepherds and farmland, of the people the Aedrias swore to
protect. The message is deliberate: House Aedria rides to battle on the back of the
lesser, and they will never forget who carries them.
House Aedria
2
The raised sword represents the houseʼs willingness to fight, not for territory or
ambition, but for justice. House Aedria is a founding member of the Council of the
Forsaken, and their knights serve the crown directly. The sword is lifted, not
sheathed. The Aedrias are not passive.
The blue shield carried in the knightʼs off-hand represents loyalty and sovereignty,
loyalty to the crown, to the common people, and to the faith. Blue is the dominant
color of the house because loyalty is the dominant virtue. Everything House
Aedria built after Kaernio, the charity, the commerce, the knighthood, the Council
was built on earning the trust their founder never deserved.
The brown border represents modesty. House Aedria is a countʼs family, not
dukes, not royalty. They sit in Eastern Aicruae across the town from House Vika,
and they have never tried to be anything grander than what they are. Brown is the
earth. Brown is the ground. The Aedrias stay close to it.
The tilted helm with oak leaf mantling beneath the shield is a mark of knightly rank
and tournament tradition a declaration that House Aedria earns its standing
through service, not inheritance. The oak leaves represent endurance and
strength. This is a family that survived its own poisoned origins and grew into
something the entire kingdom wants to be.
House Colors: Blue and Brown. Blue for loyalty, sovereignty, and devotion to the
crown and the faith. Brown for modesty, humility, and closeness to the common
people.
Motto: “Honor to the Lesser.” Created by Atiane Aedria, the woman considered the
true founder of the house. The motto is a command and a confession. It tells every
Aedria who comes after her that their purpose is not to climb higher but to reach
lower to the orphans Atiane built homes for, to the impoverished children she
created jobs for, to the women Elsenthe wrote divorce protections for, to every
person in Aicruae who has no title and no name and no one fighting for them. The
“lesser” are not lesser at all. Thatʼs the point. The motto is a rebuke of everything
Kaernio represented a man who married a powerless girl because he could and a
promise that House Aedria will never again be defined by someone who sees
people beneath him as things to use.
Power & Influence
House Aedria
3
Source of Power
Commerce The Aedria, Kanus Company), knightly service to the crown, charity,
and public goodwill. House Aedriaʼs influence comes less from military might and
more from being genuinely beloved by the common people and respected by
other houses.
Internal Power Structure
Both matriarchal and patriarchal, a dual system established by Elsenthe Aedria.
Leadership isnʼt restricted by gender.
Military Forces
House Aedria is a merchant family that also operates as a knight family. They are
one of the noble houses that produce the most knights for the king and the crown.
They donʼt command a private army the way House Vika does, but their
contribution to the crownʼs military through knighthood is significant.
Lands & Income
Seat: The town of Haleker in Eastern Aicruae, on the opposite side of town from
House Vika.
Wealth: 138,000 Rern, earned through The Aedria, Kanus Company TAKC.
Key industries: Fragrance and soap TAKCʼs perfume brand), trade, and
commerce.
Lands controlled: TBD
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Liazen Birth Family of Cairyia). Cairyia was born into House Liazen before
her marriage to Kaernio. The Liazen branch she came from had a connection to
Vikistv blood heritage, which is how magic manifested in the Aedria line. Queen
Isilian Liazen, a distant relative of Kanus Aedria, introduced the concept of
perfume to Aicruae, and her idea inspired the creation of TAKC.
House Aedria
4
House Arvento Marriage Alliance & Council of the Forsaken). Two marriage
alliances connect the families: Rorca Arvento married Bariaro Aedria, and Laitha
Arvento I married Jeart Aedria. Both families are members of the Council of the
Forsaken and belong to the neutral political faction.
House Najil Marriage Alliance). Lady Erhen Aedria married Matasen Najil and had
nine children together, including Basiol Najil.
House Patton / Royal Family Adoption & Kingʼs Affection). Zolair Aedria was
adopted as a Des (distant relative) of the royal family and received the Kingʼs
Affection.
House Caraen Council of the Forsaken). Both families are founding members of
the Council of the Forsaken.
Rival Houses
TBD
Shared Territory
House Vika. Both houses share the town of Haleker, occupying opposite ends of
the city. Both are known for inflicting “brutish punishments” on criminals
House Culture
Religion
Barqeten. Followers of Barqeten believe that by simply existing, they worship the
gods. The faith emphasizes physical and mental wellness.
Traditions
TBD
Values
The common people. House Aedriaʼs identity is rooted in service to those beneath
them, not above.
Reputation
House Aedria
5
The “IT family” of Aicruae. Everyone wants to be them. They are loved and
respected by other noble houses, a reputation built primarily through the legacies
of Elsenthe, Kanus, and Zolair, and cemented by Atianeʼs lifelong charity work.
How Others Perceive Them
TBD
History
Founding (8,516 BR)
House Aedria was created as a wedding gift. The king, a close friend of Kaernioʼs,
granted him land and a noble title when he married Cairyia Liazen. The name
“Aedria” means “Servant of the Gods.” In the public eye, the house and the
marriage were presented as happy. Behind closed doors, the reality was far uglier.
Kaernio married a 17-year-old exile at age 32 in what was effectively a coerced
union. The king at the time saw nothing wrong with it and allowed it because of his
friendship with Kaernio. The match set a precedent for what was considered
acceptable in Aicruaen society and spread considerable controversy, even as the
public image remained polished.
Rise to Power
House Aedriaʼs rise had nothing to do with its founder. Zolair Aedriaʼs
extraordinary magical talent, approaching or surpassing saint-level abilities,
brought international attention to Aicruae and changed the countryʼs trading
position globally. He earned the Kingʼs Affection and was adopted as a Des of the
royal family. His sister Elsenthe created magical instruments, reformed the houseʼs
power structure, and lowered the land tax. Atiane, considered by many to be the
“real founder,” created the houseʼs motto, designed the crest, and spent her life
building orphanages and businesses that created jobs for impoverished children.
Kanus turned a distant relativeʼs idea into a commercial empire with TAKC, earning
the house 25,000 Rern and making the Aedria name a household staple.
Major Achievements
The Aedria, Kanus Company TAKC, a fragrance and soap company that became
a commercial empire. Magical instruments created by Elsenthe Aedria.
House Aedria
6
Participation in the Battle of Jatlya Zolair served while Elsenthe administered the
territory). The Kingʼs Affection, awarded to Zolair. Zolairʼs adoption as official Des
of the royal family. The Council of the Forsaken (founding member alongside
House Arvento and House Caraen; reduced the kingdomʼs crime rate to 30%;
formed 8,051 BR.
Major Disgraces
TBD Though the houseʼs founding circumstances, Kaernioʼs marriage to a 17
year-old exile at 32, the spread of controversies surrounding the union, and his
childrenʼs refusal to give him a proper burial are all part of the record.)
The Battle of Jatlya & the Kalip Plague (8,160s BR)
In the closing years of the War of Worldʼs End, a devastating plague the Kalip
Plague swept through the war-torn lands. Men across Aicruae were scouted for
battle, and Zolair Aedria was among those called to serve. He left his sister
Elsenthe in charge of House Aedriaʼs territory while he fought at Jatlya. What he
came home to was a house better run than when heʼd left it. The people loved
Elsentheʼs leadership, and Zolair handed the family headship to her on his return.
The Battle of Jatlya is one of House Aedriaʼs major achievements not because of
what Zolair did on the battlefield, but because of what Elsenthe built while he was
gone.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs origins through its later generations.
Kaernio Aedria (8,548 BR – 8,499 BR)
Official Founder of House Aedria
Name meaning: Tired
The kingʼs friend who received land and a noble title as a wedding gift when he
married Cairyia Liazen. Kaernio was 32 when he married the 17-year-old exile. He
is the official founder of House Aedria, but a controversial figure. While the house
and the marriage appeared happy in the public eye, the reality was different. The
king at the time saw nothing wrong with the union and allowed it because of his
friendship with Kaernio, setting a precedent for what was acceptable in Aicruaen
House Aedria
7
society. His children called him “the enemy” and refused to give him a proper
burial. He died at 49.
Cairyia Aedria (8,533 BR – 8,506 BR)
Born Cairyia Liazen | “The Great Tragedy of the Warriorʼs Age”
Name meaning: Lady of the Sun
Born into House Liazen, Cairyia was exiled at 17 for “unladylike behavior,” which
included stealing and loss of virginity. The truth behind those charges was uglier:
she had been abused by her uncle at 15, and House Liazen responded by
imprisoning and starving her rather than punishing the uncle. After her exile, she
began manifesting magic thought to have been lost in the Liazen family, proof of
the familyʼs Vikistv blood heritage.
She was coerced into marriage with Kaernio at 17. Over the course of their
marriage, she suffered countless miscarriages, and her husband cheated on her
multiple times with even younger girls. She died at 27 giving birth to her second
child, Elsenthe. Her eldest was Zolair. Cairyia is remembered as “the great tragedy
of the so-called warriorʼs age or golden age.”
Lady Erhen Aedria
Dates not specified
Married Matasen Najil 8,534 BR  8,465 BR) and had nine children together. Their
son Basiol Najil 8,498 BR  8,439 BR) is among the most notable of those
children.
Zolair Aedria (8,515 BR – 8,440 BR)
“Nationʼs Treasure” | “Nationʼs Gift” | “Nationʼs Sunshine”
Name meaning: Sunlight
Eldest child of Cairyia and Kaernio. Zolair possessed extraordinary magical talent
approaching or surpassing saint-level abilities, making him one of the earliest and
youngest examples of a magic user surpassing saint abilities. His power brought
international attention to Aicruae and changed the countryʼs trading position
globally.
House Aedria
8
He received the Kingʼs Affection and was adopted as a Des (distant relative) of the
royal family. Unlike his father, Zolair respected women and allowed his sister
Elsentheʼs abilities to flourish. When he was scouted to join the Battle of Jatlya, he
left Elsenthe in charge of House Aedriaʼs territory. Upon his return, he saw the
quality of her leadership and handed the position of head of the family over to her.
He died at 75.
Elsenthe Aedria (8,506 BR – 8,442 BR)
Name meaning: Sunkissed
Only daughter and younger child of Cairyia and Kaernio. Some speculate she was
even more magically powerful than Zolair. Elsenthe created magical instruments
using her abilities.
When her brother was called to serve in the Battle of Jatlya, she was left in charge
of House Aedriaʼs territory. The people loved her. Once Zolair returned, he gave
her the position of head of the family because he saw how great a job she had
done, and because, unlike their father, he respected her as an equal and saw the
value of women.
As head of the house, Elsenthe lowered House Aedriaʼs land tax, created better
rules for divorce to help women in the territory (building on rules already
established), and established the dual matriarchal-patriarchal power structure that
defines House Aedria to this day. She died at 64.
Atiane Aedria (8,290 BR – 8,181 BR)
“The Real Founder”
Name meaning: Noble Blade
Considered by many to be the true founder of House Aedria. Atiane created the
house saying “Honor to the Lesser,” designed the familyʼs crest, and devoted her
life to charity work. She established orphanages and businesses that created jobs
for poor and impoverished children.
Atiane is the reason House Aedria is loved and respected despite its controversial
origins. She is also the reason the house sits in the neutral political faction, despite
its ties to the divine faction through the Liazen family. She died at 109.
House Aedria
9
Jeart Aedria
Dates not specified
Married Laitha Arvento I 7,651 BR  7,582 BR. Laitha was so taken with him that
she based all the male leads in her romance novels after him. She received the
title of Golden Pen for her books.
Kanus Aedria (7,532 BR – 7,415 BR)
Merchant and Heir to House Aedria
Name meaning: Little Prince
The merchant who turned the Aedria name into a brand. Kanus created a
fragrance and soap company based on an idea from his distant relative Queen
Isilian Liazen, who had introduced the concept of perfume to Aicruae. He founded
The Aedria, Kanus Company TAKC) and created a perfume brand within it.
TAKC earned House Aedria 25,000 Rern and made the family name a household
staple across the kingdom. He died at 117.
Bariaro Aedria
Dates not specified
Married Rorca Arvento, who proposed to him. They lived happily together. Rorca
died at 68, Bariaro at 71. Without Rorca, Bariaro spent his last days in agony.
The Council of the Forsaken
Formed in 8,051 BR, forty-three years after the Taguar Murders 8,094 BR. The
Council of the Forsaken was an alliance of three neutral noble families: House
Arvento, House Aedria, and House Caraen. It functioned as a medieval police
department investigating violent crimes. The Council had the kingʼs approval and
was greatly feared. Under its authority, the kingdomʼs crime rate was reduced to
30%.
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
House Aedria
10
Public goodwill, commercial success TAKC, knightly service to the crown,
charity work, magical talent Zolair and Elsenthe), founding role in the Council of
the Forsaken, and a reputation as the house everyone wants to be associated
with.
What They Lack
TBD
Vulnerabilities
TBD
Role in Narrative
Book Appearances: Book 1 A Tale of a Thousand Songs).
Plot Significance: House Aedria survives the civil war between Solis and the twins.
The familyʼs line continues through Lady Alizieya Aedria. Head of house during
Solisʼs Era is Janileandora Aedria.
Key Members in Story: Janileandora Aedria, Alizieya Aedria, Exara Aedria, Olia
Aedria. All appear in A Tale of a Thousand Songs.
