entries.title: House Arvento
entries.text:
House Arvento
House Arvento
“FOR THE HONOR OF THE LOST ONE”
Quick Facts
Status: Duke/Duchess of Northern Aicruae
Origin: Gherci (ancestors migrated to Aicruae)
House Name Meaning: Morning Wind
Founded: 8,746 BR second-oldest noble house in Aicruae, after the royal family
Founder: Lenkitta Arvento 8,784 BR  8,702 BR
Seat: Aishae, Northern Aicruae (port town, built around the family home)
Faction: Neutral (alongside House Aedria and House Caraen)
Symbol: Red Rose with Sword
Colors: TBD
Wealth: 180,000 Rern
Military: Arvento Night Soldiers not the largest force, but bolstered by magical
weapons Warrior Hearts, Gifted Objects, Swords of Aishae)
Religion: Barqeten Circle of Eternal Light)
Theme Song: “Whatever It Takes” by Imagine Dragons
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Duke/Duchess of Northern Aicruae. One of the three neutral noble
families. Second-oldest house in the kingdom, founded just thirteen years after
House Patton. Trusted advisors and scholars to the crown. Survived the War of
Worldʼs End, rebuilt under Viason Arvento, and entered a golden age of trade, law,
and cultural production.
Solisʼs Era: House Arvento survives the civil war between Solis and the Twins
Orcus and Iris) by remaining neutral and refusing to choose an official side. They
continue to exist for thousands of years, all the way to Minaraʼs Era.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
House Arvento
1
Why They Matter
House Arvento is the lie every noble family tells about itself except Arvento
actually lives it. Theyʼre the scholars who write laws protecting children and the
same family that fed a queen to hunting dogs. They invented hospitals and also
invented a poison that crushes your blood vessels over two hours while you
scream. They preach “Worthy Nobility” the idea that nobles should earn their
status while operating as the undisclosed rulers of every social circle in Aicruae,
quietly destroying anyone who falls out of their favor.
They call themselves neutral. They are not neutral. They are simply too powerful
for anyone to force into choosing a side, and too smart to give anyone a reason to
try. The royal family canʼt question them. The other houses canʼt afford to lose
them. And the Arventos know it.
What makes them dangerous isnʼt the magical weapons or the poison or the
Council of the Forsaken. Itʼs that theyʼve convinced the entire kingdom theyʼre the
reasonable ones the beautiful, elegant, scholarly family who just wants peace.
And then you remember Daneya wearing the dead queenʼs blood in a necklace,
and Tilan burning House Baliva off the map, and you realize: the morning wind
doesnʼt just carry flowers. It levels buildings.
Heraldry
The Crest: Gyronny of eight vert and or (eight triangular sections radiating from
center, alternating green and gold). At center, a red rose proper with golden
stamen and dark green leaves, pierced by a silver sword with ornate golden hilt
laid in bend sinister. In the upper dexter, a white roundel (full moon). In the upper
sinister, a silver needle threaded with red. In the lower dexter, a golden chalice. In
the lower sinister, a golden hunting horn.
Sybolism: The red rose pierced by a sword is the heart of House Arvento. The
rose reflects their Barqeten faith, which holds that caring for oneself and others is
an act of worship, while the sword cutting through it says the Arventos will destroy
what they love if honor demands it. Together they are the houseʼs oldest truth: the
morning wind carries flowers and levels buildings. The full moon honors Nimlye,
Goddess of Secrets and Fate. House Arvento operates the Council of the
Forsaken, an underground justice organization that answers to no one but the
House Arvento
2
king. They are the undisclosed rulers of Aicruaeʼs social circles. The moon
watches everything and says nothing, so do the Arventos. The needle and red
thread represents the houseʼs legacy of stitching the kingdom together through
law and medicine. The Infant Laws protecting mothers and children. The Yerian
Laws protecting women. The Arvento Code that became the kingdomʼs de facto
constitution. Finshall Arventoʼs hospitals and medical texts. Taharry Arventoʼs
breakthroughs in treating Night Terrors. The thread is red because Arvento care
has always been inseparable from Arvento blood, they heal and they hurt with
equal precision. The golden chalice symbolizes devotion and abundance,
communion with the divine through the Barqeten belief that existence itself is
worship. It also reflects the houseʼs legendary wealth and hospitality, the 180,000
Rern fortune that makes them the masters of nobility. The golden hunting horn is
the call to justice. When House Arvento sounds the horn, the Council of the
Forsaken rides. It represents the Arvento Night Soldiers and the familyʼs
philosophy that being neutral does not mean being passive, it means being the
one who decides when the hunt begins.
House Colors: Green and Gold. Green for growth, prosperity, and the fertile
territory of Northern Aicruae. Gold for wealth, divine favor, and the Barqeten belief
that a well-lived life honors the gods.
Motto: “For the Honor of the Lost One.” The motto honors Saint Galamma, the
Third Saint, called “The Lost One.” Blessed by the god Sielaph, Galamma was
kidnapped and executed at eighteen after being falsely accused of being a demon
during a time of religious hysteria. Her death became the worldʼs cautionary tale
about prejudice and rushing to judgment. House Arventoʼs devotion to justice, the
Council of the Forsaken, the Infant Laws, the Arvento Code, their relentless pursuit
of anyone who wrongs them, is framed as honoring Galammaʼs memory. They will
not let the innocent be destroyed by the ignorant. Not again.
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Social influence, magical weapons production, international trade, accumulated
wealth, and the Council of the Forsaken.
Succession & Inheritance
House Arvento
3
House Arvento follows a firstborn-inherits system: the first child born to the ruling
couple becomes heir, and that personʼs first child becomes next in line. In the case
of twins, whichever child is delivered first receives the title. Women can inherit the
familyʼs power and keep the Arvento name while married, if no male heirs are
present a right established by Warias Arvento and first exercised by his daughter
Zahali.
The house also operates on “Worthy Nobility” the philosophical principle (created
by Rorca Arvento) that nobles must act in a way befitting their status and
favorability, meaning how much the people love you matters to your standing
within the family.
Wealth
180,000 Rern. Called “the master of nobility.” They are the undisclosed leaders of
the social circles, and falling out with them is the fastest way to lose respect and
standing among the Aicruan elite.
Military
The Arvento Night Soldiers guards and knights created by Chiane Arvento,
charged with protecting Aishae, Arvento territory, and all family members. House
Arventoʼs military isnʼt the largest in Aicruae, but their supply of magical weapons
Warrior Hearts, Gifted Objects, and the Swords of Aishae) makes them a threat
nobody wants to test. Every house needs House Arvento for something, but
House Arvento is extremely selective about who they let in.
Territory
The town of Aishae in Northern Aicruae, plus the port built around it after the
Battle of Aishae 8,704 BR. Arvento territory is known for its excellent roads.
Key Industries
Gifted Objects Magical items and jewelry created by infusing gems with magic
(pioneered by Sekara Arvento)
Warrior Hearts Magical weapons (created by Aleja Arvento)
The Swords of Aishae Seven legendary swords commissioned by Toann Arvento
House Arvento
4
International Trade Trade route with Vikistv, opened by Liaduer Arvento, focused
on magical goods
Social Influence Undisclosed control over noble social circles across Aicruae
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Patton Royal Family) The oldest alliance in Aicruae. Stems from the
personal friendship between King Haliour Layern Patton I and Lenkitta Arvento,
who served as his close friend and advisor during the founding of the kingdom.
Lenkitta also served as advisor to King Benjaien Nefest Patton. The Arventos have
functioned as trusted advisors and scholars to the throne since the very
beginning.
House Aedria Two marriage alliances Rorca Arvento married Bariaro of House
Aedria; Laitha Arvento I married Jeart Aedria). Both families are members of the
Council of the Forsaken.
House Caraen Marriage union between Jomerra Arvento and Philero Caraen. Both
families are members of the Council of the Forsaken.
Rival Houses
House Vika Ongoing rivalry. TBD specifics of rivalry]
House Baliva Former/Destroyed) Generational blood feud spanning centuries.
Began with the kidnapping of Mozuna Arvento by Gaver Baliva, escalated through
Tilan Arventoʼs campaign of destruction, and culminated in the War of Worldʼs End
8,201 BR  8,152 BR, also called the Hundred-Year War. House Baliva was
completely destroyed.
Marriage Alliances
Rorca Arvento →  Bariaro of House Aedria
Laitha Arvento I →  Jeart Aedria
Jomerra Arvento →  Philero Caraen
House Arvento
5
Daneya Arvento →  Olar Patton (forced marriage the kingʼs cousin was given to
Daneya as compensation after the queen deformed Daneyaʼs face)
House Culture
Religious Affiliation
Barqeten one of the three sub-religions within the Circle of Eternal Light. Followers
of Barqeten believe that by simply existing, they are worshipping the gods. They
place great importance on both physical and mental wellness, believing that
because they were created by god, they should do the most to take care of
themselves and others to make the gods proud. Barqeten is also followed by
Houses Leva, Aedria, and Yurea.
Traditions
TBD
Values
Beauty, elegance, self-preservation, scholarly pursuit, justice (through the Council
of the Forsaken), and wellness (rooted in Barqeten faith).
Reputation
At their peak, the family had built an immense fortune and held staggering
influence. They took part in almost every war, secured peaceful victories through
sharp diplomacy, and backed talented artists from across the world. The name
“Arvento” was etched into every corner of the world.
“House Arvento is feared and respected by the other houses despite its neutral
status because of just how much power they wield. Arvento means Morning Wind
for two reasons: their sheer beauty and ferocious strength, which is capable of
breaking down even the tallest building. Even the royal family canʼt question them.
Theyʼre just as bad as the other houses but no one has the guts to say it.”
How Others Perceive Them
The undisclosed leaders of social circles. Falling out with them ensures loss of
respect and standing. Elegant and beautiful on the surface, but dangerous when
House Arvento
6
pushed.
History
Founding
Lenkitta Arvento whose ancestors traced back to Gherci created House Arvento in
8,746 BR with the help of her friend King Haliour Layern Patton I, just thirteen
years after the founding of House Patton and the kingdom of Aicruae. Lenkitta
was self-reliant and believed that her family was meant to be divine workers of the
gods. She served as a close advisor to two kings Haliour I and Benjaien Nefest
Patton) and helped bring forth the period known as the Warriorsʼ Age. She is
widely praised as the reason behind Aicruaeʼs early success.
Rise to Power
House Arventoʼs defense at the Battle of Aishae 8,704 BR) marked their
transformation from loyal counselors to a true military power. They constructed a
port at Aishae as a forward base, granting them maritime dominance in Northern
Aicruae.
Major Achievements
Battle of Aishae 8,704 BR Defended the coastal town against House Baliva; built
the port that became their seat of power.
Infant Laws 8,683 BR Humanitarian laws created by Jomerra Arvento, protecting
infants and mothers regardless of social class. Allowed children to legally separate
from abusive family members.
The Arvento Code 8,126 BR Comprehensive set of laws standardizing fair
taxation, trade rights, and port regulations across Aicruae. Became the de facto
constitution and influenced the later Imperial Code.
Council of the Forsaken 8,051 BR Underground justice alliance with Houses
Aedria and Caraen, created by Wilgen Arvento. Has the kingʼs approval. Since its
founding, the council has brought Aicruaeʼs crime rate down to 30%.
Opening Trade with Vikistv International trade route for magical goods,
established by Liaduer Arvento.
House Arvento
7
Gifted Objects Magical items created by infusing gems with magic. Pioneered by
Sekara Arvento, who became the wealthiest person alive during her lifetime.
Warrior Hearts Magical weapons company created by Aleja Arvento.
The Swords of Aishae Seven legendary swords commissioned by Toann Arvento.
Medical Breakthroughs Treatment for Sela Meysei Night Terrors), pioneered by
Taharry Arvento. Hospital establishments and “The Greater Truth” (a medical/sexed text), created by Finshall Arvento.
The Poison Kan Created by Sina Arvento to execute the men responsible for the
Taguar Murders.
Major Disgraces
The Daneya Arvento Incident Daneya was deformed by the queen after an affair
with the king. Her brother Taveln had the queen eaten by hunting dogs. Daneya
wore the queenʼs collected blood in a necklace, poisoned her own son and
husband, and became the first Arvento to receive punishment from the crown.
The Mozuna Arvento Kidnapping Mozuna was kidnapped at age sixteen by Gaver
Baliva. She returned pregnant. Her father had Gaver hunted and killed.
The War of Worldʼs End 8,201 BR  8,152 BR Started by Tilan Arvento to destroy
House Baliva. The hundred-year war nearly annihilated House Arvento itself. Tilan
and both his sons died. Only Viason Arvento, a twelve-year-old orphan, survived
to rebuild.
The Caxel Arvento Scandal Former heir who abandoned his legal wife and noble
title for a commoner woman. Forced his legal wife to marry his much younger
brother. Caxel, his lover, and their two sons all died of famine the following year.
Key Events Timeline
Founding of Aicruae, Lenkitta serves as advisor 8,746 BR
Battle of Aishae 8,704 BR
Infant Laws created 8,683 BR
Bloody Winter, Casmin Arvento fights alongside Dexona Vika 8,259 BR
War of Worldʼs End 8,201 BR  8,152 BR
House Arvento
8
The Arvento Code established 8,126 BR
Taguar Murders response 8,094 BR
Council of the Forsaken formed 8,051 BR
The Council of the Forsaken
The Council of the Forsaken was created in 8,051 BR by Wilgen Arvento,
granddaughter of Sina Arvento (the woman who invented the poison Kan). Where
Sina answered violence with poison, Wilgen answered it with institutions.
The council is an alliance of the three neutral noble families Arvento, Aedria, and
Caraen functioning as an underground justice organization. They investigate
violent crimes, track down perpetrators, and deliver punishment. They operate
with the full approval of the crown.
Since its founding, the Council of the Forsaken has brought Aicruaeʼs crime rate
down to 30%.
That number is not a typo. A shadow organization run by three noble families,
answering to no one except the king, reduced an entire kingdomʼs crime rate to
30%. The council is greatly feared and deliberately so. They are not interested in
reform or rehabilitation. They are interested in consequences.
The council also reflects something important about Arventoʼs version of
neutrality. House Arvento, House Aedria, and House Caraen all claim to stand
apart from the factional politics of Aicruae. But the Council of the Forsaken is not
neutral. It is a concentrated, crown-backed enforcement arm operated by the
three families that call themselves neutral. They have the authority to pursue
traitors, vigilantes, and violent criminals anywhere in the kingdom.
Being neutral doesnʼt mean being passive. It means being the one who decides
what counts as justice.
The War of Worldʼs End
The War of Worldʼs End also called the Hundred-Year War lasted from 8,201 BR to
8,152 BR and nearly destroyed House Arvento entirely.
The warʼs roots go back a generation, to Mozuna Arvento. The “princess of
Arvento” beloved, privileged, known worldwide as her fatherʼs heart was
House Arvento
9
kidnapped at sixteen by Gaver Baliva. Gaver was twenty, the grandson of the head
of House Baliva, and his interest in Mozuna had turned into a sick obsession.
When Mozuna returned home pregnant, House Baliva tried to claim she had gone
willingly. Mozunaʼs father had Gaver hunted and killed.
Mozunaʼs son, Moneli, was treated as a stain on the family. His grandfather, aunts,
and uncles called him a bastard and said he should never have been born that his
father had “defiled” their beloved Mozuna. Despite this, Moneli loved his family.
It was Mozunaʼs father, Tilan Arvento, who lit the match. Tilan destroyed the
remaining members of House Baliva and started a war that consumed nearly fifty
years of bloodshed. The War of Worldʼs End earned its name it felt like the conflict
would outlast the world itself.
Tilan and both of his sons died during the war. Moneli the bastard the family
despised died trying to protect his aunt during the fighting. House Arvento was
left on the brink of extinction.
What saved them was a twelve-year-old boy.
Viason Arvento, Moneliʼs son, raised by his aunt Kaderia after both his parents
were killed took control of the family at twelve. He married his cousin Asya,
fathered seven sons and three daughters, and spent his life reversing the damage
his grandfather Tilan had caused. He repaired the relationships Tilan had
shattered within the noble hierarchy. And in a quiet act of closure, Viason buried
his father Moneli alongside his grandmother Mozuna and his grandfather Gaver
Baliva together, on the familyʼs land.
Many say the War of Worldʼs End only truly came to an end the day Viason died.
Notable Members
The Founders (8,784 BR – 8,639 BR)
Lenkitta Arvento 8,784 BR  8,702 BR Name meaning: Fair and True. Founder of
House Arvento. Self-reliant and devout, Lenkitta believed her family was meant to
be divine workers of the gods. She served as close friend and advisor to King
Haliour Layern Patton I and helped oversee the construction of Aicruae. She later
served as advisor to King Benjaien Nefest Patton the only non-royal to serve two
kings in an advisory capacity. She helped bring forth the Warriorsʼ Age and is
House Arvento
10
praised as the reason behind Aicruaeʼs early success. Her ancestors traced back
to Gherci before migrating to Aicruae.
Chiane Arvento 8,734 BR  8,701 BR Name meaning: Sweet. The first true warrior
of House Arvento. Chiane became a knight to avenge her husband and eldest son,
who she believed were set up to die in the Battle of Aishae. She created the
Arvento Night Soldiers the guards and knights charged with protecting Aishae,
Arvento territory, and all family members. Her military system became the
backbone of House Arventoʼs defense for generations.
Jomerra Arvento 8,681 BR  8,639 BR Name meaning: Withstanding/Sheltering.
A scholar who refused to marry at the typical age to further her education. She
created the Infant Laws 8,683 BR, which protected the rights of children in
Arvento territory and allowed kids to legally separate from abusive family
members. Her marriage to Philero Caraen solidified the alliance between House
Arvento and House Caraen many consider this her “biggest” contribution, but her
Infant Laws were the real legacy.
The Scholars & Healers (8,622 BR – 8,496 BR)
Taharry Arvento 8,620 BR  8,574 BR Name meaning: Peaceful Rain. An heir to
House Arvento widely considered a genius. She created and pioneered the use of
medical herbs and worked to treat patients suffering from Sela Meysei Night
Terrors).
Aleja Arvento 8,622 BR  8,590 BR Name meaning: Honoring God. One of the
saddest fates of any Arvento woman. Aleja expanded the familyʼs jewelry business
and created Warrior Hearts a company focused on producing magical weapons.
She was poisoned by her lover at age thirty-two when he tried to stop her from
leaving him.
Finshall Arvento 8,590 BR  8,496 BR Name meaning: Fishing Port. One of
Taharry Arventoʼs sons. Finshall worked with his mother to create medical books,
specifically about safer sexual practices. He was openly gay and had the full
support of his mother and the entirety of House Arvento. He lived to ninety-four,
creating hospital-like establishments within Arvento territory. His medical book
“The Greater Truth” essentially a sex-ed textbook covering personal hygiene and
sexual relations is still taught widely throughout Aicruae, though some sections
have been redacted since publication.
House Arvento
11
The Daneya Saga (8,596 BR – 8,536 BR)
Bieln Arvento 8,596 BR  8,502 BR Name meaning: Flower in Bloom. Mother of
Daneya and Taveln. When she heard what happened to her daughter, she went
mad with rage and killed several members of the late queenʼs noble house House
Baliva). She stole their treasures and gifted them to Daneya. She kept the late
queenʼs sister as Daneyaʼs ladyʼs maid and experimented on her with “herbs.”
After the queenʼs sister died, Bieln had Daneya bathe in her blood in a ritual called
the Ritual of Twelve, hoping to restore Daneyaʼs ruined appearance.
Daneya Arvento 8,572 BR  8,533 BR Name meaning: Beautiful Morning. The first
Arvento to receive punishment from the crown. Daneya allegedly seduced the
king, and the queen deformed her face in retaliation. Her brother Taveln had the
queen eaten by hunting dogs. Daneya collected the dead queenʼs blood and wore
it in a necklace known as “Daneyaʼs Luck.” Taveln then forced the king to give his
cousin Olar Patton to Daneya in marriage since the queenʼs actions had ruined
Daneyaʼs prospects. Olar Patton was rumored to have been the late queenʼs lover.
Daneya eventually poisoned both her son Rinden and her husband Olar.
Rinden Arvento 8,552 BR  8,536 BR Name meaning: Bastard Born/Inferior
Bloodline. The son of Daneya Arvento and Olar Patton. Daneya used him as a tool
to torture his father she would burn and cut his hair, and there are rumors she cut
out his tongue when he called her “mother.” Rinden grew up severely ill with much
slower development than his peers. He and his father were poisoned by Daneya
just before Rindenʼs coming-of-age ceremony. His soul is said to linger around
House Arventoʼs territory.
Warriors & Reformers (8,284 BR – 8,218 BR)
Casmin Arvento 8,284 BR  8,238 BR Name meaning: Meadow Above the Sea.
One of the four wielders of the Swords of Aishae. A war hero who fought hand-inhand with Dexona Vika in perfect sync during the Bloody Winter. Casmin and
Dexona were said to be madly in love but were separated by their families. He
gave his second sword which heʼd named Lordʼs Favorite to Dexona after the war,
and she used it to win countless fights. Casmin died ten years before Dexona, and
she spent the rest of her life sneaking away to visit his burial site.
Warias Arvento 8,274 BR  8,218 BR Name meaning: Sharp Weapon. Not an
Arvento by birth Warias was an orphan who married into the family after becoming
House Arvento
12
a well-known knight. He theorized that Arvento should always remain neutral if
they wanted to survive. He also created the family code and laws giving women
the right to inherit the family power and keep the Arvento name while married, if
no male heirs were present. His daughter Zahali was the first to benefit from this
legacy.
The War of Worldʼs End (8,239 BR – 8,101 BR)
Tilan Arvento 8,239 BR  8,170 BR Name meaning: Dryness. Father of Mozuna
Arvento. Tilan destroyed the last members of House Baliva and started the War of
Worldʼs End 8,201 BR  8,152 BR, also called the Hundred-Year War. He and both
his sons died during the conflict, leaving House Arvento on the brink of ruin. His
remaining daughter Kaderia adopted Moneliʼs son Viason and saved the house
from extinction.
Mozuna Arvento 8,217 BR  8,182 BR Name meaning: Music. Called “the princess
of Arvento.” Mozuna lived a life of comfort and incredible privilege, known
worldwide as the honor and treasure of House Arvento many called her “the heart
of her father.” She was kidnapped at age sixteen by Gaver Baliva, a relative of
House Baliva who had developed a sick obsession with her after learning she was
an Arvento. Gaver was twenty at the time. House Baliva initially claimed Mozuna
ran away with him, calling Gaver a “distant relative” to deflect criticism — but he
was actually the third son of the head of House Balivaʼs second son. Mozuna
returned home pregnant. Her father had Gaver hunted and killed. Whether Mozuna
went willingly or was taken by force remains disputed.
Moneli Arvento 8,201 BR  8,162 BR Name meaning: Source of Love. Son of
Mozuna Arvento and Gaver Baliva. Considered a bastard by the family, Moneli was
treated horribly by his grandfather, aunts, and uncles after his motherʼs death.
They claimed his father had ruined Mozunaʼs honor and that Moneli should never
have been born. Despite everything, Moneli loved his maternal family and died
trying to protect his aunt during the War of Worldʼs End. His aunt Kaderia adopted
his son Viason.
Viason Arvento 8,164 BR  8,101 BR Name meaning: Visionary Light. “The
Peopleʼs Prince.” Moneliʼs son and the last remaining heir to House Arvento after
the War of Worldʼs End. At twelve years old, Viason took control of the family and
married his cousin Asya Arvento, daughter of his aunt Kaderia. Their union
House Arvento
13
produced seven sons and three daughters. Viason reversed the tensions his
grandfather Tilan had caused within the noble hierarchy because of the
destruction of House Baliva and buried his father Moneli alongside his
grandmother Mozuna and his grandfather Gaver Baliva together on the familyʼs
land. Many say the War of Worldʼs End only truly came to an end upon Viasonʼs
death.
Justice & Philosophy (8,143 BR – 7,857 BR)
Sina Arvento 8,143 BR  8,033 BR Name meaning: Last Hope/Ray of Joy. Created
the poison Kan, designed for those convicted of horrific acts like rape or murder.
Sina believed such criminals should suffer the pain of their victims until their last
breath. Kan is blue in color and smells like strong cinnamon. Once ingested, it
slowly crushes the victimʼs blood vessels, then causes sharp chest pain. The heart
stops beating and the eyes turn blood red. It takes two hours to kill, and the victim
is in agony the entire time. Sina created Kan specifically to execute the men
responsible for the Taguar Murders in Northern Aicruae.
Wilgen Arvento 8,105 BR  8,004 BR Name meaning: Reserved. One of Sina
Arventoʼs granddaughters. She continued her grandmotherʼs work of just
punishment by creating the Council of the Forsaken 8,051 BR) an alliance of the
three neutral noble families Arvento, Aedria, and Caraen) that functions like a
police force investigating violent crimes and punishing perpetrators. The council
has the crownʼs approval and has brought Aicruaeʼs crime rate down to 30%. It is
greatly feared.
Kyatane Arvento 7,954 BR  7,867 BR Name meaning: Silent Truth. Described by
many as “a headache that wouldnʼt go away.” Known for running away and
ignoring her noble responsibilities, refusing to play her part in the family legacy.
That was until she turned seventeen after leaving Arvento on what she called a
spiritual journey, she wrote “The Rise and Fall of a King,” a book that enraged high
society for its anti-noble stance. Members of House Arvento praised her anyway.
Rorca Arvento 7,925 BR  7,857 BR Name meaning: A Thorned Rose. Created the
concept of Worthy Nobility the idea that nobles must act in a way befitting their
status. She developed this philosophy after reading her aunt Kyataneʼs book “The
Rise and Fall of a King.” Rorca is quoted as saying: “A king is nothing without his
subject, while the people can survive just fine without a King.” She was described
House Arvento
14
as gentle and compassionate and married Bariaro of House Aedria she proposed
to him, and he accepted. They lived happily until Rorca died at sixty-eight. Bariaro
died at seventy-one. Without Rorca, he spent his last days in agony.
The Golden Age (7,651 BR – 7,256 BR)
Laitha Arvento I 7,651 BR  7,582 BR Name meaning: Snowy Trail. Quick to anger,
focused, imaginative, and wacky. The second Arvento woman to marry into House
Aedria. Laitha I was a skilled writer who composed several books “Mischief of the
Night,” “Why the Songbird Sings,” and “Loverʼs Sincerity.” Her novels were wildly
popular with noble ladies who dreamed of romance free from titles and obligation.
She became the first and only woman to receive the title of Golden Pen. Every
male lead in her books was based on her husband Jeart Aedria, and each novel
was supposedly inspired by their love story in dramatized form.
Sekara Arvento 7,442 BR  7,376 BR Name meaning: Maiden. Born after the
Siege of Highwater. Seeking to make her family safer in the aftermath of that
devastation, she developed the idea of infusing gems and jewels with magic to
create items for specific purposes. These became known as Gifted Objects.
During her lifetime, Sekara Arvento was the wealthiest person alive.
Liaduer Arvento 7,429 BR  7,312 BR Name meaning: To Seek. Expanded House
Arventoʼs production of Gifted Objects by partnering with a Magic User from
Vikistv to mass-produce them. He also opened trade between Aicruae and Vikistv
the first international magical trade route. During his lifetime, House Arvento
accumulated over 55,000 Rern, an amount that tripled well after his death.
Caxel Arvento 7,411 BR  7,397 BR Name meaning: Bird/Winged Creature. A
former heir to House Arvento who threw away his noble title to be with a common
woman who had borne him two sons. He abandoned his legal wife and forced her
to marry his much younger brother to secure the family line. Caxel, his lover, and
their two sons died of famine the following year. The scandal tainted House
Arvento for a long time.
Toann Arvento 7,400 BR  7,321 BR Name meaning: Oak Wood. A devout believer
with a particular devotion to Saint Aliirusk. Toann believed he was a reincarnation
of Aliirusk and spent much of his life searching for the legendary sword Allironek.
When he failed to find it, he commissioned seven “divine” swords the Swords of
Aishae. By the time they were finished, he was too old to wield them, so he gifted
House Arvento
15
them to his children: each of his three sons received two swords, and his daughter
received four.
Raninic Arvento 7,305 BR  7,256 BR Name meaning: Overwhelming Joy. Son of
Liaduer Arvento. Rebuilt House Arventoʼs home in Aishae and centered a trading
port around it. He redesigned the house crest and created the family motto (“For
the Honor of the Lost One”). Known as “the creator of New Age Arvento” the
person who brought forth the golden age of the family.
The Daneya Arvento Incident
The Daneya Incident is the darkest chapter in House Arventoʼs history and thatʼs
saying something for a family that also fought a hundred-year war.
Daneya Arvento was called “beautiful morning.” She became involved with the
king, and when the queen discovered the affair, she deformed Daneyaʼs face in a
fit of rage. What followed was a cascade of violence that spiraled far beyond
revenge.
Daneyaʼs brother Taveln retaliated by having the queen eaten alive by hunting
dogs. After the queenʼs death, Daneya collected the blood from the body and wore
it in a necklace she called “Daneyaʼs Luck.” Taveln then forced the king to give his
cousin, Olar Patton, to Daneya in marriage since the queenʼs actions had
destroyed Daneyaʼs ability to find another suitable match. There was a cruel irony
to this arrangement: Olar Patton was rumored to have been the dead queenʼs
lover.
Daneyaʼs mother, Bieln, made things worse. She killed several members of House
Baliva (the queenʼs family), stole their treasures for Daneya, and kept the dead
queenʼs sister as Daneyaʼs personal servant. Bieln experimented on the queenʼs
sister with herbs, and after the woman died, Bieln forced Daneya to bathe in her
blood in the Ritual of Twelve a desperate attempt to restore Daneyaʼs ruined
appearance.
The worst was still to come. Daneya turned her suffering outward onto her own
family. She used her son Rinden as a tool to torture his father Olar. She burned
and cut the boyʼs hair. Rumors say she cut out his tongue when he called her
“mother.” Rinden grew up severely ill. Just before his coming-of-age ceremony,
Daneya poisoned both Rinden and Olar.
House Arvento
16
Daneya became the first Arvento to receive any kind of punishment from the
crown. She was called a witch. And Rindenʼs name meaning “Bastard Born/Inferior
Bloodline” tells you everything about how the family saw the child she created and
destroyed.
His soul is said to still linger around House Arventoʼs territory.
Strengths & Weaknesses
What Theyʼre Known For
Magical weapons and items Gifted Objects, Warrior Hearts, Swords of Aishae)
Social dominance over the Aicruan nobility
Legal innovations (the Arvento Code, the Infant Laws)
The Council of the Forsaken
Scholarship and literary output (five major books, medical texts)
Medical advances Night Terrors treatment, hospitals, “The Greater Truth”)
International trade connections with Vikistv
What They Lack
TBD
Vulnerabilities
Internal family drama has nearly destroyed them more than once. The Daneya
Incident brought crown punishment for the first time. The War of Worldʼs End killed
three generations of heirs and left a twelve-year-old in charge. The Caxel scandal
tainted their reputation for years. For a family that preaches “Worthy Nobility,” the
Arventos have a pattern of producing members who are anything but.

Crest: A powerful red bull or horned creature rearing up on its hind legs in a
rampant pose against a red and yellow shield divided by a bold diagonal line from
upper right to lower left. The bull is rendered entirely in red with black outlines and
detailing, appearing to be leaping or charging upward against the yellow triangular
section in the upper left, while the lower right portion matches the bullʼs crimson
coloring.
Symbolism: The bull represents indomitable strength, stubborn determination, and
the raw force of will that drives the house forward. The rampant pose suggests
active aggression and readiness for confrontation. The red coloring throughout
emphasizes the bloodline, martial courage, and passionate intensity that defines
their character. This is a house that achieves its ends through sheer force of
determination.

entries.title: House Caraen
entries.text:
House Caraen
House Caraen
“FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE LAND AND THE SOULS THAT INHABIT IT”
Quick Facts
Status: Knight/Dame
Origin: Aicruae Capital City, Lajazer)
Founded: 8,643 BR
Founder: Milane Caraen
Seat: Caraen Towers, Lajazer (capital city of Aicruae)
Faction: Neutral Faction
House Name Meaning: Gift from the Gods
Spirit Animal: None. House symbol is the Watchtower (two watchtowers with
moon).
Colors: Blue Loyalty, Vigilance, and the Sky)
Wealth: 68,000 Rern
Military: Over 100,000 men 3rd strongest military in Aicruae, after House Vika and
House Patton)
Religion: Rillic
Theme Song: “This Mountain” by Faouzia
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Knight/Dame. One of three notable noble families living in the
capital alongside the royal family. Primary duty: defending the capital city of
Lajazer.
Solisʼs Era: TBD
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Caraen
1
House Caraen is what happens when loyalty becomes identity. Founded by an
orphan from the slums who owed everything he had to the king who elevated him,
the Caraens built their entire existence around one purpose: protecting the royal
family and the capital city they call home. They are not wealthy. They are not
politically ambitious. They rank among the lowest noble houses in terms of power
and money. But they command the third largest military in all of Aicruae, over
100,000 men whose sole job is making sure the capital doesnʼt fall.
Nobody hates them. Nobody particularly loves them either. As the saying goes,
“theyʼre kinda just there.” And yet, across centuries, Caraen soldiers have bled
and died for the throne without question. Isweyi Caraen refused an offer of escape
during the Siege of Highwater and fought for nearly two hours to protect the royal
heirs. Oahiat Caraen died at the Battle of GreyNest alongside Dexona Vika, stalling
an enemy long enough to turn the tide of a war. Their loyalty has never been in
question. Whether the throne has always deserved it is another matter entirely.
Heraldry
The Crest: A lozenge (diamond-shaped) shield, rotated so its points face up,
down, left, and right. The entire field is a solid cornflower blue. At the center rises
a gray stone castle with a central tower crowned by three turrets, flanked by two
smaller towers, all featuring crenellated battlements. In the upper right corner, a
small white circle represents the moon watching over the fortress.
Symbolism:
The castle is the Caraen Towers. Not a symbol of a castle. The actual seat of
House Caraen, built at the very front of Lajazer, the capital city of Aicruae,
positioned so that anything coming for the royal family has to go through them
first. Milane Caraen was an orphan from the slums. King Haliour Layern Patton II
gave him a title and a purpose, and Milane put his family between the crown and
everything that wanted to take it. The castle on this crest isnʼt a boast about
wealth or power. Itʼs a job description. House Caraen exists to stand in front of the
city and not move.
The three turrets on the central tower and the two flanking towers show
redundancy. Not grandeur. If one position falls, thereʼs another behind it. If that
one falls, thereʼs a third. House Caraen commands over 100,000 men, the third
strongest military in Aicruae behind only House Vika and House Patton, and every
House Caraen
2
single one of those soldiers serves one function: hold the line. Isweyi Caraen
proved it at the Siege of Highwater when she refused an offer of escape and
fought for nearly two hours to protect the royal heirs. Oahiat Caraen proved it at
the Battle of GreyNest when he died alongside Dexona Vika buying time that
turned the war. The towers donʼt fall because Caraen soldiers donʼt leave.
The white moon is the watcher that never sleeps. House Caraen follows Rillic, the
faith that says believers exist to fuel the godsʼ strength and give them a stronger
tether to the mortal world. The moon is that tether made visible. It hangs over the
fortress the same way the Caraens hang over Lajazer: always present, always
watching, whether anyone notices or not. The moon also speaks to what other
houses say about them. “No one neither hates nor loves them. Theyʼre kinda just
there.” The moon is kinda just there too. But try navigating without it.
The cornflower blue field is loyalty, vigilance, and the sky. Just one color. No
divisions, no secondary fields, no complications. House Caraen doesnʼt have a
spirit animal. They donʼt have a secondary symbol. They donʼt have a dual power
structure or a famous commercial empire or a legendary weapon. They have blue.
One job. One color. One thing they do, and they do it with 100,000 soldiers who
will die for a capital city most of them were born in. Blue is the sky over Lajazer.
The Caraens live under it, fight under it, and get buried under it. The lozenge
shape instead of a traditional shield is worth noting. In real-world heraldry, the
lozenge was historically used for women, for non-combatants, for families that
held land through service rather than conquest. House Caraen is a knight family.
The lowest rank of nobility. They hold 68,000 Rern, which is nothing compared to
the houses they stand beside in the capital. They didnʼt earn their crest through
war or wealth. They earned it because a king looked at an orphan and saw
something worth keeping. The diamond shape says: we donʼt carry a warriorʼs
shield. We carry something else. A promise.
House Colors: Blue. Just blue. Loyalty, vigilance, and the sky over the city they
protect.
Motto: “For the protection of the land and the souls that inhabit it.” The longest
motto in Aicruae, and the most literal. Thereʼs no metaphor in it. No double
meaning. No quiet arrogance dressed up as humility. House Caraen protects the
land. House Caraen protects the people living on it. Thatʼs the whole motto and
the whole house.
House Caraen
3
Caraen means “Gift from the Gods.” Milane was a gift the king received. The
family he founded has spent every generation since then trying to be worthy of it.
The motto doesnʼt say “for the protection of the king.” It says “the land and the
souls that inhabit it.” Every soul. Not the noble ones. Not the royal ones. All of
them. Thatʼs the Rillic faith talking. If you exist to fuel the godsʼ strength, then
every life on that land is sacred fuel. You protect it all or you protect nothing.
Itʼs not a flashy motto. It doesnʼt fit on a banner the way “Loyal is the hound to the
master” does. But it doesnʼt need to. House Caraen isnʼt trying to impress anyone.
Theyʼre trying to keep the city standing. The motto says what it means and means
what it says. So does the family.
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Military strength and centuries of loyal service to the crown. House Caraen is not
a wealthy noble family and ranks among the lowest in terms of raw power and
wealth. Their influence comes from their role as the capitalʼs defenders and their
unbroken track record of protecting the royal family.
Internal Power Structure
Traditional patriarchal structure, but similar to House Vika, women are not limited
to the sidelines.
Military Forces
Primary duty: Protecting the capital city of Lajazer.
Ranked 3rd in military strength across Aicruae, behind House Vika and House
Patton.
Forces: Over 100,000 men ready to defend the city.
Lands & Income
Seat: The Caraen Towers, located at the very front of the town of Lajazer, the
capital city of Aicruae. One of three notable noble families living in the capital
(alongside the royal family).
House Caraen
4
House Total Wealth: 68,000 Rern.
Key Industries: TBD
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Arvento, Marriage alliance through Philero Caraen and Jomerra Arvento
8,681 BR  8,639 BR. Both families are members of the Council of the Forsaken.
House Aedria, Both families are members of the Council of the Forsaken.
Rival Houses
TBD
Royal Connections
Founded through the direct patronage of King Haliour Layern Patton II, who gifted
Milane Caraen his title of nobility. The Caraen family has served as protectors of
the royal family ever since.
House Culture
Religion
Rillic. Believers of Rillic hold that they were put on this planet to fuel the godsʼ
strength and give them a stronger tether to the physical/mortal world.
Traditions
TBD
Values
TBD
Reputation
Very respected. House Caraen is one of the few noble houses to be generally
respected rather than feared or hated. They have protected the royal family for
House Caraen
5
centuries, earning the trust of the nobility. “No one neither hates nor loves them.
Theyʼre kinda just there.”
History
Founding (8,643 BR)
Milane Caraen was born an orphan in the slums of Lajazer. He became a sword for
hire, and at age 16, was recruited by The Etrai of the royal castle to serve as a
knight for the royal family. He caught the attention of King Haliour Layern Patton II,
who granted him the title of nobility at age 19, founding House Caraen. Milane
became a close personal friend of the king, who was devastated when Milane
died.
Rise to Power
TBD
Major Achievements
Treaty of Oahiat 8,248 BR. A blood treaty named in honor of Oahiat Caraen, who
died at the Battle of GreyNest alongside Dexona Vika. The treaty married Maikor
of Pireayneaʼs children to Oahiatʼs children.
Talta Ikati. Akare Caraen bonded with a minor earth deity and became a Talta Ikati,
making her the first woman of Aicruae to hold the position of tower lord Lady.
Silver Pen. Nadera Caraen earned this literary honor for her work immortalizing
her mother Isweyiʼs heroism through books, songs, and plays.
Major Disgraces
TBD
Founding Story (Expanded)
TBD
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs origins onward.
House Caraen
6
Milane Caraen (8,662 BR – 8,600 BR)
Founder of House Caraen
Name meaning: Long Stretch of Road
Born an orphan in the slums of Lajazer. Became a sword for hire. At 16, he was
recruited by The Etrai of the royal castle to become a knight for the royal family.
He gained the recognition of King Haliour Layern Patton II and was granted
nobility at 19, founding House Caraen. A close personal friend of the king, who
was devastated by Milaneʼs death.
“Without his majesty, I would be nothing, a meaningless life among the masses, he
gave me purpose and so I shall fight in his honor.”
Asjart Caraen (8,611 BR – 8,579 BR)
Knight of Prince Teravian Geraser Patton
Name meaning: Tortoise
Grandson of Milane. Became knight of Prince Teravian Geraser Patton. Deeply
loyal to the crown and a dedicated servant to the prince. Asjart died two years
before the prince, after which the princeʼs health deteriorated.
Philero Caraen (dates unknown)
Marriage Alliance with House Arvento
Married Jomerra Arvento, solidifying the relationship between Houses Arvento
and Caraen.
Oahiat Caraen (8,283 BR – 8,248 BR)
“Blood Treaty Bearer”
Name meaning: All Hearing
Nurse and soldier. Oahiat battled alongside Dexona Vika at the Battle of GreyNest.
Both women died after being badly injured by Maikor of Pireaynea. Though they
lost the battle, they stalled Maikor long enough for the Aicruean army to turn the
tide of war. The Treaty of Oahiat, a blood treaty that married Maikorʼs children to
Oahiatʼs children, was named in her honor.
House Caraen
7
Dilion of the Tower (dates unknown)
Abusive husband, father, and lord who neglected his wife, children, and land.
Father of Akare and Baciyo Caraen.
Baciyo Caraen (8,271 BR – 8,240 BR)
Name meaning: Rooster
Dilionʼs only son and heir. Sickly from birth, bedridden and presumed half dead.
His father became obsessed with curing him through rituals and sacrifices. One
ritual “fixed” him at age 10, but it corrupted his mind. Baciyo grew twisted like his
father. He developed an extreme fixation (kink) on pain and was said to have
experimented on servants and animals.
Akare Caraen (8,265 BR – 8,203 BR)
First Female Tower Lord Lady of Aicruae
Name meaning: Obedient
Youngest daughter of Dilion. Lived in constant fear of her father. At age 23, she
bonded with a minor earth deity and became a Talta Ikati. Her position as a Talta
Ikati allowed her to become the first woman of Aicruae to hold the position of
tower lord Lady.
Basania Caraen (7,996 BR – 7,967 BR)
“The Jewel of High Society”
Name meaning: Beauty
Well-respected lady known throughout the world for her beauty. A scholar and
prized pupil of the Cidet. Basania fell in love with Hailea Kulio (six years her senior)
at age 17. She spent her life sending Hailea flowers and gifts and bullying romantic
rivals, particularly Takerei. She was the first of Haileaʼs followers to commit suicide
after Haileaʼs death. Basania killed herself at age 29, days after her birthday. Her
nanny found her five days later. She was married and had one son before her
death.
Isweyi Caraen (7,499 BR – 7,463 BR)
“The Queen of the Tower”
House Caraen
8
Name meaning: Nightʼs Child
National hero. Isweyi died protecting the royal family during the Siege of
Highwater 7,463 BR. Revolutionists offered her escape, but she refused, striking
her sword Relma into oneʼs chest.
“You dare to offer me treason on a silver platter, I am Isweyi of the Caraen lineage,
I was born of the tower, and I shall die by the tower.”
She fought for nearly two hours and died saving an heir to the throne.
Nadera Caraen (7,465 BR – 7,415 BR)
Silver Pen Recipient
Name meaning: Amber
Daughter of Isweyi. Only two years old during the Siege of Highwater and never
knew her mother well. Nadera worked tirelessly creating books, songs, and plays
about her motherʼs victory, immortalizing Isweyi as a national hero. She was a
talented writer who earned the Silver Pen.
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
Military defense of the capital city, centuries of unbroken loyalty to the crown,
generally respected by the nobility, and producing soldiers and protectors who die
for their duty without hesitation.

Why They Matter
House Catern holds the Archduke rank because of what they guard: the twin
territories of Aryanara and Vekta, where the founders of the Circle of Eternal Light
House Catern
1
once taught. Their motto claims three things at once: guardianship of truths from
the primordial era, protection of the physical lands where the twins taught, and
spiritual allegiance to the Circleʼs founding principles. They stand as a bulwark
against competing beliefs like the Brotherhood of Westwinds. In a kingdom where
religious power outranks the crown, being the guardians of Gherciʼs oldest sacred
ground makes House Catern something more than just another noble house. They
are keepers of the origin story itself.
Heraldry
Crest: A mighty white elephant stands at the center, flanked by two flaming
braziers that burn with red and white fire. The elephant is depicted in profile with
trunk raised, positioned upon a black horizontal band that divides the shield, with
the upper and lower fields both in white. Below the elephant, a red poppy or
similar flower with green leaves provides a touch of life and remembrance.
Symbolism: The elephant, associated with strength, wisdom, memory, ancient
power and endurance, connects directly to the mottoʼs reference to “the age of
origin.” The ceremonial fires suggest the forge of civilization and the eternal flame
of tradition. The red poppy beneath the elephant introduces life and
remembrance. The combination positions House Catern as guardians of primordial
strength and keepers of foundational traditions for the lands of Aryanara and
Vekta.
Motto: “For the age of origin and for the strength of Aryanara and Vekta.”
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Guardianship of the twin territories of Aryanara and Vekta. Their Archduke rank
reflects this responsibility. The spiritual weight of protecting the Circle of Eternal
Lightʼs birthplace gives them religious and territorial authority.

entries.title: House Dajanyi
entries.text:
House Dajanyi
House Dajanyi
“FOREVER LASTING”
Quick Facts
Status: Marquess/Marquis
Origin: Coelum (migrated to Aicruae)
Founded: 8,804 BR (official noble recognition)
Founder: Xahaner Dajanyi (official founder; house originally created by Rigu
Dajanyi)
Seat: Port Vento, Aicruae (owned by House Arvento but primarily maintained by
House Dajanyi)
Faction: Common People Faction
Spirit Animal: Dolphin (a reference to the nickname “The Sea Monsters” they
earned during their time in Coelum)
Colors: Green (the Sky, growth, air, divinity, prosperity) & Blue Sea, calmness,
endurance)
Wealth: 139,000 Rern
Military: TBD
Religion: Order of the Pure Ones (one of the handful of families in Aicruae to
follow this order, and the most notable among them)
House Name Meaning: “One who carries a sword” (originally “A traveler” until
Lunteo Dajanyi changed it)
Theme Song: “Onward & Upward (feat. Fleurie)” by Tommee Profitt
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Not yet a noble house. For the longest time they were known as
“the wandering pirates,” voyaging the Quather Sea since the era of Saintess
Nairan 10,0129,983 BR. They settled in Coelum for access to two bodies of
water before migrating to Aicruae around 8,978 BR. Officially recognized as
nobles in 8,804 BR.
House Dajanyi
1
Solisʼs Era: Marquess/Marquis. Seated at Port Vento in Aicruae, a property owned
by House Arvento but primarily maintained by House Dajanyi. Very influential as
the countryʼs heroes, holding the Marquis position.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Dajanyi started as pirates. Not metaphorical ones. Not “we have a roguish
ancestor” pirates. Actual, ship-raiding, treasure-hoarding, sea-faring pirates who
earned the nickname “The Sea Monsters” while terrorizing the waters around
Coelum. Their mythological origin traces back to the survivors of the Mirrors of
Nimlye, an event that drove an entire crew of pirates to madness and mutual
slaughter in a single night.
And then they became nobles.
That transformation, from wanted criminals to one of the most respected houses
in Aicruae, is what makes House Dajanyi matter. Rigu Dajanyi survived a cursed
treasure haul and built a pirate dynasty. His descendant Xahaner petitioned for
noble status and won. Mericani wrote the 60/40 Agreement that turned piracy into
a regulated business under Aicruaen law. Hilatoma became a national hero by
single-handedly preventing two kingdoms from falling during the War of Fera. And
Lunteo beat the king himself in a tournament, catapulting the family from Baron all
the way to Marquis.
They are the house that proves you donʼt need to be born into power. You can
take it. You can earn it. You can fight your way from the bottom of the ocean to the
top of the social ladder, and if youʼre good enough, theyʼll change the definition of
your name to match.
Heraldry
The Crest: A shield divided per fess by a sharp zigzag line resembling waves or
jagged coastline. The upper field is a soft seafoam green, the lower field
cornflower blue. In the upper left sits a golden eight-pointed star with orange-red
tips. Dominating the blue lower field is a large sea serpent in blue-green with a
green dorsal ridge, coiled in an S-shape, mouth open with yellow eyes and a red
House Dajanyi
2
tongue showing. Along the right edge of the shield, overlapping the border, a
downward-pointing sword with a blue-wrapped grip rests partially outside the
field.
Symbolism:
The sea serpent is the familyʼs history wearing its real face. House Dajanyiʼs spirit
animal is listed as a dolphin, a nod to “The Sea Monsters” nickname they earned
terrorizing the waters around Coelum. But the creature on this crest isnʼt a dolphin.
Itʼs something older and meaner. Coiled, jaws open, eyes bright. This is what the
Dajanyis looked like before they became nobles. This is Rigu Dajanyi surviving the
Mirrors of Nimlye while every other pirate on his crew went mad and killed each
other. This is generations of sea raiders building a dynasty out of stolen treasure
and salt water. The serpent doesnʼt apologize for what it is. Neither does House
Dajanyi.
The zigzag division between the green and blue fields isnʼt smooth. It cuts across
the shield like teeth, like waves breaking against rock, like the jagged coastline the
Dajanyis sailed along for centuries before they ever set foot in Aicruae. That line is
the border between what the family used to be and what they became. Above the
line: the sky, the air, the world of nobility and recognition. Below the line: the sea,
the deep, the old pirate blood that still runs through every generation. The
Dajanyis crossed that line when Xahaner petitioned for noble status and won. But
the line is still there. You can see it. They want you to see it.
The seafoam green upper field represents the sky, growth, and divinity. Green is
one of the houseʼs two colors, and for the Dajanyis it carries the weight of their
faith. They follow the Order of the Pure Ones, one of only a handful of families in
Aicruae to do so and the most prominent among them. The green field is air and
prosperity. Itʼs whatʼs above the water. Itʼs where you go when you stop being a
pirate and start being a marquis. Lunteo Dajanyi beat the king himself in a
tournament and elevated the family from Baron to Marquis. Thatʼs the green field.
The air up top where the Dajanyis finally got to breathe.
The cornflower blue lower field is the sea. Calmness and endurance. This is the
water the Dajanyis have been sailing since the era of Saintess Nairan, roughly
10,000 BR. Over a thousand years on the Quather Sea before they even had a
name for themselves. Blue is patience. Blue is the thing beneath everything else,
the foundation the family was built on before the titles and the 139,000 Rern and
House Dajanyi
3
Port Vento. They live at a port owned by House Arvento but maintained by Dajanyi
hands. The sea is still theirs even when the land belongs to someone else.
The golden star in the upper field is guidance and divine favor. Navigation. The
thing that tells a sailor which way is home. For the Dajanyis, who spent centuries
as wanderers before they settled anywhere, the star is the fixed point they sailed
toward. Itʼs also the moment the gods smiled on them, if you believe that sort of
thing. The Order of the Pure Ones would say the star is proof that the Dajanyis
were always meant to be more than pirates. Rigu would probably say itʼs just a
star, and stars donʼt care what you are.
The sword overlapping the shieldʼs edge is the house name made visible. Dajanyi
means “One who carries a sword,” a meaning Lunteo changed it to after the
original definition, “A traveler,” no longer fit a family that had stopped traveling and
started conquering. The sword breaks past the border of the shield because
House Dajanyi has never stayed inside the lines. They crossed from Coelum to
Aicruae. They crossed from piracy to nobility. They crossed from Baron to Marquis
by beating the king in single combat. The sword doesnʼt sit politely inside the
crest. It reaches past it. Thatʼs the whole family in one detail.
House Colors: Green and Blue. Green for the sky, growth, divinity, and prosperity.
Blue for the sea, calmness, and endurance. One color for whatʼs above the water.
One for whatʼs below.
Motto: “Forever Lasting.” Two words. The shortest motto among the major houses
and somehow the most ambitious. Rigu Dajanyi built a pirate crew out of cursed
treasure and madness, and his descendants turned it into a noble house that
survived into Solisʼs Era as Marquesses holding the title of national heroes.
“Forever Lasting” isnʼt a prayer. Itʼs a dare. It says: try to end us. The sea couldnʼt.
The Mirrors of Nimlye couldnʼt. A thousand years of being called wanderers and
pirates and sea monsters couldnʼt. We were here before you knew our name, and
weʼll be here after you forget yours.
Mericani wrote the 60/40 Agreement that turned piracy into regulated business.
Hilatoma saved two kingdoms alone during the War of Fera. Lunteo knocked the
crown off the kingʼs head in a tournament ring and walked away a Marquis.
“Forever Lasting” is the family looking at all of that and saying: weʼre not done yet.

TBD
Reputation
Very influential as the countryʼs heroes, holding the Marquis position.
Common Sayings About House Dajanyi
TBD
History
Mythological Origin
House Dajanyi traces its origins to the myth of the Mirrors of Nimlye. A group of
pirates discovered an island full of treasures that happened to house three of the
goddess Nimlyeʼs five mirrors, said to reveal the secrets of the world to anyone
who looked into them. The pirates thought the mirrors were nothing more than
shiny objects, but at nightfall the moonlight hit the glass and every pirate who
looked into them went mad. They slaughtered each other. Brother killed brother,
friends turned on friends. By morning, the mirrorsʼ light had gone dark. Rigu
Dajanyi was among the few who survived that night. Full myth below.)
Ancient History
House Dajanyi has existed since the time of Saintess Nairan 10,0129,983 BR,
voyaging the Quather Sea. For the longest time they were referred to as “the
wandering pirates.”
First Settlement & Coelum Period
Around 9,617 BR, the family first decided on a permanent location. They initially
settled in Coelum for access to two bodies of water, earning the nickname “The
Sea Monsters.” They remained there until Equateiy and Vikistv began taxing
Coelumʼs water, prompting migration to Aicruae around 8,978 BR.
House Dajanyi
6
Noble Recognition (8,804 BR)
The royal family of Aicruae officially acknowledged their noble bloodline status in
8,804 BR. Xahaner Dajanyi, the official founder, established that House Dajanyi
was more than a family of pirates. He brought attention to the house and
cemented the accomplishments of his predecessors.
Rise to Power
Major achievements include Hilatoma Dajanyiʼs heroism during the War of Fera,
Lunteo Dajanyiʼs victory at the Kingʼs Tournament (which elevated the family from
Baron to Marquis), and Mericani Dajanyiʼs 60/40 Agreement that regulated piracy
under Aicruaen law.
Major Disgraces
TBD
UIB Connection
Canon notes that “House Dajanyi (former pirates) knows the networks even if
theyʼre now legitimate,” referring to their knowledge of the Underground
Information Brokers.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs earliest known ancestor to its most recent
notable member.
Rigu Dajanyi (9,741 BR – 9,675 BR)
“Creator of House Dajanyi”
Name meaning: Friend to many
Rigu is the ancestor of House Dajanyi who survived the Night of Blood mentioned
in the myth “The Mirrors of Nimlye.” He was a skilled thief and pirate and cocaptain of the group of pirates that found Nimlyeʼs mirrors. He managed to survive
the night with a handful of treasures that he used to create a new crew of pirates
run exclusively by his family. He brought the family to Coelum, took Ailimara Kifan
as his wife, and settled the family there.
House Dajanyi
7
He could have married Sorara Jivaya, but her family didnʼt approve. Despite this,
Ailimara was said to have been the reason behind his every joy and laughter.
Note: Rigu created the house, but Xahaner Dajanyi receives official founder credit
as the one who established it as a noble house.
Xahaner Dajanyi (8,830 BR – 8,753 BR)
Official Founder of House Dajanyi
Name meaning: Autumn
Descendant of Rigu. The one who moved the family from Coelum to Aicruae and
made the case that they were nobles, not just pirates. He brought attention to the
house and cemented his predecessorsʼ accomplishments. Official noble
recognition came in 8,804 BR under his leadership.
Mericani Dajanyi (8,827 BR – 8,748 BR)
“The Protector”
Name meaning: Protector
Sister to Xahaner. An accomplished pirate who traveled the world 72 times. She
wrote the “60/40 Agreement”: pirates protected by Aicruaen laws must give 40%
of their loot to the royal family in exchange for protection and access to ships and
weapons. She also helped her brother petition to maintain noble status while
continuing piracy.
Nauebia Dajanyi (8,712 BR – 8,630 BR)
“The Great Beauty”
Name meaning: Beautiful
Scandalous reputation: rumored to be a prostitute and/or the kingʼs lover. The
rumors were likely baseless, created by jealous individuals, but they stuck enough
to damage her reputation permanently. She married Aisari Der Dajanyi and had
three children.
Hilatoma Dajanyi (8,675 BR – 8,610 BR)
“Aicruaeʼs Great Hero”
House Dajanyi
8
Name meaning: Sweetheart
Daughter of Nauebia. The great hero of Aicruae during the War of Fera. She
prevented both Aicruae and Coelum from falling to House Mena. She personally
carried out the punishment and execution of all involved in the war, including
Fransei Mena. She is often compared to Fransei Mena.
Lunteo Dajanyi (7,957 BR – 7,893 BR)
“The Swordsman Who Beat a King”
Name meaning: Moonlight
Unlike his predecessors, Lunteo was famous for his sword skill rather than for
voyages. He changed the meaning of the name “Dajanyi” from “A traveler” to “one
who carries a sword.” He beat the king in a tournament, catapulting House
Dajanyiʼs status from Baron to Marquis.
The Mirrors of Nimlye
The goddess Nimlye had 5 mirrors, said to reveal the secrets of the world to
anyone who looked into them. Due to the off-putting nature of the mirrors, Nimlye
had to scatter them across the earth. She had hoped that no one would find them
ever again.
One day, a group of pirates stumbled across an island engulfed in treasures that
happened to house 3 of those mirrors. The pirates, unaware of what the mirrors
contained, thought nothing more of them than shiny, glistening objects. But once
they brought the mirrors back to their ship and nightfall came, the reflection of the
moon hit the mirrors. It caused them to look away from their tasks and stare
directly into the glass.
What they saw was said to be so disturbing that they all went mad and killed each
other. Brother turned on brother. Friends became foe. And at the end of the night,
the light of the mirrors no longer shined.
The location of the remaining two mirrors has yet to be known.
Rigu Dajanyi was among the survivors of this event. The treasures he salvaged
from that night became the foundation of the Dajanyi pirate dynasty.
House Dajanyi

entries.title: House Hige
entries.text:
House Hige
House Hige
“DIE WITH HONOR OR DO NOT DIE AT ALL”
Quick Facts
Status: Baron/Baroness
Origin: Aicruae Western)
House Name Meaning: Highborn; A person of Noble Status
Founded: 7,460 BR
Founder: Mokar Hige
Seat: Melert (orig. Dira), Western Aicruae
Faction: Divine Faction
Spirit Animal: White Bear
Colors: Blue, Yellow and Green
Wealth: 15,000 Rern
Peak Wealth: 18,000 Rern
Military: Minimal
Religion: Leneyez Circle of Eternal Light)
Theme Song: Billie Eilish “No Time To Die”
Status by Era
Pre - Empire: Baron
Solisʼs Era: Diminished. House Hige no longer exists as an independent noble
house. In the decades following the civil war, Solis rewarded their loyalty with
lands and coin, but without military strength or political connections beyond the
crownʼs favor, the house couldnʼt sustain itself. The last head of House Hige
married his only surviving daughter to House Arvento, folding the Hige bloodline
into the ducal house. The Hige Distribution Company was absorbed into Arventoʼs
trade network. The white bear banner no longer flies over Melert.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
House Hige
1
Minaraʼs Era: A historical footnote. The Hige bloodline continues through House
Arvento, and some Arvento members still claim descent from House Hige,
meaning having “some” relation to Lady Emillea, mother of Emperor Solis himself.
Key Connections
Allies: None Pre-Solis)
Royal Tie: House Patton Via Emillea)
Rivals: House Vika
Why They Matter
House Hige is the underdog story of Aicruaeʼs nobility, a family that clawed its way
out of peasantry and never stopped fighting for the respect it was rarely given.
Their founder stole money from a dead man to buy a title during a time when
being noble could get you killed. For generations, every other house treated them
as a joke.
Then Lady Emillea Hige became the mother of the most powerful man in history.
Her public murder by Princess Iris didnʼt just destroy a family; it lit the match that
set the entire world on fire. The Hige white bear on Solisʼs banners was a promise:
the wronged and the low-born could rip everything apart.
Nicknames People Call Them During This Era
“The Flour Dusters” (their business is moving food, they smell like grain wagons)”
“The Western Barons”
“The Firstborn of Dira” Their original seat before famine forced relocation. Old
blood, even if nobody cares.)
Heraldry
Crest: Quarterly counterchanged vert and azure (quartered green and blue, with
opposite corners matching). A silver bear rampant at center, tongue showing red.
One golden wheat sheaf in each quarter. A golden braided rope runs along the top
edge of the shield.
Symbolism: Green represents prosperity, growth, and the fertile lands of House
Higeʼs territory
House Hige
2
Blue stands for loyalty, steadfastness, and justice. The silver bear rampant
symbolizes strength, protection, and ferocity in defense of what is theirs, a bear
does not seek conflict but will not back down from it. The four wheat sheaves
represent abundance, the agricultural wealth of their holdings, and their role as
providers to the realm. The golden rope signifies unity and the ties that hold the
house together
Motto: “Die with honor, or do not die at all”
Pre-Empire Era: Baron of Western Aicruae
Status: Baron/Baroness
Faction: Divine Faction (believes in monarchy and the nobility class system)
Seat: Originally the Town of Dira, relocated to the Town of Melert Western
Aicruae) due to famine. One of only two noble houses to ever change location.
Religion: Leneyez (sub-religion of the Circle of Eternal Light)
The Underdog Factor: House Hige held the lowest rank, the least wealth, and zero
allies among Aicruaeʼs nobility. No other house took them seriously. Theyʼd tried to
branch out diplomatically, only to be rejected every time. Their internal structure
was “very wonky” because they could barely keep themselves afloat, let alone
manage house affairs properly, leaving family members divided and desperate.
Despite all of this, the house persisted. Their distribution company kept them
financially alive, and when Lady Emillea caught the eye of King Benjamin II, it
changed the trajectory of the entire world.
Founding Story
Founded: 7,460 BR (three years after the Siege of Highwater)
Founder: Mokar Hige
Origin: Mokar was an ambitious peasant who stole money from his master, a
young noble who died during a hunting expedition gone wrong. He used that
money to buy a noble title during one of the worst times to be a noble in the
country, when nobody wanted to be nobility, and the title itself came with the risk
of death.
House Hige
3
Mokar and his wife Henra didnʼt announce their new status immediately. They
continued living as peasants, waiting for the chaos of the Siege of Highwater to
completely die out before officially revealing their nobility.
The White Bear Origin: the white bear on the Hige crest comes directly from
Mokarʼs past. The young noble master he served used Mokar as bait to hunt a
white bear. The master failed and was killed by the animal. Mokar was forced to
outsmart and kill the bear himself. When founding the House, he chose this
symbol so everyone would know House Hige was just as noble as everyone else,
giving the House a pure but ferocious identity.
Power & Influence
Wealth: 15,000 Rern (the least of any noble house). Peak of 18,000 Rern was
reached under Benamʼs management. Their wealth status sits just above a wealthy
merchant group.
Military Strength: The littlest among all noble houses. Too new and underfunded to
maintain a proper military or guard. They field local levies and retainers rather than
grand armies.
Internal Structure: Best described as “very wonky”, they barely had enough
resources to stay afloat, let alone manage themselves. This left family members
divided and willing to do anything to survive.
Key Business Asset: The Hige Distribution Company, founded by Adrione and
Benam Hige, this company moved food from one corner of the kingdom to
another. It was the familyʼs primary income source and their one genuine
achievement. Saperin IIʼs marriage was strategically used to advance the
manufacturing of carts that carried Hige goods.
Alliances: None during the Pre-Empire period. No other noble house took House
Hige seriously, and every attempt to build diplomatic relationships was rejected.
Their only significant connection came through Emilleaʼs relationship with King
Benjamin II.
House Culture
Notable Members
House Hige
4
These are all the notable members of House Hige.
Founding Generation
Henra Hige 7,510 BR  7,460 BR
“The Mother of House Hige.” Protected the family during the Siege by becoming a
maid to a wealthy feudal noble, then betrayed that noble at the right time. Died
around the houseʼs official founding. Mother of Adrione, Benam, Saperin I, and
Biba. The name Henra means Muse.
Mokar Hige 7,489 BR  7,452 BR
Founder. Stole money from his dead master and bought a noble title during the
aftermath of the Siege of Highwater. Killed the white bear that became the house
symbol. The Name Mokar Means to Shine.
Second Generation (Children of Mokar & Henra)
Adrione Hige 7,468 BR  7,422 BR
The brains behind the Hige Distribution Company, she conceived the idea of
moving food across the kingdom. Incapable of having children. The Name Adrione
means Carrier/Bringer of Victory.
Benam Hige 7,465 BR  7,410 BR
Twin to Biba, first heir. Managed the distribution company to its peak wealth
18,000 Rern). Incapable of having children. Along with Adrione, forced Saperin I
into producing heirs for the family. The Name Benam means Godʼs Fury.
Biba Hige 7,465 BR  7,436 BR
Twin to Benam. Drowned herself after learning of Saperin Iʼs death because she
was very close to her and distraught over losing her. Blamed Benam, Adrione, and
herself for what happened to her sister because she couldnʼt save her sister from
House Hige
5
the will of Benam and Adrione. Incapable of having children. The name Biba
means Small Bear.
Saperin Hige I 7,461 BR  7,436 BR
The only child capable of having children. Forced at age 16 to bed a friend of her
brother to produce heirs. Gave birth to four surviving children (two died), died at
age 25 during her sixth childbirth. Her children: Tolence, Kason, Saperin II,
Breleys. The name Saperin means Sapphire.
The Saperin I Tragedy
Three of four siblings were incapable of having children. The entire future of
House Hige fell on the youngest, Saperin I, who was used as a broodmare by her
own brother and sister. She was dead by 25. Biba, the sibling who loved her most
but couldnʼt protect her, walked into the water and never came out.
Third Generation (Children of Saperin I)
Tolence Hige 7,440 BR  7,357 BR
Very like his uncle Benam, equally incompetent, equally ambitious. Quoted: “There
is no such thing as a god, only men.” Treated the women in his life as objects to
trade for social advancement. Only took advice from men, including his brother
Kason. The name Tolence means Tolerant.
Kason Hige “The Fool” 7,438 BR  7,349 BR
Earned his epithet by convincing Tolence to invest with Pasilerad Kacer, a con
man Kason believed could perform miracles. They gave Pasilerad the family funds
and their youngest sister Breleysʼs hand in marriage believing him to be a local
investor. The scheme was only uncovered after Pasileradʼs death, they thought
they were accumulating money overnight, but it turns out Pasilerad was scamming
people using House Hige as a cover. The name Kason means Innocence.
Saperin Hige II 7,437 BR  7,353 BR
House Hige
6
Like her mother, used as a political tool by her brothers. Married a distant cousin
at 18; the marriage advanced cart manufacturing for the distribution company.
Unlike her mother, she lived a happy life with a loving husband and children. The
name Saperin means Sapphire.
Breleys Hige 7,436 BR - 7,354 BR
Married to Pasilerad Kacer at age 12 (he was 30. Spent her entire married life
being abused while her family ignored it. Pasilerad left her partially blind. Couldnʼt
give him children. Escaped at 18, took half his money, and seemingly disappeared
from the face of the earth. The name Breleys means Paper.
Potely Hige 7,414 BR  7,382 BR
Daughter of Tolence. Became a lady-in-waiting to Dowager Lady Ailua of House
Aedria hoping to build relations. Tried to seduce the youngest son while serving as
his tutor. Failed, was fired by House Aedria, and disowned by her own family to
save face. Further cemented House Higeʼs reputation as a joke. The name Potely
means a woman from a high river village.
In Story Characters: A Tale of A Thousand Songs
Lady Emillea Hige 7,270 BR  7,241 BR
Concubine/consort of King Benjamin II. Mother of Emperor Solis. Appointed regent
for Solis after the king named him heir at the Festival of Mourning. When the king
died four months later and the twins staged their coup, Emillea was captured first.
While Solis hid under a floorboard, Princess Iris forced Emillea to drink poison in
front of a jeering crowd. This became the defining trauma of Solisʼs life and the
catalyst for the civil war. The Name Emillea means Eager Heart.
Key Events Timeline
7,463 BR  The Siege of Highwater. Henra protects the family by working as a
maid and betraying her employer at the right moment.
House Hige
7
7,460 BR  House Hige officially founded by Mokar, three years after the Siege.
Henra dies around this time.
7,455 BR  Adrione and Benam found the Hige Distribution Company, moving
food across the kingdom.
7,445 BR  Saperin I forced at age 16 to produce heirs for the family, as her three
siblings are all incapable of having children.
7,436 BR  Saperin I dies in childbirth at age 25 (sixth pregnancy). Biba drowns
herself in grief.
7,424 BR  Breleys Hige married to Pasilerad Kacer at age 12 by her brothers.
Years of abuse follow.
7,419 BR  Saperin IIʼs marriage advances cart manufacturing for the distribution
company.
7,418 BR  Breleys escapes at 18, takes half of Pasileradʼs money, and vanishes.
7,395 BR  Potely Hige tries to seduce the youngest son of House Aedria. Fired
and disowned. House Higeʼs reputation plummets further.
7,260 BR  Lady Emillea Hige becomes concubine/consort of King Benjamin II,
elevating House Higeʼs court visibility.
7,250 BR  Solis is born.
7,241 BR  Solis named heir at the Festival of Mourning when heʼs nine. Emillea
appointed regent. King Benjamin dies. The twins coup. Emillea is publicly forced to
drink poison by Princess Iris while Solis hides under a floorboard. House Hige
members largely eradicated.
Heraldry & Identity
Crest:
Colors and Their Meanings:
Spirit Animal: White Bear; representing strength and the ability to survive harsh
conditions.
Motto: “Die With Honor or Do Not Die at All”
House Name Meaning: Highborn: a person of noble status (an aspirational choice
for a family that started as peasants).
House Hige
8
Reputation & Perception
Public Image: “A little fish in an ocean of sharks and whales.” Since their founding,
House Hige has been treated as lapdogs by every noble house and never given
real respect or authority. Other houses see them as opportunists who donʼt
understand their “place” in high society.
The Pattern: Every generation of Hige tries to climb, and most get knocked back
down. Potely tried to seduce her way into House Aedria and got fired. Kason
trusted a con man and lost the family fortune. Tolence treated women as currency
and got nowhere. Only Emilleaʼs connection to the king broke the cycle, and it cost
her life.
The Irony: The family named itself “Highborn” while being the lowest-ranked,
poorest, most disrespected house in the kingdom. Their motto demands dying
with honor in a family where members have been scammed, abused, disowned,
and drowned themselves. The gap between aspiration and reality is House Hige,
until Emillea and Solis make good on the name.

Why They Matter
House Iarnailo is a warning dressed up as a welcome. Their motto, “Sweet is the
poison of the flower,” says exactly what they are: beautiful on the surface,
dangerous underneath. The thistle on their crest says the same thing differently:
House Iarnailo
1
resilient, thorned, and not to be grabbed carelessly. Where other houses lead with
military force or religious weight, House Iarnailo leads with allure and the
understanding that hidden weapons are often more effective than visible ones.
Heraldry
Crest: A green thistle with a pink bloom rises prominently against a white field,
divided horizontally by a grey band. The thorned stem and jagged leaves are
rendered in careful detail.
Symbolism: The thistle represents resilience, protection, and noble suffering. The
soft pink of the flower contrasts sharply with the aggressive green thorns,
creating visual tension that mirrors the houseʼs philosophy: beauty that conceals
danger, sweetness that masks poison. The grey horizontal band suggests
pragmatism or neutrality as a foundation. The white background implies purity or
innocence that the thorned flower disrupts. This crest warns as much as it
welcomes.
Motto: “Sweet is the poison of the flower.”
