Why They Matter
House Jivaya belongs to Coelumʼs Sea Faction, a group that believes the sea has
vast resources that can help their people thrive and grow. The Sea Faction
House Jivaya
1
prioritizes trade and commerce and is always looking for ways to expand their
reach.
TBD Further significance to be developed.]
Heraldry
Crest: The crest is mounted upon a uniquely shaped shield featuring a bold
triangular chevron design that points upward, creating a dynamic sense of
movement and aspiration toward the horizon. The composition is divided into
three main sections: two white triangular fields flank the top left and right, meeting
at a peak, while a prominent chevron of deep blue cuts diagonally across each
side, and the lower portion is rendered in solid black, representing the mysterious
depths of the ocean. Golden or yellow crescent-shaped embellishments
punctuate the white areas like breaking waves or navigational markers, adding
decorative detail that speaks to the houseʼs seafaring heritage. Dominating the
center of the shield is an elaborate shipʼs wheel rendered in white with a bright
blue inner circle, its eight spokes radiating outward like compass points, each
spoke tipped in gold, with the wheelʼs central hub glowing yellow like a beacon or
compass rose.
Symbolism: The wheel represents navigation, mastery of the seas, and the ability
to chart oneʼs own course through uncertain waters. The upward-pointing chevron
structure suggests both the prow of a ship cutting through waves and the
aspiration to reach new shores. The blue and black color progression from top to
bottom mirrors the oceanʼs journey from sunlit surface to abyssal depths,
reinforcing the houseʼs conviction that “The Sea is where we must go.”
Motto: “The Sea is where we must go.”

Heraldry
Crest: This noble crest presents a quartered shield with a striking balance of
silver-grey and gold, divided vertically down the center and then horizontally
across the middle, creating four equal sections that alternate between grey (upper
left and lower right) and white or pale cream (upper right), with the lower left
quarter rendered in brilliant gold. At the heart of the composition rests a large
white circle, representing the full moon, which dominates the central intersection
of the quartering and serves as the backdrop for the houseʼs primary symbol: two
crossed swords arranged in an X formation, their blades gleaming silver-white
while their hilts and grips are wrapped in rich brown leather, topped with golden
pommels that catch the light. The swords cross precisely at their centers, creating
perfect symmetry and balance.
Symbolism: The duality of the crossed swords symbolizes what defines House
Kifan: tradition and progress, earthly strength and celestial wisdom, the warriorʼs
blade and the mysticʼs vision. The moon behind the swords reinforces their motto
“The Moon is where we come from,” suggesting that their martial prowess is
guided by lunar wisdom and spiritual connection. The crossing of the blades
represents their openness to new ideas meeting old values, the intersection of
past and future, and the protective stance they take as guardians of both
terrestrial and celestial heritage.
Motto: “The Moon is where we come from.”

House Kivier
House Kivier
“RISING ABOVE ALL OTHERS”
Quick Facts
Status: Duke/Duchess
Origin: Equateiy
Founded: 8,900 BR (oldest noble house in Equateiy; founded alongside the nation
itself)
Founder: Yemaser of House Kivier
Seat: TBD
Faction: Second Movement Party
Spirit Animal: Lion
Colors: Gold Wealth, Achievement) & Yellow Nobility)
Wealth: TBD
Military: TBD
Religion: TBD
Theme Song: TBD
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Duke/Duchess. The secretive power behind Equateiyʼs throne.
House Kivier acts as the unofficial and official rulers of Equateiy, viewing
themselves as royalty though they never formally claimed a crown. Their true
history remains shrouded in mystery.
Solisʼs Era: Duke Reasaec Kivier financed Orcusʼs side of the Aicruan civil war
through Equateiyʼs wealth. During Year Five of the war, Reasaec traveled to
Aicruae alongside Grand Sorcerer Sevtor to personally support Orcus. When the
war turned, Reasaec attempted to flee by ship back to Equateiy. Solis personally
attacked the fleeing ship, took Reasaecʼs head, and sent it to Gherci with a note
written in Ananara: “The head of a rat, do as you please with it.” The King of
House Kivier
1
Gherci had Reasaecʼs head preserved, his mouth forced open, and hung it at the
castle entrance.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Kivier founded Equateiy itself in 8,900 BR, making it the oldest nation on
the continent and House Kivier the oldest noble house still in existence. They
chose never to become monarchs, and no one knows why. That mystery is part of
what makes them dangerous. They rule without a crown, control the wealthiest
nation in the world, and keep their real history locked away. Equateiyʼs strategy
has always been economic leverage over military confrontation: “Smiling in
person, scheming behind the scenes” defines their diplomacy. Their currency, the
Pel, is valued at roughly $50 each, the highest in the world, and their banking
system underpins the economies of multiple nations, including Coelum, which
gives 40% of its national earnings to Equateiy for continued support.
Heraldry
Crest: A magnificent golden lionʼs head with its mouth open, revealing a red
tongue, set against a bright yellow shield framed by a distinctive checkered border
in alternating cream and yellow squares. The lion is rendered in bold black
outlines with detailing in its mane and facial features, dominating the center of the
crest with an expression of fierce nobility.
Symbolism: The golden lion symbolizes supreme courage, royal authority, and the
unwavering strength to lead. The lion has long represented kingship and
dominion, making it the emblem of a ducal house that values staths and command
over all rivals. The checkered border representing thinking and calculated moves.
Motto: “Rising Above All Others.”
Power & Influence
Source of Power
House Kivier
2
Economic dominance, banking, financial leverage, and secrecy. House Kivier
controls the wealthiest nation in the known world and uses economic
entanglement rather than military force to exert influence.
Internal Power Structure
TBD
Military Forces
TBD
Lands & Income
Seat: TBD
Key industries: Sophisticated banking and financial services, jewel and precious
metal mining, maritime trading, luxury goods production and export,
manufacturing of quality goods.
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
TBD
Rival Houses
TBD
Political Faction
Second Movement Party: This faction believes that wealth is the key to a
successful society and that the government should prioritize policies that promote
economic growth. House Kivier leads this faction alongside House Imbrer, House
Ganane, House Balewer, House Uaver, House Vesmen, and House Adiye.
House Culture
Religion
TBD

Values
Wealth, commerce, cosmopolitanism, meritocracy. Equateiy is a society where
wealth determines status more than birth.
Reputation
House Kivierʼs true history remains a mystery, partially because Equateiy is so old
and partially because the house is so secretive. They view themselves as royalty
despite never taking a crown. Other nations view Equateiy as “the place of sin, the
land of secrets.”
History
Founding (8,900 BR)
Yemaser of House Kivier founded Equateiy in 8,900 BR during the Warriorsʼ Age. It
is among the oldest of existing countries, with some claim to formation before the
Warriorsʼ Age, though depending on who you ask, that claim holds no grounds.
House Kivier became the countryʼs founders and first official nobles, but why they
chose not to become monarchs remains unknown.
Rise to Power
TBD

TBD

Duke Reasaec Kivierʼs failed gambit in backing Orcus during the Aicruan civil war.
Reasaec was beheaded at sea by Solis, and his head was sent to Gherci as a
trophy.
Notable Members
House Kivier
4
Yemaser of House Kivier (dates unknown)
Founder of House Kivier and Equateiy
Founded Equateiy in 8,900 BR, establishing it as the first kingdom during the
Warriorsʼ Age. Beyond the founding, almost nothing about Yemaser is known
publicly, a pattern of secrecy that House Kivier has maintained ever since.
Duke Reasaec Kivier (dates unknown, died 7,217 BR
Duke of Equateiy
Equateiyʼs chief financier of Orcusʼs war effort during the Aicruan civil war. During
Year Five, he traveled to Aicruae alongside Grand Sorcerer Sevtor to personally
support Orcus. When the war turned against Orcus, Reasaec attempted to flee by
ship back to Equateiy. Solis personally attacked the fleeing ship and took
Reasaecʼs head. He sent it to Gherci with a note written in Ananara: “The head of a
rat, do as you please with it.” The King of Gherci had Reasaecʼs head preserved,
his mouth forced open, and hung it at the castle entrance.
Succession
TBD

Economic dominance, the highest valued currency in the world (the Pel), financial
leverage over other nations, secrecy, banking and trade networks that span the
continent.

Plot Significance: House Kivierʼs gamble on Orcus represents Equateiyʼs broader

entries.title: House Kulio
entries.text:
House Kulio
House Kulio
“IN SEARCH OF KNOWLEDGE, IN PURSUIT OF GLORY”
Quick Facts
Status: Count/Countess
Origin: Aicruae Western)
House Name Meaning: Favored Child
Founded: 8,321 BR
Founder: Asaran Kulio, Nabiakaro Kulio, and Dazet Kacer
Seat: Hadiber, Western Aicruae Capital of Western Aicruae)
Faction: Divine Faction
Spirit Animal: Owl
Colors: Yellow Faithfulness, Wisdom, Glory)
Wealth: 125,000 Rern
Military: Minimal (guards only; not a military house)
Religion: Leneyez
Theme Song: “Yellow Flicker Beat” by Lorde
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Count/Countess. A respected but mid-tier noble house, known
more for their divine ancestry and political maneuvering than for military strength
or wealth.
Solisʼs Era: Secretly Pro-Solis through Mihel Kulio. House Kulio survives the
transition from kingdom to empire. Mihel Kulio gains the title of Duke in Solisʼs new
government, but ultimately abandons the house, leaving for the Mystic Isles and
swearing off descendants. The house continues through the Kacer branch.
Crandonaʼs Era: The Main Kulio line is gone. Mihel, the last legitimate heir,
accepted a Dukeʼs title from Solis and then abandoned it fleeing to the Mystic Isles
and swearing his bloodline would end with him. It did. His sisters Harnua and
Esterica both died during the civil war. With no direct heirs, leadership passed to
House Kulio
1
the Kacer branch the line descended from Dazet, the bastard co-founder. The
Kacers did not inherit Mihelʼs dukedom. That title was a personal reward, not a
hereditary elevation. House Kulio reverted to Count, and the Kacers took the seat
at Hadiber until the empire was offically founded in 7,163 BR. They took it badly.
Where the Main line balanced self-indulgence with occasional greatness Haileaʼs
sacrifice, Mihelʼs strategic brilliance the Kacer branch leaned into the indulgence
without the counterweight. Pasilerad Kacerʼs legacy looms large: the con man, the
child-bride husband, the man whose bones were dug up and burned. The Kacers
who followed learned the wrong lessons. By Crandonaʼs Era, House Kulio is
wealthier than ever from agricultural trade but more dissolute than ever in
reputation. The Testing still happens. No one passes.
Minaraʼs Era: House Kulio survives. Thatʼs the kindest thing anyone says about
them. The Kacer branch has held the seat for over two and a half millennia. The
divine gifts are completely gone not faded, not diminished, gone. No Kulio has
shown prophetic ability in living memory. The Testing is a formality performed out
of habit. The Asata prayers are mumbled sounds that even the Kulios suspect
mean nothing. What remains is wealth, scandal, and a name that still opens doors
barely. They still practice polygamy. Other houses tolerate them because Kulio
gold spends as well as anyoneʼs, but no one looks at a Kulio and thinks of fallen
gods anymore. They think of fallen standards.
Why They Matter
House Kulio is a house that lives on reputation it can never quite earn. They
descend from gods, and everyone knows it. Their ancestors fell from the sky,
spoke the language of divinity, could see the future, could heal with a touch. But
somewhere between that divine origin and the present day, the bloodline curdled.
The powers faded. What replaced them was vanity, self-indulgence, and a talent
for spectacle that made the other houses keep their distance without ever turning
their backs entirely.
They matter because they are the proof that divine blood doesnʼt guarantee divine
character. Hailea Kulio could heal plagues and see the future, and she died at
thirty-five saving strangers while her followers threw rocks at the woman she
loved. Ayera Kulio made her husband drink his other wivesʼ blood. Jando Kulio
broke hearts like a hobby until someone stabbed roses into his eye sockets.
House Kulio
2
Pasilerad Kacer was so beloved in life and so despised in death that people dug
up his bones and set them on fire.
And then there are the three Kulio siblings who get caught in the civil war: Mihel
the strategist who loses his eye and his leg and both his sisters, Esterica the
empress who dies drinking poison meant for her husband, and Harnua the saint
who put the poison there. House Kulio is a family that destroys itself from the
inside out, generation after generation, and somehow keeps surviving anyway.
Nicknames People Call Them During This Era
“The Fallen Ones”
“Heavenʼs Bastards”
“Those Who Fell”
“Lords of Hadiber”
“The Western Counts”
“Children of the Sky/Sky Children”
“The Seers of Hadiber”
“The Bedwarmers of Hadiber” (referencing their polygamy)
Heraldry
Crest: Per bend or and gold (a shield of golden yellow with subtle diagonal bands).
At center, a green oak tree with a brown trunk, spreading roots, and golden acorns
nestled in its foliage. A gray owl perches atop the treeʼs crown. Four smaller gray
owls sit upon the twisting roots below. In the upper dexter corner, a coral sun with
wavy rays.
Symbolism: The gold field stands for faithfulness, wisdom, and glory. The oak tree
with acorns signals endurance a tree that grows slowly but stands for centuries,
and reflects the houseʼs steady foundation in learning. The five owls represent the
familyʼs exile from the sky; they cannot go home. The one perched high and four
grounded in the roots show knowledge passed from one generation to the next,
even in displacement. The sun serves as a reminder of what was lost always
visible, never reachable.
Motto: “In Search of Knowledge, In Pursuit of Glory.”
House Kulio
3
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Politics, trade, and inherited divine respect. House Kulio has no armies, no fleets,
no great fortresses. What they have is a name that traces back to the gods
themselves, and the social capital that comes with it. Their real power is influence:
knowing the right people, making the right marriages, and leveraging their divine
ancestry whenever itʼs convenient.
Internal Power Structure
House Kulio practices polygamy. The family divides into Main and Side branches
based on birth order. The firstborn child becomes the heir, and their family line
becomes the Main family. All other siblings either join the Side family or marry out
into other houses. This system has produced fierce internal competition over who
holds the Main line, and itʼs the reason figures like Ayera Kulio could seize control
through sheer ruthlessness.
Military Forces
House Kulio is not a military family. They maintain household guards but nothing
substantial. They dabble in politics and trade instead. This lack of hard power is
both their greatest vulnerability and the reason theyʼve survived as long as they
have. No one sees them as a threat worth destroying.
Lands & Income
Seat: The city of Hadiber in Western Aicruae, considered the capital of the
western region. Before Aicruae was officially founded, the original capital was on
the western coast, possibly near what is now modern Hadiber.
Wealth: 125,000 Rern. Middle class among noble houses. Not rich, not poor.
Key industries:
Agricultural taxation, Western Aicruae feeds the kingdom. House Kulio takes a cut
of everything that grows in their territory grain, fruit, livestock. They donʼt farm
themselves; they collect from those who do.
House Kulio
4
Mill ownership, Kulio controls the processing infrastructure across Hadiber and
surrounding towns. Farmers can grow what they want, but if they want it milled,
stored, or preserved, they pay Kulio rates.
Market control, Hadiber is the commercial hub of Western Aicruae. House Kulio
oversees market access, trade licenses, and merchant disputes. Every transaction
in the capital feeds their coffers, one way or another.
Trade brokering, Kulios position themselves as middlemen between agricultural
producers and buyers from across Aicruae. They negotiate bulk contracts,
arrange transport, and take a percentage of every deal. Less glamorous than
prophecy, but it pays the bills now that the visions have dried up.
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Vemer Marriage Alliance). Jando Kulio married Fasi Vemer, linking the two
houses. Given that Jando was murdered shortly after, the allianceʼs long-term
stability is questionable.
Rival Houses
House Arvento: The Arventos are everything the Kulios are not: restrained, loyal,
respectable. Dukes who earned their rank through steadfast service to the crown,
not claims of divine blood. They find Kulioʼs revolving wives, public scandals, and
self-indulgence distasteful. The Kulios, in turn, dismiss Arvento as boring
functionaries with no imagination.
House Caraen: Both houses claim divine connection, and thatʼs precisely the
problem. Caraenʼs name means “Gift from the Gods” they were blessed, elevated,
chosen. Kulioʼs ancestors were punished, cast down, stripped of divinity. Caraen
sees Kulioʼs divine heritage talk as embarrassing: you donʼt brag about falling from
grace. Kulio sees Caraen as upstarts whose “gift” is secondhand favor compared
to actual godhood, however lost.
House Vika: Before their eradication, the Vikas looked at Kulio the way wolves look
at lapdogs. Dukes versus Counts. Eastern military power versus Western political
maneuvering. Vika dismissed Kulio as self-indulgent pretenders who confused old
House Kulio
5
blood with actual strength. Kulio resented being dismissed. The rivalry ended
when Solis burned Vika to the ground but old Kulios still remember the sneers.
Royal Connections
Ayera Kulio married her only daughter into the royal family of Gherci, giving House
Kulio a foothold in a foreign court. During the civil war era, Esterica Kulio married
Emperor Solis, making House Kulio the family of the first empress of the Solisian
Empire.
House Culture
Religion
Leneyez. Believers sacrifice both people and farm life to the gods during monthly
prayers and festivals, believing that sacrifice maintains both the physical and
spiritual well-being of the gods. House Kulio shares this religion with Houses
Patton, Vika, Vemer, Najil, and Hige.
Traditions
The Testing, At age seven, every Kulio child undergoes a ritual testing for
prophetic ability. The child is brought to a darkened room, given a cup of bitter
herbal tea meant to open the mind, and asked what they see. Elders watch for
signs: trembling, speaking in fragments, eyes rolling back. In the early
generations, children emerged with visions. Now, they emerge with nothing but
stomachaches. The ritual continues anyway. The family keeps hoping.
Asata Prayers, Kulio ceremonies births, marriages, deaths, the start of each new
year begin with recitations in Asata, the divine language their ancestors once
spoke fluently. The phrases have been passed down phonetically for centuries.
No living Kulio understands what they mean. Some scholars believe the words are
blessings; others suspect theyʼre fragments of a longer lament. The family recites
them regardless. To stop would be to admit the sky has forgotten them entirely.
The Branching When the firstborn heir comes of age, a formal ceremony
designates which siblings belong to the Main family and which to the Side. The
heir receives an oak branch cut fresh that morning; the others receive roots. Itʼs
House Kulio
6
meant to symbolize unity branches and roots are both part of the same tree but
Side family members have been known to burn their roots in private.
The Counting When a new wife enters a Kulio household, she is formally
presented to the existing wives in order of seniority. Each wife places a hand on
the newcomerʼs shoulder, one after another, literally counting her place in the
hierarchy. The main wife or first wife must then kiss the new wifes head and give
her a gift. The ceremony is brief and civil. What happens after the ceremony is not
always either.
Values
House Kulioʼs values are shaped by one inescapable truth: they are fallen gods
who can never go home.
Divine heritage, Kulio blood carries the remnants of divinity, and they know it. This
breeds a quiet superiority; they believe they are inherently set apart from other
noble houses, regardless of rank or wealth. The two owls on their crest one in the
branches, four among the roots remind them they belong in the sky but are bound
to the earth.
Knowledge and foresight, The founders could speak Asata and see the future.
Those gifts have faded, but the reverence for them hasnʼt. Kulios hoard
knowledge, collect prophecies, and prize insight over brute force. Their motto is
sincere: “In search of knowledge, in pursuit of glory.”
Personal freedom, They answer to the sky, not to earthly judgment. This justifies
the indulgence other houses whisper about, the polygamy, the lovers, the
scandals. Kulios donʼt see themselves as immoral; they see themselves as
operating by older, higher rules that mortals canʼt comprehend.
Legacy over reputation, The bloodline must continue. The divine gifts must be
passed down before they fade entirely. How the line continues through how many
wives, how many bastards, how many questionable marriages matters less than
ensuring it does.
Fatalistic hedonism Exile is permanent. The sky is closed. So they take what
pleasure and power they can in the time they have, never fully committed to the
mortal world theyʼre stuck in.
Reputation
House Kulio
7
The other houses neither like nor hate House Kulio. They respect them to a certain
extent as descendants of divine beings, but the houseʼs history of self-indulgence,
scandal, and moral failure makes everyone question whether those divine origins
mean anything at all. House Kulio is tolerated, not feared. Respected on paper,
side-eyed in practice.
History
Founding (8,321 BR)
House Kulio was founded by Asaran Kulio, his legitimate son Nabiakaro, and his
illegitimate son Dazet. All three were descendants of the People of the Sky, the
lesser gods who accepted Vapazʼs punishment after the War of Gods I and were
cast down to live among mortals. Through their gift for prophecies, their ability to
speak Asata (the language of the gods), and their strong divine powers, the
founders earned noble titles and status. Dazet, born to Asaranʼs childhood friend
rather than a legal wife, became the founder of the houseʼs second branch: House
Kacer.
Rise to Power
House Kulio rose through divine prestige rather than military conquest or wealth
accumulation. Their powers, particularly prophecy and divine healing, made them
valuable to other noble houses and to the crown. But their rise was always
tempered by their behavior. Every generation seemed to produce someone
brilliant and someone terrible, often in the same person.
Major Achievements
The Medal of Heroes, awarded to Hailea Kulio upon her death for sacrificing
herself to save plague victims. This is the houseʼs single greatest honor and one of
the highest distinctions in all of Aicruae.
Esterica Kulioʼs marriage to Emperor Solis and her role as the first empress,
including reshaping the empireʼs agricultural framework and founding two famous
libraries.
Major Disgraces
House Kulio
8
Ayera Kulioʼs murders (poisoning her husbandʼs other wivesʼ children, forcing her
husband to drink their blood, then roasting him alive).
Jando Kulioʼs reputation as a serial heartbreaker whose murder left the house
leaderless, with a six-year-old inheriting the title.
Pasilerad Kacerʼs posthumous exposure as a con man and abuser, resulting in his
grave being dug up and his bones burned.
Harnua Kulioʼs assassination of Empress Esterica (her own half-sister) and her
subsequent execution by burning at the stake.
The Kacer Branch
The Kacer branch, founded by Dazet Kacer, has operated as the houseʼs
secondary line since the beginning. Its most infamous member is Pasilerad Kacer,
one of the most universally despised men in Aicruaeʼs history. But the branchʼs
survival is the reason House Kulio endures into later eras. When Mihel Kulio
abandoned the Main line and left for the Mystic Isles, the Kacer branch carried the
family name forward.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs founders to the civil war generation.
Asaran Kulio (8,376 BR – 8,213 BR)
“The Founder” — Name meaning: Treasure
Father of both Nabiakaro (legitimate) and Dazet (illegitimate). One of the three
creators of House Kulio. Could speak Asata, the language of the gods, and was a
skilled magic user. Despite these abilities, Asaran is described as “forgettable”
outside of them. He wasnʼt a warrior, a great politician, or a memorable
personality. He was a man with divine blood and not much else, who managed to
turn that blood into a title. He lived to 163, an unusually long life likely tied to his
divine heritage.
Nabiakaro Kulio (8,348 BR – 8,273 BR)
“The Young Lord” — Name meaning: Deer
House Kulio
9
The first official young lord of House Kulio and the only legal son of Asaran. Could
speak Asata and was a strong magic user. Nabiakaro represents the house at its
most straightforward: divine gifts, noble title, competent stewardship. Nothing
flashy. Nothing scandalous. He set the template that later Kulios would either
follow or violently deviate from.
Dazet Kacer (8,356 BR – 8,257 BR)
“The Bastard” — Name meaning: Caring Child
Bastard son of Asaran Kulio, born to a childhood friend. Helped his father and
half-brother acquire House Kulio but, because his mother wasnʼt legally married to
Asaran, he couldnʼt carry the Kulio name. Instead he became the heir of the
familyʼs second branch, known as Kacer. Could speak Asata and was a skilled
magic user. His branch would ultimately be the one to carry the family forward
when the Main line collapsed centuries later.
Hailea Kulio (8,002 BR – 7,967 BR)
“The Woman of the Sky” — Name meaning: Bright Beauty
One of the most powerful magic users to ever exist outside of being a Saint.
Hailea could heal through divine power and see the future. She was idolized all
her life. High society women sent her letters almost daily. She was a celebrity in
the truest sense, worshipped by strangers who believed they knew her.
But Haileaʼs story is also the story of what happens when devotion turns to
obsession. Her lover Takerei was branded “the witch of the great hill” by Haileaʼs
followers, who believed Takerei had bewitched their idol. They threw stones at
Takerei, ripped her clothes, and harassed her in the capital. The most aggressive
of them, Basania Caraen, led a public campaign of cruelty against Takerei.
Hailea died at 35, using her last strength to save victims of the Kalip plague, a
disease that caused vomiting, spotting, and loss of the ability to breathe. She died
of magical collapse. Nine of her followers committed suicide after her death “to be
with her,” with Basania Caraen being the first.
She received the Medal of Heroes upon her death. Her legacy is often
overshadowed by the drama surrounding her lovers, but she remains one of the
most recognized figures in all of Aicruae.
House Kulio
10
Ayera Kulio (7,842 BR – 7,800 BR)
“The Great Sinner” — Name meaning: A Thousand Days
One of the three wives of Uteo Kulio. Ayera poisoned the children of her husbandʼs
other wives, then forced Uteo to drink his other wivesʼ blood before roasting him
alive in a fire. She ruled as regent to her son afterward, utterly unchallenged. She
had her only daughter marry into the royal family of Gherci, and after her sons
came of age, she left Aicruae entirely, moving in with her daughter at the Gherci
royal palace. She lived to 42.
Ayera is one of those figures who is neither excused nor fully condemned by
history. She was operating in a polygamous system where co-wives and their
children were direct threats to her own childʼs inheritance. Her methods were
monstrous. Her motivations were not uncommon.
Jando Kulio (7,649 BR – 7,621 BR)
“The Red Beast” — Name meaning: The Apple of Oneʼs Eye
Considered very handsome. A serial romantic who, like many Kulio members, had
no shortage of lovers. Jando led many noble girls on and broke their hearts with a
casualness that became infamous. His charm was the kind that felt deliberate,
weaponized.
He was found stabbed to death outside a brothel with two roses stuffed in his
eyes. Believed to be murdered in revenge by someone whose heart heʼd broken,
or someone connected to one of them. His death left House Kulio in shambles. He
was the only male heir capable of assuming control, and the title fell to his
younger brother, who was six years old.
Marriage Alliance: Married Fasi Vemer, connecting House Kulio to House Vemer.
Pasilerad Kacer (7,401 BR – 7,302 BR)
Name meaning: Great Thinker
The Kacer branchʼs most infamous member and probably one of the most
universally disliked men in all of Aicruaeʼs history. An accomplished con man who
stole from poor and rich alike. For a time, he was the only person both classes
could agree to hate.
House Kulio
11
While alive, everyone believed he was a god. He had the charisma, the divine
ancestry talking points, the appearance of virtue. After his death, the truth about
his actions came out. His grave was dug up and his bones were set on fire.
His marriage to Breleys Hige was an abusive nightmare. Pasilerad was 30 when he
married 12-year-old Breleys. He left her partially blind. She escaped at 18 with half
his money. She is one of the few people in House Kulioʼs history who got out, and
got even, while still breathing.
Count Eserindeo Kulio (Civil War era, ~7,220s BR)
Father of Mihel, Esterica, and Harnua — Name meaning: Abundant Fortune
Head of House Kulio during the lead-up to the civil war. Had multiple wives (at
least seven recorded). His mother, wives, children, and half-siblings died during
the civil war as casualties of a plague that swept the region around the same time.
First Wife; Mihela Kulio: Mother of Mihel and Harnua. Hated Estericaʼs presence
because the young girl caught the attention of Prince Solis. Mihela believed
Esterica was trying to steal what belonged to her daughter Harnua, and sent sixyear-old Esterica to be raised by a cousin, Ser Minsupt, in the countryside.
Fourth Wife; Yeaevi Kulio: Mother of Esterica Kulio.
Mihel Kulio (7,259 BR - 7,205 BR)
“The Fallen” — Name meaning: First Light
Oldest son of Count Kulio and his first wife. Full brother to Harnua, half-brother to
Esterica. Mihel was the strategic mind behind House Kulioʼs support for Solis
during the civil war. He met Solis on the Mystic Isles to plan the rebellion and
served as a secret operative throughout the conflict. In Year One of the war 7,221
BR, he lost an eye. In Year Two 7,220 BR, he lost a leg. After his injuries ended
his combat usefulness, he pivoted to logistics and diplomacy, helping secure aid
from Gherci.
After the war, Solis rewarded him with the title of Duke. But Mihel had lost both his
sisters. Esterica was dead from the poison Harnua had meant for Solis. Harnua
was dead by burning at the stake. Lost in guilt and haunted by what his family had
become, Mihel left for the Mystic Isles, swore off women, and promised his family
House Kulio
12
line would end with him. The Kulio Main line died with that promise. The house
survived only through the Kacer branch.
Esterica Kulio (7,248 BR – 7,214 BR)
“The White Deer” | First Empress of the Solisian Empire — Name meaning: Star of
the Evening
Half-sister to Mihel and Harnua. Daughter of Count Eserindeo Kulio and his fourth
wife Yeaevi. Sent away to the countryside at age six by her fatherʼs first wife, who
resented the attention Prince Solis paid to young Esterica.
During the civil war, Esterica infiltrated Solisʼs camp to prove her familyʼs loyalty.
She reformed agriculture, executed soft-power plays including the famous
“handkerchief tea party” and rumor campaigns against Harnua, and ultimately
married Solis, becoming the first empress.
As empress, she reshaped the empireʼs agricultural framework and opened two
famous libraries. She gave birth to two children: Maen 7,217 BR) and Coyre 7,214
BR.
She died in 7,214 BR, six months after giving birth to Coyre. Harnua had disguised
herself as a wine bearer during a celebration and poisoned Solisʼs cup with Ilkai, a
god-killing herb. Esterica drank from the cup instead. She died instantly.
Legacy: Titled “Mother of a Dynasty.” Her daughter Coyre later built a museum in
her honor.
Harnua Kulio (7,251 BR – executed 7,214 BR)
“The Great Tragedy” | Thirteenth Saint — Name meaning: Everlasting Flame
Full sister to Mihel, half-sister to Esterica. A Saint anointed by the goddess
Nellebrie.
Harnuaʼs arc is one of the most dramatic in the houseʼs history. After Orcusʼs
death, her religious devotion curdled from consoling faith into zealotry. She
murdered Cidet officials on Orcusʼs behalf, plotted fratricide against Mihel (nearly
killing him in his sickbed before Esterica and Solis intervened), publicly defended
Iris, and co-plotted the assassination of Princess Kamerida of Gherci.
Her final act was a bargain with Nellebrie, who lent her the power to kill Solis, still
under the protection of the god Razar. During a celebration, Harnua disguised
House Kulio
13
herself as a wine bearer and poisoned Solisʼs cup with Ilkai. Esterica drank from it
instead and died instantly.
Harnua was captured by Solis and burned at the stake.
Final Miracle: With her dying breath, she used the last of her saintly power to raise
a second moon in honor of Orcus. Orcusʼs moon is bigger than Solisʼs moon and
spins three times faster, always beating Solisʼs in rotation.
Her death canonized her as the controversial thirteenth saint and created the
thirteenth month, Agarisono 40 days). She was the last Saint to ever be recorded,
second only to Reron in terms of infamy.
The Sky People: Origin of House Kulio
During the War of Gods I 30,000 BR, not all minor and lesser gods sided with
the New Gods. Some allied with the Old Gods. When the Old Gods lost, Vapaz
punished these rebellious lesser gods by stripping them of their divinity and
casting them down to live among mortals.
Those who fell divided into two groups based on how they responded to their
punishment.
The People of the Sky accepted what had happened to them. They recognized
that Vapaz had spared their lives when he could have destroyed them entirely, and
they valued that mercy, even through the shame of losing everything they had
been. They chose to intermarry with Sun-Forged humans, the ordinary mortals
without divine ancestry, and they dispersed across the world. Their divine blood
diluted over millennia, but traces remained: the ability to speak Asata, the gift of
prophecy, strong divine powers that surfaced unpredictably in certain
descendants. House Kulio descends from these people.
The People of the Mountain rejected Vapazʼs judgment entirely. They refused to
accept mortality, refused to integrate with humans, refused to let go of what they
had lost. They gathered atop a high mountain that would eventually become
Vikistv and waited centuries for a way to reclaim their power. Eventually, Grand
Mage Verna struck a bargain with the goddess Iswan: “Take my blood and soul, all
that I have to divinity, and create, and we shall honor you, we shall never aspire to
divinity again.” Iswan agreed. The magic she gave them corrupted their souls,
making them neither divine nor mortal, and left them vulnerable to sun and fire.
House Kulio
14
Two groups of fallen gods. One accepted the loss. One couldnʼt. The People of
the Sky became noble houses and intermarried with humans. The People of the
Mountain became the magic users of Vikistv, persecuted after Solisʼs conquest.
The same punishment, the same fall, and two completely different civilizations
emerged from the choice of how to carry it.
Divine Abilities (Degraded Over Generations)
The founders of House Kulio carried abilities inherited from their divine ancestors,
but these powers weakened with each generation as the bloodline mixed with
mortal humans.
Asata: The language of the gods. The founders could speak it fluently. By
Harnuaʼs era, some understanding remained, but the full fluency was gone. By
later eras, only sacred phrases survived, preserved as prayers. Asata was
primarily a spoken language, as divine communication doesnʼt require writing.
Gift for Prophecies: The ability to see fragments of the future. This manifested
most powerfully in Hailea Kulio, who could see the future clearly enough to act on
it.
Strong Divine Powers: Including divine healing, foresight, and other abilities that
surfaced unpredictably. Hailea Kulio was the most powerful example, possessing
both divine healing and prophetic sight so strong that she was considered one of
the most powerful magic users to ever exist outside of being a Saint.
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
Divine ancestry the only noble house in Aicruae descended from actual gods,
however fallen. The Sky People heritage sets them apart, and they never let
anyone forget it.
Prophetic legacy Hailea Kulio was one of the most powerful magic users outside
of Sainthood. Even though the gifts have faded, the memory of what Kulio blood
once produced commands a certain awe.
Trade dominance in Western Aicruae they control Hadiber, the mills, the markets,
and the contracts. The breadbasket flows through Kulio hands.
House Kulio
15
Scandal the polygamy, the lovers, the murdered stepchildren, the bodies outside
brothels. Other houses gossip about Kulio the way people gossip about a neighbor
whose parties get too loud. Disapproving, but unable to look away.
What They Lack
Military strength they have guards, not armies. In a fight, they need allies.
Respect other houses acknowledge Kulioʼs divine blood and then roll their eyes at
their behavior. The self-indulgence undercuts the reverence their ancestry might
otherwise command.
Internal unity the polygamy system breeds rivalry between wives, between Main
and Side families, between half-siblings who eye each otherʼs positions. Kulios
scheme against each other as readily as against outsiders.
Discipline generations of “we answer to the sky, not to earth” have produced a
house that does what it wants. This makes them unpredictable but also unreliable.
Vulnerabilities
The gifts are fading each generation is more mortal than the last. The Testing
produces nothing. The Asata prayers are just sounds. Their main claim to
specialness is disappearing, and everyone knows it.
Succession chaos polygamy plus Main/Side divisions plus ambitious wives equals
constant instability. Ayera Kulio poisoned her husbandʼs other children. Jandoʼs
death left a six-year-old in charge. The next crisis is always one bad marriage
away.
Dependent on royal favor without military power, Kulio needs the crownʼs
protection. If they back the wrong side or fall out of favor, they have no fallback.
Their own history Pasilerad Kacerʼs grave was dug up and his bones burned.
Ayeraʼs atrocities are still whispered about.
Role in Narrative
Book Appearances: A Tale of a Thousand Songs Book 1, through Esterica,
Harnua, and Mihel Kulio.
House Kulio
16
Plot Significance: House Kulio sits at the center of the civil warʼs most personal
betrayal. Esterica marries Solis and becomes his empress. Harnua, anointed by
Nellebrie, tries to kill Solis and accidentally kills her own half-sister instead. Mihel
supports Solis from the shadows, loses everything, and walks away from the
family entirely. The houseʼs three siblings represent three different responses to
the war: loyalty, devotion turned to fanaticism, and survival at the cost of
everything that mattered.
Key Members in Story: Esterica Kulio (first empress, major character), Harnua
Kulio (thirteenth saint, major antagonist), Mihel Kulio (secret Solis ally, supporting
character).
Cross-References

(branch family), Emperor Solis Elias Patton, Princess Iris Aleka Patton, Prince

Verna, Sun-Forged Humans, A Tale of a Thousand Songs Book 1, Agarisono

entries.title: House Leva
entries.text:
House Leva
House Leva
“A SORROWFUL WINTER AND A WELCOMING SPRING”
Quick Facts
Status: Count/Countess
Origin: Aicruae Common, elevated when Brimena caught the queenʼs attention)
House Name Meaning: Messenger of the Gods
Founded: 8,902 BR
Founder: Brimena Leva
Seat: Jasereiey, Aicruae (communal block living; the family owns all houses on
one block)
Faction: Common People Faction
Symbol: Star & Ship, and the bust (head sculpture) of the Aicruaean Woman (no
spirit animal)
Colors: TBD
Wealth: 147,000 Rern
Military: 50+ ships (twice House Dajanyiʼs fleet); crew not limited to family
members
Religion: Barqeten
Theme Song: “Be Careful (feat. Laney Jones)” by Tommee Profitt
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Count/Countess. A common-born house elevated to nobility after
Brimena Leva attracted the queenʼs attention with her quick mind. Despite their
count-level rank, House Leva is feared and respected for their wealth and naval
power.
Solisʼs Era: Survived. House Leva survived the civil war between Solis and the
twins for two reasons: they did not join the twinsʼ side, and they were able to
escape the twinsʼ initial coup.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
House Leva
1
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Leva is the only matriarchal house in the world, governed by a system
called the Divine Matriarch that grants power solely to women. They were
common-born, raised up because one woman was too clever to ignore. And from
that point forward, every generation was shaped by women who refused to let the
house fall, no matter what it cost them.
Theyʼre a count family. Thatʼs it. No duke title, no vast armies on land. But they
have over fifty ships, twice the fleet of House Dajanyi, and a reputation as “the
kingʼs thieves” that makes other nobles uneasy. They strike first in trade, politics,
and battle. They turn rogues into officers. Pedigree means nothing to them.
Results do.
Their wealth, their naval strength, their survival through the civil war: all of it was
built and maintained by women. From Brimena, who created the concept of the
Divine Matriarch, to Oera, who gave birth to eighteen daughters and married them
into noble houses across the world, to Varegua II, who buried her mother, her
grandmother, and her aunts before she was fifteen and still held the family
together. House Leva is the proof that you donʼt need noble blood or a standing
army to build something that lasts. You need women who wonʼt quit.
Heraldry
The Crest: The House Leva crest takes an unusual oval form rather than a
traditional shield shape, its field a deep, rich red. In the center is a womanʼs profile
facing left, rendered in a style similar to a classical cameo or Renaissance portrait.
Her skin is brown, her hair a deep purple styled in elaborate curls gathered at the
nape of her neck, and she wears a golden yellow headwrap with radiating
sections. Her expression is serene, eyes gazing forward toward some distant
point. Above her head sits a small golden eight-pointed star, and below her
portrait sits a tiny detailed ship with full sails.
Symbolism:
The Woman of Aicruae is the center of everything. Not a goddess. Not a myth. A
sailor. A common woman who looked up at the stars and decided she could read
House Leva
2
them, who climbed aboard a ship and decided she could steer it, and who came
home with enough gold that the queen couldnʼt ignore her anymore. Sheʼs
Brimena Leva before she was Brimena Leva. Sheʼs Xanti crossing the Quather Sea.
Sheʼs Varegua I completing that same crossing in two weeks with five people.
Sheʼs every woman who ran this family for over a thousand years because the
Divine Matriarch said women rule and men protect. The crest doesnʼt show a
symbol of the house. It shows the houseʼs religion. The belief that women create
the future.
The purple hair marks her as something more than mortal. Purple is the color of
royalty, and the Levas have never been royals. Theyʼre counts. But the Woman on
the crest isnʼt wearing a crown. Sheʼs wearing purple because the house decided,
on their own terms, that the women who built this family earned the same honor
as queens. Inene Leva placed her two-year-old daughter as heir over six older
brothers and dared anyone to argue. Oera gave birth to eighteen daughters and
married them across the world. The purple says: we donʼt need your permission to
be sacred.
The golden headwrap ties to House Levaʼs name. Leva means “Messenger of the
Gods.” The gold radiating outward from her head is the light of divine
communication, the same faith that drives their Barqeten beliefs. Barqeten holds
that by simply existing, you worship the gods. The Woman on the crest exists.
Thatʼs enough. The headwrap also reads as wealth, as warmth, as the practical
beauty of a woman who works the sea and still looks like she belongs on a coin.
The eight-pointed star above her head is heaven. The ship below her chin is the
sea. She sits between them. Thatʼs the whole life of House Leva in one image.
Stars for navigation, for faith, for the divine guidance that Brimena believed in
when she created the Divine Matriarch. And a ship for the work. The actual,
physical, dangerous work of crossing oceans and bringing back 90,000 Rern for
the crown and 50,000 Rern in gold artifacts and building a fleet of fifty ships that
makes other houses nervous. The star says where theyʼre going. The ship says
how they get there.
The red field is sacrifice. The Levas have bled for this house in ways most families
canʼt imagine. Sonua died in childbirth at nineteen. Her daughter Varegua II buried
her mother, her grandmother, and her aunts before she turned fifteen. Then
Varegua II gave birth to twenty-four sons, one after another, waiting for the
House Leva
3
daughter who would continue the Divine Matriarch, and when that daughter finally
came, the girl was sick and needed 2,000 Rern in medicine just to survive.
Varegua took odd jobs from royals and nobles to pay for it. Red is the cost. Every
generation of Leva women has paid it.
The oval shape instead of a traditional shield is its own statement. House Leva
doesnʼt follow the rules other houses follow. Theyʼre the only matriarchal house in
the world. They live in communal block housing instead of a manor. They recruit
crew from outside the family. They trade salt with House Vika and get called “the
kingʼs thieves” and donʼt care. An oval crest for a house that has never fit inside a
regular frame.
House Colors: Red, Purple, and Gold. Red for sacrifice, passion, and the blood
cost of building something from nothing. Purple for the sacred status of the Divine
Matriarch and the women who carry it. Gold for divine guidance, for the wealth
theyʼve pulled from every ocean, and for Barqeten faith that says existence itself
is worship.
Motto: “A Sorrowful Winter and a Welcoming Spring.”
Motto Meaning: The motto is the story of House Leva told in one breath. Every
generation faces a winter. Brimena was a common woman in a world that didnʼt
care about common women. Winter. The queen noticed her. Spring. Xanti crossed
the Quather Sea and came home rich. Spring. Sonua died at nineteen giving birth.
Winter. The baby survived and became Varegua II. Spring. Varegua II lost
everyone she loved before she was fifteen. Winter. She held the house together
anyway, had twenty-four sons, and finally got her daughter. Spring.
The Levas donʼt pretend the sorrow isnʼt real. They donʼt skip over it or dress it up.
The motto puts winter first because thatʼs how life works for this family. The loss
comes first. Always. But the second half of the motto isnʼt a hope. Itʼs a fact.
Spring comes. It has come every single time for House Leva, carried on the backs
of women who refused to let the line die, who sailed harder, worked longer, and
buried their dead without stopping. The spring is welcoming because the Levas
have earned it. Every time.
Oeraʼs name means “Joy in Spring.” She was the spring. Eighteen daughters. A
legacy planted across the world. The motto was written for women like her. And
for the winters that came before her and after her. The Levas carry both.
House Leva
4
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Naval strength, trade, wealth, and fear. Despite holding only a count-level title,
House Leva commands respect and wariness from other noble houses. Their fleet
is formidable and their reputation as “the kingʼs thieves” precedes them.
Internal Power Structure
House Leva follows the Divine Matriarch, the only matriarchal system in the world,
providing power solely to women. Brimena Leva created the concept, believing
that because women have the ability to create life, they were superior to men.
Women rule. Men guide them and protect the children.
Military Forces
50+ ships, twice the size of House Dajanyiʼs fleet. Their crew is not limited to
family members, meaning they can recruit broadly. Despite their wealth and
weaponry, their power is still limited by their count-level rank. They are feared and
respected regardless.
Lands & Income
Seat: Jasereiey, Aicruae Solisʼs Era). The family lives in communal block housing,
owning all houses on one block.
Key industries: TBD. Holds a business alliance with House Vika for salt trading.

Allied Houses
House Vika Business Alliance). House Vika initiated a partnership in a salt trading
business owned by House Leva.
House Dajanyi Marriage Connections). Five of Oera Levaʼs eighteen daughters
married into House Dajanyi.

TBD
History
Founding (8,902 BR)
Brimena Leva, the daughter of a local lord, attracted the attention of the queen
with her quick mind. The queen gave her a noble title and put her in charge of the
royal fleet and a group of sailors. Brimena then founded House Leva and created
the concept of the Divine Matriarch, believing that women, because they can
create life, were meant to rule, and that men were meant to guide them and
protect the children. The name Brimena means “bridge.”
Rise to Power

Major Achievements
Two Quarti Medals: Xanti Leva earned the first for her voyage to the Quather Sea,
which secured 90,000 Rern for the royal family. Varegua Leva I earned the second
after recovering 50,000 Rern worth of gold artifacts from locations across the
world and completing the voyage of the Quather and Fetora seas in two weeks
with a crew of five.
Major Disgraces
TBD
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs origins to its most recent known
generation.
Brimena Leva (8,942 BR – 8,872 BR)
Founder of House Leva | Creator of the Divine Matriarch
Name meaning: Bridge
The daughter of a local lord who attracted the attention of the queen with her
quick mind. She was given a noble title and placed in charge of the royal fleet and
a group of sailors. Brimena founded House Leva and created the concept of the
Divine Matriarch. She believed that because women have the ability to create life,
they were superior to men. Women were meant to rule. Men were meant to guide
them and protect the children.
Xanti Leva (8,527 BR – 8,501 BR)
First Quarti Medal Recipient
Name meaning: Ocean / Body of Water
Xanti received the Quarti Medal for her voyage to the Quather Sea, which secured
over 90,000 Rern for the royal family. She was deeply respected. So respected, in
fact, that the queen had two portraits composed entirely of gold commissioned of
her. One was given to the Leva family (a copy of the original) and the other was
hung in the royal treasury.
House Leva
7
Varegua Leva I (8,249 BR – 8,185 BR)
Second Quarti Medal Recipient
Name meaning: A Tall Plant
The second Quarti Medal holder. Varegua I recovered 50,000 Rern worth of gold
artifacts from various locations all over the world and returned them to the Leva
family and the royal family. She accomplished the impossible: her voyage of the
Quather Sea and Fetora Sea was completed in two weeks, with a crew of only five
people.
Inene Leva (7,705 BR – 7,619 BR)
Enforcer of the Divine Matriarch
Name meaning: Ice
Inene was known for her many male lovers, twenty-three in total, who fathered her
seven children. Like her ancestor Brimena, she believed that men were meant to
guide women in powerful positions. And she was the one to truly enforce the
Divine Matriarch, placing her two-year-old daughter as her heir over her six older
brothers.
Oera Leva (7,651 BR – 7,570 BR)
“High Mother”
Name meaning: Joy in Spring
Oera was the daughter of Inene Leva and House Levaʼs literal divine matriarch.
During her lifetime she took several husbands, like her mother, and gave birth to
eighteen children. All girls. For this she is called “High Mother.” Her daughters
married into House Dajanyi and lesser houses across the world.
Sonua Leva (7,626 BR – 7,607 BR)
Name meaning: Wave
The granddaughter of Oera, born to Oeraʼs firstborn daughter. Sonua was deeply
loved by her grandmother and by House Leva, but she died in childbirth at age 19.
Her daughter survived. Oera named the surviving girl Varegua Leva II because she
resembled their famous ancestor.
House Leva
8
Varegua Leva II (7,607 BR – 7,504 BR)
Name meaning: A Tall Plant
Named by her great-grandmother Oera after the famous ancestor she resembled.
Varegua IIʼs life was filled with tragedy. She lost her mother, her grandmother, and
several of her aunts before she had reached fifteen. She carried the weight of
securing the familyʼs legacy: she needed to marry and give birth to another divine
matriarch. She gave birth to twenty-four sons before finally having a girl, who was
weak and needed expensive medicine to live (around 2,000 Rern worth of
medicine). Varegua II took odd jobs from the royal family and other nobles to
afford the treatment, which thankfully worked.

Why They Matter
House Malrancis
1
The house motto says “A home for those with none,” and the one member we
know who eventually lived that motto to the letter. Danik Malrancis was
abandoned in the woods at birth and raised by wolves. As an adult, he became the
father figure to five young women who wandered into the Caprlolan forest: Ala,
Hicksora, Amuseri, Eveli, and Thoati. He hunted for them and protected them, but
kept his distance because he saw himself as a monster. He later joined Crandonaʼs
rebellion and was killed by Avromvog Stanyad. His death is one of the storyʼs most
devastating losses. A man who was himself abandoned and homeless built a
home for others, and thatʼs what House Malrancis is supposed to be about.
Heraldry
Crest: Bold vertical stripes alternate between vibrant red and pure white, with a
dark brown wolf in a rampant stance at the center. The wolfʼs form cuts across the
striped background, its mouth open and tail curved.
Symbolism: The wolf represents loyalty, family bonds, and the protective instincts
of the pack. The red and white stripes create a sense of order and structure, and
also suggest barriers separating the protected from the threatening wilderness
beyond. The wolfʼs placement over the stripes (rather than confined within a
single field) suggests the houseʼs role as guardians who stand between civilization
and chaos, offering sanctuary to the displaced. The brown coloring of the wolf,
earthier than the more common black or silver, emphasizes the houseʼs grounded,
practical approach to their duty of providing refuge.
Motto: “A home for those with none.”

entries.title: House Mena
entries.text:
House Mena
House Mena
“THE WEAK SHALL FALL TO THE STRONG”
Quick Facts
Status: Marquess/Marquis
Nickname: The Mena Beasts
Origin: Aicruae Northern)
Founded: 8,736 BR
Founder: Phiyano Mena
Seat: Atop a mountain in the Town of Paler, Northern Aicruae
Faction: Neutral Faction (shares values of both the Divine Faction and the
Common People Faction)
Spirit Animal: Giraffe
Colors: TBD
Wealth: 87,000 Rern (reduced after War of Fera reparations; originally a vast
fortune from Cidet reconstruction payment)
Military: 5,000 soldiers on stand-by (on par with House Caraen)
Religion: Rillic (sub-religion; believes humans fuel the godsʼ strength and give
them a tether to the mortal world)
House Name Meaning: Mountain
Theme Song: “Indestructible” by Welshly Arms
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Active. Founded in 8,736 BR by Phiyano Mena after completing
reconstruction of the Cidet. Their noble title was granted by the Cidet, not the
Imperial Palace.
Solisʼs Era: Survived. House Mena survived the civil war between Solis and The
Twins. Their line continues all the way up until the events of A Princess in Love,
when members of House Mena were killed by Merigen Bleelack for failing to
swear loyalty to him.
House Mena
1
Crandonaʼs Era: Eradicated. Members of House Mena were killed by Merigen
Bleelack for failing to swear loyalty to him during his six-year rule.
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Mena didnʼt claw their way to nobility through warfare or inheritance. They
built it. Literally. Phiyano Mena, a man born so ugly that people joked his father
had slept with a horse, reconstructed the Room of Glory in the Cidet and helped
build the Hall of Heroes for the Castle of Aicruae. The Cidet itself granted him his
noble title, not the crown. That distinction mattered. It meant House Menaʼs
legitimacy came from religious and architectural achievement, and that
relationship gave them something no other house had: exclusive passage to the
Cidet whenever they wanted.
But what makes House Mena truly strange in Aicruaeʼs history is the beast. Early
members of the house displayed physical traits that clashed with Aicruaean
beauty standards so severely that Phiyano was nicknamed “Sand Face” because
people said his features shifted like sand in a desert. His granddaughter Sirrah still
carried the beast traits, and one of her nine husbands conducted experiments to
“cure” her of them. Those experiments killed her. It took generations, but Bartyei
Mena eventually became the first member known for his looks rather than in spite
of them. The beast disappeared from the bloodline. What replaced it, though, was
a family curse of a different kind: brilliance paired with catastrophe.
Fransei Mena proved that at fourteen years old. Born during political unrest, she
single-handedly secured her familyʼs position and orchestrated the scheming that
triggered the War of Fera. She was so valuable, so essential to the kingdom, that
even after the war, House Mena couldnʼt be directly punished. So Fransei took the
fall alone. Hilatoma Dajanyi hanged her, and she died at fourteen, and her family
lived because of the work sheʼd already done.
House Mena is a house that earned everything the hard way and lost it all twice:
once through Franseiʼs execution, and again centuries later, when they were
wiped out entirely for refusing to kneel.
Heraldry
House Mena
2
The Crest: A lozenge (diamond-shaped) shield on a field of dark charcoal black.
At center stands a golden giraffe in profile facing left, spotted in black, tall and
upright on all four legs. Seven arrows fly toward the giraffe from multiple
directions. Six have wooden shafts with golden arrowheads and purple fletching.
One, positioned directly above the giraffeʼs head, carries blue fletching instead of
purple. None of the arrows have struck the animal. The giraffe stands unbothered.
Symbolism:
The giraffe is the strangest spirit animal in Aicruae and thatʼs the point. Every other
house picked something fierce. Panthers, hounds, sea serpents. House Mena
picked the tallest animal alive. Not the fastest, not the deadliest, not the most
beautiful. The tallest. Because Mena means “Mountain,” and thatʼs what this family
is. Phiyano Mena was born so ugly people said his father slept with a horse. They
called him “Sand Face.” He rebuilt the Room of Glory in the Cidet and the Hall of
Heroes for the Castle of Aicruae, and the Cidet itself gave him a noble title for it.
Not the crown. The Cidet. He didnʼt need to be beautiful or loved. He needed to be
useful, and he was so useful they had to make him a lord.
The giraffe carries that same energy. It doesnʼt look like a predator. It doesnʼt
move like one either. But it stands taller than everything around it. It sees farther. It
reaches higher. And if youʼve ever watched one fight, you know a giraffe can kill a
lion with a single kick. The Mena Beasts earned their nickname honestly. Early
members of the house carried physical traits that clashed with Aicruaen beauty
standards so badly that one of Sirrah Menaʼs nine husbands ran experiments on
her trying to “cure” her of them. Those experiments killed her. The beast in the
bloodline was real, and the giraffe on this crest doesnʼt hide it. It wears its
strangeness standing up.
The seven arrows flying at the giraffe and missing tell the story of a family the
world kept trying to bring down. House Mena has been shot at from every angle
for their entire existence. Phiyano was mocked for his face. Sirrah was
experimented on and killed. Fransei was hanged at fourteen. The house lost its
fortune paying War of Fera reparations. And in Crandonaʼs Era, they were wiped
out entirely by Merigen Bleelack for refusing to swear loyalty. Seven arrows,
seven directions, and not one of them hits the giraffe. It isnʼt dodging. It isnʼt
running. Itʼs standing still. The arrows miss because House Mena doesnʼt flinch.
House Mena
3
The single blue-fletched arrow among six purple ones is different on purpose. Six
purple arrows represent the attacks that come from noble society, from the world
of status and beauty standards and political scheming that House Mena never fit
into cleanly. Purple is devotion and noble spirit, the same purple from the Divine
Factionʼs aesthetic. Those are the arrows shot by people who think theyʼre above
the Menas. The blue arrow is something else. It comes from above, straight down.
Blue is loyalty. That arrow is the one the Menas never saw coming. The betrayal
by someone they trusted. The Cidet that gave them their title but couldnʼt protect
Fransei. The crown that let a fourteen-year-old girl hang for a war she started to
save her family. The blue arrow is the one that should have killed them. It still
missed.
The dark charcoal black field is grief, constancy, and the mountain itself. Mena
means “Mountain” and this family lives on top of one, literally, in the Town of Paler
in Northern Aicruae. Black is the color of something that absorbs everything.
Every blow, every humiliation, every generation of being called beasts and
monsters and ugly. The black field swallows all of it. The giraffe stands gold
against it because House Mena has always been the brightest, strangest thing in
the room, and the darkness around them has never been able to put that light out.
The golden color of the giraffe is wealth and divine favor. The Cidet paid House
Mena for the reconstruction work, and that payment became their original fortune.
Gold is also the color of the Rillic faith, where believers hold that they exist to fuel
the godsʼ strength and give them a tether to the physical world. The giraffe is gold
because the Menas believe they were built by the gods for a reason. Not to be
pretty. Not to be liked. To be strong. And to last.
House Colors: Black and Gold. Black for the mountain, for grief, for the ability to
absorb everything thrown at them. Gold for divine favor, for the wealth they
earned by building sacred spaces, and for the belief that strength is its own kind
of beauty.
Motto: “The Weak Shall Fall to the Strong.” The most brutal motto in Aicruae, and
the most honest. House Mena doesnʼt dress its philosophy up in metaphor or
softening language. If youʼre weak, you fall. If youʼre strong, you stand. Thatʼs it.
Phiyano was strong. They laughed at his face and he built them a Hall of Heroes.
Sirrah wasnʼt strong enough to survive what her husband did to her, and she fell.
Fransei was the strongest person in the kingdom at fourteen years old, strong
House Mena
4
enough to trigger a war and save her familyʼs position, and they hanged her for it.
She fell too. But the house stood. The motto doesnʼt promise survival for
individuals. It promises survival for the family. If youʼre strong enough, the name
continues. If youʼre not, the name finds someone who is.
The really ugly truth of the motto is that House Mena applies it to themselves as
much as anyone else. Sirrah fell because the beast in her blood made her a target
and she couldnʼt escape. Fransei fell because she was fourteen and the world
doesnʼt care how smart you are at fourteen. The Menas in Crandonaʼs Era fell
because they refused to bend to Merigen Bleelack, and he killed them for it. “The
Weak Shall Fall to the Strong” isnʼt a threat pointed outward. Itʼs a mirror. The
giraffe on the crest is standing because itʼs the one that didnʼt fall. Not yet.
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Architectural and religious prestige. House Mena earned their noble title through
the reconstruction of the Cidet, and that relationship granted them exclusive
passage to the Cidet whenever they pleased (normally the Cidet must invite you).
Their wealth originally came from the Cidet reconstruction payment, though it was
reduced after War of Fera reparations.
Military Forces
5,000 soldiers on stand-by.
Lands & Income
Seat: Atop a mountain in the Town of Paler, Aicruae Solisʼs Era).
Key industries: TBD
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
TBD
Rival Houses
House Mena
5
TBD
Relationship with the Crown
Tense, due to the War of Fera.
Relationship with House Dajanyi
Tense. Tension remains over War of Fera events. Hilatoma Dajanyi executed
Fransei Mena.
Marriage Alliances
House Patton Royal Marriage): Duke Nayiler Mena married Princess Aliedea
Cawiloan Patton, daughter of King Haliour Layern Patton I and Queen Walica
Kevena Patton.
Connection to House Najil: Distant relatives. Lady Vaseiula Mena married Ser
Winsafantero Paneta. Their son Zacareneal Paneta 8,707 BR  8,705 BR) was the
father of Asa Najil/Asa Panetta, the founder of House Najil.
House Culture
Religion
Rillic (sub-religion). Believers hold that they were put on this planet to fuel the
godsʼ strength and give them a stronger tether to the physical/mortal world.
Traditions

How Others Perceive Them
TBD
House Mena
6
History
Founding (8,736 BR)
Phiyano Mena, born in a rural village in Northern Aicruae in the town that would
become Paler, earned his noble title after completing the reconstruction of the
Cidet. His renovations to the Cidet and his aid constructing the Heroʼs Hall earned
him the title. Notably, his title was granted by the Cidet itself, not the Imperial
Palace. As part of this relationship, House Mena was granted exclusive passage to
the Cidet whenever they liked, a privilege normally reserved only for those the
Cidet formally invites.
Rise to Power
TBD
Major Achievements
Construction of the Hall of Heroes for the Castle of Aicruae.
Reconstruction of the Room of Glory in the Cidet, incorporating religious relics and
creating some of the greatest architectural works the world has ever seen.
Granted exclusive passage to the Cidet whenever they liked.
Major Disgraces
The War of Fera. Fransei Mena led the scheming that triggered the war and was
executed by hanging at age 14 by Hilatoma Dajanyi. However, because Fransei
had worked to make House Mena so essential to the kingdom before the war, the
house itself could not be directly harmed. Fransei took the punishment alone while
her family survived.
Notable Creations
TBD
The Mena Beast Trait
A defining and unusual feature of the early house. Phiyano Mena had a “hideous
appearance” that contrasted Aicruaean beauty standards, earning him the
nickname “Sand Face” because people believed his face moved in every direction
House Mena
7
like sand in a desert. Rumors claimed his father Huiarge had intercourse with a
horse (most likely false, but used to explain his appearance). His granddaughter
Sirrah and great-grandson Nabeyano were the last known members to display
traits of the beast. Sirrahʼs husband Mauzepe conducted research and
experiments to cure her physical traits, but the experiments ended with Sirrahʼs
death. Bartyei Mena, Sirrahʼs son, is credited as the reason House Mena no longer
resembles a beast. The family started gaining popularity for their attractive looks
beginning with him.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs origins through the generations.
Phiyano Mena (8,758 BR - 8,700 BR)
Founder of House Mena
Born in a rural village in Northern Aicruae, in the town that would become Paler.
His upbringing was strange due to rumors surrounding his birth. Some claimed his
father Huiarge had intercourse with a horse, a story most likely false but used to
explain his hideous appearance, which contrasted sharply with Aicruaean beauty
standards. Nicknamed “Sand Face” because people believed his face moved in
every direction like sand in a desert.
Despite these rumors, Phiyano was an accomplished warrior and scholar,
considered one of Aicruaeʼs brightest minds. His renovations to the Cidet and his
aid constructing the Heroʼs Hall earned him a noble title, founding House Mena in
8,736 BR. His title was granted by the Cidet, not the Imperial Palace.
Duke Nayiler Mena (8,747 BR - 8,679 BR)
Royal Marriage Alliance
Husband of Princess Aliedea Cawiloan Patton, daughter of King Haliour Layern
Patton I and Queen Walica Kevena Patton. Nayiler was given the temporary title of
Duke specifically so he could marry the princess. Father of twin daughters Lady
Naern Mena and Lady Vaseiula Mena.
Vamedeus Der Mena (8,732 BR - 8,698 BR)
House Mena
8
House Champion
Phiyanoʼs prized nephew and half-cousin/first husband of Sirrah Mena. Set to
become the next head of House Mena, but died during a tragic hunting incident at
age 34. He left behind two sons, Bartyei and Nabeyano, and a grieving wife.
Before his death, he requested to sing to his wife. In Aicruae, singing is held in a
romantic and loving light. It is an indication of love because it is believed to have
started life itself. His wife Sirrah grieved for a decade before remarrying multiple
times.
Lady Naern Mena (8,716 BR - 8,660 BR)
Twin Daughter of Princess Aliedea and Duke Nayiler Mena
Married Count Jinegi Liazen. Their daughter, Lady Isalian Liazen, became Queen
Isalian Liazen, wife of King Haliour Layern Patton II.
Lady Vaseiula Mena (8,716 BR - 8,692 BR)
Twin Daughter of Princess Aliedea and Duke Nayiler Mena
Married Ser Winsafantero Paneta. Their son Zacareneal Paneta 8,707 BR  8,705
BR) was the father of Asa Najil/Asa Panetta, founder of House Najil.
Sirrah Mena
Second Daughter and Heir of Phiyano Mena | Wife of Vamedeus Der Mena
One of the last known members to display traits of the beast. Had nine husbands
over her lifetime. Her first husband was Vamedeus Der Mena, her half-cousin. One
of her later husbands, Mauzepe, carried out research and experiments to cure her
physical traits. The experiments ended with Sirrahʼs death, leaving House Mena in
mourning.
Bartyei Mena (8,703 BR - 8,625 BR)
Older Son of Vamedeus and Sirrah | Father of Fransei
The reason House Mena no longer resembles a beast. Starting with Bartyei, the
family began gaining popularity for their attractive looks. But despite his
appearance, Bartyei was “extremely dumb (only good for swinging a sword)” and
caused House Mena to fall into turmoil. His inability to run the Mena territory
House Mena
9
caused a shockwave in high society for decades, so severe that his fourteenyear-old child was the only one who could fix it, at the cost of her own life.
Nabeyano Mena
Son of Vamedeus and Sirrah
One of the last known members to display traits of the beast.
Inarala Mena (8,672 BR - 8,597 BR)
“The Little Beast of Mena”
First great-granddaughter of Phiyano Mena, born to his eldest daughterʼs line. The
first woman in Aicruaeʼs history to receive the name “Gafer,” a term for a woman
who doesnʼt marry, essentially a shrew. Known for her nasty temper, which scared
men, earning her the additional nickname “Paer Ga” (a wicked woman with a slick
tongue).
Said to have been so rude that thousands of noblemen petitioned King Hailour
Layern Patton II to remove her tongue. The king refused and laughed them off
because his wife, Queen Isalian, was best friends with her.
Fransei Mena (8,669 BR - 8,655 BR)
The War of Fera
Born during a time of political unrest, the young Lady Fransei of Mena worked
hard to secure her familyʼs position due to her fatherʼs negligence. Despite her
age, she sought to equip her family with suitable advisors and took a large part in
the scheming that led to the War of Fera.
Executed by hanging at age 14 by Hilatoma Dajanyi, known as “Aicruaeʼs great
hero” who prevented Aicruae and Coelum from falling to the Mena family. But
because Fransei had worked to make her family so essential to the kingdom
before the war, House Mena could not be directly harmed for the familyʼs role in
the conflict. Fransei took the punishment herself while her family survived.
Despite her behavior, House Mena was not harmed. Fransei was a genius, revered
and respected even by her enemies and the king.
Hilatoma personally carried out the punishment and execution of all War of Fera
participants. Fransei and Hilatoma are often compared to each other. Fransei was
House Mena
10
a genius unparalleled in brains, so much so that even her enemies would fight her
as they would fight anyone else. She was revered and respected even by the king
despite her age for her brilliance.
Queen Yaseira Neacei Patton (7,340 BR - 7,268 BR)
Queen from House Mena
From House Mena; married King Jesuin Walica Patton. Described as “anything but
weak,” Yaseira was a skilled hunter and horsewoman who reportedly outshot her
husband at their wedding tournament. Their marriage was passionate but volatile,
full of legendary arguments and equally legendary reconciliations. She bore four
children, though only Darien (the future King Darien Lacern Patton) survived to
adulthood.
