entries.title: House Najil
entries.text:
House Najil
House Najil
“LOYAL IS THE HOUND TO THE MASTER”
Quick Facts
Status: Knight/Dame
Origin: Aicruae Western)
Founded: 8,704 BR
Founder: Asa Najil (née Paneta)
House Name Meaning: Bold, Brave and True
Seat: The Aoner, Western Aicruae (one of three towns in Western Aicruae)
Faction: Divine Faction
Spirit Animal: White Dog Hound
Colors: Violet-Purple Devotion & Noble Spirit) & Hunter Green Loyalty & Growth)
Wealth: 72,000 Rern
Military: Limited (knight family, lowest rank of nobility; members traditionally serve
as knights to the crown)
Religion: Leneyez
Theme Song: “Meet Me On The Battlefield” by SVRCINA
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Knight/Dame. The lowest rank of nobility, but wealthier than their
status would suggest thanks to the inherited Paneta fortune.
Solisʼs Era: Eradicated. After the events of the civil war, House Najil was destroyed
for conspiring with the twins to usurp the throne from Solis. They lost their noble
status and were banished from Aicruae.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Najil
1
House Najil was built on a defiant act: a bastard daughter, rejected by her own
blood, buying her way into the noble class and swearing herself as a knight to the
king. From the start, Najil was a house that had to fight for its place at the table.
They were never fully accepted by high society, never granted the kind of power
or influence that came with higher titles. And yet they persisted, married into the
right families, and even placed one of their own on the throne as queen.
Their motto says it all, and so does how they died. “Loyal is the hound to the
master.” For generations, that loyalty defined them. Then they sided with the twins
against Solis, and it destroyed them. A house born from stubbornness and
survival, wiped out by a single act of disloyalty to the very crown theyʼd sworn to
serve.
Heraldry
The Crest: The House Najil crest is divided per fess (horizontally across the
middle), with a rich violet-purple field above and a deep hunter green below. The
division between the two fields follows an undulating, hill-like line that mimics
rolling terrain. In the green lower field sits a cream-colored hound in a dignified
seated position, its posture alert and attentive, long ears hanging, gaze steady.
Surrounding the dog on both sides are oak branches bearing green leaves and
golden acorns. Two branches with acorns hang from above in the purple field, and
more acorn-laden branches frame the hound below.
Symbolism:
The cream-colored hound is the house itself. Seated. Watching. Waiting for a
command. Asa Najil, nicknamed “the Lady of the Garden,” built this house from a
bastardʼs inheritance and a purchased title, and the first thing she did was swear
herself as a knight to the king. She chose the role of the loyal servant because she
knew sheʼd never be accepted as an equal. A hound doesnʼt sit at the table. A
hound sits at the masterʼs feet and earns its place by being useful, by being
faithful, by being ready when called. That was the Najil strategy for generations.
Stay loyal. Stay useful. Stay alive.
And it worked. Silaria Najil became a champion coveted for beauty and strength.
Queen Cecea married King Sayero and connected the house directly to the royal
line. Matasen married into House Aedria and produced nine heirs. The hound kept
sitting. The hound kept being loyal. Until Solisʼs Era, when House Najil sided with
House Najil
2
the twins against the emperor and learned exactly what happens when a hound
turns on its master. They were eradicated. Stripped of their title. Banished from
Aicruae entirely.
The garden setting honors Asaʼs nickname. The hound doesnʼt sit on a battlefield
or in a throne room. It sits in a garden, surrounded by growing things, because
Asa built this house the way you build a garden. You plant it. You tend it. You wait.
The rolling green hills behind the hound look like Western Aicruae, like the territory
around the Aoner where the Najils made their home. Itʼs quiet land. Unassuming.
Just like the family that lived there.
The oak branches and golden acorns are about what small things can become. An
acorn is nothing. It fits in your hand. But given time, given the right soil, it becomes
something nobody can move. Asa was an acorn. A bastard daughter rejected by
House Paneta, inheriting half a fortune she was never supposed to touch. She
planted herself in that soil and grew into something the Paneta family never could
have predicted. Her daughter Silaria was an acorn that became a warrior legend.
Queen Cecea was an acorn that became a queen. The acorns on the crest say:
donʼt underestimate the small thing. Itʼll outgrow you.
But acorns can also rot. Nilinlo ran away to the Cidet at nine and got kicked out for
drinking. Basiol watched his wifeʼs affair like entertainment and went mad when
she died. The same family that produced champion warriors and a queen also
produced scandal after scandal. The oaks grew twisted sometimes.
The violet-purple field is devotion and noble spirit. House Najil follows Leneyez,
the faith that requires sacrifice to maintain the physical and spiritual well-being of
the gods. Devotion is the entire identity of a Leneyez believer. You give something
up. You offer your best. Thatʼs what the Najils did for centuries. They gave their
knights to the crown, gave their daughters to royal marriages, gave their loyalty
without reservation. Purple also carries a claim to nobility that House Najil always
had to fight for. They were knights. The lowest rank. But purple says they saw
themselves as something more. Asa bought the title, but she believed she
deserved it.
The hunter green field is loyalty and the natural world. Green for the garden.
Green for growth. Green for the Western Aicruaen countryside where this family
put roots down and held on for generations despite never being fully accepted by
House Najil
3
high society. The green is stubborn. Itʼs the color of something that keeps growing
whether anyone wants it to or not. That was House Najil.
House Colors: Violet-Purple and Hunter Green. Purple for devotion, noble spirit,
and the Leneyez faith that demands sacrifice. Green for loyalty, growth, and the
stubborn refusal to stop growing even when nobody thinks you belong.
Motto: “Loyal is the hound to the master.” The motto is the proudest and saddest
thing about House Najil all at once. Itʼs what Asa swore when she knelt before the
king and became a knight. Itʼs what every Najil after her lived by. Silaria won her
tournaments for the crown. Cecea married into the royal family. Dela served as a
knight to the very king whom she might have had every right to turn aganist. The
hound was loyal. Always.
And then it wasnʼt. When it counted most, when the civil war split the kingdom
between Solis and the twins, House Najil picked the wrong master. They
conspired against the throne theyʼd sworn to serve and lost everything. Their title.
Their land. Their name. The motto survived longer than the family did. Thatʼs the
tragedy of it. “Loyal is the hound to the master” is carved into a crest that belongs
to a house that no longer exists because it forgot the one thing it promised never
to forget.
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Little to no actual political influence due to their knight rank, the lowest tier of
nobility.
Internal Power Structure
Traditional patriarchal.
Military Forces
Limited. As a knight family, House Najil is not particularly powerful in terms of
military strength. However, being a family of knights, its members possess
warrior-like qualities. Najil members traditionally serve as knights to the crown.
Lands & Income
House Najil
4
Seat: The Aoner in Western Aicruae (one of three towns in Western Aicruae).
Wealth: 72,000 Rern, inherited from the Paneta fortune. While they hold the lowest
rank of nobility, they have maintained that fortune over the years.
Key industries: TBD
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Arvento, Decent relationship established through a marriage alliance
between Halcai Arvento and Alema Najil.
House Mena, Distant relatives through Asa Najilʼs fatherʼs lineage. The union of
Lady Vaseiula Mena and Ser Winsafantero Paneta produced Zacareneal Paneta,
who was Asa Najilʼs father. This gives House Najil distant royal blood connections.
House Aedria, Marriage alliance through Lady Erhen Aedria marrying Matasen
Najil, a union that blessed the house with nine heirs.

House Patton Royal Family): Queen Cecea Sanitte Patton 8,618 BR  8,545 BR)
came from House Najil and married King Sayero Walica Patton, producing Prince

connected House Najil directly to the royal line and greatly elevated the houseʼs

History
Founding (8,704 BR)
House Najil was created when Asa Paneta used her inherited wealth to buy herself
a noble title, changing her name to Asa Najil. Born as the bastard daughter of
Zacareneal Paneta, Asa was never accepted by the Paneta family, who boasted
royal blood connections. When Zacareneal died at age 26, he left half the family
fortune to Asa in his will, crippling the legitimate Paneta family. Asa used this
inheritance to purchase a noble title and swore herself as a knight to the king,
knowing she would never be fully accepted by high society.

TBD

TBD

House Najil conspired with the twins to usurp the throne from Solis. After the civil
war, the house was eradicated, losing their noble status and being banished from
Aicruae entirely.

Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs founder to its later generations.
Asa Najil (8,742 BR – 8,683 BR)
Founder of House Najil | “The Lady of the Garden”
Name meaning: New Dawn
Bastard daughter of Zacareneal Paneta, born to Zacarenealʼs mistress, Minguna.
Asa was never accepted by the noble House Paneta. When her father Zacareneal
died at age 26 without a legitimate heir, he left half the Paneta fortune to her in his
will. She used the inheritance to buy herself a noble title, because the Paneta
family would never accept a bastard. She swore herself as a knight to the king,
founding House Najil in 8,704 BR. Despite her title, she was never fully accepted
by noble society. She died at 59.
Silaria Najil (8,713 BR – 8,613 BR)
Asaʼs Only Heir
Name meaning: Bottom of the Lake
A famous warrior and champion from a young age. Silaria was also a renowned
beauty who attracted suitors from all over the world, “coveted for beauty and
strength.” She married at age 25 to a man sponsored by her mother, “breaking the
heart of noblemen across the world.” She won countless tournaments and battles
over the course of her lifetime. She died at 100.
Queen Cecea Sanitte Patton (8,618 BR – 8,545 BR)
The Royal Connection
Name meaning: Little Crow
From House Najil. Married King Sayero Walica Patton, becoming queen. Mother of
Prince Benjamin Lawerence Patton and Princess Toavaliae Javivata Patton. This
marriage connected House Najil directly to the royal line and was the most
significant elevation of the houseʼs prestige in its history. She died at 73.
Nilinlo Najil (8,572 BR – 8,546 BR)
House Najil
7
“The Scandal”
Name meaning: A Sequence of Light
Ran away to the Cidet at age 9. Ten years later, he was kicked out for drinking
liquor. Not much is known about him due to his time spent away from high society.
His story caused a major scandal for the house. He fathered only one illegitimate
heir before his death at 26.
Dela Najil (8,569 BR – 8,506 BR)
“The Crescent Moon”
Name meaning: Half of a Day
Rumored lover of Princess Toavaliae Javivata Patton. The two were often seen
quite intimate at court. Princess Toavaliae reportedly wanted to name her first son
(the crown prince) after Dela.
The love story was a tragic one. Princess Toavaliae was forced to marry her
brother, King Benjamin Lawerence Patton I, while Dela had to become a knight
loyal to serving the King, her loverʼs abuser. Dela married Ser Edesfar Kasie
despite her true love. She died at 63.
Matasen Najil (8,534 BR – 8,465 BR)
Son of Dela
Name meaning: Morning of Spring
Born to conflicting parrents,Dela Najil and Ser Edesfar Kasie. His childhood was an
unhappy one; his parents lived apart, constantly bouncing him between them. He
grew up meek and socially awkward. “Women would run away from him
screaming and men would poke at his weak nature.” He struggled to find a wife
well into his thirties, a social anomaly for a nobleman of that era.
Eventually he married Lady Erhen Aedria, who fell in love with him. Their union
blessed House Najil with nine heirs. He died at 69.
Basiol Najil (8,498 BR – 8,439 BR)
Son of Matasen
Name meaning: Rising Tree
House Najil
8
First child and son of Matasen Najil and Lady Erhen Aedria. Despite growing up in
a household where his parents genuinely loved each other, Basiol developed a
twisted understanding of love. He was a voyeuristic and controlling husband. He
secretly watched his wifeʼs affair, only intervening when they planned to run away
together. “He thought he owned his wife and that his wife was simply a tool for
him.”
He wanted his wife to have nine children, like his mother, but she died after four.
After her death, he refused to eat or drink and had delusions that she was still
alive. He died at 59.

Why They Matter
House Ochanan belongs to Coelumʼs Land Faction, a group that believes the land
is the very foundation of their culture and must be protected at all costs. The Land
House Ochanan
1
Faction has a strong sense of tradition and is not open to change. They prioritize
agriculture and the cultivation of the land.
TBD Further significance to be developed.]
Heraldry
Crest: The crest of House Ochanan is quartered into four distinct sections, each
representing a different aspect of the land they hold sacred. The upper left quarter
features a warm rust-red field crossed by horizontal yellow stripes, suggesting
cultivated earth and harvest rows or the stratified layers of geological time. The
upper right presents a radiant golden sun against a pale yellow field, symbolizing
the life-giving energy that makes all agriculture possible. The lower left is
rendered in cool white with soft blue accents, evoking winter landscapes, snowcovered fields, and the dormant seasons during which the land rests and renews.
The lower right displays horizontal stripes of grey-blue suggesting water,
irrigation, and the rivers and rains that sustain the fertile territories of Coelum.
Straddling all four sections, a large grey wolf stands in profile at the center of the
shield, its body positioned across the dividing lines as if claiming dominion over
every element of the natural world. The wolf, rendered in rich brown tones with its
mouth open and tail curved, embodies loyalty, family bonds, and the protective
instincts of the pack.
Symbolism: The wolfʼs placement across all four quadrants unifies the disparate
elements (land, sun, snow, and water), embodying the houseʼs belief that “The
Land is the blood of our people.” Just as the wolf is bound to its territory, so too
are the Ochanans inseparably connected to their soil, tradition, and the primal
strength of the pack that protects it.
Motto: “The Land is the blood of our people.”

entries.text:
House Orana
House Orana
“THE BLOOD OF THE FALLEN, TRUE AND STRONG”
Quick Facts
Status: High Kings / Masters of the Tower
Name Meaning: TBD
Origin: Vikitsv
Founded: TBD
Founder: TBD House descended from Vernaʼs eldest son Liaerto I
Seat: Vikitsv The Magic Tower)
Faction: Nationalist Party
Spirit Animal: Black Bear
Colors: Silver Nobility, Truth), Azure/Blue Unwavering Loyalty), Black Power,
Sacrifice), White Purity
Wealth: TBD
Military: TBD
Religion: Monotheistic worship of Iswan, goddess of alchemy. Respect for
Nellebrie who created Mount Aicren.
Theme Song: TBD
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: High Kings and Masters of the Tower. The ruling house of Vikitsv
and the most powerful line of magic users in existence. House Orana governs
through the Council of Scholars and commands the Magic Tower, the single most
important institution in the country.
Solisʼs Era: Destroyed. After Grand Sorcerer Sevtorʼs magical attack on Valea killed
15,000 people during Year Five of the civil war, Solis retaliated by having Liacaion
poured into House Oranaʼs chambers and setting them ablaze. Nearly every
member of the house burned to death. Only Mekean Orana escaped, dyeing her
hair and settling in Equateiy to continue the bloodline.
House Orana
1
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD Note: Mekean Oranaʼs descendants eventually produce
Merigen Bleelack.)
Why They Matter
House Orana is the reason Vikitsv matters at all. They are the Magic Tower, and
the Magic Tower is the state. Without them, the country is just a frozen mountain
with blue-haired people and no arable land.
Their power comes from blood. Not politics, not military alliances, not money.
Blood. House Orana descends directly from Vernaʼs eldest son Liaerto I, and Verna
personally had Liaerto drink his blood, making the Orana line the purest and most
powerful magical bloodline currently in existence. That distinction puts them in a
category no other noble house can touch.
But that power painted a target on them. When Grand Sorcerer Sevtor entered the
Aicruan Civil War on Orcusʼs side and leveled Valea, killing 15,000 people in a
single magical strike, Solis didnʼt just retaliate against Sevtor. He burned the entire
house alive. The most devastating single act of magic in the civil war era was
answered with the complete destruction of the family that made it possible.
House Orana also guards a dangerous secret: they likely know of the Ilkai herbʼs
existence on Mount Aicren. Within Vikitsvʼs scholarly circles, even the knowledge
of Ilkai is considered forbidden.
Heraldry
Crest: A fearsome black bear rampant upon a diagonal azure band that cuts
across a silver field, all framed within an ornate blue border adorned with white
fleur-de-lis. The bear stands upright in a posture of supreme authority, its claws
extended as if reaching for the crown symbol positioned above. A clear
representation of their position as High Kings and Masters of the Tower.
Symbolism: The black bear, powerful and protective yet capable of terrible
ferocity, represents both the sacrifices made to maintain their rule and the
unyielding strength required to hold the highest seat of power. The bear also
embodies their motto, “The Blood of the fallen, true and strong.” The diagonal
House Orana
2
band suggests the path of ascension. Silver and blue represent nobility, truth, and
unwavering loyalty to the realm.
Motto: “The Blood of the Fallen, True and Strong.”
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Magic. Pure, unmatched, bloodline magic. House Orana is a direct pure breed line
of Verna descent through his eldest son Liaerto I. Verna personally had Liaerto I
drink his blood, which makes the Orana line the most powerful magic users
currently in existence. The Magic Tower, which holds all of Vikitsvʼs power, is their
seat of authority.
Internal Power Structure
Vikitsv operates as a magocracy/meritocracy. House Orana rules through the
Council of Scholars, and the Grand Sorcerer (head of House Orana) leads the
Magic Tower. The Magic Tower can train roughly 400 wizards at a time.
Military Forces
TBD Note: Vikitsvʼs primary defense is geographic. The mountain location
makes invasion impractical, and the three-month journey up Mount Aicren has
killed many who attempted it. The Magic Tower itself functions as a military asset,
as demonstrated by Sevtorʼs attack on Valea.)
Lands & Income
Seat: The Magic Tower, located on the right side of Mount Aicren, below the
capital city of Berlailia.
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
TBD
Faction Allies: As members of the Nationalist Party, House Orana shares political
alignment with House Renililas, House Yailk, House Qari, and other noble houses
House Orana
3
who believe Vikitsv is superior to other nations and must protect its interests at all
costs.
International Alliances
Equateiy Strategic Ally): Both secular, both opposed to the traditional religious
bloc. Allied together backing Orcus during the Aicruan Civil War.
Rival Houses
TBD
International Rivals
Gherci Ideological Opposition): Vikitsvʼs focus on magic directly opposes Gherciʼs
religious orthodoxy. At international gatherings, Vikitsv sided with Equateiyʼs
proposals, favoring scientific and less theocratic policies.
House Culture
Religion
Monotheistic worship of Iswan, goddess of alchemy. Respect for Nellebrie who
created Mount Aicren. House Orana and the Magic Tower likely know of the Ilkai
herbʼs existence on Mount Aicren but guard this knowledge carefully. Even within
Vikitsvʼs scholarly circles, knowledge of Ilkai is considered forbidden.
Traditions
TBD
Values
TBD
Reputation
TBD
History
House Orana
4
Founding
TBD Note: House Orana was founded by descendants of Vernaʼs eldest son
Liaerto I, who Verna personally had drink his blood. The Magic Tower was created
in 7,749 BR.)
Rise to Power
TBD Note: Their pure Verna bloodline and command of the Magic Tower made
them the natural rulers of Vikitsv under a magocracy/meritocracy system.)
The Aicruan Civil War
House Orana backed Orcusʼs rebel side to prevent the Solisian empire from
threatening magical autonomy. Grand Sorcerer Sevtor, a direct descendant of
Liaerto I and head of House Orana, personally traveled to Aicruae during Year Five
of the civil war with Duke Reasaec Kivier of Equateiy. Sevtorʼs purpose was
twofold: to support Orcus and to avenge Iris, who had been betrothed to his
second son Cequailian.
Sevtor launched a devastating magical attack on Valea, killing 15,000 people. It
was the single most destructive use of magic in the civil war era and
demonstrated what organized, well-resourced magic users could accomplish
when deployed as military weapons.
Destruction of House Orana
After the Valea attack, Solis, Jaifey Yuera, and Mihel Kulio kidnapped Maeret
Orana, Sevtorʼs third son. Despite Maeretʼs repeated pleas for mercy, explaining
he had no control over his fatherʼs actions, Solis permitted experiments on him.
They discovered that fire is deadly to magic users because their bodies, which
rely on cold, cannot handle high temperatures. This weakness is specific to magic
users of Vernaʼs bloodline, whose magic is tied to Vikitsvʼs freezing climate atop
Mount Aicren.
Solis used this discovery to destroy House Orana. He sent a spy to infiltrate their
castle, pour Liacaion into their chambers, and set the fire. All members of House
Orana burned to death. The screams echoed throughout Aicruae that night. Only
Mekean Orana escaped by dyeing her hair and settling in Equateiy, continuing the
family line that eventually leads to Merigen Bleelack.
House Orana
5
The destruction of House Orana effectively decapitated the Magic Towerʼs
leadership and triggered Solisʼs broader persecution of magic users across the
empire. Vikitsvʼs open opposition led to forcible integration, and imperial armies
eventually purged Vikitsvʼs nationalist core.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically by known dates. Members without dates are listed by their
appearance in the narrative timeline.
Grand Sorcerer Sevtor ([TBD] - 7,217 BR)
Grand Sorcerer of the Magic Tower | Head of House Orana
Direct descendant of Vernaʼs eldest son Liaerto I, making him part of the purest
and most powerful magic bloodline in existence. Sevtor led the Magic Tower and
ruled Vikitsv. During Year Five of the Aicruan Civil War, he traveled to Aicruae with
Duke Reasaec Kivier of Equateiy to personally support Orcus and avenge Iris, who
was betrothed to his second son Cequailian. He launched a magical attack on
Valea that killed 15,000 people, the most devastating single act of the war. Solis
retaliated by having Liacaion poured into House Oranaʼs chambers and setting
them ablaze. Sevtor burned alive with nearly all of his house.
Cequailian Orana
Second Son of Grand Sorcerer Sevtor
Betrothed to Princess Iris Aleka Patton. Further details TBD
Maeret Orana ([TBD] - 7,217 BR)
Third Son of Grand Sorcerer Sevtor
After Sevtorʼs devastating attack on Valea, Solisʼs forces kidnapped Maeret and
experimented on him to discover the weakness of magic users. Despite his
repeated pleas for mercy and insistence that he had no control over his fatherʼs
actions, Solis ignored him and permitted further experiments. They discovered
that fire is deadly to magic users because their cold-dependent bodies cannot
handle high temperatures. Maeret was killed along with most of House Orana
when Solis had their chambers set ablaze.
House Orana
6
Mekean Orana
Sole Survivor of House Oranaʼs Destruction
When Solis had her entire family burned alive in their chambers, Mekean escaped
by dyeing her hair and settling in Equateiy. She continued the Orana bloodline in
exile. Her descendants eventually include Merigen Bleelack, who becomes
significant in later eras.
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
The most powerful magical bloodline in existence (direct Verna descent through
Liaerto I, command of the Magic Tower, monopoly on magical exports that makes
Vikitsv the second most influential country globally, geographic nearimpregnability Mount Aicrenʼs three-month journey and freezing climate),
exclusive knowledge of Ilkaiʼs existence.
What They Lack
TBD
Vulnerabilities
Fire. Magic users of Vernaʼs bloodline rely on cold, and their bodies cannot handle
high temperatures. This weakness, discovered through Solisʼs experiments on
Maeret Orana, was ultimately used to destroy the entire house. Their geographic
isolation, while protective, also means limited agricultural resources and heavy
reliance on food imports.
Role in Narrative
Book Appearances: Book 1 A Tale of a Thousand Songs), primarily through Grand
Sorcerer Sevtorʼs involvement in the civil war Chapters 5557.
Plot Significance: House Oranaʼs entry into the Aicruan Civil War marks the point
where the conflict escalates from a domestic succession dispute to an
international crisis. Sevtorʼs attack on Valea is the single most destructive act of
the war, and Solisʼs retaliation against House Orana (burning them alive,
House Orana
7
experimenting on Maeret) marks his transformation from justified avenger to war
criminal. Mekean Oranaʼs survival in exile ensures the bloodlineʼs continuation into
later eras through Merigen Bleelack.
Key Members in Story: Grand Sorcerer Sevtor (minor antagonist), Cequailian
Orana (betrothed to Iris), Maeret Orana (victim of Solisʼs experiments), Mekean
Orana (survivor, ancestor of Merigen Bleelack).

entries.title: House Patton
entries.text:
House Patton
House Patton
“ABOVE HUMAN, BELOW GOD”
Quick Facts
Status: Royal Family of Aicruae / Imperial Family of the Solisian Empire
Origin: Aicruae
House Name Meaning: Victorious Winner
Founded: 8,759 BR
Founder: King Haliour Layern Patton I
Active Years:
Seat: Lajazer, Capital City of Aicruae (atop a mountain-like cliff)
Faction: Divine Faction
Spirit Animal: Panther
Colors: Blue Loyalty & Strength) & Black Constancy & Grief)
Wealth:  Rern Pre-Empire)
Military: 200,000 soldiers First Army & Second Army) ranked #2 in Aicruae
Religion: Leneyez
Theme Song: “Legendary” by Welshly Arms
כה
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Royal Family of Aicruae. The unbroken dynasty that founded and
ruled the kingdom for nearly two millennia, from King Haliour Iʼs coronation in
8,759 BR through the reign of King Benjamin Lawerence Patton II.
Solisʼs Era: Imperial Family. After winning the civil war against his half-siblings Iris
and Orcus, Emperor Solis Elias Patton unified Aicruae, Gherci, Coelum, Pireaynea,
Equateiy, and Vikistv into the Solisian Empire. House Patton went from ruling one
kingdom to ruling the known world.
∼300,000
House Patton
1
Crandonaʼs Era: Imperial Family. Still the ruling dynasty, though the empireʼs
internal tensions are building toward the birth of Goteivati III and the coming Dark
Ages.
Minaraʼs Era: Imperial Family in name. Emperor Veo Olem Patton sits the throne,
but is effectively controlled by Empress Macenja, who is actually the infiltrator
Vandrea in disguise.
Nicknames People Call Them During This Era
“The First House”
“The Clan Killers”
“The Wolves of the Mountain”
“The Blood of Razar”
“Lords of the Six Clans” (referencing the clans Haliour I united)
“The High Seat”
“The Old Blood”
“The Cliff Kings” ( Lajazer sits on a sheer mountain. Impregnable. Intimidating.)
Why They Matter
House Patton is the spine of the entire series. They founded Aicruae, ruled it for
nearly two thousand years, conquered the world under Solis, and then slowly
rotted from the inside out. The question that runs through all four books is whether
the Patton bloodline deserves its power and what it costs to hold it.
Theyʼve produced the greatest rulers in history and the absolute worst. The same
house that gave the world Emperor Solis also gave it Goteivati the Damned, who
murdered his wife and children and created a culture that worshipped male
dominance. The same family that built Lajazer on an impregnable cliff spent
generations tearing itself apart from within.
Everyone bows to House Patton. Not from love from obligation and power. That
distinction matters, and itʼs the crack in the foundation that every enemy
eventually tries to exploit.
Heraldry
House Patton
2
Crest: Per bend sable and azure (diagonally divided, black above and blue below),
charged in chief with a golden key and a golden labyrinthine knot. Two sable
panthers rampant combatant, each crowned with a golden coronet. In base, a
golden eight-pointed star.
Symbolism:
The black field represents constancy and the grief that comes with ruling
The blue stands for loyalty and strength
The diagonal division symbolizes the boundary between burden and duty
The golden key represents the unlocking of divine destiny / access to power /
guardianship of the realm.
The labyrinthine knot represents, the complexity of rule.
The paired crowned panthers reflect the prophetic dream of King Haliour Layern
Patton I-he saw two panthers fighting on a cliff, surrounded by fire, bleeding gold.
When the fight ended, the sun overtook the sky. Their crowns mark their royal
nature.
The golden star represents the sun that overtook the sky in the Kingʼs dream,
symbolizing the golden dawn of House Pattonʼs rule
Motto: “Above Human, Below God.” The house stands above mortal concerns yet
beneath divine authority.
Power & Influence
Source of Power
The Crown of Aicruae and later the Solisian Empire. Divine right ideology. Nearly
two millennia of unbroken rule. Every other noble house must bow to them thatʼs
not just some custom, thatʼs law.
Internal Power Structure
House Patton is the royal family, so its power structure follows the traditional line
of succession: King/Queen, then heirs Princes and Princesses), then extended
members of the royal family. Unlike other houses where strength or cunning can
____
House Patton
3
elevate a member, House Pattonʼs hierarchy is rigid and formal, which is precisely
why succession crises hit them so hard.
Military Forces
Ranked #2 in Aicruae for military strength (second only to House Vika), House
Patton commands two exclusive military organizations:
The First Army, soldiers loyal to the crown.
The Second Army, soldiers loyal to the heirs.
Combined: 200,000 soldiers. After Solisʼs conquest and the eradication of House
Vika, House Patton absorbs or disbands Vikaʼs 310,000-strong military, making the
imperial army unchallenged.
Lands & Income
Seat: The capital city of Lajazer, built atop a mountain-like cliff, a virtually
impregnable location chosen by Haliour I after his prophetic dream.
As the royal family, House Patton holds ultimate authority over all of Aicruae. After
Solisʼs conquest: the entire Solisian Empire (six unified kingdoms). Key industries
include royal taxation, crown lands, tribute from vassal houses, and the
agricultural wealth of Aicruae itself, a flourishing farming country that ensures
consistent income.
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Arvento Duke/Duchess): The crownʼs most trusted ally. This alliance dates
back to the friendship between King Haliour I and Lenkitta Arvento at the founding
of Aicruae. A neutral house, extremely loyal, serving as trusted advisors and
scholars to the throne across generations.
House Vika Duke/Duchess): Marriage alliance through Mihai Julie Vika, who
married King Benjamin Lawerence Patton II. House Vika was the crownʼs strongest
military ally and its most dangerous one. King Darien Lacern Patton arranged this
marriage specifically because Vikaʼs power had grown to rival the royal familyʼs.
The alliance ended catastrophically when the Vika-blooded twins Iris and Orcus
launched their civil war against Solis.
House Patton
4
House Hige Baron/Baroness): Connected to the crown through Lady Emillea Hige,
concubine of King Benjamin Lawerence Patton II and mother of Emperor Solis. A
minor house elevated by proximity to the king, though never truly respected by the
other noble families.
House Kulio Count/Countess): Allied through marriage, Esterica Kulio becomes
Solisʼs first empress.
House Najil: Divine Faction ally. Connected through the marriage of Queen Cecea
Sanitte House Najil) to King Sayero Walica Patton.
House Caraen: Protects the capital city of Lajazer. Founded by Milane Caraen,
who was granted nobility by King Haliour Layern Patton II. Deeply loyal, they
provide personal knights to the royal family.
Rival Houses
Houses of the Common People Faction, House Leva, House Dajanyi, and House
Yurea, are ideologically opposed to the monarchy and the noble class system.
Marriage Alliances
House Vika, House Hige, House Kulio, House Yurea, House Najil, House Liazen,
and House Mena.
House Culture
Religion
Leneyez, a sub-religion of the Circle of Eternal Light. Leneyez followers believe in
sacrificing both people and farm life to both sets of gods during monthly prayers
and festivals. Adherents believe these sacrifices maintain the physical and
spiritual well-being of the gods. House Patton also has a special connection to the
god Razar, who appeared to King Haliour I in the vision that set him on his path to
kingship.
Traditions
House Pattonʼs coronation rites unfold over two days, each element tracing back
to King Haliour Iʼs founding vision.
House Patton
5
The Climb, On the morning of coronation, the heir ascends the final stretch to
Lajazer on foot while the court watches from the cliffs above. Multiple paths exist,
ranging from gentle slopes to near-vertical rock faces. The route the heir chooses
is noted and remembered. Those who take harder paths earn respect; those who
choose easy routes invite whispers that follow them throughout their reign. The
ritual reenacts Haliourʼs rise from bastard orphan to king a reminder that Patton
rulers must earn their throne, not simply inherit it.
The Anointing. During the formal ceremony, sacred oil mixed with gold dust is
applied to the new monarchʼs forehead by the highest-ranking priest of Razar. The
gold echoes Haliourʼs dream, where the panthers bled gold and the world turned
golden at dawn.
Day of Golden Light. The day after coronation, two panthers are brought before
the assembled court. Their behavior is read as an omen for the coming reign.
Calm panthers signal stability; aggression warns of conflict ahead. At King Viake
Recreadion Pattonʼs coronation, one panther leapt into the crowd of nobles and
mauled a manʼs face. People dismissed it as an accident. After the Massacre of
Light, they remembered.
Values
Sacred duty of rule. Hierarchy and ceremony. Divine mandate. Family legacy
though that legacy is often complicated by internal conflict. Loyalty and strength.
Reputation
Ambition hidden beneath polite piety. Everyone must bow to them, not from love
but from obligation and power. House Patton has produced both the greatest and
worst rulers in history, and the other noble houses know it. The Pattons are
respected, feared, obeyed but rarely loved.
History
Founding ( 8,759 BR
King Haliour Layern Patton I was a bastard born to a man sworn to the gods and a
commoner woman. Abandoned at birth and orphaned at twelve, he joined a
mercenary group at fourteen. At twenty-two, the god Razar appeared to him in a
House Patton
6
vision, showing him his fate as a poor man. When Haliour asked how to change it,
Razar told him to become king.
So he did. Haliour killed his mercenary leader, united the clans, defeated the
warlord Dures, and married Duresʼs daughter Walica. He founded Aicruae at age
thirty and established House Patton two weeks later. Guided by his prophetic
dream of the two panthers, two beasts fighting on a cliff, surrounded by fire,
bleeding gold, until the sun swallowed the sky he built the capital Lajazer atop a
mountain cliff, a virtually impregnable location symbolizing the Pattonsʼ authority.
Then he destroyed all records of life in Aicruae before his dynasty.
Rise to Power
House Patton rose through military conquest during the Warriorsʼ Age. King
Haliour Iʼs alliance with Lenkitta Arvento secured internal stability, while marriage
alliances with Houses Vika and Hige consolidated power. The houseʼs unbroken
dynasty lasted nearly two millennia from the founding of Aicruae in 8,759 BR
through the reign of King Benjamin II until Solis expanded the kingdom into an
empire encompassing all six nations.
Champions of the Warriorsʼ Age. Survived Bloody Winter ( 8,259 BR, the first
successful coup against the royal family. Withstood the Siege of Highwater ( 7,463
BR, a major peasant uprising. And under Emperor Solis, unified all six kingdoms
Aicruae, Gherci, Coelum, Pireaynea, Equateiy, and Vikistv into the Solisian Empire.
Major Disgraces
The Massacre of Light ( 8,558 BR King Viake Recreadion Patton and his queen
slaughtered 90,000 followers of the Order of the Pure Ones, devastating the Pure
Onesʼ presence in Aicruae.
The Aicruan Civil War  : The royal family torn apart. The
twins Iris and Orcus seized power from their half-brother Solis after their father
King Benjamin IIʼs death, publicly poisoning Lady Emillea Hige while nine-year-old
Solis watched. Five years of devastating war followed.
Emperor Goteivati III “The Damned” 0 AR Ushered in the Dark Ages. Murdered
his wife and children. Renounced Matsiali culture and created Pataouit, an
(7,221−7,217BR)
House Patton
7
oppressive ideology that worshipped male dominance and stripped women of all
authority.
Key Events Timeline
Founding of Aicruae ( 8,759 BR - House Patton creates the nation.
The Massacre of Light 8,558 BR - King Viake slaughters 90,000 Pure Ones
followers.
Bloody Winter 8,259 BR — First successful coup against the royal family; over
3,000 dead.
Siege of Highwater 7,463 BR - Peasant uprising inspired by Bloody Winter.
Aicruan Civil War 7,2217,217 BR - Solis defeats siblings Iris and Orcus.
Conquest of the Six Kingdoms 7,2167,163 BR - Solis creates the unified Solisian
Empire.
Birth of Goteivati III 0 AR - Beginning of the Dark Ages.

When the king died four months later, the twins staged their coup. Emillea was

while nine-year-old Solis watched from under a floorboard. Her execution became

Emperor Maen Patton (7,217 BR - 7,140 BR )
Name Meaning: Firstborn Son, Wolf of Heart.
Title: Second Emperor of the Solisian Empire
Parents: Emperor Solis Elias Patton + Empress Esterica Kulio
Spouses: Empress Saiye Patton (first wife), Empress Tenami Patton (second wife),
Empress Kesdeivoa Patton (third wife)
Children: None
Born during Civil War Year Five while his parents fought to survive, Maen spent his
earliest years in hiding, passed between loyalist households while battles raged
across Aicruae. He was young when his father finally claimed the throne and five
when his mother died from Harnuaʼs poison. These first years marked him
House Patton
13
permanently he learned that the world was violent, that power was survival, and
that love was a vulnerability enemies would exploit. He inherited the throne at
fifty-four when his father finally died at eighty-seven, and his first act was to
rename his fatherʼs empire. . Maen ruled in his fatherʼs shadow for twenty-three
years and never escaped it.The defining tragedy of his reign was his inability to
produce an heir. His first wife Saiye gave him fifteen years of marriage and three
stillbirths before she died in childbed with a fourth. Tenami, his second wife, was
barren from the start or he was, though no one dared suggest it. Kesdeivoa,
chosen for her youth and her familyʼs renowned fertility, produced nothing in eight
years of marriage. The court whispered that he was cursed. That the gods had
looked at what Solis built through blood and decided the line would end.Maen
responded to failure the way he responded to everything: with cold fury and
calculated cruelty. Physicians who could not explain his wivesʼ barrenness
disappeared. Courtiers who whispered too loudly about succession found
themselves reassigned to distant provinces. He punished disloyalty with a
precision his father would have recognized, but where Solis had been brutal in
pursuit of an empire, Maen was brutal in pursuit of control over a court that pitied
him.He never forgave his father for dying. Not really. Solis had been the center of
Maenʼs universe the conqueror, the legend, the man who built an empire from the
ashes of civil war. When Solis died, Maen discovered that he had spent fifty-four
years preparing to be his fatherʼs heir and no time at all preparing to be his own
man. The empire he inherited was stable, prosperous, and fundamentally Solisʼs
creation. Every decision Maen made was measured against what his father would
have done. Every success was credited to Solisʼs foundation. Every failure was
Maenʼs alone.He grew harder with age. The ambitious young
prince who had once dreamed of expanding his fatherʼs conquests became a
suspicious old emperor who trusted no one and loved nothing. When he died at
seventy-seven, childless and largely unmourned, the throne passed to his sister
Coyreʼs eldest son a nephew he had barely acknowledged.The Solisian Empire
endured. The Patton dynasty endured. Maen did not.
Princess Coyre Patton
7,214 BR - 7,118 BR
Name Meaning: Heartʼs Joy
House Patton
14
Titles: Princess of the Solisian Empire; Duchess of the Anbai Lands Gift from Solis
for being his firstborn daughter)
Parents: Emperor Solis Elias Patton + Empress Esterica Kulio
Spouse: Duke Shaniser Dajanyi
Children: Emperor Elleinaj Patton I
Coyre was born approximately six months before her motherʼs death and never
knew her. Esterica Kulio the empress who had survived the civil war, who had built
libraries and reformed agriculture, who was called “the Mother of a Dynasty”
existed for Coyre only as a portrait on a wall and a name spoken with reverence by
people who had actually known her. She grew up watching her father mourn a
ghost and her brother Maen harden into something cold and ambitious. She
learned early that being Estericaʼs daughter meant being measured against an
impossible standard.
When her father married Tixsei Yurea, Coyre was four years old old enough to
understand that this new woman was not her mother and young enough to be
expected to accept her anyway. Tixsei was kind to her, in the distant way
stepmothers are often kind, but Coyre never warmed to her. What she did warm
to, unexpectedly, were Tixseiʼs children.
Snieoa came first a half-sister born when Coyre was six. Then Bier, two years
later. They were the children of the second wife, marked from birth as lesser in the
succession, and perhaps thatʼs why Coyre claimed them. She had spent her
childhood being Estericaʼs daughter, Maenʼs sister, Solisʼs princess roles defined
by other people. With Snieoa and Bier, she could simply be Coyre. The older sister
who read them stories. Who defended Bier when the other children mocked his
weakness. Who let Snieoa follow her everywhere like a small, adoring shadow.
Bier was sickly from the start. A cough that never quite cleared. A pallor that
deepened every winter. Coyre spent her adolescence learning which physicians
were competent and which were frauds, which herbs eased breathing and which
made it worse, which prayers the priests claimed would help and which were
empty ritual. She was sixteen when she stopped believing the priests. She was
twenty-three when she stopped believing anyone could save him.
Bier died at twenty-two, in a room Coyre had barely left for three weeks. She held
his hand when he stopped breathing. She washed his body. She walked behind
House Patton
15
his funeral procession with a face so blank that courtiers whispered she felt
nothing at all.
She felt everything. She simply decided, in that moment, that she would never
show it again.
After Bierʼs death, the warmth Coyre had shown her half-siblings vanished. Snieoa
tried to reach her bringing flowers, suggesting walks, asking to sit together as
they once had and Coyre turned her away every time. Not cruelly, not with anger,
but with a polite distance that was somehow worse. Snieoa eventually stopped
trying. She married Count Atano Yurea, moved to his estates, and built a life that
had nothing to do with the sister who had once been her whole world.
Coyre married Duke Shaniser Dajanyi at twenty-five a political match, though not
an unhappy one. Shaniser was steady, practical, and intelligent, and he
understood that his wife had walls he would never breach. They produced one
son, Elleinaj, and raised him with the careful attention of people who knew the
succession might one day matter.
It did. When Maen died childless in 7,140 BR, the throne passed to Elleinaj and
through him, to Coyreʼs bloodline. She lived long enough to see her son crowned,
to see her granddaughter Cenainaya married to Snieoaʼs grandson, to see the two
branches of Solisʼs descendants finally reunited. She built a museum in her mother
Estericaʼs honor, commissioned scholars to document Estericaʼs agricultural
reforms and library foundations, and gave Esterica the title she still carries in
history: “the Mother of a Dynasty.”
She died at ninety-six, sharp-minded to the end, having outlived her father, her
brother, her husband, and nearly everyone who remembered the girl she had been
before Bierʼs death. The woman who remained was formidable, accomplished,
and utterly alone exactly as she had chosen to be.
Princess Snieoa Patton (  BR
 BR)
Name Meaning: Gentle Rain
∼7,208
−∼7,131
House Patton
16
Title: Princess of the Solisian Empire (birth); Duchess of the Kaeilen Lands Gift
from Solis, part of her dowry)
Spouse: Count Atano Yurea
Children: Duke Eavanileto Yurea
Snieoa was born into a family that had already decided she did not matter. Her
mother Tixsei was the second wife, married after the great Estericaʼs death, and
no child of Tixseiʼs would ever be measured by anything other than how they
compared to Estericaʼs children. Her halfbrother Maen was the heir, brilliant and
cold and already being groomed for empire. Her halfsister Coyre was Estericaʼs
daughter, carrying the weight of that legacy in her very blood. Snieoa was simply
the girl who came after pleasant enough, politically useful for a future marriage,
but fundamentally unimportant.
She might have believed it, if not for Coyre. Her half-sister claimed her and Bier
from infancy, folding them into a world of shared secrets and fierce protection.
Coyre was the first person who made Snieoa feel like she mattered for herself
rather than for her bloodline. She followed Coyre everywhere as a child, adoring
and imitative, and Coyre let her patiently, kindly, in ways that the court found
surprising from Estericaʼs famously composed daughter.
But Coyre was not the center of Snieoaʼs world. Bier was.
Her brother was two years younger, sickly from birth, and Snieoa appointed
herself his protector before she was old enough to understand what protection
meant. She fought children who mocked his weakness. She sat with him through
fevers, telling him stories to distract from the coughing. She made elaborate plans
for their future adventures they would have when he was better, places they
would visit, a life outside the suffocating court where no one would care if Bier
could not ride a horse. She refused to believe he was dying even when the signs
became undeniable.
His death at twenty-two broke something in her. Not visibly Snieoa wept at the
funeral and then composed herself, returned to court, continued with her life. But
the part of her that had loved fiercely and protected recklessly went quiet. She
looked at Coyre across Bierʼs grave and saw a stranger a woman so controlled, so
cold, that Snieoa could not find the sister she had once adored. She tried to reach
House Patton
17
her. She brought flowers. She suggested walks. She asked to sit together as they
once had, three siblings against a court that undervalued them.
Coyre turned her away. Politely, distantly, with a composure that felt like a door
closing forever.
Snieoa stopped trying. She decided, consciously or not, that if Coyre did not want
her, she would build a life that did not need Coyre. She married Count Atano Yurea
at twenty-six a match that reunited her with her motherʼs family, giving her a place
where being Tixseiʼs daughter was an asset rather than a liability. She threw
herself into the Yurea estates, into her husbandʼs political ambitions, into creating
a world where the Patton name was something she carried rather than something
that defined her.
She had one son, Eavanileto, and raised him to be everything she wished she
could have been confident, healthy, positioned for greatness. When Eavanileto
later married Empress Cenainaya, Coyreʼs granddaughter, Snieoa watched the two
branches of her family reunite and felt nothing at all. By then she had spent
decades not feeling anything about her siblings. Maen had ignored her existence.
Coyre had rejected her grief. Bier was dead.
She outlived Maen by nine years, dying at seventy-seven on her husbandʼs
estates, surrounded by grandchildren who knew her only as a composed and
practical woman. She did not speak of Bier. She did not speak of Coyre. She had
learned, long ago, that some losses were too heavy to carry and too sharp to
examine, and she had simply set them down and walked away.
Prince Bier Patton (  BR
BR)
Name Meaning: Steadfast
Title: Prince of the Solisian Empire
Parents: Emperor Solis Elias Patton + Queen Consort Tixsei Yurea
Spouse: None
Children: None
Biography:
Bier was born struggling to breathe and never stopped. The physicians called it
∼7,206 −∼7,184
House Patton
18
weak lungs, a constitutional fragility, a tendency toward illness that no amount of
care could cure. His mother Tixsei spent his infancy in terror that every cough
would be his last. His father Solis when Bier was born, legendary and intimidating
visited the nursery rarely and left disappointed each time. A son who could not
run, could not train with weapons, could not sit a horse without exhausting himself
what use was such a son to an emperor?
Coyre was his refuge. His half-sister was eight years older, the daughter of the
great Esterica, and she should have had no reason to care about the sickly child of
her fatherʼs second wife. But Coyre claimed him anyway, the way she claimed
Snieoa, and Bier spent his childhood trailing after a sister who actually looked at
him when he spoke. She read to him when he was too tired to read himself. She
learned which foods settled his stomach and which made him worse. She argued
with physicians on his behalf and won.
He was a gentle child, timid by nature and made more so by a body that betrayed
him constantly. The court frightened him the politics, the maneuvering, the way
people looked at him with pity or contempt. He preferred small rooms and quiet
company. He preferred Coyre
and Snieoa, who loved him without expecting him to be strong. He preferred
books about faraway places he knew he would never have the health to visit.
Snieoa was his closest friend, two years older and fiercely protective in her own
way. Where Coyre was composed, Snieoa was passionate she raged at the
children who mocked Bierʼs weakness, planned elaborate revenges she never
carried out, and swore that when she was grown, she would make everyone sorry
for how they had treated him. Bier loved her for it, even when her plans
embarrassed him. He loved her for seeing him as someone worth defending rather
than someone to be pitied.
He knew he was dying long before anyone admitted it. The coughs grew worse in
his late teens. The fevers came more frequently. He watched Coyreʼs face grow
more controlled each time she visited and understood what her composure cost
her. He tried to be brave for her sake to joke about his condition, to pretend he
believed the physiciansʼ reassurances, to act as though he had years left instead
of months. He was not sure he succeeded.
He died at twenty-two, in the winter, with Coyre holding his hand and Snieoa
weeping in the corner. His last clear thought was that he was sorry sorry for
House Patton
19
leaving them, sorry for being the kind of brother who could only be mourned
instead of relied upon, sorry for every burden his illness had placed on the people
who loved him.
He was buried with full imperial honors, a prince of the Solisian Empire. The
funeral was magnificent. Solis did not attend he too frail to travel, they said,
though some might suspect his father simply had no interest in mourning a son he
had never valued. Maen attended but did not speak to Coyre or Snieoa. The family
fractured around Bierʼs grave, and none of them ever found their way back
together.
Emperor Elleinaj Patton I ( ~7,185 BR
 )
Name Meaning: Eternal Blessing from above
Elleinaj spent his first fifty-five years preparing to be nothing more than a dukeʼs
heir. His mother Coyre was a princess, yes, but his uncle Maen was emperor and
still young enough still healthy enough that surely the succession would pass to
Maenʼs children. Elleinaj was raised on the Dajanyi estates, educated in
administration and diplomacy, groomed to manage lands and negotiate trade
agreements. A perfectly adequate future for a perfectly adequate prince.
Then Maenʼs first wife died without surviving children. Then his second wife
proved barren. Then his third wife, year after year, failed to conceive. And
gradually, inexorably, the court began to look at Elleinaj.
He did not want the throne. He had met Maen cold, suspicious, cruel to anyone he
perceived as a threat and understood that being his uncleʼs heir meant becoming
his uncleʼs target. Elleinaj cultivated insignificance. He stayed on the Dajanyi
estates. He avoided court. He married Banalioya Yurea, a match that connected
him to his step-grandmother Tixseiʼs family but carried no political ambitions. He
had one daughter, Cenainaya, and hoped that would be enough.
It was not. Maen died childless in , and the throne fell to Elleinaj whether
he wanted it or not. He was fifty-five years old, entirely unprepared for imperial
∼
7,092 BR
7,140BR
House Patton
20
rule, and faced with a court full of factions that had spent decades maneuvering
for exactly this moment.
He surprised everyone, including himself. The decades he had spent avoiding
attention had also been decades spent watching learning how power actually
worked, which courtiers could be trusted, which factions would destroy the
empire if allowed to dominate. He was not brilliant. He was not charismatic. But he
was observant, patient, and genuinely uninterested in cruelty for its own sake,
which made him unusual among Patton emperors.
His mother Coyre became his closest advisor, though their relationship remained
complicated. She had raised him with the same emotional distance she applied to
everything after Bierʼs death, and Elleinaj sometimes wondered if she loved him or
simply recognized his usefulness. He never asked. Asking would have required
her to answer, and he suspected both of them preferred not to know.
His greatest achievement was marrying his daughter Cenainaya to Eavanileto
Yurea the grandson of his aunt Snieoa, reuniting the two branches of Solisʼs
descendants that had been divided since Bierʼs death seventy years earlier. The
match was politically expedient, dynastically logical, and quietly satisfying to an
emperor who had spent his life watching his family fracture. Their son Xayesa
would eventually inherit, carrying both Estericaʼs and Tixseiʼs blood, finally healing
a wound no one had been willing to acknowledge.
Elleinaj ruled for forty-eight years and died at ninety-three, having outlived his
mother, his wife, and most of his enemies. Historians remember him as a
competent administrator who stabilized the empire after Maenʼs suspicious reign
not a great emperor, but a necessary one. He would have found that assessment
entirely accurate and not particularly troubling.
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
Nearly two millennia of unbroken rule. Sacred authority. Elaborate ceremony.
Producing both the greatest and worst rulers in history. The ultimate political
power in Aicruae and, after Solis, the entire known world.
House Patton
21
What They Lack
Genuine affection from their vassals, obedience comes from power, not love.
Internal family harmony. The Pattons have a pattern of turning on each other that
repeats across generations.
Vulnerabilities
Succession crises the civil war between Solis and the twins is the most
devastating example, but internal fractures recur throughout the dynasty. Weak
kings who allow wives or advisors to truly rule Viake Recreadion). Deep-seated
resentment among the peasantry that periodically erupts Bloody Winter, Siege of
Highwater). In Minaraʼs era: infiltration by Vandrea posing as the Empress,
effectively hollowing out the dynasty from within. And a recurring tendency
toward obsession whether wielded for good Haliour II) or evil Viake.
Role in Narrative
Book 1 A Tale of a Thousand Songs): Central focus. Solisʼs civil war against Iris
and Orcus. The family is torn apart by King Benjamin IIʼs choices, and the war that
follows reshapes Aicruae forever.
Book 2 A Tale of Three Sisters): Background. The consequences of Solisʼs empire
on the three sisters.
Book 3 A Princess in Love): Central focus. Crandonaʼs story and the birth of
Goteivati III the moment the Patton dynasty begins its descent into the Dark Ages.
Book 4 Crown of Glory): Central focus. The corrupted imperial family. Emperor
Veo is a puppet, Vandrea wears the empressʼs face, and Minara the hidden Patton
princess must reclaim a heritage she doesnʼt know she has.

Empress Macenja Vandrea), Prince Elleraian, Minara (secret princess).

House Pontia stands apart from the dysfunction that defines most noble houses in
this world. The Pontia clan is described as happy, well-off, and influential, wellHouse Pontia

connection to their ancestors, and the trefoil hair ornament all offer a contrast to
the broken, power-hungry families surrounding them. Eventually through Amuseri,

Traditions
Trefoil Wire Hair Ornament: A single continuous strand of wire forming three
graduated loops (largest at bottom, smallest at top) worn diagonally across the
crown of the head and locked into three side-by-side plaits. The three loops
represent the three stages of life: childhood (smallest), adulthood (middle), and
elderhood (largest). The diagonal cross-brace creates tension and friction across
the three plaits, and the inward-turned hook makes it self-locking.
Ancestral Traveling: An ancestral tradition of letting your heart guide you to your
perfect destination. Traveling as a rite of passage is the way of the Pontia
ancestors.
Spiritual Connection
Deep spiritual connection to ancestors, who communicate with the most
connected clan members. Of all the Pontia, Amuseri was the most connected to
the ancestors, and they would tell her things sometimes because of that bond.

Amuseri Pontia (Born 19 BR)
Crandonaʼs Ally
Born to the Pontia clan, Amuseri had no reason to leave home. She was simply
bored with her life and looking for something fulfilling. She told her family she was
running away, but they didnʼt stop her because they knew there was no stopping
Amuseri, and because it was the way of their ancestors: traveling and letting your
heart guide you to your perfect destination.
She found her way to the Caprlolan forest and joined the group living under Danik
Malrancisʼs protection. Later, she joined Crandonaʼs campaign to reclaim the
throne. She survived the rebellion.
Out of all the members of the Pontia clan, Amuseri was the most connected to the
ancestors, and they would tell her things sometimes because of that bond.
She wore a distinctive trefoil wire hair ornament, a Pontia clan tradition: a single
continuous strand of wire forming three graduated loops (largest at bottom,
smallest at top) worn diagonally across the crown of the head and locked into
three side by side plaits. The three loops represent childhood (smallest),
adulthood (middle), and elderhood (largest).
Other members of Danikʼs forest group: Ala, Hicksora, Eveli, and Thoati. All five
women thought of Danik as their father.

serpentine branch, set against a striking pattern of alternating black and blue
bendlets (diagonal stripes).

and the ability to navigate storms with grace and brilliance. In heraldic tradition,
exotic birds symbolize nobility, eloquence, and the ability to thrive in foreign lands,
while their colorful plumage suggests wealth and far-reaching connections. The
diagonal pattern creates a sense of dynamic movement, like wind or falling rain.
The alternating colors suggest the houseʼs ability to move between different
realms, darkness and light, war and peace, with equal facility and impact.

Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Reidskelisia
1
House Reidskelisia is a maritime house, and fittingly, their most significant
member came from the sea itself. Ala Reidskelisia was born at sea to a pirate
captain and spent her childhood training to inherit her motherʼs command. But
when the pirate group docked in the Caprlolan Kingdom, Ala walked off the ship
and into the forest, choosing freedom over legacy. She lived as a hunter, was
taken in by Danik Malrancis as a father figure, and eventually joined Crandonaʼs
rebellion. During the final battle, Ala killed Avromvog Stanyad with her arrows,
avenging Danikʼs death in one of the rebellionʼs most personal confrontations.
Heraldry
Crest: A striking blue sea horse or hippocampus in a rampant pose, rearing up
with its curled tail and webbed fins visible, positioned centrally against a divided
shield featuring a blue wavy base (representing water), a white or silver middle
section with crenellations (suggesting castle battlements), and a gray upper
section, also crenellated. The mythical creature is rendered in bright blue with
darker detailing and a distinctive mane flowing backward, appearing to be
emerging from or swimming through the waves below.
Symbolism: The sea horse, a legendary creature of the oceans and symbol of the
seaʼs treasures, represents maritime commerce, the boundless riches found in
trade and shipping, and the mystical allure of wealth that seems to flow as
endlessly as the tides. The castle elements suggest fortified harbors and the
defensive structures that protect and enable this oceanic prosperity.
Motto: “Our Wealth Knows No Limits.”

Why They Matter
In a kingdom where most houses worship a pantheon, House Renalagardoʼs motto
pledges honor to “the one true god.” Thatʼs a declaration that Vapaz stands so far
House Renalagardo
1
above the other gods that the rest barely count. It sets them apart. Their crest puts
a golden fly at the heart of a black rose, pairing something most people would
swat away with something most people would call beautiful. The message: even
the smallest and most overlooked things serve the divine purpose. For a Baronlevel house, thatʼs a telling philosophy. They find the sacred in what others
dismiss.
Heraldry
Crest: Against a cream-colored field divided by a golden horizontal band, a large
black rose with green leaves and detailed petals dominates the composition. At its
heart sits a golden fly rendered with remarkable precision.
Symbolism: The black rose traditionally symbolizes rebirth, farewell, or devotion
unto death. The golden fly, often associated with decay but rendered here in
precious metal, suggests that even the smallest and most overlooked creatures
serve the divine purpose. The golden band reinforces prosperity and divine light.
The overall composition suggests House Renalagardo finds religious truth in
paradox, seeing the sacred in the profane and honoring “the one true god”
through the recognition that all creation, beautiful or base, serves the divine will.
Motto: “Honor to the one true god.”

Pre-Empire Era: Representative. A military-aligned house within Equateiyʼs First

Solisʼs Era: Count. After Equateiy was absorbed into the empire, House
Schmidtavaca held the title of Count. The family was known as musical geniuses.
Crandonaʼs Era: Count Schmidtavacaʼs household survived into the era of the
rebellion. His sickly second son Wioli joined the fighting against Merigen and was
killed.
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
House Schmidtavaca
1
Why They Matter
House Schmidtavaca Started off as a representative family in Equateiy but after
absorbing to create the empire, eventually by Crandonaʼs era they are counts and
became a kind of family renowned for their musical abilities. House Schmidtavaca
is a family of musical geniuses, but their legacy in the story is defined not by
music but by love and tragedy. During Crandonaʼs Era, Wioli Schmidtavaca, the
sickly second son who couldnʼt live up to his familyʼs gifts, fell in love with Eveli
Cathon in the Caprlolan forest and died trying to retrieve her body during the
rebellion against Merigen. He was struck down by over forty arrows. His death
inspired a folk song that outlasted anything his talented family ever composed:
“Wioli you desperate fool, you took a knife to your heart, then your golden hair
went dark.”
Heraldry
Crest: An ornate golden heraldic rose with five stylized petals and a detailed
center, positioned prominently on a shield divided into quarters by a bold purple
diagonal cross or saltire, with the rose placed at the intersection where the purple
bands meet in the center. The background is divided into alternating sections of
white or silver and gold or yellow, creating a striking checkerboard effect behind
the purple saltire.
Symbolism: The golden flower represents beauty, achievement, and the
blossoming of virtue. The purple cross, the color of nobility and sacrifice, serves
as the literal shield that protects the flower. The alternating light and gold sections
suggest the duality of defense and display, the hidden and the revealed, that
characterizes a house whose reputation and dignity form their truest protection.
Motto: “Our Honor is Our Shield.”

Wioli Schmidtavaca Born 17 BR, DECEASED
“The Desperate Fool”
The sickly second son of Count Schmidtavaca. Born to a family of musical
geniuses, but he was no such genius, much to his parentsʼ disappointment. He
spent most of his days staring out his bedroom window, doing nothing besides
sleeping. His brothers and cousins teased and bullied him, calling him a fool. His
parentsʼ embarrassment grew enough that they shipped him off to the countryside
for “treatment.”
While staying in the countryside, he met the girls living in the Caprlolan forest and
fell in love with Eveli Cathon. When Eveli was killed during the rebellion against
Merigen, Wioli stormed into battle despite being sick, trying to retrieve her body.
He was struck down by over forty arrows.
Memorialized in a folk song: “Wioli you desperate fool, you took a knife to your
heart, then your golden hair went dark.”

deeper meaning. Upon a shield divided vertically by a bold brown pale (center

careful attention to its pointed ears and slender muzzle, moves from left to right

survives through wit alone, embodies the houseʼs philosophical question:

middle path, relying on intelligence and adaptability rather than brute force or
divine favor, thriving in the spaces between extremes through cunning
observation and tactical flexibility.
