entries.title: House Vemer
entries.text:
House Vemer
House Vemer
“STRENGTH TO THE KING”
Quick Facts
Status: Marquess/Marquis
Origin: Southern Aicruae
House Name Meaning: The Last Warrior
Founded: 8,265 BR
Founder: Ualvo Vemer I
Seat: Basar Tari, Southern Aicruae (shared with House Yurea)
Faction: Divine Faction
Spirit Animal: Sperent Black Mamba)
Colors: TBD
Wealth: 126,000 Rern
Military: Foot soldiers and trained assassins (numbers undetermined)
Religion: Leneyez
Theme Song: “The Beginning of the End” by Klergy x Valerie Broussard
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Marquess rank, Divine Faction. House Vemer rises from the
posthumous glory of Ualvo Vemer I and the forced marriage alliance of the Code
of Rose. As Southern Aicruaeʼs legitimate economy collapses, the house entangles
itself with the UIB the Underground Illegal Business operating out of Basar Tari.
They claim theyʼre too weak to stop the criminal networks. In truth, they profit
from them. By the time of the civil war, House Vemer is wealthy, connected, and
deeply compromised.
Solisʼs Era: Survives the civil war by surrendering to Emperor Solis and claiming
their support of the twins was solely due to the Code of Rose, the marriage
obligation binding them to House Vika. No one believed them, but no one could
prove otherwise. House Vika is ash. The Code of Rose is a dead alliance with a
House V emer
1
dead house. House Vemer survives the civil war by surrendering to Solis and
blaming their loyalty to the twins on a marriage obligation no one believes. But
survival comes with scrutiny. The new empire is larger, more centralized, and less
tolerant of lawless corners. Imperial administrators arrive in Southern Aicruae. Not
many, and not with much enthusiasm, the south is still a wasteland no one wants,
but enough to make the old arrangements uncomfortable.
The UIB doesnʼt disappear, but House Vemer begins creating distance. Quietly.
Carefully. The bribes become less direct. The kickbacks route through more
intermediaries. Publicly, the Vemers emphasize their legitimate authority as prison
administrators and border wardens. Itʼs not a reformation. Itʼs repositioning. The
empire is watching now, and the snake house knows when to shed its skin.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: Two and a half millennia changes everything even House Vemer. The
rehabilitation took centuries. Imperial pressure forced the first steps: cutting
obvious UIB ties, professionalizing the prison administration, cooperating with
crown investigators just enough to avoid scrutiny. But somewhere along the way,
survival strategy became genuine ambition. Generations of Vemers grew tired of
being the house everyone whispered about. They produced capable leaders,
married into respectable families, invested in infrastructure, and slowly painfully
built a reputation that didnʼt reek of criminality. By Minaraʼs Era, the UIB
connection is ancient history. Scholars mention it in texts about Pre-Empire
corruption. The current Vemers acknowledge it the way old families acknowledge
embarrassing ancestors: briefly, carefully, and with emphasis on how far theyʼve
come. House Vemer is no longer the snake house running a criminal operation
under a noble crest. Theyʼre the house that pulled itself out of the mud. The black
mamba still coils on their banner. The motto still says “Strength to the king.” But
the two tongues have become one. Mostly.
Nicknames People Call Them During This Era
“Southern Vipers”
“The Kingʼs Snakes”
“The Victors of Little Hill”
“Vikaʼs Leash” (after the Code of Rose, theyʼre tied to House Vika through
House V emer
2
marriage)
“Vikaʼs Dogs” (implying theyʼre subordinate to Vika through the marriage alliance)
Why They Matter
House Vemer is what happens when a family builds its legacy on one dead manʼs
glory and then spends every generation after trying to hold onto something they
never fully earned.
Ualvo Vemer I won the Battle of Little Hill and died for it. His son Hasken forced his
way into a marriage with the most desirable woman in Aicruae, Aintana Vika, the
Winter Rose, because he believed the son of a great hero deserved nothing less.
That marriage, the Code of Rose, tied House Vemer to House Vika and gave them
a legitimacy they couldnʼt manufacture on their own. But the alliance came at a
cost. Haskenʼs obsession with Aintana poisoned the family for generations: a son
who feared him, triplet granddaughters named as trophies, and a succession line
that nearly collapsed because no one would marry into a house still haunted by a
dead manʼs grip.
And beneath the surface, something darker. House Vemer shares control of Basar
Tari with House Yurea, and both houses have disclosed ties to the UIB, the
Underground Illegal Business, a criminal network dealing in assassination,
smuggling, human trafficking, and every kind of trade the crown pretends doesnʼt
exist. On the surface, House Vemer claims theyʼre too weak to stop the UIB. The
official line is that they tolerate it for the overall well-being of the territory. The
truth is that Vemer members are secretly involved, and the bribes keep flowing.
Their motto says “Strength to the king,” but the question is which king, the one on
the throne, or the one paying them under the table.
Theyʼre the house that looks legitimate if you donʼt look too hard. And most people
donʼt.
Heraldry
Crest: Argent (silver/gray) field. In chief, a blue open eye with black outline. At
center, a sable serpent coiled and striking, with purle underbelly, tongue
extended, pierced by a purple bend sinister (diagonal bar running upper left to
lower right). In base, a blue iris flower with golden stamens and green leaves.
House V emer
3
Symbolism: The silver/gray field represents neutrality, survival, and adaptability.
The open blue eye is the symbol of Vapaz, King of the Gods, representing divine
authority, watchfulness, and legitimate power. It reinforces their motto: “Strength
to the King.” The open eye declares House Vemerʼs allegiance to the divine order
and the throne (though whether they truly serve the king on the throne or the one
paying under the table is another question). The coiled serpent represents their
spirit animal, the Sperent (black mamba), deadly precision, calculated strikes, and
the willingness to eliminate threats before anyone realizes there was a problem.
The purple bar cutting through the serpent symbolizes restraint, control, and a
divided nature, the snake is dangerous, but it serves. The blue iris flower
represents loyalty and a message, the iris is traditionally a flower of
communication and hidden meanings, fitting for a house tied to information
brokering and secrets. The blue ties it to their house colors.
Motto: “Strength to the King.”
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Criminal connections, the UIB network, the Code of Rose marriage alliance, and
the legacy of Ualvo Vemer I. House Vemerʼs power is not built on open military
dominance or trade empires, itʼs built on proximity to dangerous people and the
willingness to look the other way. Their seat in Basar Tari, the unofficial hub of the
UIB, gives them access to assassination services, smuggling routes, information
brokering, and illegal trade that most noble houses pretend not to use but quietly
benefit from.
Internal Power Structure
Male advantage system. Women can inherit if no male heir is present, but only on
the condition that she keeps the Vemer name and does not take her husbandʼs
surname. The family line, and the Vemer name is protected above all else.
Military Forces
Foot soldiers and trained assassins. Exact numbers are undetermined, but the
assassin training aligns with the houseʼs relationship to the UIB and its reputation
House V emer
4
for being “dangerous and willing to take out anyone who gets in their way.”
Lands & Income
Seat: Basar Tari in Southern Aicruae, shared with House Yurea. Southern Aicruae
is described as a “barren wasteland with nothing to offer” the legitimate economy
is weak, and crime fills the vacuum. The region houses the largest prison in all of
Aicruae, and the distance from the capital Lajazer means less crown oversight.
Most guards and officials in Basar Tari have been silently corrupted.
Key industries: House Vemerʼs wealth doesnʼt come from the land. Southern
Aicruae is a barren wasteland with a dead legitimate economy. Their 126,000 Rern
comes from other sources.
Prison administration Basar Tari houses the largest prison in all of Aicruae. The
crown pays for its operation. House Vemer administers it. What gets skimmed in
the process is between the Vemers and their accountants.
Border tariffs Southern Aicruae borders Pireaynea, a country with a difficult
relationship with Aicruae. Whatever trade passes through legitimate or otherwise
House Vemer taxes. The tariffs are modest. The bribes to avoid the tariffs are
better.
Assassin services House Vemer trains assassins. Officially, theyʼre for house
defense. Unofficially, noble houses across Aicruae know who to contact when
problems need to disappear quietly. The Vemers donʼt advertise. They donʼt need
to.
Information brokering The UIB deals in secrets: blackmail material, noble
indiscretions, political vulnerabilities. House Vemer takes a cut of what passes
through their territory. Knowledge is cheaper than assassination and often more
effective.
UIB kickbacks The real source of Vemer wealth. They tolerate the Underground
Illegal Business the smuggling, the gambling, the trafficking, the trade in
prohibited goods and the UIB pays them for the privilege. Itʼs not legitimate
income. Itʼs not even hidden income. Itʼs just income no one can prove.
Smuggling facilitation Stone Powder from Equateiy. Joyless Death poison
produced by House Vika and sold through back channels. Luxury goods from
House V emer
5
Pireaynea avoiding crown tariffs. It all moves through Southern Aicruae, and
House Vemer makes sure it moves smoothly.
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Vika Code of Rose): Marriage alliance through Aintana Vika and Hasken
Vemer. This was not a love match, Aintana rejected Hasken, and he forced the
marriage through a royal order. The Code of Rose became the defining alliance of
House Vemerʼs history, tying them to the most powerful military house in Aicruae.
When the civil war came, House Vemer used the Code of Rose as their excuse for
backing the twins and later as their excuse for surrendering to Solis.
House Kulio Marriage): Fasi Vemer married Jando Kulio, creating the Kulio-Vemer
alliance.
House Yurea Territorial): Both houses share control of Basar Tari and both have
disclosed ties to the UIB. The relationship is less a formal alliance and more a
mutual understanding: they tolerate each other because the alternative is
exposing what they both have to hide.
Rival Houses
House Arvento The Arventos created the Council of the Forsaken to investigate
violent crimes. They are fiercely loyal to the crown, incorruptible, and everything
House Vemer pretends to be. The Arventos know about the UIB. They know
Vemer tolerates it. They know the “too weak to stop it” excuse is a lie. But
Southern Aicruae is outside their jurisdiction, and the crown has written it off. So
the Arventos watch, and wait, and remember. If House Vemer ever gives them an
opening, theyʼll take it.
House Caraen Capital protectors, Council of the Forsaken members, and bearers
of a name that means “Gift from the Gods.” Caraen sees Vemer as everything
wrong with the Divine Faction nobles who claim divine right while running a
criminal enterprise in the kingdomʼs most lawless region. The Caraens donʼt hide
their contempt. They just canʼt prove anything yet.
House Aedria The third leg of the Council of the Forsaken. House Aedria is the “IT
family” beloved, respected, the house everyone wants to be. They represent what
House V emer
6
nobility is supposed to look like. House Vemer represents what it actually looks
like when no oneʼs watching. The two have nothing in common except mutual
awareness that they exist on opposite ends of the same system.
House Yurea Co-conspirators make the worst rivals. House Yurea shares Basar
Tari with House Vemer, and both houses have disclosed ties to the UIB. On the
surface, itʼs a mutual understanding they tolerate each other because exposing
one means exposing both. Underneath, itʼs a cold war. They know too much about
each other. Every deal, every bribe, every body. If one house ever decides the
other is more liability than ally, Southern Aicruae will get very bloody very fast.
The Common People Faction House Leva, House Dajanyi, House Yurea all of them
look at House Vemer and see hypocrisy in noble clothing. Vemer claims Divine
Faction membership, insisting on the divine right of nobility, while running a
criminal operation that exploits the poorest people in the kingdom. The Common
People Faction doesnʼt have the power to bring Vemer down. But they have the
resentment, and resentment has a long memory.
Shared Territory
House Yurea: Both houses occupy Basar Tari in Southern Aicruae and are equally
implicated in the UIB criminal network.
House Culture
Religion
Leneyez.
Traditions
The Shedding: When a Vemer heir takes control of the house, they must publicly
“shed” the previous leadership. The form this takes is up to the heir: some burn a
piece of their predecessorʼs clothing, others destroy a personal possession,
others change their manner of dress entirely. The only rule is that something must
visibly go. The ritual acknowledges that the snake has grown new skin the old is
discarded, the new is what matters now. Sentimental heirs have been known to
burn a single glove. Ruthless ones have burned livestock belong to the previous
House V emer
7
leader. What you choose to shed says something about what kind of leader youʼll
be.
Rose and Fang Once a year, House Vemer commemorates the Code of Rose their
marriage alliance with House Vika. Red roses are placed on the family altar
alongside the Black Mamba imagery: petals and scales, beauty and venom. The
tradition began when both houses were powerful. It continued after Solis burned
House Vika to the ground. Vemers still lay the roses. Whether itʼs loyalty, guilt, or
just habit, no living Vemer will say.
Values
House Vemer understands the difference between what you say and what you do.
Loyalty on paper Their motto is “Strength to the king.” Their founder died winning
a battle for the crown. Every Vemer swears service to the throne. It sounds noble.
Itʼs meant to. But “strength to the king” doesnʼt specify which king, and Vemers
have always been flexible about where their strength gets pointed. They sided
with the twins during the civil war, then surrendered to Solis and claimed the Code
of Rose made them do it. The motto isnʼt a promise. Itʼs a shield.
Ruthlessness as clarity The Black Mamba is their symbol for a reason. Vemers
donʼt pretend to be good. They pretend to be loyal, which is different. Behind
closed doors, theyʼre honest about what they are: dangerous, calculating, willing
to take out anyone in their way. The UIB operates in their territory because Vemers
allow it. The crown looks the other way because Vemers are useful.
Survival above all Their founder was a bread makerʼs son. They rule a barren
wasteland the crown has written off. Theyʼve never had the luxury of principles.
Morality is for houses with options. Vemers do what they must forge alliances,
tolerate crime, force marriages, switch sides and they sleep fine.
Usefulness over affection Vemers donʼt expect to be loved. They expect to be
needed. As long as theyʼre strong enough to be useful to whoever holds power,
theyʼll survive. Thatʼs the only currency that matters.
Reputation
Best described as “sort of influential due to their rank and social position.” House
Vemer sits in a strange middle ground, they hold noble status and Divine Faction
membership, but their seat is in the most lawless region of Aicruae. The other
House V emer
8
houses know about the UIB ties. The crown knows. Everyone knows. But Southern
Aicruae has been essentially written off, and as long as House Vemer keeps things
quiet and keeps saying “strength to the king,” no one pushes too hard.
Their spirit animal tells you everything. The black mamba doesnʼt roar or charge,
itʼs fast, it calculates, and it kills with deadly accuracy. House Vemer doesnʼt fight
wars. They take out problems before anyone realizes there was a problem to
begin with.
Common Sayings About/from House Vemer
“Loyalty feeds no one.” Said only among family, never at court. A reminder that
pretty words donʼt keep the house alive. Vemers are loyal when itʼs useful and
practical when itʼs not. Anyone who confuses the performance for the priority
wonʼt last long.
“Two tongues, one throat.” The closest thing Vemers have to a proverb. What you
say in public and what you say in private both come from the same mouth. Neither
is a lie. Theyʼre just different truths for different rooms.
“Strong for the king. Stronger for ourselves.” A private twist on their official motto.
Children learn “Strength to the king” first. They learn this version later, when
theyʼre old enough to understand the difference.
“The south makes its own law.” Part defiance, part resignation. The crown has
written off Southern Aicruae as a barren wasteland, so the people who live there
Vemers included operate by their own rules. Said with varying degrees of pride
depending on whoʼs speaking.
History
Founding (8,265 BR)
Ualvo Vemer I was the son of a bread maker, no noble blood, no military dynasty,
no birthright. He earned everything on the battlefield. His victory at the Battle of
Little Hill in 8,264 BR was significant enough to earn him posthumous nobility,
because Ualvo didnʼt survive to see the title. He died following the battle, and the
noble status was granted posthumously. House Vemer was founded in 8,265 BR, a
house born from a dead heroʼs glory. The name Vemer means “The Last Warrior.”
House V emer
9
Rise to Power
House Vemer began with a corpse and a debt.
Ualvo Vemer I was a bread makerʼs son with no name, no title, and no future until
he won the Battle of Little Hill and died doing it. The crown granted him nobility
posthumously, which meant his son Hasken inherited a title but no infrastructure,
no allies, and a seat in Southern Aicruae, the kingdomʼs wasteland.
Hasken built what his father couldnʼt. When Aintana Vika daughter of the most
powerful military house in Aicruae rejected his marriage proposal, he petitioned
the crown for a royal order forcing her hand. He got it. The Code of Rose bound
House Vemer to House Vika, and suddenly the bread makerʼs grandson had the
backing of dukes. The Vemers leveraged that alliance ruthlessly, climbing from
new-money nobodies to Marquess rank within two generations.
Their other asset was their territory. Southern Aicruae offered nothing legitimate
barren land, a prison colony, desperate people. But desperate people create
opportunities. The UIB grew in Basar Tariʼs shadows, and the Vemers grew
alongside it. They collected bribes, looked the other way, and built wealth where
no wealth should exist. By the time of the civil war, House Vemer was entrenched:
not respected, but too useful to remove.
Major Achievements
Battle of Little Hill 8,264 BR The victory that created the house. Ualvo Vemer
died for it; his descendants have lived off it ever since.
Code of Rose Haskenʼs forced marriage to Aintana Vika secured an alliance with
the most powerful house in Eastern Aicruae. The Vemers punched above their
weight for generations because of it.
Surviving the civil war They backed the losing side and still kept their seat. The
excuse was flimsy, but theyʼre still here.
House Kulio marriage alliance Fasi Vemer married Jando Kulio, connecting Vemer
to another divine-faction house and expanding their network westward.
Major Disgraces
The Forced Marriage Hasken Vemer couldnʼt accept rejection. He used a royal
order to drag Aintana Vika to the altar. The Code of Rose is an alliance built on
House V emer
10
coercion, and everyone knows it.
UIB Complicity House Vemer publicly claims theyʼre too weak to stop the criminal
networks in their territory. Privately, they profit from them. The crown pretends not
to notice. Other houses donʼt pretend.
Civil War Cowardice They sided with Iris and Orcus, then surrendered and blamed
the Code of Rose. No one believed them. The reputation for convenient loyalties
has never faded.
Jando Kulioʼs Murder Fasi Vemerʼs husband was found stabbed outside a brothel
with roses stuffed in his eyes — likely killed by a scorned lover. The marriage that
was supposed to strengthen both houses ended in scandal. What Fasi did after
remains a subject of whispers.
The UIB Connection
House Vemer and House Yurea are the two noble houses with disclosed ties to the
Underground Illegal Business. Members of both houses are secretly involved in
the UIBʼs operations, which include assassination, kidnapping and ransom,
information brokering, illegal gambling, prostitution networks, human trafficking,
and the smuggling of prohibited goods including Joyless Death poison and Stone
Powder imported from Equateiy.
The official reasoning is that theyʼre “too weak to stop the UIB activities and must
pretend it doesnʼt exist for the overall well-being of the territory.” In practice, both
houses tolerate UIB activity in exchange for bribes. The UIB has no single leader
itʼs a loose network of multiple competing groups with territorial agreements, and
local bosses control specific towns and trade routes. Basar Tari is the unofficial
hub, and most of its guards and officials have been silently corrupted.
The UIB persists because Southern Aicruae is a barren wasteland with a dead
economy. The largest prison in Aicruae draws desperate people families of
prisoners, released convicts with no options and the distance from the capital
means less crown oversight. Crime runs more rampant in Southern Aicruae than
anywhere else, and people are leaving for Western Aicruae. The crown has
essentially written off the south.
Role in the Civil War
House V emer
11
House Vemer sided with the twins Iris and Orcus) during the Aicruan Civil War,
tied by the Code of Rose to House Vika. After the war ended and Solis won, House
Vemer surrendered and claimed their involvement was purely due to the marriage
obligation. No one believed them, but the excuse was just thin enough to survive
on. House Vemer endured where House Vika was eradicated.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs origins to the generations that followed.
Ualvo Vemer I (8,298 BR – 8,264 BR)
“The Great Hero” | Founder of House Vemer — Name meaning: Dark
The son of a bread maker who became a war hero. Ualvo won the Battle of Little
Hill in 8,264 BR, a victory significant enough to earn him nobility but he didnʼt live
to receive the title. He died following the battle, and the noble status was granted
posthumously. Everything House Vemer has, everything they claim to be, traces
back to this one man who bled out before he could see what his name became.
“War can change a manʼs fate. It could be for the better or for the worst but that
manʼs life will have been changed.”
Hasken Vemer (8,274 BR – 8,206 BR)
Son of Ualvo | Architect of the Code of Rose — Name meaning: Sweet and True
Hasken believed he deserved the best and to him, the best was Aintana Vika, the
Winter Rose, the most beautiful woman in the Aicruaen nobility. When she
rejected him, he didnʼt accept it. He obtained a royal order forcing her to marry
him, because in his mind, the son of the great hero Ualvo Vemer deserved nothing
less than the jewel of House Vika.
That forced marriage became the Code of Rose the alliance that would define
House Vemer for centuries. Aintana gave him three sons, but their marriage was a
one-sided love affair. She could never love him as much as he loved her. And
Haskenʼs obsession didnʼt end with his wife. When his son Rashar produced triplet
daughters who resembled Aintana, Hasken demanded all three be named after
her, threatening to disinherit Rashar if he refused. His intimidation was so
House V emer
12
thorough that even after his death at age 68 from a “mysterious illness” suitors
were still too afraid to approach his granddaughters.
Hasken got what he wanted: the most beautiful woman in Aicruae, an alliance with
the most powerful military house, and a legacy stamped with Aintanaʼs face. What
he couldnʼt get was her love, her willingness, or a family that didnʼt fear him.
Rashar Vemer (8,254 BR – 8,178 BR)
Son of Hasken — Name meaning: Wrath of the Sun
One of Haskenʼs three sons, and the one his father hated most because Rashar
looked like Hasken rather than Aintana. That was the crime. Looking like his own
father. Rashar was terrified of Hasken his entire life, and that fear bled into how he
treated his own daughters. When triplet girls were born who looked like their
grandmother Aintana, Rashar wanted to cut their hair — their hair was the same
color as Aintanaʼs, and he couldnʼt stand the reminder. His wife stopped him,
arguing that no man would marry daughters with shorn hair. So the hair stayed,
and the girls grew up looking exactly like the woman their grandfather was
obsessed with.
The Triplets and the Code of Rose
The ghost of Aintana Vika haunted House Vemer for three generations and
nowhere more visibly than in the faces of three girls who never asked to carry her
name. The Code of Rose was supposed to be a marriage alliance. What it actually
became was a cage for Aintana, who never loved the man who forced her into it;
for Rashar, who could never be enough for his father; for three girls named after a
grandmother they never chose to resemble; and for House Vemer itself, which
built its identity around a woman who wanted nothing to do with them.
Anatina Vemer I (8,225 BR – 8,149 BR)
Name meaning: The Roseʼs Daughter
The eldest of the triplets. Named after her grandmother Aintana at Haskenʼs
demand the same grandfather who terrorized her father and forced her
grandmother into marriage. Anatina I never married. Haskenʼs intimidation of
suitors was so complete that even after his death, no man would come near her.
House V emer
13
She spent her life resenting her father Rashar and her grandmother Aintana for not
stopping Hasken when they had the chance. Died at 76, unmarried.
Anatina Vemer II (8,225 BR – 8,132 BR)
Name meaning: The Roseʼs Daughter
The only triplet sister to marry. Mother of Tena Vemer. Widowed fairly early on
into her marriage. Of the three sisters, she was the one who carried the Vemer line
forward without her marriage and her daughter Tena, the house might have
collapsed entirely. Died at 93.
Anatina Vemer III (8,225 BR – 8,127 BR)
Name meaning: The Roseʼs Daughter
The youngest triplet. Like her sister Anatina I, she never married. Died at 98, the
longest-lived of the three.
Tena Vemer (8,159 BR – 8,087 BR)
Name meaning: 100 Years of Beauty
Daughter of Anatina Vemer II and the heir who saved House Vemer from
extinction. Tena was described as “the light and joy of her motherʼs life,” raised in
extreme shelter by her widowed mother. She was “the long-awaited heir who
cemented Rasharʼs line and created a continuation that helped maintain the Code
of Rose.” Her birth signified a new age for House Vemer proof that the line would
survive, that the alliance with House Vika still held, and that Haskenʼs obsession
hadnʼt destroyed the family entirely. It had only warped it.
Fasi Vemer (7,652 BR - 7,595 BR)
Name meaning: Silent Bloom]
The marriage to Jando Kulio was political an alliance between House Vemer and
House Kulio, snake and owl, southern pragmatism and western divine blood.
Jando was handsome, charming, and incapable of fidelity. He led noble girls on
before the marriage. He continued after. Fasi said nothing. She attended court
functions at his side, smiled when expected, and watched her husband collect
lovers the way other men collected horses.
House V emer
14
Then Jando was found stabbed to death outside a brothel. Two roses had been
stuffed into his eyes.
The roses were the detail everyone remembered. Roses —the symbol of the Code
of Rose, House Vemerʼs defining alliance. A Vemer signature, or someone wanted
it to look that way. Suspicion fell on Fasi immediately. A patient wife who finally
stopped being patient. A Vemer who remembered that her house dealt in
assassins. Nothing was ever proven. Fasi expressed appropriate grief, wore
appropriate mourning, and returned to Southern Aicruae after a respectable
interval.
She never remarried. Whether that was choice or circumstance is a matter of
interpretation. Suitors may have been cautious about courting an alleged
husband-killer. Or Fasi may simply have had no interest in repeating the
experience. She lived another twenty-six years, dying at fifty-seven in the family
seat at Basar Tari.
House Kulio never formally accused her. The alliance technically survived. But
after Fasi, no Kulio married a Vemer again.
Married Jando Kulio, creating the Kulio-Vemer alliance. Beyond the marriage, little
is recorded about Fasi but the alliance with House Kulio gave House Vemer a
second marriage connection to a major noble house, diversifying their political ties
beyond the Code of Rose.
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
The Code of Rose alliance with House Vika, UIB connections, trained assassins,
survival instincts (surrendering to Solis after the civil war rather than dying for a
lost cause), and a willingness to operate in the grey areas that other noble houses
pretend donʼt exist.
What They Lack
Legitimate power Their entire foundation rests on one dead hero, a forced
marriage, and criminal income. Strip away the UIB and House Vemer is a
Marquess family ruling a wasteland with no army, no trade, and no allies.
House V emer
15
Military strength They have foot soldiers and assassins, but no army. In an open
war, they lose. Their survival depends on never fighting one.
Respect The other Divine Faction houses tolerate Vemer because the alternative is
acknowledging what everyone already knows. No one admires them. No one
wants to be them. Theyʼre useful, and thatʼs the ceiling.
A clean reputation The UIB whispers follow them everywhere. The civil war
surrender follows them everywhere. The Code of Rose a marriage built on
coercion follows them everywhere. House Vemer canʼt escape its own history.
Their strongest ally House Vika is gone. Solis burned them to the ground. The
Code of Rose is a dead alliance now, and Vemer has nothing to replace it. Their
marriage connection to House Kulio is weaker, and Kulio has its own problems.
Vulnerabilities
The UIB is a leash, not a partnership House Vemer depends on criminal income.
That means they depend on criminals. If the UIB ever decides Vemer is more
useful as a scapegoat than a partner, thereʼs nothing protecting them.
House Yurea knows everything Co-conspirators make the worst enemies. House
Yurea shares Basar Tari and shares the UIB connection. If the relationship sours,
Yurea can bury Vemer and Vemer can bury Yurea. Mutually assured destruction is
not stability.
The Council of the Forsaken is watching Arvento, Caraen, and Aedria created a
body specifically to investigate violent crimes. They know about Vemer. Theyʼre
waiting for proof, or for Vemer to slip. One mistake, one witness, one disgruntled
UIB boss looking to trade information for immunity and the Council has what it
needs.
Southern Aicruae is collapsing People are leaving for Western Aicruae. The
legitimate economy is dead. The only thing keeping the region functional is crime,
and crime doesnʼt build infrastructure. Eventually, there wonʼt be enough people
left to exploit.
Their survival depends on a lie They told Solis the Code of Rose made them fight
for the twins. No one believed it. But no one could disprove it either, and Solis had
bigger problems than one snake house in the south. If anyone ever finds evidence
that Vemerʼs support for the twins was genuine letters, witnesses, anything their
House V emer
16
survival story falls apart. Their strongest claim from then on was the Code of Rose
made them have to listen to the Twins, and everything they did was because they
had no choice but to and that it was an order.
Role in Narrative
Book Appearances: TBD
Plot Significance: House Vemerʼs ties to the UIB and their Code of Rose obligation
to House Vika position them at the intersection of organized crime and noble
politics. Their survival of the civil war when their strongest ally, House Vika, was
eradicated, raises questions about what deals they made and what they were
willing to sacrifice to endure.
Key Members in Story: TBD
Cross-References
House Vika, House Kulio, House Yurea, House Patton, Ualvo Vemer I, Hasken
Vemer, Aintana Vika The Winter Rose), Rashar Vemer, Anatina Vemer I, Anatina
Vemer II, Anatina Vemer III, Tena Vemer, Fasi Vemer, Jando Kulio, Emperor Solis
Elias Patton, Basar Tari, Southern Aicruae, Battle of Little Hill, Code of Rose
House Vika Alliance), The UIB Underground Illegal Business), Joyless Death
Poison, Stone Powder Drug, Leneyez Religion), Divine Faction, Aicruan Civil
War, Lajazer, Western Aicruae
Keywords
House Vemer, Vemer, The Last Warrior, Strength to the King, Southern Aicruae,
Basar Tari, Divine Faction, Black Mamba, Sperent, Khaki, Blue, Silver-Gray,
Leneyez, The Beginning of the End, Klergy, Valerie Broussard, UIB, Underground
Illegal Business, Ualvo Vemer I, The Great Hero, Hasken Vemer, Aintana Vika,
Winter Rose, Code of Rose, Rashar Vemer, Anatina Vemer I, Anatina Vemer II,
Anatina Vemer III, Tena Vemer, Fasi Vemer, Jando Kulio, House Vika, House Kulio,
House Yurea, Battle of Little Hill, Aicruan Civil War, Trained Assassins, Rern,
Triplets, Roseʼs Daughter, Male Advantage System, Bread Maker, Posthumous
Nobility

entries.title: House Vika
entries.text:
House Vika
House Vika
“THE TRUTH SHALL PREVAIL ABOVE ALL LIES”
Quick Facts
Status: Duke/Duchess
Origin: Aicruae Eastern)
House Name Meaning: The Gods Chosen Warrior
Founded: 8,520 BR 4th oldest noble house in Aicruae)
Founder: Axiker Vika
Seat: Haleker, Eastern Aicruae
Faction: Divine Faction
Spirit Animal: Wild Boar
Colors: Dark Purple Sovereignty) & Light Purple/Lavender Bravery)
Wealth:  Rern
Military: 310,000 men The Iveraʼs: 270,000 | Swords of Mertyeria: 40,000
Religion: Rillic
Theme Song: “Team” by Lorde
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Duke/Duchess, One of the most powerful houses in Aicruae, with
military strength rivaling the royal family.
Solisʼs Era: Eradicated, Following Orcusʼs death in 7,217 BR, Emperor Solis ordered
the complete destruction of House Vika. The Iveraʼs and the Swords of Mertyeria
were disbanded and or absorbed into the imperial military. The Vika estates in
Haleker were seized. Any remaining members bearing the Vika name were
executed or forced to renounce their house and take new names. After 1,303
years, House Vika ceased to exist.
Crandonaʼs Era: None.
Minaraʼs Era: None.
∼195,000
House V ika
1
Why They Matter
House Vika is the military backbone of Aicruae and one of the root causes of the
civil war that tears the kingdom apart. Their power grew so vast that King Darien
Lacern Patton married his son Benjamin II to Duke Rarieloʼs only daughter, Mihai
Julie Vika, specifically to keep House Vika loyal. That marriage produced the twins
Iris and Orcus, and when Benjamin took a concubine and publicly favored his
illegitimate son Solis over the Vika-blooded heirs, it set in motion a civil war that
ended with House Vikaʼs total eradication.
They are the house that proves a simple truth in this world: being the strongest
doesnʼt mean you survive. Being 310,000 soldiers strong, being feared by every
other noble house, being ranked number one in all of Aicruae but none of it saved
them when the political winds shifted.
Nicknames People Call Them During This Era
“The Eastern Shield”
“The Boars of Haleker”
“The Eastern Arm (as in, the military arm of Eastern Aicruae)”
“Halekerʼs Own”
“The Haleker Horde”
“The Purple Tide”
“The Mad House”
“The Victors of Summers” Their founding battle. Where Axiker earned the title.)
“The Champions of Afera” Led the coalition that destroyed House Baliva.)
“The Lords of Highwater”
“The Godsʼ Chosen Warriors”
“Axikerʼs Line”
Heraldry
Crest: A shield divided into eight triangular sections radiating from the center,
alternating between deep plum purple and light lavender pink. A brown wild boar
runs across the shield, low to the ground and moving on a diagonal. Its tusks are
bright white, its mouth is open with a red tongue showing, and its coat is shaded in
chestnut tones with darker color along the spine. The shield is framed by a wreath
House V ika
2
of green laurel branches bearing small red berries, joined at the base by a red
Tudor rose with a white center and green leaves.
Symbolism: The darker purple sections stand for sovereignty; the lighter lavender
represents bravery. The boar, known for charging without hesitation, reflects
House Vikaʼs fearsome nature: if triggered, they turn feral and willing to do
anything to survive. Wild boars are also commonly found in House Vikaʼs territory
around Haleker. The laurel wreath symbolizes victory, endurance and honor. The
red rose represents passion and bloodline.
Motto: “The Truth Shall Prevail Above All Lies.”
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Military strength, fleet power, trade influence, fear and intimidation. House Vika is
generally powerful, with decent influence in every aspect of Aicruean life.
Internal Power Structure
House Vika believes the strongest should lead. To be the head of the family or
hold power within the house, you need to be powerful and strong. It doesnʼt
matter if you are a man or woman, as long as you can fight, you have power.
Military Forces
House Vika is ranked number one in Aicruae for military strength, commanding
two exclusive military organizations:
The Iveraʼs, A mercenary force of 270,000 men, working exclusively for House
Vika.
The Swords of Mertyeria, 40,000 men, also working exclusively for House Vika.
Combined: 310,000 soldiers. This force was so large it rivaled the crownʼs own
military, which is precisely why King Darien arranged the marriage alliance.
Lands & Income
Seat: The town of Haleker in Eastern Aicruae (their Dukedom seat).
House V ika
3
Key industries: Trade, manufacturing, and military services. Also holds a business
alliance with House Leva for salt trading.
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Patton Royal Marriage), Queen Mihai Julie Vika married King Benjamin
Lawerence Patton II, tying House Vika directly to the crown. This marriage was
arranged by King Darien Lacern Patton to ensure House Vikaʼs loyalty, as their
power had grown to rival the royal familyʼs.
House Vemer Code of Rose), Marriage alliance through Aintana Vika and Hasken
Vemer.
House Leva Business Alliance), House Vika initiated a partnership in a salt trading
business owned by House Leva.
Rival Houses
House Arvento, Ongoing rivalry.
Shared Territory
House Aedria, Both houses share the town of Haleker, occupying opposite ends of
the city. Both inflict “brutish punishments” on criminals. House Aedria is also a
member of the Council of the Forsaken.
House Culture
Religion
Rillic. Believers of Rillic hold that they were put on this planet to fuel the godsʼ
strength and give them a stronger tether to the physical/mortal world.
Traditions
Trial of the Name, Over the years, Vika children are put through tests to prove they
are worthy of their name. If they donʼt participate, start to perform badly, or fail
completely, they are disowned.
House V ika
4
Poison Immunity Training, All Vika are administered poison from the ages of seven
to roughly fifteen through eighteen, developing immunity against poison by
gradually self-administering non-lethal amounts.
Values
Military prowess, strength-based leadership, and survival at all costs. “We protect
whatʼs ours” is the houseʼs defining philosophy.
Reputation
Infamous among the other noble houses for being snobbish and too powerful.
House Vika has an estranged relationship with other houses theyʼve been isolated
because of their history of mental illness. But at the same time, the other houses
need House Vikaʼs fleet and military, so they use them as much as possible.
Common Sayings About House Vika
“Nothing is scarier than Vika at the head of an army.”
“Vikaʼs are built for war from birth.”
History
Founding (8,520 BR)
Axiker Vika, the son of a prostitute named Pokuerya, rose from nothing. His
mother had killed her abusive husband and fled to a nearby town, becoming a sex
worker to feed her three children. Two of Axikerʼs siblings died in winter. He
survived, vowed to create a respectable family, and earned a noble title for his
valor during the Battle of Summers, founding House Vika in 8,520 BR. His mother
Pokuerya chose the house name, meaning “The Gods Chosen Warrior.” She lived
just long enough to see it founded before dying at 54.
Rise to Power
House Vika began as a house of noble knights loyal to the king, but after winning
countless wars they gained recognition and climbed the social ladder. They
formed political alliances with noble houses like Vemer and Leva to secure their
position, and eventually their military power rivaled that of the royal family itself.
House V ika
5
Major Victories
The Battle of Summers (founding battle), the Battle of Little Hill, the Battle of
Bears, Bloody Winter (first recorded successful coup against the royal family of
Aicruae), the Siege of High Water, and the Battle of Rivers Point.
Notable Creations
Joyless Death, A poison made from Nerai, a toxic yellow plant. Created by Yarsi
Vika to take her own life rather than be married to an abusive cousin. Designed to
put its victims to death calmly.
“So the Warrior Goes Marching On”, House Vikaʼs battle song, composed by
Jeneo Vika on the battlefield after learning of his wife Pataryiʼs death. Played at
the start and end of every battle.
Major Disgraces
The houseʼs history of mental illness has caused isolation from other houses.
Notable disgraces include Axiker Vikaʼs “Sunset Hour” (persecuting those with
mental illness and disabilities, before suffering mental decline himself), Ceva the
Mad stabbing her brother at a family dinner, the truth behind the Siege of High
Water Vono hiding while a female soldier named Ashara won the battle), and the
cruel treatment of Yarsi Vikaʼs body after her suicide.
Eradication (7,217 BR)
After Orcusʼs death, Emperor Solis Elias Patton ordered the complete eradication
of House Vika. Before the war, House Vika had been “too militarized to eliminate
and too intermarried with the royal line to ostracize” but the twinsʼ coup and civil
war sealed their fate. The Iveraʼs and the Swords of Mertyeria were disbanded or
absorbed into the imperial military. The estates in Haleker were seized. Remaining
members were executed or forced to renounce the Vika name. The fourth oldest
noble house in Aicruae, founded in 8,520 BR, was gone after 1,303 years.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs origins to its final generation.
Pokuerya Vika (8,571 BR – 8,517 BR)
House V ika
6
“The Mother of Vika”
Name meaning: Star
Pokuerya killed her abusive husband Mihadlen Agasetire and fled to a nearby
town, where she became a prostitute to support her three children: Axiker, Belia,
and Dreskien. Two of her three children died in the winter following her husbandʼs
murder. Her eldest, Axiker, went on to found House Vika. Pokuerya chose the
houseʼs name, meaning “The Gods Chosen Warrior”, and lived just long enough to
see it established. She died at 54.
Axiker Vika (8,542 BR – 8,470 BR)
Founder of House Vika
Name meaning: He Who Is Like the Sun
The son of a prostitute, Axiker rose from nothing, vowing to create a respectable
family and not repeat his fatherʼs mistakes. He earned his noble title during the
Battle of Summers and founded House Vika in 8,520 BR. But the vow he made, he
ultimately failed. Axiker had a zero-tolerance policy for those with mental health
issues or disabilities, taking pleasure in what he called the “Sunset Hour”, target
practice against those who displayed such characteristics. Ironically, in his later
years, he exhibited the same traits he despised: found peeing on walls, talking to
himself, and deteriorating mentally. He died at 72.
Ceva Vika (8,376 BR – 8,352 BR)
“Ceva the Mad”
Name meaning: Godʼs Origin / Proof of God
One of House Vikaʼs most estranged members. Ceva had strange, eerie
“prophetic” dreams and claimed to see the end of the world coming. At a family
dinner, she stabbed her older brother Raimaeo Vika (one of her three older
brothers, Raimaeo, Xavien, and Eseraen) several times in the chest. He spent
several days fighting his wounds before dying. Ceva was 19. After a few more
years battling her mental illness, she died at 24. She is considered a stain on
House Vika and one of the key figures who cemented the reputation that all Vika
have some sort of mental illness.
Jeneo Vika (8,345 BR – 8,268 BR)
House V ika
7
“The Lord of Thousand Years”
Name meaning: Flame
Father of Sekid Vika and ancestor of Vono Vika. Known for training two successful
generations of House Vika generals, Sekidʼs generation and young Dexonaʼs
generation. His greatest legacy is the creation of House Vikaʼs battle song “So the
Warrior Goes Marching On,” composed on the battlefield after receiving news of
his wife Pataryiʼs death during one of his campaigns. In his final days, Jeneo
hummed the song every day while looking out the window. Full song and
performance details below.)
Sekid Vika (8,299 BR – 8,227 BR)
“The Great Warrior of Haleker”
Name meaning: Stranger
The greatest fighter of House Vika. He never lost a fight and was willing to get
bloody for his family, he pioneered the houseʼs defining philosophy of “we protect
whatʼs ours.” But what set Sekid apart was that he didnʼt take pleasure in killing.
He was a gentle man, perhaps too gentle for his own good. with a deep hatred of
blood, which contradicted his role as a knight and warrior. He believed in honor
and a divine code of conduct. Sekid won 47 battles over his 72 years, the most
notable being the Battle of Rivers Point, where he invented a battle strategy called
the Fox Maneuver (also known as the Great Ambush).
Dexona Vika (8,286 BR – 8,248 BR)
“The Champion of Little Hill”
Name meaning: Plant
The first female highborn general recorded in history. Before her, no noble lady
had wielded a sword and guided an army. Dexona was incredibly strong-willed
and earned many victories that brought honor to House Vika, including the Battle
of Little Hill, the Battle of Bears, and Bloody Winter, the first recorded successful
coup against the royal family of Aicruae. She died at 38 at the Battle of GreyNest,
one of the only battles she ever lost. Her body was returned to her family with her
hair shaved and her neck chopped nearly through. She was buried on the familyʼs
land in Haleker.
House V ika
8
Aintana Vika (8,270 BR – 8,183 BR)
“The Jewel of House Vika” | “The Winter Rose”
Name meaning: Of a Bright Pink Hue
Aintana married Hasken Vemer, son of the great warrior Ualvo Vemer, at age 17,
forming the marriage alliance known as the Code of Rose. She gave him three
sons, but theirs was a one-sided love affair: she could never love him as much as
he loved her. Aintana died at 87 and requested to be buried away from her
husband, underneath a cherry tree.
Ooya Vika I & Ooya Vika II (8,007 BR – 7,967/7,966 BR)
The Conjoined Twins
Name meaning: Given by their dying mother)
Two conjoined twins born to the high lady Iayeta Vika, who died in childbirth
before she could name them both. Her last words were an attempt to name one of
the twins “Ooya” so both sisters took the name in her honor. Despite being joined
at the hip, both lived functional lives. They both married a man named Wasler, a
lesser feudal lord, though only Ooya Vika II produced an heir a healthy baby girl.
Ooya II died first in 7,967 BR. Ooya I lived with her dead conjoined twin, suffering
from the illness that came with it, before dying less than a year later in 7,966 BR.
Yarsi Vika (7,882 BR – 7,863 BR)
Creator of Joyless Death
Name meaning: Joy
An alchemist who created the poison known as Joyless Death, made from Nerai, a
toxic yellow plant. She designed the poison to take her own life after learning her
father planned to marry her to her mentally unstable, physically violent cousin,
who was twice her age and had killed his previous wife.
“I would rather die by my own hands than by that of a drunken man you all
should have me call my husband.”
She succeeded. Upon her death at 19, her body was not buried on family land but
laid to rest in the ocean. The words “foolish daughter” were engraved on her
forehead. Before her death, she had one child out of wedlock, supposedly by the
House V ika
9
King of Aicruae, a child named Tacah, who died in infancy two months after birth.
She gave birth to Tacah at 16; the supposed father would have been 25.
Vono Vika (7,496 BR – 7,429 BR)
“The Bloody Prince of the Damned Vika”
Name meaning: Fearless
Son of House Vika hero Vasernio Vika. Vono was a terrible man who had multiple
wives and bastards. Behaving in similar sportsmanship as his ancestor Axiker
Vika. His most notable “accomplishment” is the Siege of High Water, though the
truth is that Vono didnʼt win it. A female soldier named Ashara did. During the
siege, Vono was hiding over three miles from the battlegrounds. He had everyone
who participated on House Vikaʼs behalf killed except Ashara, whose tongue he
ripped out so she couldnʼt tell anyone the truth. He then forced her to bear five of
his children, saying she was “too fierce and needed to be taught the feminine duty
of being a wife and mother.” Ashara would go on to have seven more of his
children, twelve total, not counting stillbirths (seventeen pregnancies altogether).
She was the only one of Vonoʼs wives he didnʼt kill and whose children lived to
adulthood. Vono claimed he liked how much Ashara looked like him, saying “it was
like having sexual relations with himself.” Ashara is an ancestor of Iris and Orcus,
who bear a resemblance to her.
Duke Rarielo Vika (7,318 BR – 7,252 BR)
Duke of Vika | Father of the Vika Queen
Name meaning: One of Many Blessings
Father of Lemalen Vika and Queen Mihai Julie Vika. Arranged his daughterʼs
marriage to Prince Benjamin (later King Benjamin II) to cement the Vika-Patton
alliance. His death at 66 created a power vacuum in House Vikaʼs leadership and
removed the moderating influence that had kept the marriage alliance stable. Duke
Rarielo died suspiciously, from poisoning.
Lemalen Vika (7,285 BR – 7,262 BR)
Heir to the Dukedom
Name meaning: Gift Given Unto Thee
House V ika
10
Older brother of Mihai Julie Vika by three years. As heir apparent, he would have
inherited House Vika and commanded its military forces. He died in an ambush
one month before his sisterʼs wedding at age 23, leaving Mihai as Duke Rarieloʼs
only surviving child. His death was never solved. Some whispered it was
orchestrated by those who wanted the Vika-Patton alliance to fail. His death
ensured House Vika would eventually pass to the collateral line through Gaceqi.
Gaceqi Vika (7,314 BR – 7,258 BR)
Lord of House Vika
Name meaning: He Who Stands Alone
Duke Rarieloʼs younger brother. Father of Beazen Vika. Gaceqi predeceased his
brother, which meant that when Duke Rarielo died in 7,252 BR, leadership passed
to Gaceqiʼs son Beazen rather than to Gaceqi himself. Died at 56.
Beazen Vika (7,288 BR – 7,223 BR)
Acting Duke / Regent of House Vika
Name meaning: Ferret
Son of Gaceqi Vika. First cousin to Queen Mihai Julie Patton, first cousin once
removed to Iris and Orcus. After Duke Rarieloʼs death in 7,252 BR, House Vika
technically fell under Prince Orcusʼs control as the male heir through Queen
Mihaiʼs bloodline, but Beazen served as the actual administrator and head of
house operations. He managed House Vika through the turbulent years of Queen
Mihaiʼs decline and growing tensions at court. His death in 7,223 BR, two years
before the civil war, allowed Iris to take direct control of House Vika and its military
forces. Died at 65.
Mihai Julie Vika (7,282 BR – 7,247 BR)
Queen of Aicruae | “The Vika Queen”
Name meaning: As of the Will of Allan, the Goddess of Nature
Only daughter of Duke Rarielo. Married to Prince Benjamin Lawerence Patton
(later King Benjamin II) at approximately age 20 in 7,262 BR. The marriage was
arranged to ensure House Vikaʼs loyalty to the crown. She bore twin children: Iris
and Orcus. When her husband took Lady Emillea Hige as his concubine and
fathered a son Solis whom he publicly favored, Mihai was driven to madness, a
House V ika
11
decline described as psychosis and schizophrenia precipitated by humiliation at
court. She died at 35, six years before her husband and before the twinsʼ coup.
Iris Aleka Patton (7,256 BR – 7,218 BR)
“The Damned” | “The Lady of Sorrow” | Final Head of House Vika
Name meaning: Lovely Flower
Elder twin daughter of Queen Mihai Julie and King Benjamin II. Half-Vika by blood.
After Beazenʼs death in 7,223 BR, she took direct control of House Vika and its
armies. Seductive, violent, and deeply wounded by her fatherʼs neglect, she and
her twin brother Orcus staged a coup after their fatherʼs death, publicly poisoning
Lady Emillea while nine-year-old Solis watched. During the civil war, she
commanded the Vika forces against Solis. Killed at the Battle of Rewqo in 7,218 BR
after killing fifteen men. Buried beneath a temple of Nellebrie. She was the last
head of House Vika.
Orcus Emere Patton (7,256 BR – 7,217 BR)
“The Unlawful”
Name meaning: Teller of the Future
Younger twin son of Queen Mihai Julie and King Benjamin II. Half-Vika by blood.
Calm, cold, and analytical, the strategist to his sisterʼs fury. Sterile, he could
produce no heirs. After losing a duel to Solis in the throne room, he stabbed
himself rather than accept banishment:
“I would rather join our sister than live in this wretched place.”
Buried beside Iris at Rewqo.
Succession of House Vika
Duke Rarielo Vika, Head of House until his death in 7,252 BR.
Beazen Vika, Acting head from 7,252 BR to 7,223 BR, under Orcusʼs nominal
control.
Princess Iris Aleka Patton, Direct control from 7,223 BR until her death in 7,218 BR.
House Vika was eradicated by order of Emperor Solis in 7,217 BR. No succession
followed.
House V ika
12
“So the Warrior Goes Marching On”
Composed by Jeneo Vika on the battlefield after learning of his wife Pataryiʼs
death. Played at the start and end of every House Vika battle.
Verse 1
She fell while I was far from home,
No hand of mine to hold.
The gods gave word, the gods gave none
So the warrior goes marching on.
Chorus:
March on, march on, the sun still burns,
March on, march on, till I return.
For her bones lie cold and her voice is gone
So the warrior goes marching on.
Verse 2
My children call across the hills,
I hear them in the wind.
Iʼll keep them whole, Iʼll keep them fed
So the warrior goes marching on.
Chorus
Verse 3
When steel meets steel, Iʼll see her face,
When blood runs hot, her name.
I swore to find her, life or death
So the warrior goes marching on.
Final Chorus (slower, heavier):
March on, march on, the sun still burns,
March on, march on, till I return.
House V ika
13
This soldier, this husband, this hollow man
So the warrior goes marching on.
Performance Notes
Performed at 74 BPM a slow, deliberate pace that lets soldiers pound shields or
stomp in unison. Opens with a single war horn, blown low and long, signaling the
army to silence before the first verse. War drums carry the rhythm throughout,
their deep boom marking each beat across thousands of voices. The drums never
stop from first verse through final chorus, symbolizing the warrior who keeps
marching regardless of grief. During chorus sections, the drums intensify with a
double-hit on “march on, march on,” giving soldiers a natural point to strike
shields or stamp feet.
In formal ceremonies at Haleker, a bowed low-string instrument joins the drums,
playing a single sustained note beneath each verse that swells during the final
chorus. The low-string instrument is never used on the battlefield, only at
funerals, victory feasts, and the annual remembrance of Pataryiʼs death. The song
ends as it begins: the drums fall silent, and the war horn sounds once more,
holding its note until breath runs out.
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
Military dominance (ranked #1 in Aicruae), commanding two exclusive military
organizations, war victories across centuries, fierce warriors bred from childhood,
self-preservation instincts, wealth, trade influence, and the defining ethos: “We
protect whatʼs ours, at all costs.”
What They Lack
Social acceptance, trust from other houses, internal family stability.
Vulnerabilities
A history of mental illness running through the bloodline, isolation from other
noble houses, internal family dysfunction, and the ever-present risk of their own
members turning volatile.
House V ika
14
Role in Narrative
Book Appearances: Book 1 A Tale of a Thousand Songs) primarily through Queen
Mihai Julie and her children Iris and Orcus.
Plot Significance: House Vikaʼs power and the marriage alliance to House Patton is
a root cause of the civil war. The breakdown of the Benjamin-Mihai marriage and
Benjaminʼs preference for Solis over the Vika-blooded twins triggers the conflict
that reshapes Aicruae.
Key Members in Story: Queen Mihai Julie Patton (deceased before the main story,
but heavily referenced), Princess Iris Aleka Patton Vika blood, major antagonist),
and Prince Orcus Emere Patton Vika blood, major antagonist).
Cross-References

Why They Matter
House Y ailk

TBD
Note: House Yailkʼs Nationalist ideology, with its motto “Destroy our enemies and
aid our people,” stands in sharp contrast to the actions of Natav Yailk, who sold
out Vikitsv to Solis to save himself. The irony is built into the canon: a house that
preaches destroying enemies and aiding its people produced a man who did the
opposite.)
Heraldry
Crest: A dramatic saltire of blue upon white, with a fierce black dragon displayed
at the center. The dragonʼs red tongue is extended and its wings are spread wide
in a posture of absolute dominance.
Symbolism: The dragon, the most powerful and terrible of heraldic beasts,
embodies their uncompromising motto: “Destroy our enemies and aid our people.”
It represents both the devastating force they bring against foes and the protective
majesty they extend over those under their care. The saltire X-shaped cross)
suggests conflict, crossroads, and decisive action. The contrasting blue and white
fields represent the duality of their purpose: the purity of protection and the
righteous fury of destruction. The dragon positioned at the intersection
symbolizes their role as the fulcrum point between mercy and vengeance, always
poised to act in service of their people.
Motto: “Destroy Our Enemies and Aid Our People.”

The Fall of Vikitsv (~7,214 BR)
Natav Yailk of Torad was set to become the next Grand Sorcerer of Vikitsv after

entries.title: House Yurea
entries.text:
House Yurea
House Yurea
“LIGHTING THE PATH”
Quick Facts
Status: Viscount/Viscountess Solisʼs Era)
Origin: Southern Aicruae
House Name Meaning: Ruler of the Hill
Founded: 8,209 BR
Founder: Millaursa Yurea
Seat: Basar Tari, Southern Aicruae (shared with House Vemer)
Faction: Common People Faction
Symbol: Beacon
Colors: Green Hope, Growth) & Blue Constancy) & Gold Glory, Guidance)
Wealth: 99,000 Rern
Military: Weak (merchant-based family with little military strength. “Itʼs the only
real thing they lack.”)
Religion: Barqeten (sub-religion of the Circle of Eternal Light)
Theme Song: “Live Like Legends” by Ruelle
Status By Era
Pre-Empire Era: Viscount/Viscountess. Founded in 8,209 BR by Millaursa Yurea in
the town of Basar Tari, Southern Aicruae.
Solisʼs Era: Viscount/Viscountess. Jaifey Yurea rises to General of the Second
Army. His daughter Tixsei becomes queen after Estericaʼs death.
Crandonaʼs Era: TBD
Minaraʼs Era: TBD
Why They Matter
House Y urea
1
House Yurea is a family of merchants and inventors in a world that runs on
swords. They have almost no military power, and thatʼs the one thing everyone
notices. But what they do have is ideas. Millaursa Yurea created the Godʼs Trial
skill tests for every job in the kingdom. She built a matchmaking system that raised
the kingdomʼs birthrate by 90% and earned the royal familyʼs protection through
the Aursa Bill. She started a clothing business thatʼs generated over 10,000 Rern
since its founding.
Then thereʼs the family itself. Behind the innovations, House Yureaʼs internal
politics are vicious. Variae, the rightful heir, was banished at sixteen by his
scheming stepmother Tasiye to protect her own son Denattoʼs claim. Denatto had
Variaeʼs daughter Pyhia imprisoned, her hand cut off, her eyesight destroyed, and
finally poisoned at nineteen. He killed Variae with Baseik Fever. And then Denattoʼs
own son Soinis, the boy he locked in a dog cage every night from ages six to ten,
poisoned him right back.
By Solisʼs Era, the house produces Jaifey Yurea, a military genius whose
knowledge surpasses even the emperorʼs. He becomes a kingmaker who canʼt
make his own king, and his daughter Tixsei fills the void left by Estericaʼs death as
the political solution to a personal loss. A merchant family with no army somehow
places a queen on the throne. Thatʼs House Yurea.
Heraldry
Heraldry
The Crest: A shield-within-shield composition. The outer field is deep forest
green, while a secondary escutcheon sits at the center with curved, cloud-like
edges in soft periwinkle blue. Rising from a small patch of green ground within the
inner shield is a golden beacon: a tall tripod structure of dark metal supporting a
brazier from which bright yellow-gold flames leap and curl upward. The fire is
stylized with flowing, almost liquid tendrils of flame.
Symbolism: The beacon is the whole identity of House Yurea pressed into a single
image. Millaursa Yurea didnʼt come from nobility. She came from ideas. The Godʼs
Trial, the matchmaking system, the clothing store, jobs for women who had
nothing. She built a fire where there wasnʼt one and made people follow the light.
The beacon on this crest isnʼt a memorial. Itʼs a statement. House Yurea believes
they are the ones who show everyone else the way forward.
House Y urea
2
The tripod structure grounds the flame. Three legs holding up the fire. A practical
image for a practical family. House Yurea doesnʼt have an army. Theyʼve never
had one. What they have is commerce, innovation, and positioning. Three legs.
Take one away and the fire falls. But as long as all three hold, the light burns
higher than houses twice their size. Jaifey Yurea proved that when he went from
merchantʼs son to General of the Second Army. Tixsei proved it when she went
from lady-in-waiting to queen. No soldiers. No territory worth fighting over. And
still, they put a crown on one of their own.
The green field is hope and growth. Thatʼs what the house was built on. Millaursa
believed in the future so hard she designed systems to shape it. The Godʼs Trial
didnʼt just test skills. It told people what they were good at and gave them a
direction. The matchmaking system didnʼt just raise the birthrate by 90%. It gave
young people a choice outside arranged marriage. Green is the color of something
still growing, still becoming. House Yurea has never stopped becoming.
The periwinkle blue inner shield is constancy. The steady sky the light reaches
toward. Blue is the thing underneath the ambition. Itʼs Soinis, locked in a dog cage
from ages six to ten, enduring it because someone had to protect his mother and
siblings. Itʼs Variae, banished at sixteen, coming back anyway because the family
was still his. But constancy cuts both ways in this house. Denatto was constant.
Tasiye was constant. The cruelty inside House Yurea has been just as steady as
the loyalty, and the blue holds both.
The golden flames are glory and guidance, but theyʼre also the danger of believing
your own story. House Yurea calls themselves the light. They believe theyʼre
destined for greatness. And in many ways theyʼve earned it. But the beacon burns
in every direction. Denatto believed he was destined too. He murdered his brother
and his niece and sat on the family seat for a few months before his own son
poisoned him right back. The flame doesnʼt care who it burns. It just burns. House
Yureaʼs greatest strength and their greatest blind spot have always been the same
thing: they think the fire exists to guide others. Sometimes the fire just exists.
House Colors: Green and Gold. Green for hope, growth, and the living world. Gold
for glory, guidance, and the belief that House Yurea was made to lead.
Motto: “Lighting the Path.” The motto does exactly what House Yurea always
does. It sounds humble and it isnʼt. “Lighting the Path” positions the family as
guides, as servants of a greater good. Millaursa meant it that way. She genuinely
House Y urea
3
believed the systems she built helped people. But the motto carries a quieter
arrogance too. If youʼre the one holding the torch, youʼre the one deciding which
direction everyone walks. House Yurea has always been better at leading than
they are at admitting they want to. A merchant family with no army that put a
queen on the throne didnʼt get there by accident. They got there because theyʼve
been lighting the path for centuries, and by now, everyone just follows.
Power & Influence
Source of Power
Merchant wealth, innovation, and political maneuvering. House Yureaʼs influence
comes from ideas, business, and strategic positioning rather than military force.
Internal Power Structure
Dual inheritance system (matriarchy and patriarchy-based household). Leadership
can pass through either line.
Military Forces
Weak. House Yurea is a merchant-based family with little military strength. “Itʼs the
only real thing they lack.”
Lands & Income
Seat: The town of Basar Tari in Southern Aicruae (shared with House Vemer).
Key industries: The Yurea Clothing Store (family business generating over 10,000
Rern since opening). TBD for additional industries.]
Alliances & Rivalries
Allied Houses
House Toallu Family Connection). Related through the union of Variae Yurea and
Lady Rlyana Toallu, which produced Pyhia Yurea.
House Leva Faction Alliance). Both are aligned through the Common People
Faction.
House Y urea
4
House Dajanyi Faction Alliance). Also aligned through the Common People
Faction.
Rival Houses
TBD
House Culture
Religion
Barqeten, a sub-religion of the Circle of Eternal Light. Followers of Barqeten
believe that by simply existing, they are worshipping the gods. They care deeply
about both physical and mental wellness, believing that because they were
created by god, they should do the most to take care of themselves and others to
make the gods proud.
Traditions
TBD
Values
TBD
Reputation
TBD
Common Sayings About House Yurea
TBD
History
Founding (8,209 BR)
Millaursa Yurea founded the house with a habit of creating things never done
before. She designed the Godʼs Trial, a system of skill tests for every job in
Aicruae. She made jobs for local women in sewing and stitching through the Yurea
Clothing Store. She created a matchmaking system for young couples seeking
House Y urea
5
alternatives to arranged marriages (though nobility largely preferred arranged
marriages). The King loved this system because it helped him find his wife, and he
protected it with the Aursa Bill. After the kingdomʼs birthrate rose by 90%,
Millaursa was bestowed with nobility.
Rise to Power
TBD
Major Achievements
Godʼs Trial: Skill tests designed for every job in the kingdom.
The Aursa Bill: A protected matchmaking system that raised the kingdomʼs
birthrate by 90%.
Yurea Clothing Store: The family business, generating over 10,000 Rern since
opening.
Major Disgraces
Denatto Yureaʼs murder of his half-brother Variae and his niece Pyhia shocked
high society. Pyhia was imprisoned, had her hand cut off on her fatherʼs orders
(forced by Denatto), lost her eyesight from torture, and was poisoned at 19. Variae
was exposed to Baseik Fever by his stepmother Tasiye and half-brother Denatto,
dying two years after Pyhia. Denatto became known as “the great demon” for
these killings.
Notable Members
Listed chronologically, from the houseʼs origins to its current generation.
Millaursa Yurea (8,255 BR – 8,142 BR)
Founder of House Yurea
Name meaning: Protector of Life
Millaursa had a habit of creating things never done before. She designed the
Godʼs Trial skill tests for every job in Aicruae. She made jobs for local women
through the Yurea Clothing Store, providing work in sewing and stitching. She
created a matchmaking system for young couples who wanted alternatives to
House Y urea
6
arranged marriages, though nobility largely preferred the traditional route. The
King loved this system (it helped him find his wife) and protected it with the Aursa
Bill after the kingdomʼs birthrate rose by 90%. She was bestowed nobility as a
result.
Euonia Yurea (8,170 BR – 8,102 BR)
“Aursa Reincarnated”
Name meaning: Mighty
A Der (distant relative) brought into the main family by her uncle, who believed she
resembled his mother Millaursa and would lead the family into a golden age. She
earned the nickname “Aursa reincarnated” for being as smart and calculating as
her grandmother. Her becoming heir was controversial: her uncle had two
potential male heirs, and she wasnʼt part of the main family. She became the first
female matriarch since Millaursa, roughly 70 years after the founderʼs leadership.
Euonia expanded the clothing store and opened business with Gherci.
Maren Yurea
Father of Variae and Denatto
Described as “gentle.” Marenʼs first wife produced Variae, the legitimate heir. His
second wife, Tasiye, produced Denatto. Marenʼs gentleness allowed Tasiyeʼs
scheming to go unchecked, with devastating consequences for the family.
Tasiye Yurea
Marenʼs Second Wife | Mother of Denatto
A scheming woman who saw her stepson Variae as a threat to her son Denattoʼs
claim. She orchestrated Variaeʼs banishment when he was 16 and later conspired
with Denatto to expose Variae to Baseik Fever. Poisoned by her own grandson
Soinis alongside Denatto.
Variae Yurea (8,041 BR – 7,961 BR)
Name meaning: The Variation of Me/Someone
The firstborn son from Marenʼs first wife, making him the legitimate heir. Banished
at age 16 because his stepmother Tasiye saw him as a threat to Denattoʼs claim.
House Y urea
7
He fled to Equateiy and lived with House Toallu, where he fell in love with Rlyana
Toallu. When Rlyana became pregnant, she abandoned both him and their child
Pyhia. Variae later returned home but lost his daughter to his half-brotherʼs
scheming. He died of Baseik Fever (exposed to it by Tasiye and Denatto) two
years after Pyhiaʼs death, unable to get revenge.
Denatto Yurea (8,037 BR – 7,961 BR)
“The Great Demon”
Name meaning: Oneʼs True Love / Loving Child
Son of Maren Yurea and his second wife Tasiye. Grew up spoiled due to his
scheming mother and gentle father. Had a sadistic habit of teasing his brother
Variae. Called “the great demon” for killing his half-brother and niece in a way that
shocked high society. He had Pyhia imprisoned, forced Variae to cut off her hand,
and ordered her poisoning at 19. He became heir after their deaths but only ruled
for a few months before being poisoned by his own son Soinis alongside his
mother Tasiye.
Pyhia Yurea (7,982 BR – 7,963 BR)
Name meaning: My Happiness
Born in Equateiy to Lady Rlyana Toallu and Variae Yurea. Her mother gave her to
Variae, viewing her as a disgrace to Toallu family honor. Raised as a poor person
until age 13, when her grandfather died and both she and Variae were allowed to
return to the Yurea family. Treated poorly upon return. Denatto had her
imprisoned, forced her father to cut off her hand, and she lost her eyesight from
torture during imprisonment. Extremely isolated from high society. Poisoned at
age 19 on her half-uncleʼs orders.
Soinis Yurea (7,980 BR – 7,927 BR)
Name meaning: Lover of Battle
Eldest male heir of Denatto, supposedly his prized and well-favored son. In reality,
Denatto was abusive to everyone, especially Soinis. He locked Soinis in a dog
cage every night from ages 6 to 10. Soinis endured it, often defending his mother
and siblings. He grew close to his cousin Pyhia, viewing her as a sister. At 17, he
learned of Pyhiaʼs murder. His mother pressured him not to fight his father. At 19,
House Y urea
8
after learning his uncle Variae had died, Soinis poisoned his father Denatto and
grandmother Tasiye, exposed his fatherʼs crimes, and became heir.
Jaifey Yurea
General of the Second Army
A soldier from Gherci,( not a notable member of the Aicruae branch but of the
distant Gherci branch of Yurea) and military genius whose knowledge even
surpasses Solisʼs. Becomes close with Solis, training together and discussing
military strategies (causing Mihel to question his position). Appointed General of
the Second Army. His ambition becomes apparent when he presents his daughter
Tixsei as a potential lady-in-waiting to Esterica. Leads a campaign to recapture
Nyeo successfully. Co-architect of the Maeret Orana torture program. Pushes for
the decapitation play at sea. Despite his power, he is blocked when Solis declares
Maen heir. “A kingmaker who canʼt make his own king.”
Tixsei Yurea
Jaifeyʼs Daughter | Queen
Introduced as her fatherʼs gambit. Presented as a potential lady-in-waiting to
Esterica. Grows close to Solis during Estericaʼs forced absence, embodying the
threat in Estericaʼs nightmares. After Estericaʼs death (poisoned by Haruna after
birthing Coyre), Tixsei becomes queen. “The political solution to a personal void.”
Strengths & Weaknesses
Known For
Innovation, political maneuvering, merchant wealth, and the ability to place
themselves near power without commanding armies. The Godʼs Trial, the Aursa
Bill, and the Yurea Clothing Store all show a house that builds influence through
ideas and commerce. By Solisʼs Era, they produce a military genius and a queen.
What They Lack
Military strength. Itʼs the only real thing they lack, and itʼs the most dangerous
thing to lack in Aicruae.
House Y urea
9
Vulnerabilities
TBD
Role in Narrative
Book Appearances: Book 1 A Tale of a Thousand Songs), primarily through Jaifey
Yurea and Tixsei Yurea.
Plot Significance: Jaifey rises to become General of the Second Army and
positions his daughter Tixsei as a political player at court. After Estericaʼs death,
Tixsei becomes queen, making House Yurea one of the most consequential
families in Solisʼs inner circle despite having almost no military power of their own.
Jaifey is also co-architect of the Maeret Orana torture program and pushes for the
decapitation play at sea. His ambitions are ultimately checked when Solis declares
Maen heir.
Key Members in Story: Jaifey Yurea General of the Second Army, kingmaker),
Tixsei Yurea (lady-in-waiting turned queen).

entries.title: Locations
entries.text:
LOCATIONS
CONTINENTAL OVERVIEW
Quick Reference Map - Solisʼs Era]
COUNTRIES & CAPITALS
Aicruae - Capital: Lajazer Westernmost)
Pireaynea - Capital: Civer South-central)
Gherci - Capital: Tarmet Central)
Coelum — Capital: Atriki North-central)
Equateiy - Capital: Ociyaran Northeastern highlands)
Vikitsv - Capital: Berlailia Eastern peninsula)
RELATIVE POSITIONS (From Gherci)
North: Coelum
Southwest: Pireaynea
West: Aicruae
East: Vikitsv
Northeast: Equateiy
MAJOR SEAS
The Quather Sea - Northwest, borders Aicruae
The Fetora Sea - Southern coastline (shared by Vikitsv, Pireaynea, Aicruae)
The Oberya Sea - Northeastern coastline (borders Equateiy, Vikitsv)
Henem Bay - North of Coelum
LOCA TIONS
1
OTHER NOTABLE FEATURES
The Mystic Isles - Southwest of Aicruae, isolated archipelago
Mountain Ranges - Northwest of Coelum (northern border); sharp ridges
separating Equateiy from Coelum and Vikitsv
Major Rivers - One flowing south through Gherci from near Coelum; tributaries
crisscrossing Vikitsv
CONTINENTAL OVERVIEW
Quick Reference Map - Crandonaʼs Era]
NATIONS & CAPITALS Current vs Former Names)
Tanan Grand Duchy - Capital: TBD Formerly: Aicruae) - Westernmost
Caporiolan Kingdom — Capital: TBD Formerly: Gherci) — Central, Imperial Seat
Lingia - Capital: TBD Formerly: Pireaynea) - Southwest
Hikai - Capital: TBD Formerly: Coelum) - Northeast
Uxridian Grand Duchy - Capital: TBD Formerly: Equateiy) - Easternmost
Theolisseia - Capital: TBD Formerly: Vikitsv) - Southeast
Thult - Formerly: The Mystic Isles) - South, “The Land of Sand”
RELATIVE POSITIONS (Empire-Centric)
West: Tanan Grand Duchy (agrarian, now a duchy)
Southwest: Lingia (dry, bordering wastelands)
Center: Caporiolan Kingdom Imperial Capital, administrative seat)
Northeast: Hikai (scholarly or mystical, elevated zone)
East: Uxridian Grand Duchy (powerful duchy with sea access)
Southeast: Theolisseia (wilderness, borderland forests)
South: Thult (dead zone, magical collapse)
LOCA TIONS
2
MAJOR SEAS
_
The Quather Sea - West, borders Tanan Grand Duchy
Orburydon Sea Formerly the Oberya Sea)— Northeast/East, borders Hikai and
Uxridian Grand
Duchy
Thult Southern Waters) — South of Lingia (formerly The Fetora Sea)
LANDSCAPE CHANGES FROM SOLISʼS ERA
Tanan Grand Duchy: Predominantly green and temperate; fertile with gentle
elevation. Agrarian and stable.
Caporiolan Kingdom: Transitional terrain-rolling plains, central rivers, moderate
elevation. Strategic heartland suitable for administration and overland trade. No
direct coastline.
Lingia: More arid than in Solisʼs Era; hot, semi-dry zone transitioning toward desert
near Thult.
Hikai: Alpine and elevated terrain; lighter green forests and plateaus. Likely
spiritual or arcane in culture.
Uxridian Grand Duchy: Balanced region with sea, river systems, and forests.
Powerful economic and naval region.
Theolisseia: Dense forested and humid subtropical zone. Rivers throughout-ideal
for resource extraction. Wild and culturally distinct.
Thult Mystic Isles): Now barren or desertified. Historically magical, but war-torn,
corrupted, or drained of power. The Academy may be the last remnant of past
