Basic Information: Aicruae is called the land under the sun, and Aicruae was given
this nickname because of both the beautiful climate of the region and the fact that
the country is primarily devoted to the God Razar The God of the Sun).
Capital: Lajazer
The Capitalʼs Move: Before the country was officially founded, the capital/or
central hub of the region that would later become Aicruae was located on the
edge of the territory, along the western coast or border, possibly near what is now
modern Hadiber in Western Aicruae. For a while this unofficial position of the
capital was King Hailour Layern Patton Iʼs stronghold because during The Warriors
Age, a time of scattered warlords it was the best hope of a stable location. But
once Aicruae was fully established and King Hailour Layern Patton I was able to
actualize his goal of ushering in “peace” he moved the capital toward the more
present location of Aicruae for three reasons. When Aicruae was moving towards
being a kingdom, King Hailour Layern Patton I realized that an edge of the country
capital was harder to defend, after an invasion scare the crown relocated to the
center for better military position. Though this was the official reason given, a
major part of the decision was the idea to put the capital, “on top of a giant
mountain-like cliff” because of King Hailour Layern Patton Iʼs dream of the two
panthers, he deeply believed in this dream and the original capital predated the
dream, and once Hailour had his vision he demanded relocation to the divinelyindicated site. A few had challenged him, saying his so-called dreams were the
ravings of a mad man swayed by war and momentum until the economic shift
happened. As Aicruaeʼs economy developed the center became more important
for trade routes, and a centrally located capital made more sense for
administration of a fully fledged country. When King Hailour Layern Patton I
destroyed all records before him, he sadly destroyed the old capital too, in an
attempt to erase the previous era, and unfortunately no one knows what happened
to the old capital. The old capital is likely to have been buried underneath modern
Western Aicruae, and this might explain why this region is so productive since it
was near a place that was once a center of power and received the best prefounding infrastructure because of that.

BASIC INFORMATION; Aicruaeʼs Legal Framework
Name: Justice & Conflict Resolution System.
Type: Multi-tiered legal framework. Nation: Aicruae].
Governing Philosophy: Code of Esa, “just punishment” reflects crime severity.
VILLAGE-LEVEL DISPUTE RESOLUTION ;
First Level: Family/Community Mediation Most disputes never reach any
official; families handle it themselves Village elders (usually oldest male heads
of household) gather to hear both sides mostly focused on restoring the
LOCA TIONS
27
common harmony, not punishment. Common resolutions: public apology, labor
exchange, shared meals, small payments
Example (fence line dispute): Two farmers argue over where oneʼs field ends and
anotherʼs begins. Both families meet with village elders. Oldest residents who
remember the original boundaries are consulted. Physical evidence examined (old
fence posts, tree lines). Decision is made; losing party must accept publicly. Both
parties share a meal and the matter is “buried”. If either party refuses resolution,
then it escalates.
Second Level: Temple Arbitration Local priests (who are respected and
theoretically neutral) can mediate Swearing oaths before the gods this carries
serious weight because Priests more often than not impose religious penalties:
extra offerings, pilgrimage, public penance. This is free but carries spiritual
obligation.
Third Level: Noble Court The Ashanti (land-owning noble) of the territory holds
court Cases brought here are recorded (if the noble keeps records) The
nobleʼs decision is legally binding Costs: petitioners usually bring
gifts/payments; this favors the wealthy Punishments can include fines, labor,
corporal punishment, or imprisonment
Fourth Level: Higher Noble or Royal Courts Only for serious crimes or appeals
from wealthy parties Commoners almost never reach this level Reserved for:
murder, theft of significant value, crimes involving multiple territories, anything
touching noble interests

Western Aicruae Farmer (The Aoner region)
Dawn First Light of Razar): Wake before sunrise; the day begins with a brief
prayer facing east, touching forehead then chest (heart toward Razar). Simple
breakfast: leftover grain porridge, perhaps with berries or a boiled egg (eggs
are plentiful here). Children assigned morning chores: feeding chickens,
collecting eggs, drawing water from the well.
Morning: Field work begins at first full light; planting, weeding, or harvesting
depending on season. The “sun never leaves the sky” in Western Aicruae, so
workers wear the head covering constantly. Mid-morning break for water and
dried fruit; work continues until the sun is directly overhead.
Midday High Sun): Mandatory rest during the hottest hours; this is both
practical and religious Razarʼs gaze is too strong for mortal work). Main meal
of the day: bread, cheese, vegetables, possibly fish if near a river. Napping in
shade; children might play games.
Afternoon: Return to fields. Women who arenʼt field-working handle textile
tasks: spinning, mending, preserving food. Children old enough to work
(around 810) help with lighter tasks: carrying water, chasing birds from crops.

Aicruae was a country where people believed that the gods chose the king, Divine
right used to justify brutal politics and silence opposition. Where threats to the
offical faith result in purges, exile, etc. A place where trials were used as theater,
verdicts were decided in advance; the trial was about optics, not justice. And
where repentance used to frame the state as merciful, even while killing the
accused. A place where executions were very public and used as warnings,Heads
displayed, titles stripped, bloodlines erased. Imprisoned nobility prision was often
a political holding cell, not a punishment but they were not exempt from
punishment either in cases of crimes like treason. A place where clothing marked
rank, wearing the wrong color or fabric was a crime. Pageants * Touranments
were usually politics disguised as entertainment. A place where histroy was
written by the victors,History was propaganda; todayʼs traitor is tomorrowʼs
villainized footnote.
In Aicruae, a queenʼs worth was often tied to producing male heirs, making every
pregnancy a national affair. Behind the scenes, mothers, wives, and widows
manipulated marriages and alliances, while disposable consorts were cast aside,
annulled, or accused once their usefulness ended.
Ladies-in-waiting served as informants, turning womenʼs spaces into surveillance
hubs and rumor
mills. Dowager queens could be too powerful to ignore yet too dangerous to trust.
Nobles competed fiercely for influence, with retainers displaying livery colors as

feudal loyalty outweighed national unity. On the battlefield, legitimacy was
decided, victory seen as Godʼs favor, while a single loss could erase a rulerʼs right
to reign. The crown could change hands multiple times in a generation, with kings
promising mercy only to execute rivals “for the good of the realm.” Servants and
attendants often funneled secrets to opposing factions. Dangerous advisors who
heard the monarchʼs private thoughts could become terrifyingly influential. Falls
from grace were common, disgrace, loss of titles, imprisonment in a tower, or

Population/Demographics
Gherci has a total population of 389 Million People, making it historically the
largest population of any country—once so big that other countriesʼ populations
could barely be equivalent to it. The country is  Female and  Male. This
drastic gender disparity traces back to the Battle of Relirian 7,402 BR, when
Reronʼs rampage killed men disproportionately-soldiers, village defenders, those
who tried to stop him. Gherci, as the largest and most central nation, contributed
the most troops to the coalition that fought him, and the slaughter was so total that
Gherci lost an entire generation of men. The ratio never fully recovered, and
because of this disparity the population has been steadily declining at a rate of
 annually for almost 50 years.
The people of Gherci are  of Taili origin Brown/darker-skinned people with
African and South Asian features), 30% of Nemeri origin Honey-skinned people
with Latino features), and 6% other.
Economy
Gherciʼs economy is based on trading and tourism. People mainly visit Gherci to
tour the various temples located all over the country in dedication to the gods. The
country also gets significant money from temple donations-visitors donate
generously at Gherciʼs grand temples, making this a major revenue stream. An
entire industry of pilgrimage hospitality (inns, markets, guides) thrives here. Many
higher nobles from other countries like to buy from Gherciʼs modest fashion.
Centrally located, Gherci acts as a hub for overland caravans, with goods from
Aicruae (food, raw materials) and from Equateiy/Vikitsv (luxuries, gems) passing
through Gherciʼs markets.
The currency of Gherci is called Miuae, valued at about 26 dollars each, making it
the third most valued currency in the entire world.
Culture

The Silora forest :
The Silora Forest is a forest located within Vikistv. During Solisʼs conquest of
Vikistv (  BR, Vandrea and Apharia Asleleri were deep within the
Silora Forest at the time of the attack, which is why they managed to escape
while their father was executed and their sister Enyokia was sold into slavery.
Vandrea used her magic to shield them from Solisʼs soldiers as they fled
through the forest and crossed the sea by boat.
The Silora Forest holds symbolic weight in Vandreaʼs story. At the end of A
Tale of Three Sisters, after burying both her sisters and returning to Vikistv,
Vandrea walks through the streets seeing statues of Solis and people
worshipping the Circle of Eternal Light. She eventually makes her way back to
the Silora Forest, where she grasps a dirty dahlia on the ground and hears a
whispering voice Renedin) asking her if she wants revenge. The forest where
she escaped is the same forest where her path toward vengeance begins.

Political Fractions ;
The Nationalist Party
They believe that their nation is superior to others and therefore must protect their
interests at all costs. This includes House Orana, House Renililas, House Yalik,
House Qari and some other noble houses.
Traditionalist Pary
This faction believes in the power and importance of tradition and the sacrifices
made by those who have come before them. This includes House Navefa, House
Miaran, House Iriandet, House Anasetanya, House Leum and some other noble
houses.
The Mystic Isles
The Mystic Isles are a neutral territory belonging to the gods. While it legally
belongs to Aicruae, no king has staked actual claim to it since the countryʼs
founding. Many believe that the isles are a link between the world of the gods and
the world of the mortals. Many who venture there never return, and many have
claimed to hear the voices of the gods while visiting.
The isle is comprised of only two gates. Legend says one leads to salvation and
the other leads to ruin. Supposedly the gates were created after the birth of the
twin gods Ekhasostio and Paxtino. Both gods stand at their respective gates
waiting to test any individual wanting to pass through them.

MISSION STATEMENT
“Greetings esteemed guests, and welcome to The Solisian Academy, where the
pursuit of excellence is not merely a goal, it is a way of life. We take immense
pride in our unwavering commitment to maintaining our impeccable standards,
which have remained steadfast for over a decade. Our admission process is highly
selective and reserved only for those who possess exceptional qualities, ensuring
that our prestigious institution remains exclusive and reserved for the elite. Here at
The Solisian Academy, we are dedicated to cultivating the next generation of
leaders who will shape the future. Our mission is to instill in our students the
values of compassion, integrity, and accountability, which are essential for
success in any field. Our courses are designed to challenge and inspire our young
scholars, surpassing even the most exclusive private schools. Our ultimate aim is
to create perfect lords and ladies who will grace the highest echelons of society
with their intelligence, poise, and grace. We aspire to not only
ensure our students achieve success but to embody the spirit of our beloved
Solis, who now rests in the land of the eternal sun. We firmly believe that by
nurturing our studentsʼ minds and hearts, we can create a brighter future for all.
We cordially invite you to join us and become part of the esteemed Solisian
family.”

the Fetora Sea, directly south of the Civer-Atriki border on the main continent.

ACADEMY RULES

No Fighting.
All Students are Equal Regardless of Standing; Any Unfair and Biased Treatment
will not be tolerated.
Students are required to take daily checkups and wellness monitoring.
Students are not allowed to be addressed by their position or standing while
attending The Academy.
No talking during lunch; doing so will result in a point loss.
Male and Female students are not allowed to enter the dorms of each other.
Male and Female students must not display or participate in any acts of a public
showing of love, regardless of their relationship.
No one is allowed out past 11. The barrier goes up at 1100 and if you are late you
are left.
Students must take six of the nine classes available at the school.
All mention of Emperor Solis outside of the classroom is strictly prohibited.
Emperor Goteivati Zivc Iʼs ten rules do not apply here.
To enter the Solisian Academy you must pass all three steps of the application
process.

Primary Purpose: Elite magical education and military training

Siroa Tatenʼs daughter, who passed away tragically in a fire. The Principal is a
defense system - she is designed to sacrifice her life to protect the school if she

CULTURE & CHARACTER
Atmosphere: Elite and regimented, with strict rules governing student behavior,
but counterbalanced by the camaraderie among students and the eccentricities of
individual professors. The Academy enforces equality among students regardless
of birth or standing - a notable contrast to the class-stratified society of the
broader Solisian Empire.
Local Customs: Titles and positions of standing are not used within Academy
grounds. The barrier rising at 1100 pm enforces a strict curfew. Silence during
lunch is mandatory.
Religious Sites: TBD

-

professors), the Principal, support staff, Outer Town merchants and residents
Social Classes Present: Students of all noble ranks attend as equals (per Rule 2;
commoners with exceptional qualities may also gain admission through the
application process
Notable Residents: Professor Leranoan Gevhilem (secretly Soli); the Taten cousins
Siroa and Lyanami); Professor Emisi Clyah (co-creator of the Principal)
HISTORY
ー

Major Historical Events: TBD
Changes Over Time: Appears across all three map eras Crandonaʼs and Minaraʼs),
suggesting it has endured through major political upheavals. Emperor Goteivati
Zivc Iʼs ten rules were explicitly excluded from Academy jurisdiction.

magic or cisterns.

____

135
ROLE IN NARRATIVE
-
Scenes Set Here: The majority of Crown of Glory takes place at the Academy.
Minara and Dahnyliein are sent here to study; Minara meets Nivaeran and the rest
of the core cast; the Special Division operates covert missions from this base.
Why Characters Come Here: Magical education, military training, and the social
formation of the Empireʼs future leaders.
Significance to Plot: The Academy is the primary setting where Minaraʼs
transformation from angry orphan to leader occurs. Itʼs where her allies form, her
abilities develop, and the conspiracy
surrounding the demon attacks and Macenjaʼs machinations begins to unravel.
The Special Divisionʼs covert operations against demons/monsters are
coordinated from here.
NOTES
The World Portals are located on a separate landmass to the west of the Academy
Island, connected by what appears to be a dashed pathway (possibly a bridge,
ferry route, or magical connection).
The islandʼs compartmentalized design (inner sanctum ⟶  staff/student town →
recreational café) suggests strict access control, with the barriers serving as both
physical and possibly magical boundaries.
Across eras: Appears as “The Academy” in both the Crandonaʼs Era map (south of
Lingia) and the Minaraʼs Era map (southwest of Civer). Its persistence through
regime changes suggests institutional independence or neutrality that transcends
political borders.
The Principalʼs existence as an artificial being created specifically for defense
suggests the Academy has faced serious threats in its past — and that its
founders (the Taten cousins and Emisi) anticipated future ones.

THE TRAINING GROUNDS (GAVARA CASTLE)
Location: Gavara Castle, a quick twenty-minute walk from the Solisian Academy
Description: The castle belonged to a lesser lord whose family died during the
Monstru Plague. After his death,
the castle was abandoned. Because of its proximity to the Academy, it was
“renovated” and converted into a training ground for students.
Significance: Primary training facility for Academy students and the Special
Division. Its history as a plague-ravaged noble estate reinforces the theme of
aristocratic decline in Crown of Glory.
Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4
EMILLEA HALL THE GIRLSʼ DORMITORY
Location: Solisian Academy campus
Description: The girlsʼ dormitory where Minara and the other female characters
reside and spend their time at the Academy.
Significance: Minaraʼs home base at the Academy. Named after Lady Emillea Hige,
a historical figure from
LOCA TIONS
137
A Tale of a Thousand Songs - one of the Academyʼs famous alumni connections to
the seriesʼ deeper history.
Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4
CAFE IRI
Location: An out-of-commission portal that supposedly used to lead to the world
of the gods
Description: The meetup spot for the main protagonists as they venture and
explore their world and its mysteries.
Now in the present day, it is owned by a mysterious figure named Lady Zani. Lady
Zani is actually the goddess Zopha in human form, unknown to everyone - she
gave up most of her powers to assume human form and look after her son, the
god Soli.
Significance: The fact that the cafe is located in a former portal signifies how the
gods no longer have a connection to the mortals. It also serves as a hidden divine
connection - Zopha watching over Soli from within a dead gateway to the realm
she can no longer reach.
Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4
THE GATE
Location: No fixed location - can spawn anywhere on the Mystic Isles at any given
time
Description: A moving hell dimension that brings monsters from both the realm of
the gods and the dream plane into the world of the mortals. It is essentially a
roaming rift between realities.
Significance: The big mystery of the book revolves around The Gate - no one
inside the world of the book knows why it appeared. At the end of the book, after
the Empress is defeated, Minara and the other characters believe she caused it.
The Gate is the physical manifestation of the corrupted world doors that Vandrea
damaged during A Princess in Love, now worsened by Renedinʼs influence.

👑  Tanan Grand Duchy — The Land Under the Sun
(West)
☀Formerly Aicruae. Reorganized from a sovereign kingdom into a Grand
Duchy after the empire's formation. Birthplace of the Patton dynasty
and one of two realms that holds impartial standing toward the empire.

Capital: Tericaer Name Evolution canon; Lajazer was the seat under the old
Aicruae).
Terrain: predominantly green and temperate — fertile lowlands with gentle
elevation. Agrarian and stable.
Economy: the continent's breadbasket; the granary district (the Aoner)
historically produced 48% of the world's rice, fruit, eggs, and meat.
Faith: the Circle of Eternal Light, devoted above all to Razar, the sun god —
hence "the Land Under the Sun."
Coast: the Quather Sea frontier to the west, with natural harbors and fishing

the Main Master — rivals the crown in authority.

Capital: Haleret Name Evolution canon; Civer was the seat under the old

Terrain: more arid than in earlier eras — a hot, semi-dry zone transitioning
toward desert near Thult.

the southern wastelands.

🏔  Theolisseia — The Mountain Magocracy
(Southeast)
🪄Formerly Vikitsv. The mountain kingdom and heartland of organized
magic, radiating from Mount Aicren and its Magic Tower.
Capital: Hadirel Name Evolution canon; Berlailia was the seat under the old
Vikitsv).
Terrain: dense forested, humid subtropical lowlands threaded with rivers —
ideal for resource extraction — rising to the coldest peaks in the world at
Mount Aicren.
Culture: wild and distinct; the cradle of formal magecraft and the magical
orders.

🏝  Thult & The Academy — The Southern Isles
🏜Thult — formerly the Mystic Isles. The sacred archipelago that
technically belonged to no king. Once believed to be the link between
the world of the gods and the world of mortals, the isles are now barren
and desertified — "the Land of Sand," a dead zone of magical collapse.
Thult: drawn with no political boundary; sacred and contested, garrisoned by
no one.
The Academy: the neutral island institution between the Lingia and Hikai
coasts. Before the reign of Emperor Goteivati Zivc Patton III, it was chiefly a
school for adolescent nobility; it later transformed into the empire's formal
magical-education infrastructure. It endures across every era, a sign of
institutional neutrality that transcends political borders.
🧭  How Everything Sits — Relative Positions (EmpireCentric)
Centered on the Caporiolan Kingdom, the Imperial Seat:
T h e  s o u t h e r n  i s l e s  —  T h u l t  a n d  t h e  n e u t r a l i s l a n d  o f  T h e  A c a d e m y ,  o f f  L i n g i a ' s  s o u t h e r n  c o a s t
Map of the W orld by (~1BR -50 AR)
11
West → the Tanan Grand Duchy (agrarian, now a duchy).
Southwest →Lingia (dry, bordering the southern wastelands).
Center → the Caporiolan Kingdom (imperial capital, administrative seat).
Northeast →Hikai (elevated, scholarly / mystical).
East → the Uxridian Grand Duchy (wealthy, with Orburydon sea access).
Southeast →Theolisseia (mountain wilderness and magic).
South →Thult and The Academy (the neutral, sacred isles).
The world reads as two landmasses: the western mass Tanan, Caporiolan,
Lingia) and the eastern mass Hikai, Uxridian, Theolisseia), with the southern
isles of Thult and the Academy set in the waters between them.
🚩  Canon Check — Flags & Things to Verify
⚠1 · "Capriolan" vs. "Caporiolan." The map labels the central kingdom
Capriolan, but the Name Evolution and Locations canon both spell it
Caporiolan Kingdom. Reconcile the spelling so the map matches the
bible.
⚠2 · Capitals not drawn on the map. This map shows nation names only
— no capitals. The Name Evolution canon assigns Crandona-era seats
(Tericaer, Baviet, Haleret, Osenki, Rewalen, Hadirel), while the
Locations doc still lists them as TBD. Worth locking these in and
marking them on the map.
⚠3 · The southern sea isn't labeled. Canon renames the old Fetora Sea to
Thult Southern Waters) for this era, but the map leaves the southern
waters (below Lingia and around the isles) unlabeled. Add the label to
match canon.
Map of the W orld by (~1BR -50 AR)
12
📝4 · Henem Bay is absent. The northern coastline Henem Bay in the
other eras) doesn't appear on this map, and canon notes its Crandonaera name was never recorded. A gap to fill if the northern coast matters
here.
📝5 · Duchies vs. Kingdoms. Two realms — Tanan and Uxridian — are
Grand Duchies, while the rest are Kingdoms. This tiered naming reflects
the new imperial hierarchy; worth a note on what rank each holds under
the Caporiolan crown.
✅  Strong Canon Matches
The map lines up with canon well: all six successor realms sit in their correct
positions with their correct new names; the Quather Sea (west) and Orburydon
Sea (northeast) are both correctly placed and named for the era; Thult appears as
the southern sacred isles; and The Academy sits offshore between the Lingia and
Hikai coasts, exactly where canon places the neutral institution.

entries.title: The Six Kingdoms 8,900Br 7,163 Br Map
entries.text:
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR -
7,163 BR MAP
The SIx Kingdoms 8,900 BR 7,163 BR
For nearly two thousand years, six independent kingdoms divided the continent
between them ts own laws, culture, and livelihood They traded, warred, married
across borders, and quietly despised one another, until a civil war in the west
produced an emperor who swallowed them all.
Aicruae
" The Land under the sun"
Capital: Lajazer
Founded: 8,759 BR
Dates: 8,759 BR  7,217 BR.  Solis's homeland. Came under his control 7,217 BR
(end of the Civil War), not a conquest.
Founder: King Hailour Layern Patton I
Population: 120 million
Royal House: House Patton
Note: Feudal Monarchy
Currency: Rern $20 USD
Religion: Circle of Eternal Light Razar
Parallel: Medieval France
The continent's breadbasket: wealthy, pious, and perpetually unstable. Aicruae
produced 48% of the world's food from its western farmlands while its nobles
houses schemed, bribed, and occasionally murdered their way through court
politics. The civil war that ended this era started here.
later: Tanan Grand Duchy  →  Kingdom of Lajazer
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
1
Gherci
"The Land of Eternal Silence"
Capital: Tarmet
Founded: 8,763 BR
Dates: 8,763 BR  7,215 BR. Diplomatically absorbed 7,215 BR. Renamed
Caporiolan Kingdom by Solis.
Founder: Saint Duri
Population: 389 million
Royal House: House Mava
Note: Theocratic Monarchy
Currency: Miuae $26 USD
Religion: Circle of Eternal Light (theocratic)
Parallel:  Byzantine Empire / Ethiopia
The continent's largest and most populous nation — a theocratic powerhouse
where priests outranked kings and The Teire's Main Master held supreme authority
over matters of faith. Gherci's 78% female population (a legacy of the Battle of
Relirian's devastation) shaped a society unlike any other on the continent.
later:  Caporiolan Kingdom →  Kingdom of Tarmet
Pireaynea
"The Demon's Pit"
Capital: Civer
Founded: 7,400 BR
Dates: 7,400 BR  7,216 BR. Conquered 7,216 BR. Renamed Lingia by Solis.
Founder: Deasn of Gherci
Population: 67 Million
Royal House: None
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
2
Note: Weak, country.
Currency: Brezeryiol $17 USD
Religion: Allan (monotheism)
Parallel: Medieval Southern Italy / Sicily
Founded by a seventeen-year-old exile fleeing treason charges in Gherci, Pireaynea
never outgrew its chaotic origins. Rich agricultural land went to waste under
decentralized warlord rule, earning it the nickname "The Demon's Pit" for its
rampant banditry and violent crime. The only monotheistic nation on the continent,
worshipping Allan exclusively.
later: Lingia→  Kingdom of Civer
Coelum
"The Land of Sand and Time"  "The Forsaken Land"
Capital: Atriki
Founded: 8,494  BR
Dates: 8,494 BR 7,215 BR.  Absorbed by decree 7,2157,214 BR. Renamed
Hikai by Solis.
Founder: Yuavekio the Wise
Population: Dwindled (mass exodus)
Royal House: None, line failed]
Note: Failed State
Currency: Opeali $5 USD
Religion: Mostly atheist
Parallel: Medieval Scotland / Iceland
A cautionary tale in nation form. Yuavekio "the Wise"  an ironic title for a drunken
gambler founded Coelum and promptly bankrupted it, saddling the country with a
debt to Equateiy and Vikitsv that never got paid off. Wars and plagues emptied its
villages. Its people abandoned the gods entirely. Those who stayed became known,
paradoxically, for their kindness.
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
3
later: Hikai →  Kingdom of Atriki
Equateiy
"The Kingdom of Gold" "The Land of Secrets" "Place of sin"
Capital: Ociyaran
Founded: 8,900 BR
Dates: 8,900 BR 7,167 BR . Joined the empire on its own terms 7,167 BR via
treaty War of Ociyaran ended in a draw). Renamed Uxridian Grand Duchy by
Solis.
Founder: Yemaser of House Kivier
Population: 97 Million
Royal House: House Kivier Unoffical)
Note: Oligarchy
Currency: Pel $50 USD
Religion: Circle of Eternal Light
Parallel: Republic of Venice / Florence
The oldest and wealthiest nation on the continent  a kingdom with no king, run by
the secretive House Kivier from behind a veil of banking houses and jewel mines.
Equateiy's Pel was the world's strongest currency, and its financial leverage
reached into every other nation through loans, trade deals, and the quiet funding of
foreign dissidents. Smiling in person, scheming behind the scenes.
later:  Uxridian Grand Duchy →Kingdom of Ociyaran
Vikitsv
"The Floating Land"
Capital: Berlailia
Founded: 7,945 BR
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
4
Dates: 7,945 BR 7,175 BR. Capital fell 7,214 BR. Fully pacified 7,175 BR after
forty years of guerrilla resistance. Renamed Theolisseia by Solis.
Founder: Grand Mage Verna
Population:  46 Million
Royal House: House Orana / Council of Scholars
Note: Magocracy
Currency: Kis $30 USD
Religion:  Iswan Goddess of Alchemy)
Parallel: Joseon Korea / Tibet
A mountain kingdom perched atop Mount Aicren  the coldest place in the known
world, a three-month journey to reach, and home to the only institution capable of
training wizards. The Magic Tower controlled Vikitsv's economy through the
exclusive production of magical tools no other nation could replicate. Its people
were known for their blue hair and blue eyes.
later:  Theolisseia→  Kingdom of Berlailia
Major Seas & Bodies of Water
The Quather Sea — Northwest : borders Aicruae's western coast. Primary
fishing and trade route.
The Fetora Sea: South, shared coastline between Vikitsv, Pireaynea, and
Aicruae.
The Oberya Sea: Northeast, borders Equateiy and Vikitsv. Long-distance trade
route.
Henem Bay: North, inland bay north of Coelum. Gherci's northern port access.
Continental Power Blocs
The Religious Alliance West Aicruae and Gherci  bound by shared devotion to
the Circle of Eternal Light, royal intermarriage, and extensive trade. Gherci supplied
temple wares and pilgrims; Aicruae supplied food and fish. Together they formed
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
5
the continent's dominant cultural and military bloc, though Gherci sometimes
treated Aicruae as a junior partner.
The Secular-Commercial Axis East Equateiy and Vikitsv  allied by shared
secularism, economic pragmatism, and opposition to Gherci's theocratic influence.
Equateiy provided financial leverage; Vikitsv provided magical exclusivity. Both held
Coelum's debt and used it as a pawn.
The Periphery: Coelum too poor and broken to choose sides, leaning toward
whoever held its purse strings (usually Equateiy). Pireaynea  too chaotic to maintain
coherent alliances, serving instead as a buffer zone, mercenary pool, and staging
ground for everyone else's schemes.
Mystic Isles : Nominally claimed 7,210 BR. Renamed Thult by Solis. No garrison,
no governor. Listed under Neutral Territories on this site due to its contested/sacred
status.
What Comes Next
The Aicruan Civil War 7,2227,217 BR) ended with Solis Elias Patton conquering all
six kingdoms and forging them into the Solisian Empire. Every nation was renamed,
re-bordered, and reorganized under imperial authority. Aicruae became the Tanan
Grand Duchy. Gherci became the Caporiolan Kingdom, seat of the empire.
Pireaynea became Lingia. Coelum became Hikai. Equateiy became the Uxridian
Grand Duchy. Vikitsv became Theolisseia. Even the Mystic Isles were claimed and
renamed Thult.
By Minara's Era 2,632 AR, the names shifted again  each territory now identified
by its capital city rather than its old kingdom name. The continent that once held six
sovereign nations had become six kingdoms within a single empire, each still
carrying the scars of what it used to be.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SOLIS'S CONQUEST OF THE REMAINING KINGDOMS
7,216 BR – 7,168 BR
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Synopsis: After winning the Aicruan Civil War in 7,217 BR, Solis spent
the next forty-nine years conquering every kingdom on the continent.
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
6
Pireaynea, Gherci, and Coelum fell within two years. Vikitsv's mountain
terrain enabled a forty-year guerrilla campaign. Only after fully
pacifying Vikitsv did Solis turn to Equateiy, whose six-year war with
the empire ended in a draw. Equateiy joined on its own terms. By
7,168 BR, all six kingdoms were united under a single crown.
NOTE ON PIREAYNEA'S FOUNDING DATE Canon confirms Pireaynea was founded
in 7,400 BR by Deasn of Gherci (per TIMELINE and KEY WORDS docs). The
LOCATIONS hub doc listing of 7,200 BR is an error.
NOTE ON GHERCI'S FOUNDING DATE Canon confirms Gherci was founded in
8,763 BR by Saint Duri (per TIMELINE, KEY WORDS, and Warriors' Age
overview). The LOCATIONS hub doc reference to 8,663 BR is a typo
(off by exactly 100 years).
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
7,216 BR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Event: Conquest of Pireaynea — Renamed Lingia
Location: Pireaynea (border corridor from Haleker to Civer)
Key Figures: Emperor Solis Elias Patton
Significance: Pireaynea was the first kingdom to fall after the civil
war. The country had no centralized army and no functioning government
capable of organizing a defense. Its warlords had already been exploited
by both sides during the civil war — rebel factions recruited Pireaynean
fighters with promises of loot, while loyalists bribed Pireaynean lords
to deny passage to rebels. Solis placed Pireaynea under direct military
control and renamed it Lingia. Canon confirms: "its anarchy [was]
subdued by imperial troops."
Book Reference: A Tale of a Thousand Songs, Ch. 6670
7,215 BR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Event: Absorption of Gherci — Renamed Caporiolan Kingdom
Location: Gherci Tarmet, The Teire)
Key Figures: Emperor Solis Elias Patton, House Mava, The Teire
Significance: Gherci had backed Solis financially during the civil war
after Princess Kamerida's assassination cemented their alliance. The
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
7
hub doc describes Gherci as "somewhat the senior partner" who "never
sought to conquer Aicruae" but viewed it as a "necessary counterpart."
Gherci was designated the Caporiolan Kingdom — the seat of the empire
itself — suggesting the absorption preserved some degree of Ghercian
prestige. The specifics of how this transition was negotiated are
TBD.
Confirmed by timeline: Enyokia Asleleri was later sent to Gherci to
"build infrastructure for the Solisian Empire," meaning Gherci was
under imperial authority before Vikitsv fell 7,214 BR.
Book Reference: A Tale of a Thousand Songs, Ch. 6670
7,215 BR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Event: Absorption of Coelum — Renamed Hikai
Location: Coelum Atriki
Key Figures: Emperor Solis Elias Patton
Significance: Canon confirms Coelum was "easily absorbed as a vassal
since it had no strength to resist." The country had no army, no
functioning government, and its economy was collapsed. Its two creditor
nations — Equateiy and Vikitsv, to whom Coelum owed 40% of national
earnings — were in no position to object. Duke Reasaec Kivier of
Equateiy had been beheaded by Solis in 7,217 BR, and House Orana of
Vikitsv had been burned alive the same year.
Canon describes Coelum's pre-imperial alignment: it "leaned toward
Equateiy/Vikitsv (because they owned its debt) and would likely align
against any Gherci-Aicruae bloc if pushed. But Coelum's contribution
was minimal." The renaming to Hikai "marked the formal end of Coelum's
nominal independence."
INFERRED Coelum's 40% debt payments to Equateiy and Vikitsv were
likely dissolved upon imperial absorption, as the empire would not
honor payments to nations it was conquering. Not stated in canon.]
Book Reference: A Tale of a Thousand Songs, Ch. 6670
7,214 BR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Event: Fall of Vikitsv's Capital — Beginning of Resistance
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
8
Location: Vikitsv Berlailia, Torad, Mount Aicren)
Key Figures: Emperor Solis Elias Patton, City Lord Ceval Asleleri,
Natav Yailk, Enyokia Asleleri, Vandrea Asleleri, Apharia Asleleri
Significance: Canon from A Tale of Three Sisters confirms the following
sequence:
Word reaches Vikitsv that "the King of Aicruae has gone mad"
(following Esterica's death and Harnua's execution, both 7,214 BR.
Ceval hears that Solis "is starting a war and hopes to establish an
empire in less than a month's time."
Solis arrives in Vikitsv and begins massacring people. He rounds up
all high officials.
Natav Yailk — the incoming Grand Sorcerer and Enyokia's fiancé —
had secretly sold the country out to Solis, trying to ensure his
own survival.
Ceval and Natav are both sentenced to death. Ceval briefly escapes
and lights the red torch (a danger symbol — fire can kill Vikitsv's
people) to warn his people. He is recaptured and executed.
UNRESOLVED: execution method is "beheaded" in one source, "burned
by fire" in another.]
Enyokia is spared but enslaved. Solis says she was "probably just
used by her father and fiancé." She is put into slavery to pay for
her father's "debt."
Vandrea and Apharia escape into the Silora Forest and flee across
the sea to Equateiy.
Enyokia is sent to Gherci (now the Caporiolan Kingdom) to build
infrastructure for the empire. She dies approximately three months
after arriving. Officially: deadly illness. Vandrea believes
Enyokia "was most likely burned," reasoning that illness wouldn't
kill her sister. Her body is dumped in an unmarked mass grave.
The fall of the capital also coincided with Solis's empire-wide
persecution of magic users (launched post-7,214 BR after Esterica's
death). Canon confirms this purge:
"Drove magic users into flight from Vikitsv and Equateiy"
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
9
"Created a magic-user diaspora across the empire"
"Established a precedent of state persecution of magical ability
that persisted for generations"
"Created conditions for 'black-market sorcery' in the interim"
The Magic Tower — which had been the institution that "held all the
country's power" and whose exports "no other nation could replicate" —
was stripped of its practitioners after House Orana's destruction
7,217 BR) and the subsequent purge. The physical tower was repurposed
by the empire for non-magical use. TBD — specific function.]
The Arvento-Vikitsv trade partnership that had produced Gifted Objects
was disrupted by the purge. INFERRED: the degree of disruption is
uncertain. Canon confirms "black-market sorcery" survived, suggesting
some magical practice continued underground.]
Book Reference: A Tale of Three Sisters Act 1
7,214 – 7,175 BR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Event: The Vikitsv Mountain Resistance
Location: The highlands and peaks of Mount Aicren, Vikitsv
Key Figures: Nationalist Party remnants, House Yailk loyalists,
imperial forces
Significance: Canon confirms that "Vikitsv's open opposition led to
forcible integration" and that "imperial armies eventually purged
Vikitsv's nationalist core." The word "eventually" indicates prolonged
resistance. Vikitsv's geography supports a decades-long campaign: the
country sits atop Mount Aicren (the coldest place in the known world),
takes three months to reach on average, and many have died venturing
up the mountain. House Yailk's Nationalist Party (motto: "Destroy our
enemies and aid our people") would have been among the factions
resisting.
INFERRED 40 years of resistance based on the gap between the
capital's fall 7,214 BR) and the need for Vikitsv to be fully
pacified before the War of Ociyaran began 7,174 BR. Confirmed by
Vicky as reasonable given Vikitsv's terrain. The specific military
details of this campaign are not described in canon.]
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
10
When resistance ended, Vikitsv was formally renamed Theolisseia and
placed under full imperial administration. Only then did Solis redirect
forces toward Equateiy.
Canon also confirms that by the time Vandrea returns to Vikitsv
7,2087,100 BR, she sees "people worshipping the Circle of Eternal
Light and statues of Solis everywhere" — indicating full cultural
integration had occurred.
Book Reference: TBD — referenced across multiple sources]
7,174 – 7,168 BR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Event: The War of Ociyaran The War of Coin / The War of Gesdic /
The Great Devourer)
Location: Equateiy (centered on the approaches to Ociyaran)
Key Figures: Emperor Solis Elias Patton (age 7682, commanding from
behind lines — too old to fight), Gesdic Benen (commoner, rose to
Marquess at age 32, House Kivier, the First Movement Party of Equateiy
Significance: The final war of Solis's conquest. Equateiy was the
wealthiest nation in the world, backed by the Pel (the highest-valued
currency on the continent at $50 each), House Kivier's banking empire,
and the First Movement Party — the political faction that "prioritizes
the military and law enforcement and believes that the government
should do everything in its power to defend its people."
The war earned four names:
"The War of Ociyaran" — geographic, centered on the capital
"The War of Coin" — reflecting the economic devastation on both sides
"The War of Gesdic" — honoring its most celebrated soldier
"The Great Devourer" — reflecting the extreme casualties on both
sides
Gesdic Benen, a commoner with no noble blood or connections, rose from
common soldier to Marquess during the war. The war's complexity and
scale allowed a thirty-two-year-old with no pedigree to achieve a
promotion that would have been impossible in peacetime.
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
11
The war ended in a draw. Equateiy joined the empire on its own terms,
receiving the designation "Grand Duchy" — a title that preserved its
dignity. Canon describes House Kivier as "smiling in person, scheming
behind the scenes" — consistent with a negotiated settlement that
protected their interests. Equateiy became the Uxridian Grand Duchy.
For his service, Gesdic Benen was granted lands in the Caporiolan
Kingdom (formerly Gherci) and founded House Benen. The Marquess Benen
title passed down through his line for over seven thousand years. A
distant descendant holding the same title later married the
eleven-year-old Hicksora Connorrita during Crandona's Era. Canon
confirms this Marquess Benen was "a twenty-seven-year-old man who was
given Hicksora in marriage" and that "his rank Marquess) was below
Hicksora's pre-marriage status."
Book Reference: TBD
7,210 BR
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Event: Nominal Claim of the Mystic Isles — Renamed Thult
Location: The Mystic Isles (isolated archipelago southwest of Aicruae)
Key Figures: Emperor Solis Elias Patton
Significance: Canon confirms the Mystic Isles were "never firmly
colonized by any Aicruan king" and that "local legend holds these lush
isles are a sacred realm of the gods." Canon also confirms "many who
venture there never return" and that they were "left undisturbed by
Aicruae's monarchs." Renamed Thult under the empire.
Book Reference: TBD
7,168 BR

Name Evolution Across Eras
How each territory's name evolves across the three eras. Seas that are renamed
are noted separately.
The borders of the known world have been redrawn twice since the age of
independent kingdoms. What began as six sovereign nations became an empire of
duchies and kingdoms under new names, and then was restructured again into the
late imperial order that persists into Minara's time. Below is a record of how each
territory's identity has shifted across the three major eras.

Aicruae, the westernmost kingdom and birthplace of the Patton dynasty, was
reorganized into the Tanan Grand Duchy after the empire's formation during
Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it had been renamed again to the Kingdom of
Lajazer, with its new capital at Vellin. Of the six kingdoms, Lajazer is one of two that
holds impartial standing toward the empire.
Gherci, once the largest and most populous nation on the continent, became the
Caporiolan Kingdom during Crandona's Era and served as the Imperial Seat. By
Minara's Era it was renamed the Kingdom of Tarmet, with its capital moved to Bela.
Tarmet remains the overall capital of the entire empire and holds the highest rank in
the kingdom hierarchy.
Pireaynea, long known as "The Demon's Pit" for its lawlessness, was absorbed into
the empire as Lingia during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it became the Kingdom
of Civer, with its capital at Lorne. Despite its troubled history, Civer proved richer
than expected in the late empire due to its mines.
Coelum, the impoverished northern wasteland sometimes called "The Forsaken
Land," was renamed Hikai during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it became the
Kingdom of Atriki, with its capital at Elgan. Atriki sits at the bottom of the kingdom
hierarchy, mainly comprised of farmers and low-ranking merchants.
THE SIX KINGDOMS 8,900BR - 7,163 BR MAP
16
Equateiy, once the wealthiest independent nation in the world, was reorganized into
the Uxridian Grand Duchy during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it became the
Kingdom of Ociyaran, with its capital at Zada. Ociyaran shares the second-highest
rank in the kingdom hierarchy alongside Lajazer.
Vikitsv, the mountain kingdom and heartland of organized magic, became
Theolisseia during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it was renamed the Kingdom of
Berlailia, with its capital at Zemela. Berlailia holds the third rank, home to few
aristocrats and some low-ranked magicians.
The Mystic Isles, the sacred archipelago southwest of Aicruae that technically
belonged to no king, was renamed Thult during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era,
Thult persists but has no political boundary drawn around it. Once believed to be a
link between the world of the gods and the world of mortals, the isles are now
barren and desertified.

Religion
The Divine Family Tree
The Old Gods - Born of the Great Song
Before the New Gods existed, four brothers emerged from the Great Song itself:
Mikani, God of War and Order; Poaranji, God of Strength and Sailors; Renedin, God
of Dreams and the Eternal Plane; and Haxenylian, God of Protection and Wisdom.
These four were the original divine beings, and their brotherhood would shatter
when Haxenylian broke divine law by loving a mortal woman.
The First Generation of New Gods - Children of
Forbidden Love
When Haxenylian fell in love with the mortal Lady Gaialana, their union produced
twins: Vapaz, God of the Sky, and Zopha, Goddess of the Sea. These siblings
share the same divine father and mortal mother, making them full brother and
sister. Their birth-impossible, unprecedented-triggered the War of Gods I, which
killed their father and ended the reign of the Old Gods. Vapaz would rise from that
war to become King of the Gods, while Zopha would carry the grief of their origins
forever.
The Royal Line - Vapazʼs Descendants
Vapaz married Nimlye, Goddess of Secrets and Fate, making her Queen of the
Gods. Together they have one son: Razar, God of the Sun, who stands as crown
prince of the divine hierarchy. However, Vapaz also fathered a daughter with
Iswan, Goddess of Alchemy-this daughter is Allan, Goddess of Nature. Allan is
therefore Razarʼs half-sister, sharing a father but not a mother. The relationship
between Nimlye and Iswan, given this history, remains diplomatically tense.
Zophaʼs Line
Zopha was married to Loart, the minor Old God of Wealth who defected to help
the New Gods during the war. Loart died in that conflict, leaving Zopha widowed
Religion
1
before she ever bore children. Her sons, Paxtino, God of Peace, Rebirth, and
Redemption, and Ekhasostio, God of Vengeance, Desire, and Destruction, came
later-born not from any union but from Zophaʼs tears. Myth holds that her grief
was so profound it took physical form, splitting into two opposing forces: one
embodying healing and hope, the other embodying rage and ruin. Because they
emerged after Loartʼs death and not from any father, Paxtino and Ekhasostio have
no paternal lineage. They are solely Zophaʼs children.
Iswan and Finore
Iswan, Goddess of Alchemy, is married to Finore, God of the Forge. Together they
have a son: Sielaph, God of Lightning. This makes Sielaph and Allan half-siblings
through their mother Iswan, though Allanʼs father is Vapaz while Sielaphʼs father is
Finore. The Forge-Born line represents divine craftsmanship and transformation.
The Third Generation - Razarʼs Daughter
Razar, God of the Sun, and Paha, Goddess of Horses, are the parents of Nellebrie,
Goddess of Disasters. Nellebrie is therefore Vapazʼs granddaughter and the greatgranddaughter of Haxenylian-the only known member of the divine third
generation.
Birth of Vapaz and Zopha
Lady Gaialanaʼs pregnancy was impossible. A mortal body cannot sustain divine
life - the child burns from within. Haxenylian knew this, but loved her too
desperately to let her go. So he made a bargain with his own essence: he would
split his divine nature, giving half to the child growing inside her, so the pregnancy
wouldnʼt kill her. But Gaialana was carrying twins.
The birth happened during a storm at sea. Haxenylian had taken her to a remote
island to hide from his brothers. When her labor began, the sky opened. Vapaz
was born first, during a lightning strike that split an ancient oak. The moment he
drew breath, the storm intensified - winds howled, thunder shook the earth. He
was born claiming the sky itself.
Zopha came hours later, as dawn broke and the storm calmed. She was born as
the tide pulled back, and when she cried, the ocean answered - waves rose and
Religion
2
crashed in rhythm with her breathing. Sailors three hundred miles away reported
strange tidal patterns that night.
Gaialana survived the birth. For two years, she raised them on that island while
Haxenylian visited when he could slip away from his brothersʼ watch. The twins
grew faster than mortal children speaking in sentences by six months, walking by
eight. Their divine nature asserted itself early: Vapaz called birds from the sky to
play with him; Zopha made tide pools appear in dry sand.
Then Renedin found them. He came disguised as a traveling merchant seeking
shelter from a storm. Gaialana welcomed him. That night, while the twins slept,
Renedin murdered her - not with violence, but by trapping her in an eternal dream
where she forgot to wake. Her body simply stopped breathing.
When Haxenylian arrived the next morning and found her dead, his grief cracked
the sky. The twins, now toddlers, watched their father weep over their motherʼs
body. Vapaz remembers this - a core memory that shaped everything he became.
Zopha claims she doesnʼt remember, but she dreams of it constantly.
War of Gods I - Battle Structure
The Old Godsʼ Forces: Mikani War/Order) - led the offensive Poaranji
Strength/Sailors) controlled the seas during battle Renedin Dreams -
assassinated Lady Gaialana, fought through nightmares and psychological warfare
The New Godsʼ Forces: Haxenylian Protection/Wisdom) - died defending his
children Loart Wealth - defected from old gods, died securing the new godsʼ
victory Vapaz and Zopha - young, traumatized, but powerful
DIVINE BARRIER SECTION Create as new header section):
The barrier prevents gods from existing physically in the mortal realm, not
from acting upon it
Functions like a window-gods can reach through for blessings, curses,
punishments, but cannot walk permanently in true forms
Established after War of Gods I under Vapazʼs rule
Allows: projection of will (blessings, curses), communication through
dreams/visions/oracles, temporary manifestation to saints, influence through
followers and institutions
Religion
3
Prevents: permanent physical presence, direct divine warfare on mortal soil,
demons crossing in massive amounts
World doors on Mystic Isles are weak points where the barrier thins
Breaking it would reset cosmos to primordial chaos, merging mental and
physical realms
WORSHIP AND DIVINE POWER SECTION:
Worship affects divine power, but new gods insulated themselves via Circle of
Eternal Light
Old gods were directly fueled by worship (more belief = more power,
vulnerable to faith shifts)
New gods collectivized faith—as long as religion exists across three subdenominations, gods sustained collectively
Individual gods still feel intensity fluctuations Razar stronger in summer,
Zopha during monsoons, Nellebrie paradoxically gains power during disasters)
Order of the Pure Ones threatens gods long-term—if it grew significantly,
gods would weaken measurably
AFTERLIFE KNOWLEDGE SECTION:
Mortal knowledge comes from revealed knowledge, not speculation
Sources: Saintsʼ visions (especially Saint Duri who lived 77 years), religious
texts Zyrazithia, Tome of Renedin, Book of Purity)
Accepted as religious truth rather than empirically verified fact
RENEDIN
Title: God of Dreams and the Eternal Plane
Domains: Dreams, nightmares, madness, manipulation, the subconscious, lies that
feel true, the space between realities
Colors: Shifting grey (nothing solid), pale sickly yellow (jaundice, corruption),
black thatʼs almost purple (bruise-colored)
Religion
4
Symbols: Closed eye, Mask, Door (slightly open — threshold between states),
Moth (drawn to false light), Empty mirror (reflection that lies)
Personality: Renedin is the most dangerous of the Old Gods because he believes
his own narrative. Every manipulation, every whisper, every act of cruelty - heʼs
convinced himself it was necessary. When his brothers felt secure, Renedin
reminded them of threats. When they felt paranoid, Renedin confirmed their fears.
He needed them unstable because unstable gods needed him - the one who
understood the dream realm, the one who could see what was coming.
He murdered Lady Gaialana. Not in passion, not in battle - deliberately, to provoke
a war he wanted. He knew Haxenylianʼs love for her would fracture the peace
between old and new gods. He manufactured the tragedy that killed his own
family.
His “Love” for Iswan: Renedin is capable of something that looks like love -
obsessive focus, genuine interest, even tenderness. But itʼs always transactional
beneath the surface. He loved that Iswan was powerful enough to be useful. He
loved that she believed in him. When she betrayed him, he didnʼt feel heartbreak -
he felt cheated. She was supposed to be his.
In the Garden: Heʼs partially awake, and heʼs been waiting. Not grieving his
brothers - planning. The “lonely survivor seeking justice” act is exactly that: an
act. He wants to merge the mortal and eternal planes because in dreams, he is
god. Waking reality has rules he canʼt control. Dreams are his domain entirely.
Why Heʼs Unsympathetic: Heʼs a manipulator who plays victim. He destroyed his
own family and blames everyone else. Heʼs incapable of genuine accountability.
The Danger: Heʼs patient. Heʼs been waiting thousands of years in the Garden.
And heʼs had nothing to do but think and plan and whisper to anyone whoʼll listen.
Worship Note: The Brotherhood of Westwinds believes Renedin was wrongfully
imprisoned for trying to “preserve the old ways.” Their sacred text, the Tome of
Renedin, is likely influenced by dreams heʼs sent from the Garden - heʼs been
recruiting from his prison.
POARANJI
Title: God of Strength and Sailors
Religion
5
Domains: Physical might, the sea (as dangerous force), storms, endurance,
brotherhood among men, laborers
Colors: Dark navy (deep sea), rust orange (weathered metal/rope), salt white
Symbols: Anchor, Rope (knotted), Trident, Clenched fist raised, Breaking wave
Personality: Poaranji was brute strength personified — not stupid, but
uncomplicated. He valued loyalty, physical prowess, and directness. He didnʼt
scheme; he didnʼt manipulate. When Mikani said the new gods were a threat,
Poaranji believed him. When Renedin whispered that war was coming regardless,
Poaranji prepared for it. He was a follower, not a leader, and he followed the wrong
voices.
His Death: Zopha drowned him. A god of sailors and the sea, drowned by a
goddess who became the sea through grief. He couldnʼt swim against a current
made of divine sorrow. He was strong, but strength means nothing against an
ocean.
Why Heʼs Partially Sympathetic: He wasnʼt cruel - he was used. He trusted his
brothers and they led him to destruction.
The Tragedy: Poaranji probably would have accepted the new gods if anyone had
bothered to talk to him directly. He just wanted to belong to something, and his
brothers gave him that belonging.
Worship Note: The Brotherhood venerates him as the patron of working men -
sailors, laborers, soldiers. “Strength in brotherhood” is their reading of him,
ignoring how that brotherhood led him astray.
MIKANI
Enhanced Domains: Battle, military discipline, hierarchy, conquest, law through
force, glory
Colors: Iron black, blood red, steel grey
Symbols: Sword (pointed downward — stabbed into ground, claiming territory),
Fist, Helm, Banner/standard, Chain of rank
Personality: Mikani believed in order - but his order. He was the eldest of the Old
Gods, and he saw the birth of Vapaz and Zopha (new gods, a new kind of god) as
a threat to everything heʼd built. He wasnʼt entirely wrong - they did overthrow
him. But Mikaniʼs response was disproportionate. He didnʼt try to integrate the new
Religion
6
gods; he tried to destroy them before they could grow. He was rigid where
flexibility might have saved him. Proud where humility might have earned allies.
Why Heʼs Unsympathetic: He chose war over adaptation. He saw children as
threats to be eliminated rather than family to be welcomed.
The Complexity: Mikani wasnʼt evil — he was afraid. Heʼd fought to establish order
in a chaotic cosmos, and these new beings threatened to undo everything. His
fear made him cruel. Renedin saw this fear and fed it.
Worship Note: The Brotherhood venerates him as “true order” - strength that
doesnʼt compromise. They see Vapazʼs rule as weakness pretending to be
civilization.
LOART
Title: Minor God of Wealth
Domains: Prosperity, ambition, trade, treasure, generosity, social climbing,
devotion
Colors: Rich copper (not gold - thatʼs Razarʼs), deep green (money/envy), black
(ambitionʼs shadow)
Symbols: Scales (trade/balance), Key (unlocking wealth/status), Overflowing cup,
Climbing vine, Coin with a hole (wealth that passes through)
Personality: Loart was born a minor god - barely more than a spirit of commerce.
He wanted more. When he saw Zopha, daughter of Haxenylian, he didnʼt just see
beauty - he saw elevation. But hereʼs the complexity: somewhere in his climb, he
actually fell in love. His ambition brought him to Zopha;
genuine devotion made him stay. He became generous where heʼd been grasping.
He died throwing himself between danger and the twins - children that werenʼt
even his. A social climber doesnʼt do that.
Why Heʼs Sympathetic: His ambition was human and relatable. He grew beyond it.
His final act was pure selflessness.
The Tragedy: Zopha will never know if he loved her first or loved her status first.
She chooses to believe the former, but the doubt is part of her endless grief. And
Loart can never reassure her - heʼs gone.
Worship Note: The Brotherhood of Westwinds venerates him as a god of “earned
wealth” and “rising above your station” - theyʼve stripped away the love story and
Religion
7
kept only the ambition.
Role in War of Gods I Defected from the old gods because he believed new belief
= new wealth. He died protecting Vapaz and Zopha during the final assault, taking
a blow meant for them.
Victory: Saved the Zopha and Vapaz Failure: Died doing it
HAXENYLIAN
Title: God of Protection
Domains: Fatherhood, women, children, guardianship, the home, song/voice,
sanctuary
Colors: Warm bronze (protective but warm), deep brown (earth/stability), cream
(gentleness)
Symbols: Shield, Open doorway, Cupped hands (sheltering), Songbird (for
Gaialana), Hearth
Personality: Haxenylian was the god you prayed to when you were afraid. Not a
warrior god - a protector god. The difference matters. He didnʼt seek battle; he
stood between danger and those who couldnʼt defend themselves. He was patient
with his children, present in ways other gods werenʼt. His love for Lady Gaialana
was genuine and gentle - he didnʼt desire her beauty or power, he simply loved
how she sang. That a god of protection couldnʼt protect the woman he loved is the
cruelest irony. His death holding the line for Vapaz and Zopha was completely in
character - he died as he lived.
Why Heʼs Sympathetic: He was a good father. He loved softly. He died for his
children without hesitation.
The Tragedy: His son Vapaz became a distant, politically calculating king.
Everything Haxenylian stood for - warmth, presence, protection of the vulnerable
- faded from divine culture after his death.
Role in War of Gods I Died holding the line so his children could reach safety. His
last act was pushing Vapaz and Zopha through a barrier he couldnʼt follow
through. He faced Mikani knowing he would lose, buying time.
Victory: Bought time for victory Failure: Died without seeing it

facing east so he could watch the sunrise every morning. He declared himself
“Razarʼs Chosen” and demanded his subjects bow to him at dawn as they would
bow to the sun. Razar did not appreciate this. One morning, the sun rose
everywhere except over Tavethʼs palace. His kingdom had daylight; his throne
room stayed dark. For seven days, shadows clung to Taveth while his subjects
walked in light. Taveth went mad trying to find the sun. He died still searching.

Major Myths: The Wrath of Fire: During the time of sin, a group of women stole an
offering from Razarʼs temple-a tiny sun-shaped jewel-and cast it into a lake as an
offering to Zopha, whom they deemed more worthy of worship. Razar, already
harboring a strained relationship with his aunt Zopha, did not take kindly to this
transgression. To punish them, he covered the earth in eternal sunlight for
seventy days. Crops and lakes dried up; many of Zophaʼs followers perished.
When the women came pleading, he said only: “Ask your mighty goddess to save
you.” They prayed ceaselessly, but Zopha-still grieving Loart and believing the
punishment fit their crime-did not intervene. Only after the women died did Zopha
urge her brother Vapaz to stop Razar. Why the Songbird Sings at
Dawn: Before Razar claimed the sun, mornings were silent and dark. A mortal
king, seeking to comfort mortals afraid of the night, worked with the first songbird
to create a song taught to sing just before dawn. The song was a promise: “Light
returns. Always, light returns.” When Razar heard the songbird, he was moved by
its faith and decreed that from that moment, his sun would rise without fail each
day, so the songbirdʼs promise would never be broken.

Major Myths:Allan of the Earth: The goddess Allan is said to have been “born of
humansʼ love for the earth”-though in truth, she is the daughter of Vapaz and
Iswan. The mythic version conceals her true parentage for theological reasons.)
Allan was born from flowers, trees, and grass-the embodiment
of everything pure and right with the earth. For the longest time, she loved
humans and nature equally. One day, Allan took the form of a deer and ventured
into a human forest, making friends with animals and running through fields in
bliss. When night fell, humans with pitchforks came searching for a wolf. They
burned trees, killed animals, and polluted the air. Allanʼs power weakened, but she
still approached them to protect a small wolf pup they had caught. “I am the
goddess Allan,” she told them—but they saw only a deer. “What you are doing is
wrong,” she said, but they were hungry and disillusioned and ignored her. One
man struck her stomach with his sword. She pleaded again, but they struck blow
after blow. With each wound, the goddess lost more of herself. They left her
bleeding to focus on the wolf pup, killing it before her, then abandoning the forest.
That day, Allan lost her love for humanity. The hatred that now festered in her
heart is said to have turned her once-blonde hair black.

Zopha wept for forty days and forty nights. Her tears fell into the ocean, and

became salt, saturating the ocean, ensuring that all who taste the sea taste divine
sorrow. This is why sailors leave offerings to Zopha: to thank her for sharing her
grief, making mortal sorrows seem smaller by comparison. The Myth of Ekhaostio
and Paxtino: The twin gods Ekhaostio and Paxtino were born of Zophaʼs tears.

MYTHOLOGY
Major Myths:The Mirrors of Nimlye: Nimlye possessed five mirrors said to reveal
the worldʼs secrets to anyone who looked into them. Finding their power too
dangerous, she scattered them across the earth, hoping no one would find them.
One day, pirates stumbled upon an island of treasures that housed three of these
mirrors. Thinking them merely shiny objects, they brought the mirrors aboard their
ship. When nightfall came and moonlight struck the mirrors, the pirates were
compelled to look within. What they saw was so disturbing that they went mad
and killed each other-brother turned on brother, friend became foe. By morning,
all were dead. The location of the remaining two mirrors has never been
discovered.The Mirror of Eternal Night: Centuries later, one of Nimlyeʼs remaining
mirrors surfaced in the court of a queen. It showed a world without sun and
whispered ways to summon such darkness. The queenʼs attempt to use this
knowledge plunged her kingdom into shadow. The Garden of Unspoken Names:
After the War of Gods I, the victorious new gods faced a question: what becomes
of defeated divine beings? Gods cannot truly die, yet Mikani, Poaranji, and
Renedin had been “slain.” Nimlye created the Garden of Unspoken Names-a
space outside time where the essence of dead gods exists in suspension. They
are neither alive nor destroyed, but held in eternal potential. Nimlye tends the
Garden alone. No other god may enter, for if a living god speaks a dead godʼs
name within the Garden, that entity will resurrect regardless of consequence.
Should Nimlye ever be killed or bound, the Garden would collapse, releasing all
defeated divine beings simultaneously—an apocalyptic event.

NOTES  EKHASOSTIO AND PAXTINO - THE TWIN
GODS IN ONE BODY (EXPANDED)
Ekhasostio and Paxtino are two souls sharing one body, born from Zophaʼs tears
after Loartʼs death.
They are never simultaneously conscious. When Paxtino is dominant, Ekhasostio
sleeps within their shared form, and vice versa. They experience each otherʼs time
through fragmented memories, like reading someone elseʼs journal entries after
the fact.
Transitions between them happen based on emotional state: peace, forgiveness,
and rebirth call Paxtino forward; vengeance, desire, and chaos summon
Ekhasostio.
Paxtino is gentle, patient, and genuinely kind - the god mortals want to pray to, the
one who forgives transgressions and offers second chances. He is also
melancholy beneath his kindness, knowing that every time he sleeps, his “brother”
awakens and undoes his careful work.
Ekhasostio is intense, magnetic, and dangerous. He does not see himself as evil
but as honest about mortal nature. People desire things they will not admit to
wanting; Ekhasostio grants what they are too afraid to ask for aloud.
As “Soli” in mortal form during A Tale of Three Sisters (approximately
, the post-War of Gods II era), Ekhasostio and Paxtino function as a
merged entity - two aspects of one being who can separate or merge. Soli is the
merged form controlling both aspects. This is the guise in which they meet
Apharia. NOTE This “Soli” is a completely different person from Emperor Solis
Elias Patton. The twins are associated with the gates/world doors because their
birth resonated with the weak points in Vapazʼs barrier, making the doors
navigable. But they do not literally stand guard there - that is a religious legend
mortals created to explain why the Mystic Isles feel strange.

MYTHOLOGY
Major Myths: Iswan made the bargain with Grand Mage Verna that created mortal
magic. Verna wished for the power to create spells, and Iswan was bound by the
oath of Memiet to grant his wish after receiving a portion of his soul. This bargain
is the origin of all magical ability in the world-making Iswan, whether intentionally
or not, the divine source of mortal magic.The oath of Memiet states that if a god
does not grant the wish of their follower after receiving their soul, the god shall
cease to exist. This forced Iswan to grant Vernaʼs wish despite the destruction it
would cause.
The Lie That Saved the World: The commonly known “First Divine Law”-
prohibiting mortal-immortal unions-is attributed to Vapaz.After Haxenylian died for
loving a mortal, Iswan approached Vapaz with an ultimatum: “If you forbid love
between mortals and immortals, you prevent future wars. But you also declare
Religion
34
love itself dangerous, and gods will grow cold. I offer an alternative: let mortals
become something more.” She proposed creating Saints-mortals granted
temporary divine power without becoming gods-to satisfy mortalsʼ desire for
divine connection without producing demigod offspring who could challenge the
pantheon. Vapaz agreed. ( but Iswan had a secret purpose: she intended Saints to
eventually replace gods entirely, believing mortals more adaptable and less prone
to the pride that caused the War of the Gods. Some theologians argue the entire
Saint system was Iswanʼs long-term plan to obsolete the divine order. This is a
secret plan not part of the official myth that only the goddess Iswan knows.)
People of the Mountain: Those minor gods who believed Vapaz was wrong
gathered atop a high mountain country called Vikistv. For centuries they waited,
repopulating only amongst themselves. It wasnʼt until the great sorcerer Verna
struck a bargain with Iswan: “Take my blood and soul, all that I have to divinity,
and create-and we shall honor you, we shall never aspire to divinity again.” Iswan
agreed. She had originally loved Renedin but took the side of the new gods
during the war.) The magic she gave them corrupted their souls, made them
neither divine nor mortal-they could not be hurt by normal means, but sun and fire
wounded them greatly. Iswan convinced Vapaz to allow this, for he and his son
controlled the sky, and he believed the People of the Mountain would be puppets
because of their vulnerability to sunlight.

RELIGIOUS ANOMALY COELUMʼS ATHEISM
STATUS
Nation: Coelum (“The Forsaken Land”) Religious Classification: Mostly atheistic
How Viewed by Neighbors: A tragic anomaly born of extreme suffering
ORIGIN
Historical Cause: After enduring plagues, famines, and abandonment by its
ruling class, the people of Coelum lost faith in the gods “who they say
abandoned them to die.”
Previous Practice: Coelum may have once followed the Pantheon (perhaps under
Yuavekio they nominally worshiped like Gherci), but over time shrines fell into
disuse.
Nature of Rejection: This atheism was born of despair rather than philosophy-a
collective trauma response to extreme suffering. Many Coelumites came to view
religion as a cruel joke.
CURRENT PRACTICE
Festivals: Fewer festivals or holidays; only practical seasonal events (planting if
any, harvest if any) observed without ceremony
Alternative Observance: Ancestor remembrance may have replaced formal
worship
Attitude Toward Foreign Religion: Coelumʼs people didnʼt respect holy figures from
other nations, sometimes causing friction when pilgrims passed through
SIGNIFICANCE
Coelum stands as the only known atheistic society on the continent.
Neighboring nations view it with pity rather than hostility-understanding the
atheism as a symptom of catastrophic suffering rather than deliberate heresy.

The Order of the Pure Ones
Origin and Founders: The Order of the Pure Ones was founded around ,
emerging out of the massacre that followed the deaths of early saints. Unlike the
other religions, it rejects worship of gods entirely and venerates saints as “pure
vessels.” This is why its followers were targeted by King Viake in the Massacre of
Light. According to legend, a devout woman named Naya of Enaner, a descendant
of Saint Aliiruskʼs murdered family, gathered survivors and wrote the Book of
Purity.
Beliefs: The Pure Ones teach that humanity must become holy enough to replace
the gods. Their central tenet is the “Four Abstinences”: abstaining from violence,
from consuming animal flesh, from reproduction outside designated holy unions,
and from magical practices. They view the gods as cruel (echoing the gods of
oldʼs contempt for mortals) and believe the saints proved that mortals can surpass
divinity.
Relationship with Gods/Humans: Members secretly mourn the saints slaughtered
in the Massacre of Light and hold weekly vigils. They emphasize communal
charity and pacifism; they will not fight except in defense of children. This
pacifism partly explains why they were persecuted.

Noirta and the First Song
Before gods, before mortals, before the world was the world or the sea was the
sea, there was only Noirta. Noirta is the first song-not a song sung by anyone, not
a song created for a purpose. It simply is, and always has been, and always will
be. It is the fabric of time and power, the endless cycle of souls and energy, the
force that makes existence possible. Death is but a pause in a very long song.
There is no creator deity in this cosmology. No grand architect. No parent of the
gods. Just the Song, cycling eternally, and the patterns that emerged from it.
The Crystallization of the Old Gods
The four brothers did not have parents. They were not born in any conventional
sense. They crystallized from Noirta as the cosmosʼs first and most powerful
expressions-like dew forming on grass at dawn. Inevitable. Emergent. Uncreated.
The Song played, and from that playing, consciousness condensed. The universe
had needs, and those needs took shape.
The brothers know this about themselves. They are aware that they emerged from
the same primordial chord, that they are fragments of a single original response to
existence.
Each brother crystallized in response to something the early cosmos required:
Renedin emerged because existence needed a space between states-dreams, the
threshold between waking and sleeping, between reality and possibility. Mikani
crystallized because the growing cosmos needed structure, law, boundaries.
Without him, reality would have remained formless potential. Poaranji emerged
Religion
68
because things existed that could be destroyed, and the cosmos needed a force
that could push back, resist, endure. Haxenylian came last, because once the
others existed, the cosmos needed someone to protect what had been created.
The Original Harmony
In the beginning, the four brothers existed in balance. Their domains
complemented rather than competed-structure and force, dreams and protection,
each playing its part in a cosmos that hummed with purpose. They were like
instruments in a chord: distinct voices creating something greater than any
individual note. This harmony was not enforced. It was natural. The Song played
through them, and they played through each other, and the cosmos was whole.
What Mortals Changed (  )
The brothersʼ harmony lasted until mortals learned to believe. Around ,
during an age of constant war, mortal belief began to shift the fabric of reality
itself. The gods had always drawn power from Noirta, but mortal worship created
something new-a feedback loop where belief shaped divinity and divinity shaped
belief.
This is how new gods became possible. Vapaz and Zopha were not just the
children of Haxenylian and Lady Gaialana. They were new gods, a concept that
did not exist until their birth, because mortal belief made room for them. They
were born of hybrid forces: divine parentage, shifting mortal belief, and
Haxenylianʼs love for a human woman.
The Threat the New Gods Posed
From Mikaniʼs perspective, Vapaz and Zopha were noise-disruptions to the
original harmony. The Old Gods had emerged from Noirtaʼs first song. They were
primordial. Foundational. The New Gods emerged from something different: mortal
belief, changing needs. They were born of hybrid forces the original cosmos had
not called for.
Mikani felt fear. He had fought to establish order in a chaotic universe, and these
new beings threatened to undo everything. Renedin saw Mikaniʼs fear and fed it,
whispering that war was coming regardless, that the children would eventually

Only Haxenylian stood apart. Only he saw his children as family rather than threat.
And so the brothers who had once been a single chord turned against each other.
Renedinʼs Goals
Renedin now waits in the Garden of Unspoken Names, partially awake, planning.
His goal is not destruction for its own sake. He wants to unmake the additionsstrip away the barrier, the New Gods, the whole messy overlay that came after the
original harmony. Return reality to the state where the Song played uninterrupted,
where he and his brothers were the only voices that mattered.
In his mind, he is not the villain. He is the restoration. He wants to go home.
Breaking the barrier would reset the cosmos to primordial chaos, where Renedinʼs
domain of dreams and the mental realm would have equal footing with physical
reality. In dreams, he is god. In the pure Song, before mortals complicated
everything with their belief and their stories and their capacity to change things,
he was part of something whole. That is what he wants back.
In truth, Renedin is a manipulator who plays victim. He destroyed his own family
and blames everyone else. He is incapable of genuine accountability. He has been
waiting thousands of years in the Garden with nothing to do but think and plan and
whisper to anyone who will listen. The Brotherhood of Westwinds believes he was
wrongfully imprisoned for trying to “preserve the old ways.” Their sacred text, the
Tome of Renedin, is likely influenced by dreams he has sent from the Garden-he
has been recruiting from his prison.
A Note on the Saints
The twelve primeval Saints are described in religious texts as having “come before
the world was the world, long before the sea was the sea.” This is religious poetry,
not literal chronology. The Saints were created after the War of Gods I, as part of
Iswanʼs proposal to Vapaz. They are a post-war institution, not a primordial one.
Over millennia, believers embellished the origin stories, using creation-myth
language to make their Saints sound foundational and ancient. This is consistent
with how religion works in this world. The Brotherhood of Westwinds has disputed
origin stories about Oleahakʼs prophecy. The Circle of Eternal Light merged old
