FAMILY  STRUCTURE  —  THE  MATSIALI  FORM   WHERE  A  WIFE  BELONGS:  Under  Matsiali,  marriage  added  a  house  to  a  woman;  it  did  not  subtract  one.  A  wife  remained  a  daughter  of  her  natal  house  for  life  —  its  name  still  partly  hers,  its  roof  still  open  to  her,  its  men  still  holding  standing  to  walk  through  her  husband's  gate  and  ask  hard  questions  if  she  was  wronged.  She  belonged  to  two  houses,  and  both  would  bleed  for  her.  This  is  the  quiet  foundation  under  everything  else  she  held:  her  chest  was  untouchable  because  it  was  natal  wealth  in  her  hands,  not  a  gift  his  family  had  absorbed;  her  two  lists  had  muscle  because  an  entire  second  house  stood  behind  them;  and  the  half-chest  law's  "payment  for  her  time  under  their  roof"  was  ordinary  accounting  between  houses  that  both  still  claimed  her.   Pataoiut's  first  cut  was  here.  Sever  the  natal  tie  and  a  wife  passes  into  her  husband's  house  whole  —  but  as  a  permanent  outsider,  never  quite  blood  where  she  lives  and  no  longer  her  birth  family's  business.  Every  downstream  cruelty  follows  from  that  one  severance:  a
wife  charged  with  theft  for  spending  in  her  own  home,  because  the  home  was  never  legally  hers;  a  Wall  that  must  specify  "no  natal  roof  to  return  to,"  because  her  birth  house  had  become  her  only  backup  and  the  law  had  to  name  the  woman  who'd  lost  it.   THE  INTERIOR:  The  wife  ruled  the  interior  in  both  keys;  that  structure  is  ancient.  The  Matsiali  difference  is  that  her  rule  had  recourse  past  her  husband.  He  headed  the  house  and  judged  its  disputes,  but  his  judgment  was  not  final  —  a  wife  wronged  had  her  counts,  her  kin,  and  the  magistrate  beyond  him,  so  his  arbitration  answered  to  something.  And  her  leave  on  consorts  was  real,  as  set  down  in  the  consort  entry:  taken  past  her  word,  it  was  her  ground  to  walk.  Above  them  both  stood  the  Adera,  holding  under  this  key  what  she  held  openly  and  by  right  —  the  house's  elder  sovereign,  no  filial  workaround  required.  Pataoiut  did  not  dethrone  her;  it  just  rerouted  her  power  through  her  son's  duty  and  called  it  order.   THE  LINE:  The  wall  is  ancient  and  identical  in  both  keys:  the  line  belongs  to  the  wife's  children,  by  her  body  or  her  formal  adoption,  and  to  no  one  else.  A  father's  word  buys  a  consort's  child  comfort  —  tutors,  placement,  a  knighthood,  gifts  from  his  purse  —  and  never  blood.  What  differed  between  the  eras  was  not  the  law  but  the  need.  Under  Matsiali,  a  house  of  daughters  simply  passed  to  its  eldest  girl,  so  the  wife's  adoption  door  stood  mostly  unused,  a  pragmatic  instrument  for  the  rare  house  with  no  children  of  hers  at  all.  It  took  the  daughter-ban  of  36  AR  to  turn  that  same  unchanged  door  into  the  desperate  passage  of  the  later  era.  The  golden  age  was  no  utopia  for  a  consort's  child;  the  outside  was  always  the  outside.  It  was  merely  quieter  then,  because  fewer  people  were  clawing  at  the  door.
THE  TITLES:  Dera,  Ama,  Ame,  Yena  —  the  words  are  older  than  either  key.  What  shifted  was  their  weight.  Under  Matsiali  the  Dera's  authority  was  law  with  teeth,  the  Ama's  warmth  was  a  bounded  but  dignified  place,  and  the  lower  tiers  ran  thin:  rank  caps  and  a  wife's  real  leave  kept  households  small,  so  the  sprawling  harems  of  the  later  era,  with  their  crowds  of  Ame  and  Yena,  are  a  Pataoiut  inflation,  not  an  old  custom.   CHILDREN:  Daughters  were  schooled  beside  sons  —  letters,  numbers,  the  songs,  the  law  —  as  Matsiali  schooled  women  everywhere.  The  decree  of  36  AR  cut  the  daughters'  lessons  off  mid-  generation,  and  the  first  Pataoiut  generation  of  great  ladies  was  the  last  to  have  been  taught  by  right  rather  than  by  a  father's  quiet  defiance.   THE  ILEN:  see  Marrying  In  (The  Matsiali  Form).  His  honored  place  is  that  entry's  whole  subject;  here  it  is  enough  to  say  his  children  belonged  to  his  wife's  line,  and  no  one  thought  it  strange.   Era  tags:  this  entire  entry  is  the  Matsiali  key  (Era  of  Solis);  its  counterpart  is  the  Family  Structure  entry  already  set  down,  which  is  the  Pataoiut  key  (36  AR,  through  Tanan  and  into  Lajazer).    HAIR  —  THE  SOUL,  THE  GIFT,  AND  THE  LINE  (Both  keys,  with  the  divergence  marked)
THE  DOCTRINE:  Hair  is  the  reflection  of  the  soul,  and  a  gift  from  the  gods.  It  is  received  through  your  parents  and  grows  from  your  blood  —  the  living  thread  of  your  lineage,  worn  openly  on  the  body.  All  three  truths  are  taught  as  one:  the  gods  gave  it,  the  soul  shows  in  it,  the  line  carries  it.  To  damage  it  lightly  insults  the  line.  To  cut  it  deliberately  is  to  give  up  a  piece  of  yourself  —  of  soul  and  lineage  both  —  which  is  precisely  what  makes  the  widow's  offering  an  offering,  and  not  a  haircut.   THE  FIRST  BINDING:  Children  wear  their  hair  loose;  that  is  what  childhood  looks  like.  At  coming  of  age  the  hair  is  bound  up  for  the  first  time,  before  witnesses,  and  worn  bound  in  public  ever  after  —  the  binding  is  adulthood,  put  on  in  a  morning.  For  a  daughter,  the  first  binding  and  the  first  kess  land  on  the  same  day:  bound  and  braceleted,  a  woman.  The  custom  also  keeps  the  widow  legible:  every  adult  wears  the  bun,  but  only  she  wears  it  cropped  beneath,  with  the  dot  above.   CARE,  STYLE,  AND  OATHS:  Bound  and  covered  hair  is  protected  hair;  the  care  is  the  reverence.  Among  the  Taili  majority,  styles  and  braid-patterns  carry  region  and  house  —  a  grammar  of  plaits  that  a  sharp  eye  reads  like  a  badge.  And  the  gravest  promises  are  sworn  on  the  hair:  an  oath  taken  with  a  hand  to  the  head,  and  a  lock  forfeited,  cut  and  surrendered,  by  the  one  who  breaks  it.  A  person  missing  a  lock  is  a  person  the  district  watches.   THE  SHEARS  OF  THE  LAW:  Because  the  thing  is  holy,  taking  it  is  a  sentence.  The  Code  of  Esa  punishes  sacrilege  and
treason  with  forced  shaving  before  the  public  —  the  profaning  of  the  gods  and  the  betrayal  of  crown  or  house,  which  the  doctrine  holds  to  be  one  offense  at  two  altitudes,  for  the  crown  sits  inside  the  sacred  order  the  gods  built.  The  gods'  gift  stripped,  the  soul's  mirror  confiscated.  And  the  punishment  keeps  its  own  calendar  —  a  shaved  head  is  a  walking  sentence,  and  everyone  can  read  how  recently  you  were  judged  by  how  far  it  has  grown  back.  No  fine  humiliates  longer.   THE  TWO  KEYS:  Matsiali  held  the  hair-duties  over  everyone,  men  and  women  alike,  down  to  the  widower's  shears  and  the  flat  red  line.  Pataoiut  kept  the  women's  law  whole  and  quietly  released  the  men  from  theirs  —  the  widower's  exemption  is  only  the  visible  case  of  a  general  amnesty.  Under  the  later  key,  no  man  owes  the  gods  or  the  line  anything  of  himself,  and  every  sacred  duty  that  remains  is  a  duty  that  lands  on  a  woman.   [TBD]  The  priesthood's  hair  —  how  the  Danepelie  and  temple  clergy  wear  theirs;  check  the        Religion  doc  before  setting  it.  [TBD]  The  braid-grammar  of  the  Taili  —  expandable  into  its  own  entry  if  wanted.    ##  ORIGINS  OF  THE  THREE  SUB-RELIGIONS  —  THE  FIRST  CONCORD   ###  The  Question  the  Twins  Left  Behind   Aryanara  and  Vekta  built  the  Circle's  theology  and  died  without  prescribing  its  worship.  Aryanara's  writings  gave  the  faith  its  cosmology:  the  Song,  the
cycle  of  souls,  corruption  as  the  only  true  ending.  Vekta's  teaching  gave  it  a  discipline  of  living.  Neither  sister  ever  set  down  what  form  of  worship  the  pantheon  required  of  the  faithful.  While  they  lived,  their  presence  was  answer  enough.   The  second  sister  died  around  14,200  BR,  and  the  Circle,  not  yet  a  century  old,  had  no  head,  no  council,  and  no  saint  to  consult  —  the  age  of  the  Circle's  founding  falls  entirely  inside  the  long  gap  between  Galamma's  death  and  Dorthargel's  birth,  and  no  saint  walked  in  those  years  to  carry  a  verdict  down.  What  the  Circle  had  was  a  doctrine  that  forced  the  question.  The  faith  taught,  and  the  fate  of  the  Gods  of  Old  had  proven,  that  worship  sustains  divinity.  If  worship  is  a  feeding,  then  a  feeding  is  owed.  The  twins'  students  split  three  ways  over  what  the  gods  are  owed.   ###  The  Three  Answers   **Leneyez**,  sharpest  of  the  students  at  Aryanara's  eastern  seat,  argued  her  teacher's  doctrine  to  its  coldest  end.  Faith  concentrates  where  a  life  ends.  What  is  offered  wholly,  feeds  wholly.  Blood,  she  taught,  is  the  one  worship  the  gods  cannot  mistake  for  habit.  The  lords  of  the  lowlands  took  up  her  rite  within  a  generation,  and  not  for  love  of  theology:  a  faith  in  which  judgment  is  a  feeding  makes  a  lord's  power  sacred,  and  his  executions  holy.   **Rillic**,  who  studied  at  both  seats  and  refused  to  the  end  of  his  life  to  choose  between  the  sisters,  answered  that  the  offering  is  attention.
Mortals  were  set  on  the  earth  to  fuel  the  gods'  strength  and  hold  them  tethered  to  the  mortal  world,  and  a  tether  must  be  gripped,  hour  after  hour,  or  it  frays.  His  rite  fixed  prayer  at  five  appointed  hours  of  the  day,  each  held  long  enough  to  cost  the  one  praying  something  real.  Worship  that  costs  nothing,  he  taught,  feeds  nothing.   **Barqeten**,  who  kept  Vekta's  northern  seat  after  her  death,  taught  that  the  Song  does  not  ask  to  be  fed.  It  asks  to  be  lived.  A  body  kept  well  is  a  standing  offering;  a  life  in  harmony  worships  with  every  breath  it  draws.  Her  school  held  both  other  answers  to  be  confessions  of  doubt  —  as  if  the  Song  that  made  the  world  could  hunger.   The  three  rites  still  carry  their  first  teachers'  names.   ###  The  Contention  (c.  14,200–14,171  BR)   For  a  generation  the  schools  contended,  first  in  letters,  then  in  pulpits,  then  in  the  streets.  The  lowlands  saw  prayer-houses  of  the  hours  burned  at  dawn  devotion  with  the  faithful  still  inside,  the  killers  saying  the  silence  would  feed  the  gods  better.  In  the  river  towns,  a  blood-priest  was  held  under  in  his  own  offering  basin  until  he  stopped  moving.  Congregations  unchurched  one  another.  Villages  split  down  their  middles.  Through  all  of  it  the  gods  sent  no  sign,  though  all  three  schools  begged  for  one.   ###  The  First  Concord  (14,171  BR)
 The  schools  met  at  Aryanara's  teaching-seat  in  the  eastern  heartland,  one  century  to  the  year  after  the  founding  —  a  symmetry  so  tidy  that  some  chroniclers  suspect  the  scribes  moved  the  date  to  make  it  so.  The  Concord  was  signed  out  of  exhaustion.  Every  school  was  bleeding,  none  could  destroy  the  other  two,  and  the  lords  behind  Leneyez  had  discovered  that  holy  war  is  expensive.  Its  terms:   -  **The  Three  Recognitions.**  Each  rite  is  a  true  feeding  of  the  pantheon.    No  rite  may  unchurch  another;  no  priest  may  bar  a  Circle  believer  from  a    holy  place  for  keeping  a  different  rite.  -  **The  Pekna  belongs  to  the  god,  not  the  rite.**  Every  temple  is  raised  to    a  deity,  and  any  of  the  three  rites  may  be  kept  within  it  according  to    the  custom  of  the  place.  -  **Blood  is  bound.**  The  Leneyez  rite  continues  under  fixed  terms  —  what    may  be  offered,  when,  and  by  whose  hand.  (The  terms  of  blood  are  given    under  LENEYEZ.)  -  **Assembly,  not  blade.**  Disputes  between  the  rites  are  settled  by    concord  assembled,  never  by  arms.  The  Concord  thereby  made  itself  a    standing  institution;  later  gatherings  are  numbered  from  this  one.   It  was  sealed  with  the  formula  later  fixed  in  the  Zyrazithia:  *"The  Song  is  one.  The  voices  are  three."*   ###  What  the  Concord  Bought,  and  What  It  Cost
 The  Concord  bought  seven  thousand  years  of  official  harmony,  and  it  bought  it  with  a  contract,  not  a  communion.  Each  rite  privately  holds  the  others  insufficient.  Leneyez  priests  call  the  hours  "begging."  Rillic  priests  call  the  blood-rite  "butchery  with  hymns."  Barqeten's  faithful  pity  them  both  as  children  who  think  their  mother  must  be  fed  by  hand.  The  contempt  surfaces  where  it  always  does,  in  marriage:  seven  millennia  after  the  Concord,  House  Liazen's  Rillic  devotion  was  still  reason  enough  to  fight  Queen  Isalian's  marriage  into  Leneyez  House  Patton.   The  official  histories  of  the  Circle  teach  that  its  first  century  was  harmonious  and  the  Concord  a  triumph  of  unity.  The  fragments  that  survive  from  the  contention  —  a  burned  prayer-house's  roll  of  the  dead,  a  letter  begging  a  cousin  to  flee  the  river  towns  —  say  otherwise.  The  Circle  smoothed  its  own  beginnings  the  way  it  smooths  everything.   Later  theologians  noticed  what  the  contention  proved  and  were  careful  about  saying  it  aloud:  the  gods  let  their  faithful  burn  one  another's  houses  for  thirty  years  rather  than  name  a  preferred  worship,  and  the  pantheon  has  been  sustained  across  three  sub-denominations  ever  since.  Three  feedings  are  safer  than  one.  A  god  fed  three  ways  can  never  be  starved  by  one  change  of  heart.  The  gods  have  never  confirmed  this  reading.  They  never  do.   *(Note  for  the  Pataoiut  era,  36  AR  onward:  imperial  priests,  uneasy  that  the  blood-rite  bears  a  woman's  name,  taught  that  Leneyez  was  a  man.  The
older  texts  they  failed  to  burn  say  otherwise.)*     ##  LENEYEZ  —  THE  TERMS  OF  BLOOD   The  third  clause  of  the  First  Concord  bound  the  blood-rite  in  a  graded  code,  formally  the  Terms  of  Blood,  known  everywhere  as  the  Ladder.  The  Ladder  did  not  soften  Leneyez.  It  organized  it,  and  what  is  organized  survives.  Two  of  its  clauses  are  still  quoted  seven  thousand  years  on:  *"Let  each  feed  the  god  from  his  own  table,"*  and  *"No  hand  shall  take  the  unwilling  free."*   ###  The  Beast  Tier  —  The  Monthly  Rite   The  month  is  fed  by  beasts,  graded  to  the  household's  means.  The  poor  owe  fowl.  The  freeholder  owes  a  goat  or  ewe.  The  lord  owes  a  bull.  Offering  beneath  one's  means  is  impiety  under  the  Terms,  for  a  thin  offering  from  a  fat  table  tells  the  god  what  he  is  worth  to  you  —  and  so  piety  in  Leneyez  lands  is  legible  wealth.  Every  Pekna  keeps  blood-rolls  recording  what  each  household  brought,  and  the  rolls  are  consulted  for  marriages,  appointments,  and  suits  at  law.  A  family's  standing  can  be  read  in  what  it  bleeds.   ###  The  Festival  Tier  —  Human  Blood
 Human  offering  belongs  to  the  high  occasions  only:  the  great  feasts  of  the  year,  the  consecration  of  a  new  Pekna,  a  coronation,  the  eve  of  war,  and  calamity  —  drought,  plague,  defeat  —  when  the  god's  strength  must  be  restored  at  cost.  The  Terms  fix  the  order  of  resort:   -  **The  condemned,  first.**  In  Leneyez  lands  the  execution  is  the    offering;  the  headsman's  block  and  the  basin  are  one  institution.    Courts  sit  to  the  liturgical  calendar,  and  every  commoner  knows  the    proverb:  *never  stand  trial  in  a  feast-week.*  The  record  bears  the    proverb  out  —  condemnations  rise  as  the  feasts  approach,  and  no  court    has  ever  admitted  why.  -  **The  bought,  second.**  When  the  courts  run  dry,  the  temple  buys.  A    debtor  may  be  sold  to  the  basin  by  his  creditor,  or  sell  himself,  the    basin-price  paid  to  his  kin.  The  Terms  grant  one  mercy,  and  it  is    precise:  the  bought  may  be  redeemed  at  any  hour  before  the  feast's  eve,    if  the  debt  is  met.  Families  have  beggared  three  generations  raising  a    redemption  by  the  eve.  Some  raise  it  a  day  late.  -  **The  willing,  last  and  highest.**  The  rarest  offering  is  the  free  soul    who  chooses  the  basin  —  the  old  warrior,  the  dying  matriarch,  the    penitent.  Doctrine  names  this  the  summit  of  the  Ladder,  the  costliest    feeding  the  law  permits,  and  reserves  it  for  the  summit  occasions:    coronation  and  calamity.  The  willing  one's  family  is  blessed,  paid,  and    ennobled  in  the  blood-rolls  for  three  generations.
The  offered  must  be  whole  and  hale,  for  a  broken  offering  insults  the  god  it  feeds.  The  Terms  made  this  a  screening;  the  desperate  made  it  a  door.  Jailers  in  Leneyez  lands  know  the  price  of  a  quiet  maiming  that  renders  a  condemned  man  unfit  for  the  basin  and  fit  only  for  the  rope,  and  families  pay  it,  because  of  the  two  deaths,  they  fear  the  basin  more  —  or  say  they  do.  Leneyez  doctrine  teaches  the  opposite:  that  the  offered  soul  is  carried,  favored  in  its  next  turning  of  the  cycle.  The  teaching  is  what  lets  mothers  watch.  Whether  it  is  true,  the  gods  have  never  said.   ###  The  Rite  Itself   Only  a  consecrated  Blood-priest  of  the  receiving  god  may  open  the  vein,  and  only  at  that  god's  basin,  before  the  god's  image,  at  the  appointed  hour.  The  blood  is  the  feeding;  it  is  given  whole  to  the  basin.  The  body  is  burned  the  same  night  and  the  ash  given  to  the  fields.  *The  god  keeps  the  blood.  The  land  keeps  the  rest.*  The  old  Rillic  slander  that  Leneyez  priests  eat  of  the  offering  has  never  had  a  witness  in  seven  thousand  years,  and  has  never  once  needed  one  to  spread.   ###  What  the  Terms  Protect,  and  Whom   The  clause  the  voice  school  carried  out  of  the  Concord  as  its  victory  —  no  hand  shall  take  the  unwilling  free  —  is  the  most  praised  sentence  in  the  Terms  and  the  most  carefully  made.  Slaves  are  not  free.  Debtors  are  not  free.  The  condemned  are  not  free.  The  clause  has  held  for  seven
millennia  precisely  because  it  protects  everyone  who  could  afford  to  be  angry,  and  no  one  who  couldn't.  Justice  in  Leneyez  lands  is  not  corrupted  by  the  basin.  It  is  calibrated  to  it.   *(Forward  note,  Pataoiut  era:  a  code  that  grades  offerings  can  be  regraded.  When  Goteivati  III's  priests  turned  the  rite  toward  emperor  and  ancestors  in  36  AR,  they  did  not  break  the  Ladder.  They  added  a  rung  above  the  gods.)*
entries.summary: THE NINE-COUNT — WOMEN'S RANK ADORNMENT (Era of Solis — the Kingdom of Aicruae, prior to its absorption into the Solisian Empire) In Aicruae a woman's rank is worn on her left wrist and read at a glance. The left arm is the rank arm, governed by law; the right arm is her own, for heirlooms, gifts, and whatever she plea…

entries.title: The Saints
entries.text:
The Saints
The Saints
1.Aliirusk
18,765 BR  18,740 BR
25 YEARS OLD
Aliirusk was the first human being to be gifted the power of a saint. He was
loved endlessly by both the gods and humans, but he was naive. He devoted his
short life to the gods and humans doing anything he could think of to protect
the humans even stepping in the middle of wars to try to bring peace. When he
died at the battle of Wena the gods were devastated and punished the humans
he loved dearly for causing his death. Finore the god that blessed him was
devasted that he came down to Earth himself to retrieve his body afterward
creating the legendary weapon Allironek in his honor. Aliirusk was the first of
four saints to be buried in the kingdom of the gods.
Aliirusk could be best described as nice,sweet, and loving willing to do
whatever it takes to bring peace.
Aliirusk left behind his father,mother and one year old child when he passed.
Shortly after his death his family died as well despite not receiving the god's
punishment because humans blamed his family for them being punished. This
event became known as the tragedy of Enaner. He is known today as the godly
saint.
2.Bura
17,600BR  17,540 BR
60 YEARS OLD
The Saints
1
Bura is the name of the second of thirteen saints. She led a normal life not
seeking anything besides comfort until she was gifted her powers by the
god Vapaz. She is one of only two saints to receive Vapaz's gift. She lived a long
life helping to stabilize the lives of the people around her. And compared to the
life of the saint before her Bura's life wasn't as tragic.  She is recognized for
having created thirty cities, a vast irrigation system, and helping to build
schools that taught girls something never done before. The girls she taught
went on to help her in the creation of cities and towns all across the world
though keeping them united proved to be a challenge.
Today she is nicknamed the "Mother greatest" She was creative, organized,
and trustworthy.
3.Galamma
15,870 BR  15,852 BR
18 YEARS OLD
Galamma the third saint is considered one of the most tragic saints in all of
history. She was born to a widowed mother during a heavily religious time when
people suspected others of being demons and a time when the people
suspected of being demons were often kidnapped and executed.  Due to a
misunderstanding, she was thought to be one of such people , and to sum up
people jumping to conclusions and prejudice led to her death. She was the
second saint to be buried in the kingdom of the gods. She was given her gifts by
the god Sielaph. She was among one of the few saints that many believe was
able to communicate with their god and many believe  Galamma and Sielaph
were very close.
She was best described as outgoing, adventurous, and easygoing. She is
nicknamed " the lost one" She spent her final moments full of fear and in agony.
4.Dorthargel
13,052 BR  13,020 BR
The Saints
2
23 YEARS OLD
Dorthargel developed her powers closer to the end of her life. Her powers were
gifted to her by the goddess Nellebrie who chose her because she had similar
hair to her. Hair is said to be a reflection of one's soul and
for Nellebrie Dorthargel was the first human she saw with that hair color.
Nellebrie and Dorthargel often played together and sang songs with one
another. Dorthargel while never actually seeing Nellebrie thought of her as a
mother. When Dorthargel died of illness Nellebrie blamed herself for
Dorthargel's death and she destroyed cities caused earthquakes and asked
several gods to kill her. The relationship between Nellebrie and Dorthargel was
one of the greatest reminders of god's love for the saints.  Unfortunately,
Dorthargel couldn't be buried in the kingdom of the gods because her family
had already buried her and Nellebrie did not want to disturb Dorthargel's rest
because of her selfishness.
Dorthargel is nicknamed "God's favorite"  Dorthargel was modest, generous,
and loyal.
5.Eren
12,467 BR  12,441 BR
26 YEARS OLD
Saint Eren was blessed by the queen of the gods the goddess Nimlye. Eren died
when he was 26 just three years older than the saint before him. Eren led a very
idealistic life ignoring his duties as a saint and venturing out into the world.
Unfortunately for him because he ignored his duties he was eventually hunted
down by the humans and died after suffering countless blows to his head.
He is nicknamed the " wrong choice." and he is one of the first examples of
humans disapproving of who the gods make saints. Nimlye was very fond of
him and tried to get the gods to agree to him being buried in the kingdom of the
gods but they said that he wasn't worthy. So Nimyle created a mirror and placed
his body inside of it she then had Finore refine the mirror so that it could
become a necklace and she is said to wear that necklace around her neck at all
times.
The Saints
3
Eren to most was considered foolish. He wasn't generally a bad person he was
just young and not versed in the ways of the world. This is why many
believe Nimlye favored him.
6.Argellon
11,002 BR  10,952 BR
50 YEARS OLD
Argellon is the name of the sixth saint who is nicknamed "the second choice".
He is nicknamed the second choice because he wasn't supposed to receive the
goddess Paha's gift. The gift was originally intended for his older brother but
because his brother died suddenly in war Paha gave her gift to him. He is
recognized for having created the first official temple to the goddess Paha
inside the temple his older brother is buried underneath a statue of the
goddess. He is also recognized for having created the idea of a moral code. His
code the code of Esa has been essential in the creation of many social orders.
And many people use the code as a way of upholding order.
He was buried beside his brother in the first temple of the goddess Paha upon
his death.
He was best described as headstrong, bold, and dedicated.
7.Siriande
10,567 BR  10,533 BR
34 YEARS OLD
Siriande was born the daughter of a local fisher. Due to her father's choice of
job she spent a lot of time near the sea. One day when she was playing with her
toy it flew into the sea she went to get it and nearly drowned. Luckily, she was
saved by the goddess Zopha who felt sorry for her. After saving her Zopha
gifted her powers allowing her to become a saint. While Siriande life wasn't as
long or as short as other saints her death was still tragic. Siriande died at the
age of 34 after being poisoned by her son. Many consider that fact to be tragic
The Saints
4
but the fact that she knew he was trying to poison her and she still accepted the
poison is possibly the saddest part of her story. Her son's betrayal is extremely
brutal because many historical texts describe her as a wonderful mother and
saint. No one can say for sure why her son choose to betray her but many
suspect that his reasons for killing her were related to power.
In her final moments, she begged the goddess Zopha to spare her son she
believed he was merely corrupted by the will of men. Zopha agreed but took
away his ability to speak so that he may never ask for forgiveness. That was the
first of two requests Siriande asked of the goddess the last of her two final
requests of the goddess was that she may not be buried amongst the gods but
amongst men.
Siriande is known for the construction of several dams and the creation of
several laws known as the Yerian Laws meant to grant protection for women
these laws ranged from material laws to land ownership.
She is nicknamed "Siriande the unlucky" for if she had borne a better son she
may have lived longer.
Siriande's son Ritav committed suicide five years after her death after suffering
from extreme madness. Zopha is said to have covered his grave in water to
disturb his rest so that he may never know peace for what he did to his own
mother.
8.Nairan
10,012 BR  9,983 BR
29 YEARS OLD
Narian is the name of the eight saint she is nicknamed "little princess". She was
the first saint to be born to an improvised family with her father being a very
powerful leader of a small town. She had never known hardship and unlike the
other saints did not get her gift by being extraordinary or by having a trait that
sets her apart from anyone else. She was simply a girl from a wealthy family
who happened to be in the right place at the right time. Her carriage had broken
down in a forest and while she was roaming the forest to pass the time she
The Saints
5
stumbled upon a wounded deer. Narian helped the deer who she didn't know
was the goddess Allan who had been wounded following an attack by humans.
The goddess Allan who was suspicious of her at first because of her flashy
nature grew to like her after she took off her coat and covered her with it.
Allan gifted Nairan the blessing soon after.
Nairan lived a beautiful life and she died surrounded by her three young
daughters while it's not exactly ideal to die at the age of 29 she had no choice
seeing as she suffered complications birthing her last child.
During her life, she helped create a system to help route out corruption within
the appointed government and created a movement for science that helped
create and modify medicine.
9.Karniode
9,365 BR  9,351 BR
14 YEARS OLD
Not much is known about Karniode's life despite her being born during a time
where history had begun being recorded. All that current historians know about
her is that she is said to have received her powers at the age of 13, and that she
was born blind.  For many years many people did not believe she actually
existed, or that she was a myth because she was not buried officially, and her
name and face had been burned out in almost all history books from that time
period.  It is widely believed that she received a blessing from the
goddess Zopha because some of the texts found during that time period state
that she had the ability to part oceans at will.
The main conspiracy with Karniode's life ironically is her death some say she
stumbled off a cliff and died some say she was pushed by a member of her
family with ill intent. But everyone can agree on the fact that she was definitely
buried in the kingdom of the god's making her the third of the four saints buried
amongst the gods.
After Karniode death her village was completely devasted by a tsunami and
many of the villagers died. Those that survived only talk of her in passing they
The Saints
6
often referred to her as "Gentle one". Many believe that this nickname might
have reflected her position within their society.
10.Malign
9,323 BR  9,305 BR
18 YEARS OLD
Saint Malign the ninth saint was nicknamed the "Sacred Knight." He led a very
successful life despite its length. He was a champion of economic equality
going as far as drinking nothing but salt water for several days so that people
may recognize how bad the wealth gap was. Alongside this, he was also a
dedicated champion for women's rights during his time as Saint he promoted
women to high positions despite opposition and improved upon the Yerian Laws
to meet his time's standards. He also helped to spread the idea of free speech
and press letting people talk about him as they saw fit he is quoted as having
said " If you have no enemies then you have no friends, for enemies will always
find a way into your company claiming they are your friends."
He was killed by his enemies and his sister died trying to defend him.
Malign was gifted his abilities by the god Finore. Many believe
that Finore choose him because they shared similar values.
11.Duri
8,747 BR  8,670 BR
77 YEARS OLD
Saint Duri was the longest-living saint dying at the age of 77. She is quoted to
have said, "The kind ones die early leaving behind the worst of us." Duri was
blessed by the goddess Allan who believed Duri was destined for greatness.
Duri is the only saint to have received several nicknames these nicknames
include; The mother of Gherci, Duri the wise, Queen of the people, and the true
Saint. Duri is the only saint to have founded, created, and rule an entire country. 
She was considered the most powerful of the Saints and the wisest.
The Saints
7
Duri believed highly in the gods and divine order in her city Gherci she had
monuments of all the saints before her built. Their statues stood all around the
city, acting as walls, her statue was located in the center visibly smaller than
the others. She spent her whole life helping her people and recognizing her
predecessors for their talents.
She is noted for having the most accomplishments among all the saints
including the creation of several military strategies, an official legal court, the
construction of an international trade route, and the creation of  Tanya's (public
hospitals).
She is widely known for having been obsessed with her fellow Saints especially
saint Malign(the saint that came before her) and worshipping him like an idol.
She thought that Malign was taken before his time and spent her entire life
trying to spread his beliefs.
Duri spent most of her life on the battlefield fighting for her country. She is
known to have never lost a battle and to be a true upholder of Honor.
She is the last of the four saints to be buried amongst the gods. She was buried
amongst them for all her accomplishments.
Many historical texts describe Duri as cold and standoffish but through the
finding of her diaries, a softer side of her was revealed. She wrote down the
name of every man she had killed in detail and wrote the words I am sorry by
each of their names. She is quoted to have said " To have lived as long as I have
you must make peace with our enemies even if they can not see that you have.
For the gods see all our actions and transgressions "
12. Reron
7,450 BR  7,402 BR
48 YEARS OLD
Saint Reron was blessed by the god Vapaz . Reron was the second of the two
saints blessed by Vapaz. Reron is considered to be a taboo saint in a sense
because depending on who is telling the story he was or was not a saint. Reron
is nicknamed the"ender of worlds."He destroyed villages and killed many
The Saints
8
people at will with his abilities because he felt as if the people of his world had
wronged him. They thought him to be the bastard son of Vapaz and a mortal
woman named Mevi. They hung his mother after labeling her a witch and a
temptress who seduced the god Vapaz. And left young Reron to be a beggar
after he manifested his abilities at twenty four they used his wife and kids to
threaten him to perform his duties as a saint. After a while, eventually, the
people holding his family hostage killed his wife and eldest daughter. Luckily
Reron was able to escape with his youngest child after escaping he hid her in a
surrounding village never to see her again. He died at the battle of Relirian after
being ambushed by the people who killed his wife and child despite his death he
was able to make it so no one made it out of the battle alive. Many sympathize
with him saying that he only killed and destroyed to avenge his family but many
others say that he abused his power as a saint for petty revenge.
The Saints
9

entries.title: Magic System
entries.text:
Magic System
MAGICʼS ORIGIN
Magic was not always a thing; there used to be a time when no one could match
the power of saints and gods. That was until the Grand Mage Verna made a
contract with Iswan, Goddess of Alchemy. Verna became obsessed with power
and received a wish from Iswan herself. He wished to have the power to create
spells. Since the gods could not deny him his wish because of the oath of Memiet
(an oath that says that if a god does not grant the wish of their follower after
receiving their soul, the god in question shall cease to exist), he was allowed his
wish.
Verna had twenty-seven sons. He made those sons marry their fifteen sisters, and
the children born of those unions spread the ability to use magic for multiple
generations. However, this power was kept within Vikistv (the nation Verna
founded in 7,945 BR) until the age of Solisʼs conquest.
When a magic user has a child with a non-magic user, the magic itself is like a
virus that infects the host (the child). Those closer to the source-a pure and more
direct line to Verna-have more amplified magical abilities than those who donʼt. A
child between two magic users will always be more powerful than a child between
a magic user and a non-magic user.
It wasnʼt until well into the rule of Emperor Goteivati Zivc III, after the
Reconstruction period of the empire, that magic users began to marry Sun-Forged
(normal humans with no origin tied to the gods) and fully integrate into society.
Through the course of over two millennia, magic users began to mix their pure
magical blood with the Sun-Forged, seemingly eradicating the existence of the
People of the Mountain and the People of the Sky with the exception of a few
families like those of Professors Siroa and Lyanami Taten.
THE BLOOD TRIALS
Before the Great Mage Takarʼs discovery in 1528 AR, a childʼs magical abilities
were believed to directly inherit from their parents. Children who did not possess a
parentʼs magical attributes were thought to have been bastards. The consequence
Magic System
1
of a child not displaying one of the parentsʼ attributes usually fell on the mother
and child. Both parties were punished in what is referred to as a Blood Trial.
The outcome of these trials was usually the same: the child and mother were
either burned or drowned. In cases where the mother was of nobility or high
standing, the child was simply killed, and the mother was branded with the
acronym B.W. Blood Whore), signaling that she had committed an affair.
These trials went on for over two hundred years. An estimated 400,000 women
and 600,000 children were killed (or thatʼs what was recorded; countless more
would have been undocumented killings).
The Great Mage Takarʼs discovery ended the Blood Trials by proving that a childʼs
magical abilities have no correlation to those of their parents, meaning that two
parents who fall under the Utayer magical division could produce a child who
possesses abilities belonging to the Kari magical division. The same applies to a
childʼs magical level: the likelihood of a child inheriting a parentʼs magical level is
only around . No amount of selective breeding can guarantee a childʼs
magical lineage.
THE THREE STAGES OF MAGIC
Makito Basic In this stage, a personʼs magic takes the form of the color purple. It
is the weakest of the three stages and requires approximately  of the casterʼs
magical output.
Abilities at this level are limited: small fires about the size of a fist, a gentle brush
of wind. The magic used in this stage is not very strong and can easily be
deflected.
Of the total magic users in the empire (  of the entire population, roughly 344
million people),  fall in the Makito level-approximately 206.4 million people
who canʼt even start a decent fire without meeting their magical output limit.
Rusti Intermediate) In this stage, a personʼs magic takes the form of the color red.
This is the middle ground of the three levels and requires approximately  of
the casterʼs total magical output.
Magical users at the Rusti level usually fall within the Gnati and Minarei magical
divisions. This is the highest and most attainable level for most magic users. This
40%
45%
80%
60%
69%
Magic System
2
stage is called the buffer stage because it sets you far apart from those in the
Makito level.
Of the total magic users in the empire,  (roughly 138 million) fall within the
Rusti level across all six countries.
Javehet Advanced) In this stage, a personʼs magic takes the form of the color
black. This requires approximately  of the casterʼs total magical output. This is
the highest stage a magic user can reach.
This level is sometimes referred to as dark magic because the power is said to be
world-ending. At this level, a magic user supposedly makes a deal with a god, who
in return gets a portion of their soul to use as a vessel.
The only Javehet-ranked magic user to ever exist was Verna himself, who existed
more than twenty thousand years ago. Verna created spells of death and
destruction and almost brought an end to the entire world. Thousands upon
thousands of people died during this time. He created mountains made up of
nothing and cut apart entire seas sometimes by saying just one word or simply
waving his hand.
This rank of spellcasting is considered taboo because it rivals the power of saints.
There are no Javehet magic users in the entire world, and none since Verna.
DETERMINING YOUR MAGIC LEVEL
The procedure for determining your magical level is simple and comprises only
three steps:
The magic userʼs eyes are covered with a blindfold. This is done for two
reasons: so the magic user can connect with their magical abilities, and so
they wonʼt be as focused on the pain.)
A tip of the magic userʼs finger is cut. Your magic is stored within your body
and the easiest way to release it so that we can determine your capabilities is
to briefly wound the user.)
The blood taken from the wound is thrown into an open pit of fire. The fire will
change color depending on your level of magical abilities; it will either be
purple, red, or maybe black.)
40%
80%

3
ADDITIONAL MAGIC MECHANICS
Elemental Branches: Magic is broken into elemental branches (fire, water, earth,
air, light, dark).
Sacrifice Requirements:
Sacrifices to magic must be objects of personal value
For mild magic: the blood from the caster must be fresh, approximately
drops of blood or a teaspoon amount
For hard magic: relinquishing reincarnation is a permanent pact; once the soul
is corrupted upon death, it starts to despair
Consequences of Overuse:
Overuse ages the caster
Causes madness
Could attract demonic attention
Modern users avoid Javehet-level spells because itʼs seen as taboo for these
reasons and is virtually unattainable.
MAGIC VS SAINTLY POWER SECTION:
Magic: Mortal power from Iswanʼs bargain with Verna. Corrupted divine
essence passed through bloodlines for thousands of years. Clear limits (output
capacity), causes exhaustion ⟶  pain ⟶  burnout →  permanent damage.
Inherited, trainable, bounded by mortal constraints.
Saintly Power: Direct loan from a god. Saint is vessel, not generator. Can
accomplish impossible feats because they direct divine energy. No upper limit
except godʼs willingness.
Cost of saintly power: Dependency. Power ends completely when god
withdraws favor or saint dies. Cannot pass to descendants. Connection can be
severed.
2/10
Magic System
4
Key distinction: Magic has ceiling but is reliable/heritable; saintly power is
unlimited but contingent/temporary.
GIFTED OBJECTS SECTION:
Created by House Arvento in partnership with Vikistv mages
Requires three components: skilled craftsperson (mundane creation), magic
user who “bleeds” power into object, rare materials (metals/crystals from
Vikistv)
Magic user suffers output cost during creation
Object becomes a “battery” anyone can use regardless of magical ability
Not alive or intelligent-holds specific enchantment, discharges when activated
Most become mundane when depleted; some can be recharged
High prices reflect: magic userʼs exhaustion/recovery, rare materials, skilled
craftsmanship
OUTPUT LIMITS SECTION:
Progression: Exhaustion →  Pain (burning blood, pressure behind eyes) →
Burnout (temporary loss, days to weeks) →  Permanent damage (chronic pain,
inability to use magic, accelerated aging, madness)
Experienced practitioners sense limits through training
Magic color indicates strain: Purple = normal, Red = pushing limits, Black =
Javehet-level transcendence (divine bargain)
Overuse can attract demonic attention-energy signature registers in mental

GRAND SORCERER SEVTORʼS ATTACK ON VALEA
(7,217 BR)
1
## Significance for Magic System:
This is the most destructive single use of magic in the civil war era
Magic System
5
Sevtor was the head of the Magic Tower in Vikistv and a direct descendant of
Vernaʼs eldest son, Liaerto I — making House Orana the most powerful pureblood magic line in existence
The attackʼs scale 15,000 dead) demonstrates what organized, wellresourced magic users can accomplish when deployed as military weapons
The Valea attack rewrites military doctrine: fixed “showpiece” strongholds
become politically toxic and militarily suspect after this demonstration
DISCOVERY: FIRE AS MAGIC USER WEAKNESS
Event: After the Valea attack, Solis, Jaifey Yuera, and Mihel Kulio kidnapped
Maeret Orana Sevtorʼs third son) and experimented on him to discover magic
usersʼ vulnerability.
Discovery: Fire is deadly to magic users because their bodies - which rely on cold
- cannot handle high temperatures. This weakness is specific to magic users of
Vernaʼs bloodline, whose magic is tied to the cold climate of Vikistv (which sits
atop Mount Aicren, the coldest location in the world).
Application: Solis used this discovery to destroy House Orana. He had a spy
infiltrate their castle and pour Liacaion (the worldʼs equivalent of gasoline) into
their chambers. The spy lit the fire, and all members of House Orana burned to
death - except Mekean, who escaped by dyeing her hair and settling in Equateiy,
continuing the family line that eventually leads to Merigen Bleelack.

THE ILKAI HERB
Magic System
6
⼀
Classification: Divine-level substance (not standard magic)
Properties: Capable of killing a god
Source: Obtained by Harnua Kulio through a deal with the goddess Nellebrie
7,214 BR
Usage in Story: Harnua mixed Ilkai into a cup of wine intended for Solis during a
celebration. Because Solis was under the protection of Razar, Nellebrieʼs divine
power was necessary to bypass Razarʼs shield. Empress Esterica accidentally
drank from the cup and died instantly.
Relationship to Magic System: Ilkai exists outside the standard
Makito/Rusti/Javehet magic level system. It is a substance of divine origin, not a
spell or magical technique. Its existence demonstrates that the divine and magical
systems, while related through Verna and Iswanʼs contract, operate on different
levels of power.

The Pertari Stairs
Magic System
7
The Pertari Stairs are not a place. They are a condition-what happens to a soul
that has become too discordant to rejoin Noirtaʼs song. A healthy soul, when its
body dies, naturally flows back into the cycle. Death is a pause, and then the Song
picks them up again, carrying them toward rebirth. But a corrupted soul has
changed its fundamental frequency. It tries to return to the Song, but the Song
cannot accept it. The soul reaches for the cycle and finds only climbing.
The Stairs are the experience of eternally almost-returning. The corrupted soul
feels the pull of Noirta above them, hears echoes of the Song they once belonged
to, and climbs toward it. Forever. They never arrive. They never rest. They exist in
the space between what they were and what they can no longer be.
The torment is both physical and psychological, inseparable from each other. The
climbing never stops. The soul has a body on the Stairs-not their living body, but a
memory of one, aching and heavy. Their legs burn. Their lungs seize. They
stumble and fall and rise again because there is no
alternative. The Stairs are endless in both directions; there is no going back, no
sitting down, no relief. Rest is something that belongs to souls still welcome in the
Song.
But the worse suffering is what they hear. Above them, always above them, Noirta
plays. The corrupted soul can hear the Song they were once part of. They hear
other souls cycling through-souls that lived and died and will live again.
Sometimes they recognize voices. A mother. A child. A lover from three lifetimes
ago. These souls pass through the Song like water through a river, effortless and
eternal, while the corrupted one climbs toward a reunion that will never come.
The Pertari Stairs predate the gods. They existed before Mikani crystallized from
Noirta, before Haxenylian emerged to protect what had been created. The Stairs
are not divine architecture. They are simply what happens when a soul falls out of
harmony with existence itself. No divine power has ever retrieved a soul from
them.
Paths to Corruption
Corruption is not about sin in the way temple priests sometimes teach it. A soul
can lie, steal, murder, and still return to Noirta when the body dies. The Song does
not judge morality—it judges harmony. A soul becomes corrupted when it
changes so fundamentally that it no longer resonates with what it once was. When
Magic System
8
the note it sings becomes unrecognizable to the greater melody. There are four
known paths:
Wrath Unchecked - The oldest path. The first corrupted soul did not simply kill—
killing is part of mortal existence, and the Song accounts for it. The first corrupted
soul became killing. They shed so much blood, with such sustained fury, that
violence stopped being something they did and became something they were.
Their soul rewrote itself around destruction until nothing else remained. This is
why soldiers who kill in war do not automatically corrupt. Intent matters. Context
matters. But a soul that surrenders entirely to wrath, that lets rage become their
only truth across years or even lifetimes-that soul hollows itself out and fills the
space with something the Song cannot hold.
The Ilkai Herb - Corruption from outside rather than within. Where wrath reshapes
the soul through choice, Ilkai simply breaks it. The herb grows where disaster and
transformation overlap on Mount Aicren, and it carries that contradiction into
whoever consumes it. The soul does not change-it shatters. The pieces try to
return to Noirta separately, and none of them are whole enough to rejoin. It is
called “god-killing” not because gods have literally died from it, but because it
does what even the gods cannot: it ends a soul permanently.
Magical Corruption Javehet-Level Debt) - Most magic-even powerful magic-does
not threaten the soul. The danger is debt. At the highest levels of magical practice,
a caster can reach beyond what their own power allows. They can borrow from
the world, from other souls, from forces that exist in the spaces between things.
This is where Javehet-level magic lives-in the territory of bargains. Some
payments are simple: years of life, memories, the ability to taste food or feel
warmth. These transactions leave the soul intact, if diminished. But some
sorcerers trade pieces of themselves—not memories or sensations, but
fundamental notes of their soulʼs song. Each trade changes what they are. Each
bargain rewrites them. If they trade too much, if they hollow themselves out in
pursuit of power, they cross a threshold they cannot return from. The Magic Tower
of Vikistv knows this. It is why their training is so brutal, why they turn away more
students than they accept. They are not simply teaching technique. They are
teaching restraint-how to touch the Javehet level without being consumed by it.
Souls That Refuse the Song - The rarest and the saddest path. Some souls, after
many lifetimes, grow weary. They remember too much. The weight of
Magic System
9
accumulated lives becomes unbearable-lovers lost and found and lost again,
children buried across centuries, the same mistakes made in different bodies.
These souls do not want to continue. But Noirta does not offer an exit. The Song
plays eternally, and souls are part of it whether they wish to be or not. So some
desperate souls try to force an ending. They seek out corruption deliberately—
pursuing wrath they do not feel, or searching for Ilkai on the frozen slopes of
Mount Aicren, or making magical bargains they know will destroy them. They
choose the Pertari Stairs because endless climbing feels less terrible than endless
becoming.
The Ilkai Herb (Expanded)
The Ilkai herb grows only on Mount Aicren, in specific conditions where Nellebrieʼs
disaster-creation and Iswanʼs alchemical influence overlap. This connects it
directly to Iswanʼs domain, since Vikitsv worships her as their supreme god and
the mountain itself was created by Nellebrie. The herb exists in the overlap
between disaster and alchemy, destruction and transformation.
Vekta and Aryanara, the great scholars who taught about the cycle of rebirth,
discovered Ilkai during their studies. They were the first to document that it breaks
the soulʼs cycle permanently. The herb is extraordinarily rare because most who
attempt the three-month journey up the mountain die before reaching it. House
Orana and the Magic Tower likely know of its existence but guard this knowledge
carefully. Within Vikitsvʼs scholarly circles, even there it is considered forbidden—
using Ilkai is seen as worse than murder because you are not just ending a life,
you are ending a soulʼs eternal existence.
Nellebrie, as the goddess who embodies destruction-as-renewal, told Harnua
Kulio where the Ilkai grows. The goddess of disaster understands endings. She
knows that some doors, once opened, cannot be closed.
DASERI
Fire Magic]
CLASSIFICATION
Division Name: Daseri
Magic System
10

ORIGINS
Source of Power: Derived from Iswanʼs original gift to
Verna, manifesting as an affinity for heat and flame.
Daseri is classified as a specialized branch within the broader elemental tradition.
Historical Development:

magic through the Verna contract.

Minaraʼs ability to communicate with demons may also be connected to her Gnati
classification - raw, unfiltered magic potentially bridging the gap between mortal
and demonic planes in ways refined divisions cannot.

Taught at the Solisian Academy.
DEMONS & DEMON CLASSIFICATIONS
Demons are creatures that invade the mortal world through the corrupted world
doors and The Gate. Their presence in the mortal realm has increased
dramatically during the events of Crown of Glory due to Empress
Macenja/Vandreaʼs machinations and Renedinʼs influence on the barrier between
realms.
THE OFFICIAL RANKING OF DEMONS (Most to Least
Powerful)
Valoka
Namilrane
Akotia Jerctika
Zelian
Lim
Vorel
Alem
Jali
Plova
Demons are organized into functional sub-classes based on their role:
Sub Class: Attackers
Namilrane - Horns on both the top and bottom of its face. Human-like hands that
act as its feet. It can stand and run very fast. Height: 10 ft . Very violent.
Uncommon.
Sub Class: Spirit Demons
Valoka - Spirit demons existing in the dream plane, supposedly under the
commission of the old god Renedin. Valokas are purple, have huge tongues, bugMagic System
43
like wings, and large stick-like legs that take up a huge portion of their bodies.
They always seem to be smiling. They use their smiles to lure and trap their
victims in the dream plane while they take over their bodies. The first sighting of
Valokas happened when a man named Dalika Uaer barely managed to survive
being possessed by one and composed a drawing of the creature so that others
know of their existence. Height: 8 ft . Extremely
violent. Rare.
Sub Class: Warriors
Lim Bird-like creature. Abilities: Mimicking sound, stealing sound. Method of
killing: Uses sound to lure its victims in before killing them using the venom it
shoots out.
Akotia Jerctika — A field demon/foot soldier. Height: 7 ft (usually). Description: A
cross between a moose and deer. It has a bird-like beak and deer antlers, a thick
neck, and a large exposed brain. Weakness: Can die from their brain being
punctured.
Zelian - Ground Shifter. Size: Usually 20 meters long. Worm-like in shape but with
reptile-like skin and tail. Method of hunting: Uses its tail to kill.
Sub Class: Messengers
Vorel - Minor Messenger Demon. Lumpy face, tiny ears protected by the
lumpiness of the face, small feet (runs fast despite this).
Jali - General Messenger Demon. Purpose: Relaying information to demons. A
giant eye with bird-like wings. Abilities: Teleportation.
Sub Class: Healers
Alem — Greater Healer Demon. Five tiny red balls that are dark red — best
described as four tiny red balls circling a giant red ball. Non-violent.
Plova - Lesser Healer Demon. A plant demon that can regenerate certain parts of
itself. Non-violent.
Rare. Usually used to make soup for sick people due to its healing properties.
DEMON CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM
Magic System
44
Demons are entities from Renedinʼs mental realm that can manifest in the physical
world through corrupted world doors, proximity to strained magic users, or neardeath dream states. They are classified by power and function into an official
ranking system, from most to least powerful: Valokaʼs, Namilrane, Akotia Jerctika,
Zelian, Lim, Vorel, Alem, Jali, Plova. These nine types fall into six sub-classes.
Attackers
The Attacker sub-class contains the two most dangerous physical demons.
Namilrane stand approximately ten feet tall and are extremely violent, functioning
as brute-force assault creatures.
Valokaʼs are the most powerful demons in the hierarchy - eight-foot-tall spirits
from the dream plane who serve directly under Renedin. Valokaʼs are purple in
coloration with bug-like wings and possess the unique ability to enter the dream
plane and possess victims. Unlike other demons, they have no physical form and
exist entirely on the dream plane. They can only be fought by waking up or having
someone wake you. The first recorded Valoka sighting was survived by Dalika
Uaer, who created a warning drawing after surviving possession.
Field Demons
Akotia Jerctika are the primary field demon. They stand approximately seven feet
tall and resemble a moose or deer hybrid. Their exposed brain is their primary
weakness.
Ground Shifters
Zelian are massive worm-reptile hybrids measuring approximately twenty meters
in length. They operate underground and disrupt terrain.
Warriors
Lim are bird-like warrior demons with the ability to mimic sound. They possess
venom, making them dangerous in close combat.
Messengers
The Messenger sub-class includes two types. Vorel are minor messengers used
for basic communication between demonic forces. Jali are general-purpose
Magic System
45
messengers with the additional ability of teleportation.
Healers
The Healer sub-class contains two types. Alem are greater healers that can
restore other demons. Plova are lesser healers - plant demons with limited
restorative capabilities.
MAGIC OVERUSE AND DEMONIC ATTENTION
Overuse of magic can attract demonic attention. The energy signature of a
strained magic user registers in the mental realm, potentially drawing Valoka
demons or other entities toward them. This is one of the reasons magic use
carries inherent risk even beyond the physical toll on the userʼs body - pushing
past oneʼs limits does not just risk personal harm but can create a beacon that
draws the most dangerous creatures in existence.
DEMON COMBAT AND DESTRUCTION
Demons can be destroyed in the physical realm, but they do not truly die in the
mortal sense. When a demonʼs physical form is destroyed, its essence disperses
back into Renedinʼs mental realm. Given enough time and the right conditions -
proximity to a corrupted world door, a magic user pushing past their limits, or
someone dreaming too close to death - the same demon can reconstitute.
The barrier between realms used to slow this reconstitution to centuries, but since
Vandreaʼs corruption of an unstable world door during A Princess in Love, the
process now takes only months or years. This is why demons have become an
escalating threat rather than a manageable occasional occurrence.
Valokaʼs are the exception to standard combat. Because they are dream-plane
spirits with no physical form, the only way to fight them is to wake up or have
someone else wake you from the dream state they attack through.
Permanent destruction of a demon would theoretically require destroying it within
Renedinʼs realm itself, but this has never been achieved. There is an untested
theory that destroying Renedin himself would unravel all demons - or potentially
make them worse by removing whatever control he exerts over them.

Name Evolution Across Eras
Name Evolution Across Eras
How each territory's name evolves across the three eras. Seas that are renamed
are noted separately.
The borders of the known world have been redrawn twice since the age of
independent kingdoms. What began as six sovereign nations became an empire of
duchies and kingdoms under new names, and then was restructured again into
the late imperial order that persists into Minara's time. Below is a record of how
each territory's identity has shifted across the three major eras.
Territories
The Six Kingdoms Era(  8,900 BR 7,163 BR →  Crandona's Era 150 AR →
Minara's Era 2,632 AR
Aicruae →  Tanan Grand Duchy Capital:Tericaer) →  Kingdom of Lajazer Capital:
Vellin)

Equateiy →  Uxridian Grand Duchy(Capital:Rewalen ) →  Kingdom of Ociyaran
Capital: Zada)
Vikitsv →  Theolisseia Hadirel ) →  Kingdom of Berlailia Capital: Zemela)
The Mystic Isles → Thult →  Thult (no political boundary drawn)
Aicruae, the westernmost kingdom and birthplace of the Patton dynasty, was
reorganized into the Tanan Grand Duchy after the empire's formation during
Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it had been renamed again to the Kingdom of
Lajazer, with its new capital at Vellin. Of the six kingdoms, Lajazer is one of two
that holds impartial standing toward the empire.
Gherci, once the largest and most populous nation on the continent, became the
Caporiolan Kingdom during Crandona's Era and served as the Imperial Seat. By
Minara's Era it was renamed the Kingdom of Tarmet, with its capital moved to
Bela. Tarmet remains the overall capital of the entire empire and holds the highest
rank in the kingdom hierarchy.
Pireaynea, long known as "The Demon's Pit" for its lawlessness, was absorbed
Name Evolution Across Eras
1
into the empire as Lingia during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it became the
Kingdom of Civer, with its capital at Lorne. Despite its troubled history, Civer
proved richer than expected in the late empire due to its mines.
Coelum, the impoverished northern wasteland sometimes called "The Forsaken
Land," was renamed Hikai during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it became the
Kingdom of Atriki, with its capital at Elgan. Atriki sits at the bottom of the kingdom
hierarchy, mainly comprised of farmers and low-ranking merchants.
Equateiy, once the wealthiest independent nation in the world, was reorganized
into the Uxridian Grand Duchy during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it became
the Kingdom of Ociyaran, with its capital at Zada. Ociyaran shares the secondhighest rank in the kingdom hierarchy alongside Lajazer.
Vikitsv, the mountain kingdom and heartland of organized magic, became
Theolisseia during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era it was renamed the Kingdom
of Berlailia, with its capital at Zemela. Berlailia holds the third rank, home to few
aristocrats and some low-ranked magicians.
The Mystic Isles, the sacred archipelago southwest of Aicruae that technically
belonged to no king, was renamed Thult during Crandona's Era. By Minara's Era,
Thult persists but has no political boundary drawn around it. Once believed to be a
link between the world of the gods and the world of mortals, the isles are now
barren and desertified.
Seas
The Six Kingdoms Era(  8,900 BR 7,163 BR →  Crandona's Era 150 AR →
Minara's Era 2,632 AR
The Oberya Sea →  Orburydon Sea →  The Oberya Sea (name reverts)
The Fetora Sea →  Thult Southern Waters) →  The Fetora Sea (name reverts)
The Quather Sea → The Quather Sea (unchanged) →  The Quather Sea
(unchanged)
Henem Bay →  TBD →  The Henem Bay
The seas have not been immune to renaming. The Oberya Sea, which borders the
northeastern and eastern coastline, was renamed the Orburydon Sea during
Crandona's Era before reverting to its original name by Minara's time. The Fetora
Sea, which runs along the southern coastline, was briefly known as Thult
Southern Waters) during Crandona's Era — likely reflecting the expansion of the
Thult designation across the southern reaches — before also reverting to the
Fetora Sea by Minara's Era. The Quather Sea, bordering the western coast, is the
only major body of water to retain its name unchanged across all three eras.
Name Evolution Across Eras
2
Henem Bay, the small northern coastline, also appears to persist, though whether
it carried a different name during Crandona's Era is not recorded as it not featured
on any maps from that era.

Event: Creation of The Magic Tower Location: Right side of Mount Aicren, at a lower standing than the capital city ofVikitsv Key Figures: Descendants of Verna Significance: The Magic Tower was created by the descendants of Verna in7,749 BR. Over the years the magic tower has become a vital piece of Vikitsv holding all the countryʼs power. It wascreated in such a way because it makes it so whoever wants to enter the city has to go past the tower first. The towerwas first under the control of a powerful magician named Ulian and his sons Kiear and Liaerto III but it has passed downfrom generation to generation of fathers to their sons. The current Grand Sorceer is the child of Ulianʼs son Kiear. BookReference: TBD
WAR OF THE GODS I(  )
ORIGINS
In the beginning, there were four gods-brothers born of the same song: Mikani (war and order), Poaranji (strength andsailors), Renedin (dreams and the eternal plane), and Haxenylian (protection and wisdom).
The war began when Haxenylian, the third brother, fell in love with a mortal woman named Lady Gaialana. Their unionproduced Vapaz and Zopha-the first New Gods. This was a concept unimaginable before their birth; around this time,mortal beliefs were also shifting, and with this change, new gods came into existence.
The Old Gods, especially Mikani, detested this. He turned Poaranji and Renedin against Haxenylian.
THE SPARK
War officially began when Renedin murdered Lady Gaialana, trapping her in an eternal dream where she forgot to wake. Herbody simply stopped breathing. The Old Gods then made plans to murder Haxenylianʼs children and the newer gods as well.
Haxenylian allied with minor Old Gods, most notably Loart, to defend his children and the New Gods.
THE OUTCOME
The New Gods won the war, but both Loart and Haxenylian died as casualties.
Vapaz defeated Mikani through sheer unwillingness to die
Zopha defeated Poaranji (drowned by her grief)
Renedin survived but was later imprisoned in the Garden of Unspoken Names
Vapaz became King of the Gods-the first to ever hold such a title.

Two weeks after unitingthe local clans by force, he formally established House Patton as the royal house of Aicruae. Haliour I chose the site forhis capital based on a prophetic dream — he built the city of Lajazer atop a sheer mountain cliff, making it virtuallyimpregnable and a symbol of the Patton kingsʼ authority. His rule inaugurated an unbroken Patton dynasty that lastednearly two millennia. The founding of House Patton replaced the patchwork of chieftains with a centralized monarchy.Book Reference: TBD8,746 BREvent: Founding of House Arvento Location: Aicruae Key Figures: Lenkitta Arvento, King Haliour Layern Patton ISignificance: Established just thirteen years after House Pattonʼs rise, House Arvento became the second-oldest noblehouse in Aicruae. Its founder, Lenkitta Arvento, was a close friend and ally of King Haliour I. This personal friendshipformed the basis of a lasting political alliance: House Arvento swore loyalty to the Patton kings in exchange for landsand status. Over time, House Arvento gained renown for scholarship and law, with their scholars becoming trustedadvisors to the crown. Arvento remained neutral in inter-house conflicts and steadfastly loyal to the royal family - abond that helped Aicruae weather many crises and set the stage for the kingdomʼs stability. Event: The Haunted Lake IncidentLocation: Remote lakeside area near the AcademyKey Figures: Minara Gonia, Dahnyliein Catern, Nivaeran Veir, Professor Leranoan Gevhilem SoliSignificance: During an overnight mission, Minara sleepwalks toward a lake and nearly drowns. Dahnyliein, on first watch,wakes the others and they save her. Nivaeran reveals this isnʼt the first time - Minara has been sleepwalking since arrivingat the Academy. Professor Leranoan later confirms it was the work of a Valoka (a dream-plane demon). This is the firstindication that a sinister force - Renedin - is specifically targeting Minara. Dahnyliein becomes overprotective after nearlylosing her.Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4, Ch 14
Event: The Prophecy DiscoveredLocation: Solisian Academy ArchivesKey Figures: Minara Gonia, Professor Leranoan Gevhilem SoliSignificance: The group discovers an ancient prophecy: “When the Eclipsing Sun and the False Star meet, theold god shall shatter the world.” Professor Leranoanʼs momentary reaction - a flicker of recognition quickly masked —raises Minaraʼs suspicion. “Eclipsing Sun” refers to Minaraʼs hidden title as the firstborn of the Emperor.Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4, Ch 27
Event: The Nightmare Realm TrialLocation: Dream Realm (magical dimension created by Renedin)Key Figures: Renedin, the entire Special Division, Professor Leranoan/Soli, Elleraian Betenadia PattonSignificance: Renedin traps the Special Division in a magical dream realm where each member faces their deepest fear.Elleraianʼs nightmare - his mother transforming into a demon and denouncing him as a bastard failure - is so intense that hismind cannot escape, and he collapses into a coma in the real world. Sir Tonhe, Elleraianʼs biological father, is revealed to be
TIMELINE
25
a distant descendant of Snieoa Patton. This event takes the teamʼs only healer off the field at the worst possible time.Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4, Ch 38
Event: Truths Revealed - Minaraʼs Identity, Leranoan is Soli, Macenja is VandreaLocation: VariousKey Figures: Minara Gonia, Elleraian Betenadia Patton, Professor Leranoan/Soli, Empress Macenja/Vandrea, Emperor VeoOlem PattonSignificance: Multiple long-hidden truths come to light: Minara is the true princess (daughter of Emperor Veo and EmpressMacenja), Elleraian is her half-brother, Professor Leranoan is the god Soli in mortal form, and
Empress Macenja is actually Vandrea - the vengeful sister from A Tale of Three Sisters who has been posing as theEmpress for decades. These revelations reframe the entire story and raise the stakes for the final confrontation.Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4, Ch 3445

Renedin reveals to Soli that he is Soliʼs true father. Theyfight through waves of demons Karniode and Isaeri hold the front line, Silaena rigs explosives, Vasert and Nivaerancoordinate flanking maneuvers, Dahnyliein counters the Empressʼs generals. Silaena dies heroically. Soli and Vandrea fightback to back in a climactic confrontation that ends with Vandrea dying. Minara uses her magic with Soliʼs help to ensureVandreaʼs corrupted soul enters the great emptiness rather than eternal despair. Renedin is banished back to the divinevoid.Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4, Ch 4951

Soli faces Apharia and apologizes for everything hecaused. Apharia reveals their daughter “went to meet him a while ago,” confirming to the reader that Minara is thereincarnation of Soli and Aphariaʼs child. Ancient wrongs are righted. Restless souls find peace.Book Reference: A Crown of Glory Book 4, Ch 5152
