A PRINCESS IN LOVE BOOK
INFO
A PRINCESS IN LOVE BOOK INFO
Characters from The Book: Crandona Patton, Merigen Bleelack The Traitor),Sueli
Kokariffin, Hicksora Connorrita, Ala Reidskelisia, Amuseri Pontia, Thoati Gribela,
Eveli Cathon, Danik Malrancis,Wioli Schmidtavaca, Avromvog Stanyd.
A Princess in Love is the third and final prequel to Crown of Glory, spanning from
roughly 1 BR to 14 AR - fifteen years that transform Crandona Sarleia Patton from a
sheltered princess into a battle-hardened queen.
The Setup (  )
Crandona is twenty-four years old, the 94th royal princess and the only child of
Emperor Hevet Xacrey Patton and Empress Niara Werez Patton. Sheʼs been
spoiled her entire life - her parents have never once told her no. Sheʼs deeply in
love with her fiancé, Merigen Bleelack, and has no idea what he really is: a
descendant of the great sorcerer Verna, driven mad by persecution and
experimentation, who blames the royal family for the destruction of his people.
Crandonaʼs maid, Sueli Kokariffin, also carries a secret grudge - her witch mother
was burned at the stake by imperial guards, her father and brothers killed
defending her, and Sueli spent nearly sixteen years serving the child of the people
who destroyed her family. Sueli hated her existence until she met Merigen.
The Coup (  )
After Crandona and Merigen marry, Merigen stages a coup. He murders Emperor
Hevet Xacrey Patton right before Crandonaʼs eyes. Crandona is imprisoned and
set for execution, but a guard unwilling to join the rebellion lets her out of her cell.
She flees into the forest of the Caprlolan Kingdom, traumatized and alone.
Exile and Birth (0 AR)
∼1 BR
∼1 BR
A  PRINCESS IN LOVE BOOK INFO
1
In the Caprlolan forest, Crandona gives birth to her son - the future Emperor
Goteivati Zivc Patton III. She contemplates killing the baby. His birth resets the
calendar, marking the beginning of the “Reconstruction” epoch. This child has the
blood of the sky people through Esterica Kulioʼs line and the blood of the people of
the mountain through Merigen - two groups that hate each other, creating a kind
of twisted fate where two halves of himself are at war.
Merigenʼs Rule (  )
While Crandona is in exile, Merigen takes Sueli as his wife and rules the empire for
six years. Behind the scenes, the minor antagonist Vandrea - who at this point is
thousands of years old, powered by the imprisoned god Renedin - has taken a
new identity as “the Wise Woman.” She offers Sueli the ability to create a dark
magic child with Merigen, since Sueli was unable to conceive naturally. The child,
named Reio, lives for the six years of Merigenʼs reign.
Building the Rebellion (~1-14 AR)
In the Caprlolan forest, Crandona encounters a group of people living under the
protection of Danik Malrancis, a mysterious man abandoned at birth and raised by
wolves who serves as a father figure to all who wander into the forest. Crandona
gathers her allies - Hicksora Connorrita (a dukeʼs daughter who killed her abusive
forced husband at age eleven and fled), Ala Reidskelisia (a pirate captainʼs
daughter who left the sea for freedom), Amuseri Pontia (a wealthy girl with deep
ancestral spiritual connections who left home out of restlessness), Thoati Gribela
(a witch for hire on the run from imperial knights), and Eveli Cathon (a girl whose
father declared her the “fourteenth saint” and exploited her until his death). Over
the course of years, Crandona transforms from a naive princess into a determined
leader and wages a long campaign to reclaim her throne.
The Casualties
Throughout the rebellion, on various missions to restore peace, people die. Eveli is
killed. When Wioli Schmidtavaca - the sickly second son of Count Schmidtavaca
who fell in love with Eveli during the campaign - learns of her death, he storms
into battle despite his illness to retrieve her body. Heʼs struck down by over forty
∼1−6 AR
A  PRINCESS IN LOVE BOOK INFO
2
arrows, inspiring a folk song: “Wioli you desperate fool, you took a knife to your
heart, then your golden hair went dark.”
Avromvog Stanyad, “the Silent Death,” kills Danik Malrancis in battle. Ala then kills
Avromvog with her arrows, avenging her surrogate father.
The Siege and Reioʼs Death (  AR)
Crandonaʼs forces siege the castle. During the fighting, the six-year-old Reio
jumps in front of his mother Sueli to protect her and is impaled. Sueli uses the last
of her magical abilities, then calls upon the Wise Woman. Vandrea offers to use
Sueliʼs blood to create a spell that will kill Sueli but allow Reioʼs soul to live on -
merged with the soul already present within Crandonaʼs child, Goteivati. Sueli
accepts and dies. Her sacrifice unknowingly dooms the empire: Reioʼs corrupted
soul merging with Goteivati is what will eventually turn him into the tyrant who
destroys the Matsiali culture and ushers in the Dark Ages.
The Throne Room (  )
In the climax, Crandona confronts Merigen inside the throne room. After a heavy
and bloody battle, she kills him. But the victory is immediately undermined: the
Wise Woman appears and uses Merigenʼs immense residual magic (which persists
even after his death) to open a portal corrupting the world doors on the Mystic
Isles, creating demons, trapping the gods in their realm, and leaving humanity to
face an onslaught of demonic incursions that will plague the empire for the next
 years.
The Aftermath
By the end, Crandona is queen again. Hicksora and Ala become a couple. But the
victory is hollow on every level - her son carries the corrupted merged soul of
Reio within him, the world doors have been corrupted, and the seeds of the Dark
Ages have been planted in her own womb. Everything the Golden Millennia built is
about to be destroyed by the child she fought so hard to protect.

Backstory (key events that shaped them): Crandona was born the only child and

dangerous secret and a vendetta against her family. After they married, Merigen

staged a coup, murdering her father before her eyes and seizing the throne.
Crandona barely escaped execution - a guard unwilling to join the rebellion
released her from her cell. She fled into the forest of the Caprlolan Kingdom,
where she gave birth to her son (the future Emperor Goteivati III) at age twentyfive. Alone and stripped of everything, she transformed from a sheltered princess
into a warrior queen. She gathered a group of women - Hicksora, Ala, Amuseri,
Thoati, and Eveli - and over the course of years waged a campaign to reclaim her
throne. She killed Merigen in a heavy, bloody battle inside the throne room and
became queen again, but her victory was hollow: her son carried the merged soul
of the dark magic child Reio, and the seeds of the empireʼs Dark Ages had already
been planted in her own womb.

sorcerer Verna, the Grand Mage who received magic from Iswan and founded
A  PRINCESS IN LOVE BOOK INFO

Vikistv. His mother was persecuted for being a witch - she was killed, along with
his father and other family members. Merigen was told by his adoptive parents
that his mother died giving birth to him; he only later discovered the truth. His
powers manifested far earlier and far more powerfully than most magic users.
When he revealed his abilities to his adoptive family, they experimented on him,
trying to find a “cure” for his “illness.” There was no cure. Merigen eventually went
mad - his magical power overtook him and he killed not only his adoptive family
but the surrounding people of the village he grew up in. Blaming the royal family of
the Solisian Empire for his misfortune (they created and upheld the persecution of
magic users), he set out on a path of revenge. He seduced the naive Princess
Crandona, married her, then staged a coup, murdering her father Emperor Hevet
Xacrey Patton. He ruled for six years with Sueli Crandonaʼs former maid) as his
wife, before Crandonaʼs rebellion reached the throne room. Crandona killed him in
a heavy and bloody battle - though even in death his power persisted: Vandrea
used his immense residual magic to corrupt the world doors on the Mystic Isles.
Family: Biological parents (deceased, persecuted as witches), adoptive parents

Emperor Goteivati III (biological son via Crandona)

Connorrita. Backstory (key events that shaped them): Hicksora was born Lady
Hicksora, daughter of Duke Connorrita of the Caprlolan Kingdom. Duke Connorrita
was an ambitious man who did not hesitate to sell all seven of his daughters into
marriage to advance the family name. Hicksora was eleven years old when she
was sold to Marquess Benen, a twenty-seven-year-old man. The Marquess hated
Hicksora because her status before marriage was far above his own. He often hit
her and threatened to parade her around his house so she would “know her
place.” On the night of their official wedding night, Hicksora waited for him to fall
asleep in his drunken state and stabbed him twenty-seven times in his chest. She
blamed his murder on a knight who had witnessed the Marquess hitting her. After
the funeral, Hicksora escaped, fearing her father would sell her again. She fled
into the forest of the Caprlolan Kingdom, where she eventually met Ala. They lived
together as friends - and later became a couple.

want treasure - she wanted to know the thrill of being on land, the thrill of

to the forest, living and surviving as a hunter rather than a pirate.

Backstory (key events that shaped them): Eveli was born the only daughter of her

VANDREAʼS CORRUPTION OF THE WORLD DOOR
VANDREA AND THE CORRUPTED WORLD DOOR
During the events of A Princess in Love, Vandrea corrupted an unstable world
door - one of the weak points in Vapazʼs barrier between the physical and mental
realms. This deliberate act of sabotage is the reason demons leak through
unevenly rather than flooding the world all at once. The corrupted door
destabilized the barrierʼs ability to slow demonic reconstitution, reducing the time
from centuries to months or years.
This single act is the direct cause of the escalating demon threat that reaches
crisis proportions by Minaraʼs era in A Crown of Glory.
A  PRINCESS IN LOVE BOOK INFO

ROLE IN PLOT
Vandrea appears as “The Wise Woman,” a mysterious figure who has received a
power boost from the buried god Renedin. She serves as a minor antagonist,
working her own agenda while technically serving Renedinʼs larger plans.
Key Story Beats:
Helps Sueli Merigenʼs new wife) conceive a dark magic child named Reio
Reio dies protecting his mother during Crandonaʼs siege
In the climax, uses Merigen Bleelackʼs immense residual magic to corrupt the
world doors on the Mystic Isles
This corruption traps gods in their realm and unleashes demons on the mortal
world
Creates the incursions that will plague the empire for the next  years
PURPOSE IN NARRATIVE
Her corruption of the world doors is the bookʼs lasting consequence: Crandona
wins her throne back, but Vandrea ensures the victory is hollow. The demon
incursions she enables will eventually facilitate Renedinʼs larger plan and give her
future self (as Empress Macenja) the tools to destabilize the empire from within.
CONNECTION TO OTHER BOOKS
Follows directly from A Tale of Three Sisters (her deal with Renedin)
Sets up the demon problem central to Crown of Glory

Irisʼs “wife”) Date of birth: Unknown Pireaynean) Gender: Female Sexuality:

Unknown (enslaved) Backstory: A slave girl brought back from Pireaynea during
Orcusʼs raids. Iris became obsessed with her because of her resemblance to Lady
Emillea Hige Solisʼs mother). Iris took Yera as her personal maid, tortured her, and
eventually forced her into becoming her “wife.” Although Iris claimed to love Yera,
it was obsessive possession-Yera despised Iris and wanted to rip her skin off
every time Iris touched her. Iris forced another slave who resembled herself to
impregnate Yera, then killed him. Yera went into labor for three days; when she
finally pushed the baby out, it was dead, and she was too exhausted to survive.
Her death broke something in Iris and drove her to even greater cruelty. Physical
description: Resembles Lady Emillea Hige Personality: Gentle, silenced, trapped
Character inspiration: Gilly GoT + Shireen Baratheon GoT - gentleness under
systemic abuse; tragedy as indictment of the regime

Character Name: Jaifey Yurea Role in story: Side Character / Kingmaker Date of
birth: Unknown Ghercian) Gender: Male Sexuality: Unknown Age: Adult during
war Family: Daughter - Tixsei Yurea Backstory: A devout Ghercian military genius
whose strategic knowledge surpassed even Solisʼs. He joined Solisʼs army with
60,000 Ghercian men and quickly became indispensable. Solis appointed him as
general of the second army. Jaifeyʼs ambition became apparent when he
presented his daughter Tixsei as a potential lady-in-waiting to Esterica-a dynastic
play to eventually produce an heir between Solis and Tixsei. He co-ran the Maeret
Orana torture program and pushed for brutal reprisals. His
plans were frustrated when Solis declared Maen as heir, blocking his dynastic
gambit. After Estericaʼs death, Tixsei did become Solisʼs second queen-but their
children Snieoa and Bier) never inherited the throne. Personality: Cold, doctrinal,
ruthless, ambitious Talent: Military strategy, logistics Character inspiration: Grand
Moff Tarkin Star Wars) + Tywin Lannister GoT - cold doctrine and logistics over
sentiment; “ends justify” absolutist
Character Name: Tixsei Yurea Role in story: Minor Character →  Second Empress
Date of birth: Unknown Ghercian) Gender: Female Sexuality: Straight Age: Young
woman during war Family: Father - Jaifey Yurea; Children - Snieoa Patton, Bier
Patton Backstory: Introduced as her father Jaifeyʼs political gambit. Placed as
Estericaʼs lady-in-waiting, she grew close to Solis during Estericaʼs forced
absence and represented the threat in Estericaʼs nightmares. After Estericaʼs death
by Harnuaʼs poison, Tixsei became Solisʼs second queen-the political solution to a
personal void. She gave him two children, but neither inherited the throne; Bier
died of fever at 17, and Snieoa was passed over for Maen. Personality: Poised,
calculated, patient Character inspiration: Anne Boleyn The Tudors) + Shiv Roy
Succession) - poised ascent, agenda under etiquette
Character Name: Grand Sorcerer Sevtor of Vikistv Role in story: Minor Antagonist
Date of birth: Unknown Vikistv) Gender: Male Sexuality: Unknown Age: Adult
Family: House Orana; Sons including Cequailian (betrothed to Iris) and Maeret
Orana Backstory: The grand sorcerer of Vikistv and head of House Orana, the
magical ruling family. He arrived in Aicruae with Duke Reasaec Kivier of Equateiy
to avenge Iris (who was betrothed to his son Cequailian) and prop up Orcus.
Sevtor unleashed a devastating magical strike on Valea that killed approximately
15,000 people-demonstrating the catastrophic potential of organized magic. This
act radicalized Solisʼs coalition and legitimized brutal reprisals; his entire house
A  T ALE OF A  THOUSAND SONGS BOOK INFO
2
was subsequently burned alive except for one escapee Mekean. Character
inspiration: Saruman LotR + Vilgefortz The Witcher) technomagical escalation,
city-leveling intent.

Date of birth: Unknown Equateiy) Gender: Male Sexuality: Unknown Age: Adult
Backstory: The Duke of Equateiy who financed Orcusʼs war effort. He traveled to
Aicruae personally with Grand Sorcerer Sevtor to aid Orcus after Irisʼs death.
When the war turned against Orcus, Reasaec attempted to flee by
ship. Solis personally attacked the fleeing vessel, captured him, and beheaded
him. Solis sent the head to Gherci with a note written in Ananara: “The head of a
rat-do as you please with it.” The King of Gherci had the head preserved, mouth
forced open, and hung at the castle entrance. Character inspiration: Lord Cutler
Beckett Pirates of the Caribbean) — financier-bureaucrat who outsources atrocity
for order

(catalyst) Date of birth: Unknown Gherci Gender: Female Sexuality: Unknown
Age: Adult Family: Daughter of the King of Gherci Backstory: A Ghercian princess
sent as diplomatic envoy to discuss strategic plans with Solis. Iris and Harnua
plotted to assassinate her to disrupt Solisʼs alliances. They attacked her ships,
killing Kamerida and ten of her high-ranking ladies-in-waiting. Her death triggered

exact opposite of what the twins intended. Character inspiration: Padmé Amidala
Star Wars) - diplomatic idealism that meets realpolitik steel
Character Name: Dame Kisaleli Jaeren Role in story: Minor Antagonist Date of
birth: Unknown Gender: Female Sexuality: Unknown Age: Adult Family: Trained by
Ser Wanez from age 2 Backstory: A fearsome warrior trained by Ser Wanez since
the age of two, bred for war and absolute loyalty to Orcus. In the Fight of Titian
Chapter 62, she single-handedly fought Solisʼs entire first and second army,
killing 700 men before the god Razar momentarily blinded her, allowing Solis to
slip through and stab her in the chest. Her final words were “Glory to Orcus, the
one true king.” Solis slit her throat shortly after. Talent: Legendary combat abilities
Character inspiration: The Mountain GoT + ORen Ishii Kill Bill) - bred-for-war
executioner; awe and horror in equal measure

3

loyal to Orcus who faced Solis during the final assault on the capital. When

Character inspiration: Brienne of Tarth GoT + Maximus Gladiator) - honor-first

Unknown Gender: Female Family: Mother - Dame Exara Solisʼs second assistant
general) Backstory: A noblewoman who sided with Orcus against her own mother,
Dame Exara, who served as second assistant general of Solisʼs first army. Mother
and daughter fought against each other during the final battle for the capital.
Dame Exara killed her own daughter and refused to recover the body afterward,
labeling her a traitor to the gods. Character inspiration: Yara Greyjoy GoT - dutyforward, will fight kin if the oath demands it

Unknown Gender: Female Family: Daughter - Lady Olia Backstory: The second
assistant general of Solisʼs first army. During the final battle for the capital, she

Raʼs al Ghul Batman Begins) - forger of weapons in human form; ethics

Character Name: Maeret Orana of Vikistv Role in story: Minor Character (victim)
Date of birth: Unknown Vikistv) Gender: Male Family: Father - Grand Sorcerer
Sevtor; House Orana Backstory: The third son of Grand Sorcerer Sevtor of Vikistv.
After Sevtorʼs devastating magical attack on Valea, Solisʼs forces kidnapped
Maeret and experimented on him to discover the weakness of magic users.
A  T ALE OF A  THOUSAND SONGS BOOK INFO
4
Despite Maeretʼs repeated pleas for mercy, explaining he had no control over his
fatherʼs actions, Solis ignored him and permitted further experiments. They
eventually learned that fire is deadly to magic users because their cold-dependent
bodies cannot handle high temperatures. Maeret was killed along with most of
House Orana when Solis had their chambers set ablaze. Character inspiration:
Stranger Things test subjects Brennerʼs lab) — captive asset exploited for
“science”
Character Name: Mekean Orana Role in story: Background (survivor) Date of birth:
Unknown Vikistv) Gender: Female Family: House Orana (all others killed)
Backstory: The sole survivor of House Oranaʼs extermination. When Solis had her
entire family burned alive in their chambers, Mekean escaped by dying her hair
and settling in Equateiy. She continued the Orana family line in exile-her
descendants eventually include Merigen Bleelack, who becomes significant in
later eras.
Character inspiration: Arya Stark GoT - reinvention, low profile, long game
survivor
Character Name: Vinala Hinkina Role in story: Minor Character Date of birth:
Unknown
Gender: Unknown Backstory: Co-general of Solisʼs second army alongside Jaifey
Yurea. Died while securing Solisʼs escape route during an ambush in northern
Aicruae Year Four). Solis was forced to retreat without recovering Vinalaʼs body.
Upon returning to Valea, Solis slapped Mihel in front of the court for pushing him
into the trap and banished Mihel until the mourning period ended.
Character Name: Maen Patton Role in story: Minor Character (heir) Date of birth:
7,217 BR Year Four of the war) Gender: Male Family: Father - Solis Elias Patton;
Mother - Esterica Kulio; Sister - Coyre Patton Backstory: Born during the fourth
year of the civil war to Solis and Esterica. Iris threatened to kill him, forcing
Esterica into hiding. Solis declared Maen his heir after receiving a prophetic dream
from goddess Nimlye showing history repeating itself with sons fighting for the
throne. Maen was 54 when he took the throne after Solisʼs death. He ruled for 23
years, renamed the empire “The Solisian Empire,” but produced no heirs despite
three wives. Upon his death in 7,140 BR, the throne passed to his sister Coyreʼs
eldest son. Character inspiration: Tommen Baratheon GoT — soft-hearted heir
weaponized by othersʼ agendas

Character Name: Coyre Patton Role in story: Minor Character Date of birth: 7,215
BR (two years into Solisʼs rule) Gender: Female Family: Father - Solis Elias Patton;
Mother - Esterica Kulio; Brother - Maen Patton Backstory: Born two years into
Solisʼs rule, nicknamed “the light of the kingdom” for her beauty and embodiment
of House Patton traits. Her mother Esterica died just six months after her birth,
killed by Harnuaʼs poison intended for Solis. Coyre later built a museum in honor of
her mother, titling Esterica “Mother of a Dynasty.” When her brother Maen died
without
heirs, Coyreʼs eldest son inherited the throne. Character inspiration: Grogu The
Mandalorian) emblem of renewal; everyone projects a future onto her
King Benjamin Lawerence Patton II Reign: Unknown
 BR House: Patton (Royal Family) Family:
Father of Orcus, Iris (by Queen Mihai Julie Patton), and
Solis (by Lady Emillea Hige)
The last king of Aicruae before the civil war. Benjamin IIʼs reign was marked by
personal scandal and political instability that ultimately destroyed his kingdom.
After taking Lady Emillea Hige as a concubine and fathering Solis, he openly
favored his illegitimate son over his legitimate twins, Iris and Orcus. This favoritism
drove Queen Mihai Julie Patton to madness (a combination of psychosis and
schizophrenia) and eventual death.
At the Festival of Mourning in 7,241 BR, Benjamin II made the unprecedented
decision to name nine-year-old Solis as his heir, officially disinheriting the twins.
He died suddenly four months later under mysterious circumstances. Two weeks
after his death, Iris and Orcus seized the throne and executed Lady Emillea,
sparking the civil war that would consume Aicruae.
Benjamin II is remembered as a deeply flawed ruler-contemporaries called him
“the drunken fool” behind his back. His court consisted largely of sycophants who
stroked his ego while plotting their own advancement. His decision to favor Solis
over the twins, while perhaps well-intentioned, created the succession crisis that
led to the deaths of all three of his children and the transformation of Aicruae from
kingdom to empire.
−7,241
A  T ALE OF A  THOUSAND SONGS BOOK INFO
6
Queen Mihai Julie Patton (of House Vika) Reign:
Unknown - c. 7,243 BR House: Vika (by
birth), Patton (by marriage) Family: Wife of King Benjamin II; Mother of Orcus and
Iris; Daughter of Duke Rarielo Vika
The queen whose destruction became the emotional foundation for the civil war.
Mihai Julie was the daughter of the powerful Duke Rarielo Vika, married to King
Benjamin II as a political alliance to prevent House Vika from turning against the
crown. For a time, she was renowned as the courtʼs precious gem and the love of
the kingʼs life.
Everything changed when Benjamin took Lady Emillea Hige as a concubine. The
public humiliation of watching her husband dote on another woman-and then
watching that womanʼs son be elevated
above her own children-drove Mihai into a mental break described as a
combination of psychosis and schizophrenia. She attempted suicide after Solisʼs
birth and was placed on medical supervision.
Mihai died during the twinsʼ childhood, her death accelerating their psychological
spiral. Both Iris and Orcus inherited her brown hair (unlike Solisʼs blonde), which

TIMELINE
Age 9 Harnua first fell for Orcus (childhood infatuation). Her mother wanted her to
marry Solis, the respectable prince, but Harnua was deeply infatuated with Orcus.
Rather than disappoint her mother, Harnua ignored her own feelings.

on his birthday and on the anniversary of his motherʼs death.

willing to kill for him. Orcus was emotionally unavailable - he grew up with a

entries.title: Key Words And Terms
entries.text:
KEY WORDS AND TERMS
KEY WORDS AND TERMS
THE TEIRE
The temple administration owns Gherciʼs grand central temple in the capital of
Tarmet. The Teire is the most powerful religious institution in Gherci, effectively
making the kingdom a semi-hierocratic state. The institution is led by the Main
Master (high priest) who oversees religious law, and his inner circle includes the
Lord Protector of the temple and the Supreme Inner Court keeper. The Main
Master of The Teire technically outranks the king in matters of faith and can
dictate certain policies, giving the priesthood enormous influence over Ghercian
governance.
ASATA
Asata is the divine language spoken among the gods. It is primarily a spoken
language - divine communication does not require writing - though written
fragments exist in pre-War of Gods I artifacts. Asata cannot be learned by mortals
without divine ancestry. House Kulio could speak Asata due to their Sky People
heritage, though the ability degraded over successive generations. The saint
Harnua understood some words but could not speak fluently. By Minaraʼs era, the
Kulios have lost the ability entirely and only recognize sacred phrases as prayers
without understanding their literal meaning.
THE GATE
A moving hell dimension with no fixed location that can spawn anywhere on the
Mystic Isles at any given time. The Gate brings monsters from both the realm of
the gods and the dream plane into the mortal world. It is the central mystery of A
Crown of Glory - no one in the story knows why it appeared. After the Empress is
defeated, the characters believe she caused it. The Gate is connected to the
corrupted world doors that Vandrea damaged during A Princess in Love using
Merigenʼs residual magic, now worsened by Renedinʼs influence as he attempts to
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
1
break the barrier between realms entirely. Appears in A Crown of Glory Book 4.
Cross-reference: LOCATIONS  The Gate.
Gates and world doors are the same structures referred to by different
terminology. Mortals call them “gates” while theologians and mages call them
“world doors.” They are weak points in the barrier Vapaz raised after the War of
Gods I — not created by anyone, but scar tissue from attempting to separate
realms that naturally flow into each other. The Mystic Isles were always liminal, a
place where the mental and physical realms overlapped even before the barrier
existed. When Vapaz raised the barrier, the Isles could not be fully sealed because
they were inherently in-between.
Ekhasostio and Paxtinoʼs birth - twins born of divine grief, one tear becoming two
- resonated with these natural weak points, making the doors more navigable and
responsive to mortal emotion and intention. Before the twins, the doors were just
tears in reality. After the twins, they became something closer to portals, still
dangerous but usable by those who approached them correctly.
The legend of Ekhasostio and Paxtino standing guard at the gates is a religious
interpretation, not literal truth. The twins do not physically stand there. The idea
that “one leads to salvation, one leads to ruin” reflects the actual danger: one door
was always more stable while the other was closer to breaking. Vandrea corrupted
the unstable door during A Princess in Love, which is why demons leak through
unevenly rather than flooding the world all at once.
DALIKA UAER
Dalika Uaer is the first known person to survive a Valoka demon possession. After
the encounter, Dalika created a warning drawing documenting the experience,
which became the earliest recorded visual description of a Valoka - an eight-foottall purple spirit with bug-like wings that attacks through the dream plane.
ETHNIC GROUPS (TAILI, BARIE, NEMERI, GUIO)
The four major ethnic groups of the world - Taili, Barie, Nemeri, and Guio -
originated from the dispersal of peoples after the Age of Origin, with geography
shaping distinct populations over millennia.
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
2
Taili settled the southern and central regions, primarily Gherci, adapting to warm
climates. Barie populated the western territories of Aicruae and Pireaynea,
adapting to cooler climates. Nemeri established themselves in coastal areas and
islands, primarily Coelum, developing a maritime culture. Guio settled the eastern
mountains, primarily Vikistv.
Current population distributions reflect both ancient settlement patterns and more
recent historical events including wars, migrations, and imperial conquest.
DANEPELIE
The Danepelie is the governing council of the Cidet, composed of senior priests
representing all twelve gods. No single nation controls the Danepelie — the
council guards the Cidetʼs sacred neutrality and operates with its own temple
guards (volunteers who sever all national allegiances), its own treasury (funded by
pilgrim donations), and its own religious law that supersedes secular law within
temple grounds. The High Conclave guards the Cidetʼs independence jealously.
See also: LOCATIONS doc — Cidet entry for full governance details)
MONSTRU PLAGUE
A plague that killed a lesser lord and his entire family who owned Gavara Castle,
located near the Solisian Academy. After the lordʼs death, the castle was
abandoned and eventually renovated into the Training Grounds used by Academy
students and the Special Division. The exact nature, origin, and timeline of the
Monstru Plague are not yet detailed - it is unclear whether the plague was
magical, natural, or connected to the demon incursions. Referenced in A Crown of
Glory Book 4.
HAITAK
A drug regularly used by Vandrea Asleleri for anger management. Vandrea, the
second daughter of City Lord Ceval of Torad, had anger management issues from

THE GREAT TEMPTRESS
A posthumous name given to Apharia Asleleri by the gods and goddesses after
the Second War of the Gods. Apharia, the youngest of the three sisters from
Torad, fell in love with Soli (the mortal form of the twin gods Paxtino and
Ekhasostio) while living in exile in the Nedi Forest of Equateiy. She became
pregnant by him, a union that violated the First Divine Law and triggered the
Second War of the Gods. As punishment, the god Vapaz killed both Apharia and
her daughter.
The godsʼ choice to name Apharia “The Great Temptress” places the blame on her
rather than on Soli - the god who chose to walk among mortals and pursue a
relationship with a human woman. This framing reflects the power dynamics
between gods and mortals: the mortal woman is blamed for “tempting” a god,

THE OATH OF MEMIET - ORIGIN AND PURPOSE
The Oath of Memiet was created by Iswan, Goddess of Alchemy, as a fail-safe
when she proposed the Saint system to Vapaz. The Oath functions as a binding
contract: gods cannot take from mortals without giving something in return. All
divine-mortal transactions must be mutual.
This makes the gods contractually vulnerable to mortals in ways they did not
initially anticipate. The Oath is also the reason Javehet magic (god-granted magic)
is so rare - the cost of granting it is real for the gods.
The Oath was part of Iswanʼs long-term plan to reduce mortal dependence on
divine whim. By forcing reciprocity, she ensured that gods could not simply

ECLIPSING SUN

Solisian Empire. The term carries both literal and symbolic weight - the firstborn is
the “sun” that will one day eclipse the

Prince Elleraian Betenadia Patton is publicly recognized as the first Eclipsing Sun,

true Eclipsing Sun, hidden since birth when Empress Macenja ordered her
execution for being female. An ancient Academy prophecy references the title:
“When the Eclipsing Sun and the False Star meet, the old god shall shatter the
world.” Minara is unaware of her connection to this prophecy for most of the story.
VALOKA
A type of demon that operates on the dream plane, luring souls out of their bodies

because their attacks leave no visible marks and can be mistaken for ordinary

activity as the likely cause when Minara Gonia begins sleepwalking dangerously at

orchestrated by Empress Macenja/Vandrea in service of Renedinʼs plan to break

THE SPECIAL DIVISION
A highly specialized division within the Solisian Academy established to train
soldiers with the skills necessary to combat the constant threat posed by demons
and monsters. Members of the Special Division execute covert missions and
adhere to orders issued directly by the Council of Seven. Joining the division
means the student has demonstrated the potential to protect the Empire from
attack, and their commitment must be unwavering. The division operates under a
structured role system with
assigned code names - each memberʼs code name corresponds to the name of
one of the Twelve Saints, reflecting the sacred duty the division carries. The role
structure is as follows:
Team Leader - Commands the unit in the field and makes final tactical decisions.
The Leader bears ultimate responsibility for mission success and the safety of all
members.
Frontline Manager - Coordinates offensive operations and directs the Frontline
Defenders during combat. Acts as the Leaderʼs right hand in battle.
Secondline Manager - Coordinates defensive and support operations, directing
Secondline Defenders, Healers, and Crafters. Ensures the teamʼs logistics and
fallback strategies remain intact.
Frontline Defender — The primary combatants who engage enemies directly.
Frontline Defenders are the first to face threats and bear the heaviest physical
risk.

THE WEEKDAYS
The seven-day week in the Solisian Empire is named after the gods of new. Each
day carries the name of a deity, reflecting the centrality of divine worship in
everyday life. The days are: Vapaz Monday, Razar Tuesday), Finore
Wednesday), Nellebrie Thursday), Nimlye Friday, Zopha Saturday), and Allan

Nellebrie, while Ethics and Lawful Governing meets on Nimlye and Zopha.

LIFE AND DEATH MAGIC (Vikistv Classification)
The people of Vikistv believed that magic users can be grouped into two
categories: Life and Death.
Life magic encompasses Nature, Healing, and Purity - it is the accepted,
respected form of magic practiced openly in Vikistv.
Death magic encompasses Chaos, Destruction, and the Peculiar - it is considered
extremely taboo. Practitioners of death magic are viewed with suspicion and fear.

after hearing an Equateiy townsman insult her family, she unconsciously causes
him to choke. She describes feeling “the darkness from deep within her soul” and
hears a faint voice telling her to kill him. This is the readerʼs first account of a
character tapping into the death side of magic.

Noirta:
The myth of the first song that founded the world. Noirta is more than a myth-it is
the fabric of time and power, teaching that no soul ever truly dies. Souls cycle
through existence like droplets in air. Death is but a pause in a very long song, and
like all songs, souls have a start and finish—but the best transcend, create, fade,
and repeat. Each time we die, our souls stay intact. A good person shall be reborn
as a calm infant; a bad person might become a tyrant. Souls are so intricate that
even the gods cannot change their fundamental nature.
Noirta is the first song-the fabric of time and power, the endless cycle of souls
and energy that makes existence possible. It is not a being, not a creator deity,
and not a myth in the conventional sense. It simply is, and always has been, and
always will be. No soul ever truly dies; they cycle through Noirta endlessly,
carrying experiences from past lives into new bodies. Death is but a pause in a
very long song. The four Old Gods Renedin, Mikani, Poaranji, Haxenylian)
crystallized from Noirta as the cosmosʼs first conscious expressions, but they did
not create it and do not fully understand it. There is no one above the Song. The
twin prophets Vekta and Aryanara were the first to translate Noirtaʼs cosmic nature
into teachings mortals could follow, and their work became the foundation of the
Circle of Eternal Light.

The first successful coup against the royal family of Aicruae, lasting only a few

corrupted. Souls live through multiple lifetimes, and an Eternal Sign represents the
idea that no matter what body you are born into, your soul will always be born in a

KEY  WORDS AND TERMS

When a soul changes so fundamentally that it no longer resonates with Noirtaʼs

THE AGE OF ORIGIN
The Age of Origin refers to the primordial era when Noirta, the Great Song, first
brought existence into being. This was the time before time as mortals understand
it - when the first souls were created, when the cycle of rebirth began, and when
the fabric of reality was woven from sound and divine intention.
Everything that exists now carries an echo of that original song. Souls are not
created anew with each birth but are fragments of that first chorus, cycling

endlessly through mortal forms, carrying pieces of every life they have lived
before.
The twin sisters Vekta and Aryanara, founders of the Circle of Eternal Light in
14,271 BR, devoted their lives to teaching humanity about this sacred origin. They
traveled the world spreading the truth that death holds no dominion over the soul,
that corruption alone can break the cycle, and that the divine order established at
creation still governs all existence. Aryanara recorded Vektaʼs speeches, and
these writings became the foundational texts of the Circle.
The lands that briefly bore their names after their deaths were less important than
the spiritual inheritance they left behind - a theological tradition that has endured
for over fourteen thousand years.
House Caternʼs motto, “For the age of origin and for the strength of Aryanara and
Vekta,” declares their role as guardians of this inheritance. They do not protect
physical borders so much as defend the foundational truths the sisters revealed.
Against competing beliefs like the Brotherhood of Westwinds, which venerates
only the gods of old, House Catern stands as a bulwark for the Circleʼs teachings:
that old and new are part of the same eternal song, and that humanityʼs souls have
been singing since the very beginning.

Arvento, completed around 8,126 BR during a time of relative peace. The Arvento
Code standardized principles of fair taxation, trade rights, and port regulations
across Aicruae. It became the de facto constitution of Aicruaeʼs kingdom and was
so well-crafted that when Aicruae later grew into the Solisian Empire, the Arvento
Code heavily influenced the Imperial Code that governed all nations. Distinct from
the earlier Code of Esa - Saint Argellonʼs Code of Esa established moral and
philosophical legal foundations, while the Arvento Code focused on practical
governance, commerce, and administration. See also: THE CODE OF ESA, INFANT
LAWS.

Liazen. Recognizes exceptional contributions to the kingdom beyond standard
queenly duties. No other woman in Aicruaeʼs history has received this honor.
KING CONSORT
Title given to a male royal spouse when the ruling monarch is female. Example:
King Consort Teravian Geraser Patton, husband and brother of Queen Naila Deyua
Patton. Unlike standard kings, consorts do not hold primary ruling authority.
THE GREAT LADY OF HOUSE PATTON
Honorary title bestowed upon Queen Cawiloan Heka Patton for giving birth to King
Hailour Layern Patton II, recognizing her role in continuing the dynastyʼs most
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
55
significant bloodline.
MOTHER OF THE GREAT AICRUAEAN DYNASTY
Title referring to Queen Walica Kevena Patton, the first official Queen of Aicruae
and mother of the founding royal line, though she is often overshadowed by other
family members despite this distinction.
THE BENAIN FAMILY
The most powerful family in the region before Aicruaeʼs official founding. Led by
Dures the Great (also called Dures Benain), who eventually bowed to King Hailour
Layern Patton I and offered his daughter Walica as bride. The family had a “nasty
reputation” that transferred to Queen Walica, causing her to be disrespected
despite her queenly status.
DURES THE GREAT
Father of Queen Walica Kevena Patton and the most powerful warlord in the
region before King Hailour Layern Patton I unified Aicruae. The first major figure to
bow to Hailour and acknowledge him as king. Also known as Dures Benain.
THE CASUST FAMILY
Family of Queen Vala Uinara Patton, distantly related to the Benain family through
maternal lines. Pavim Casust (father), Malejia Casust (mother), and Kaseieke
Casust (younger brother who died in infancy) comprised Valaʼs immediate family.
HOUSE MENA
Noble house connected to the royal family through Princess Aliedea Cawiloan
Pattonʼs marriage to Duke Nayiler Mena. This house produced Lady Naern Mena
and Lady Vaseiula Mena, twin daughters who maintained royal bloodlines.
PASSING ON CEREMONY
Funeral rites for deceased royalty. When King Benjaien Nefest Patton died, Queen
Cawiloan refused to attend, instead wearing white (mourning color) and visiting
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
56
her mother Queen Valaʼs grave.
THE LIAZEN ROYAL SET
Jewelry collection brought to the royal treasury by Queen Isalian Liazen from her
massive dowry, which was twice the size of the entire Aicruaean royal treasury.
HAILOURʼS FAVORITE COLLECTION
Jewelry collection commissioned by Queen Isalian Liazen, pieces that King Hailour
Layern Patton II particularly admired.
THE SNAKE EYE COLLECTION
One of Queen Isalian Liazenʼs commissioned jewelry collections added to the royal
treasury.
THE BREGARIA COLLECTION
Queen Isalianʼs largest jewelry commission, containing  pieces of flowery
jewelry made from gems in her enormous dowry. Reflects her love of flowers.
THE JEWELS OF DAGALREA
Jewelry collection added to the royal treasury by Queen Isalian Liazen.
THE RUINS OF INALIA COLLECTION
Jewelry collection added to the royal treasury by Queen Isalian Liazen.
THE CROWN OF ROSES
Symbolic gift presented by fourteen-year-old King Hailour Layern Patton II to
twelve-year-old Isalian Liazen when he won a tournament in 8,658 BR. This public
gesture made Isalian acknowledge his feelings for the first time. Represents the
turning point in their legendary love story.
THE GREAT THRONE ROOM OF AICRUAE
37+
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
57
Designed by Queen Isalian Liazen as one of her many architectural contributions
to the kingdom of Aicruae.
THE ROYAL MEETING SPACE OF AICRUAE
Layout and design created by Queen Isalian Liazen for official government
functions.
THE ROYAL TRAINING GROUNDS OF AICRUAE
Constructed with Queen Isalian Liazenʼs help for training knights and soldiers.
BALCONIES
Architectural feature introduced to Aicruae by Queen Isalian Liazen, previously
unknown in the region of Aicruae
MESSENGER BIRDS
Communication system concept created by Queen Isalian Liazen as an innovation
for the kingdom of Aicruae
ROSE-SCENTED PERFUME
The first perfumes in Aicruae, specifically rose-scented, introduced and helped
created by Queen Isalian Liazen.
GREENERY INITIATIVE
Queen Isalianʼs addition of trees and wildlife around the castle and capital city to
combat health issues, specifically cases of people passing out (likely from heat or
poor air quality).
THE GRAND WEDDING OF ISALIAN AND HAILOUR
Married in 8,656 BR (two years after the tournament), this ceremony was funded
by Queen Isalianʼs own dowry and was so grand that all of Aicruae was permitted
to attend. Their love story inspired countless songs and fantastical tales.
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
58
FAMOUS QUOTES:
Historical and Well known Quotes
Queen Isalian Liazen
“No matter how sad the fact is, Queens arenʼt allowed
to be victims…”
Queen Isalian Liazenʼs famous quote to her daughter Queen Naila Deyua Patton:
“No matter how sad the fact is, Queens arenʼt allowed to be victims. We can be
everything else though, Daughters, Wives, and Mothers. My daughter you are
going to be queen one day and you must never allow yourself to be anything but
what you are. My Daughter. Promise me that.” Later quoted by Queen Naila during
a meeting with foreign representatives who were frustrated that she ruled instead
of her husband, King Consort Teravian Geraser Patton.
King Benjaien Nefest Patton “Old Prude, Worthless
Bitch, and the Bane of My
Existence”
Epithets King Benjaien Nefest Patton used to describe his wife Queen Vala Uinara
Patton. He resented her because his mother Queen Walica placed her as his wife
to control him, and he hated that Vala was older than him and “looked more like a
king than him.”
QUEEN ISALIAN LIAZENʼS DOWRY
The largest dowry in Aicruaean history, valued at twice the entire royal treasury at
the time of her marriage. Contents included: 17 estates, 42 boxes/crates of silk
and furs, 38 full boxes/crates of jewels, and immense amounts of jewelry. This
wealth funded the Grand Wedding and many of Queen Isalianʼs architectural and
cultural contributions to the kingdom.
CHAMPIONS OF THE WARRIORS AGE
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
59
Title associated with House Pattonʼs achievements during the founding era of
Aicruae 8,759 BR. Listed among the houseʼs major accomplishments alongside
the Siege of Highwater and Bloody Winter.
CUISINE
CUISINE OF AICRUAE
Cakes & Tortes
Spiced Fruit Cake
A yeasted spice torte layered with apple-pear-raisin paste, glazed with sugar
syrup tinted pink with cherry or mulberry juice, and topped with strawberries,
apple slices, and kiwi. One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign
of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple
collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones
served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Iced Peach Cake
A one-layer peach torte with beaten-egg leavening, glazed with rosewater sugar
tinted pink via cherries or beet, decorated with poached peach rounds.One of the
dishes and desserts developed during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II
and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and
these dishes became cultural touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and
court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Cold Peach Cake
Two thin egg-raised tortes sandwiched with peach conserve loosened with
verjuice. Served chilled with no exterior frosting, the only royal cake served
without decoration.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign of
King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple
collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones
served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
60
Almond Cake
A pale egg-white almond torte made with fine flour, ground almonds, and sugar,
topped with sautéed apple and peach in honey-butter-cinnamon, finished under
the hearthʼs top heat.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign of
King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple
collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones
served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Strawberry Layer Cake
Three thin egg-raised tortes with chopped strawberries folded into the inner fruit
conserve, frosted with rosewater sugar glaze colored with strawberry or cherry
juice, crowned with a single strawberry.One of the dishes and desserts developed
during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The
royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural
touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the
kingdom.
Lemon Cake
An egg-raised torte flavored with lemon zest, frosted with saffron-tinted sugar
glaze, garnished with candied lemon slices and a halved lemon for
presentation.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign of King
Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated
on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones served at
festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Strawberry Sweet Cake
A buttered spice torte dusted with finely ground sugar and strewn with fresh or
candied strawberries.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign
of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple
collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones
served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Grape Cake
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
61
A torte flavored with mosto cotto (reduced must) and raisins, iced with grapemust sugar glaze, decorated with candied violets and elderflowers.One of the
dishes and desserts developed during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II
and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and
these dishes became cultural touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and
court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Strawberry Biscuit
Sweet short paste rounds filled with clotted cream or whipped “snowe,” layered
with macerated strawberries, capped with a thin crisp biscuit and a whole berry.
The Aicruaean equivalent of strawberry shortcake.One of the dishes and desserts
developed during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian
Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes
became cultural touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations
throughout the kingdom.
Cold Fruit Sponge
A sponge-style torte soaked with sweet cream or almond milk mixed with honey
and rosewater, folded with diced peaches, pears, and banana. Best eaten
cold.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign of King Hailour
Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe
creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones served at festivals,
weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Capital Fruit Cake
A rich yeast torte heavy with raisins, currants, and candied fruits soaked in
hippocras (spiced wine) or aqua vitae. Named for the capital city of Lajazer where
it originated as a celebration dish.One of the dishes and desserts developed
during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The
royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural
touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the
kingdom.
Cookie Tower Cake
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
62
The most elaborate of all royal cakes, a stunning two-tiered celebration cake
served on a wooden board. The base is ringed with embossed sugar cookies
standing upright, each stamped with symbolic images: house, flower, crown, sun,
moon, tree, deer, bird, and flute. Both tiers are covered in ivory frosting decorated
with jam-filled cookies arranged like jeweled medallions. The crown features white
chocolate curls piled high with brown chocolate clumps, creating a nest-like
effect. Reserved for major festivals and royal celebrations.One of the dishes and
desserts developed during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen
Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes
became cultural touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations
throughout the kingdom.
Soups
Lentil Soup
Lentils and chickpeas simmered in pottage with onion, leek, herbs, and olive oil,
enriched with saffron and verjuice. Served with soft bread. A common dish served
to both nobility and commoners during festivals.One of the dishes and desserts
developed during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II
and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and
these dishes became cultural touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and
court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Shrimp Soup
“Shrimp-rice-bean soup.” Shrimp, short-grain rice, and fava beans in fish stock
with saffron, garlic, parsley, and olive oil, finished with verjuice. A coastal
specialty that became popular at court after Queen Isalian introduced it.One of the
dishes and desserts developed during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II
and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and
these dishes became cultural touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and
court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Desserts & Beverages
Blueberry Cream
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
63
Sheepʼs milk yogurt layered with lightly honeyed bilberries and bilberry syrup
made from reduced must and berries.One of the dishes and desserts developed
during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The
royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural
touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the
kingdom.
Iced Banana
A frozen dessert of whipped cream or almond milk sweetened and folded with
quince or apple purée, served chilled. One of the earliest frozen treats in
Aicruaean cuisine.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign of
King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple
collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones
served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Grape Tart
A grape tart with egg-yolk custard in pastry, studded with raisins and fresh
grapes, glazed with reduced must gelled with quince or apple pectin, topped with
whole grapes.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign of King
Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated
on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones served at
festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.
Sweetened Grape Pie
A variation of grape pie with rich almond-milk or dairy custard thickened with egg
yolks. No glaze, the creamy filling is the focus.One of the dishes and desserts
developed during the reign of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian
Liazen. The royal couple collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes
became cultural touchstones served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations
throughout the kingdom.
Strawberry Wine
KEY  WORDS AND TERMS
64
Served two ways: as strawberry-infused hippocras (spiced wine strained over
strawberries) or as a straight fruit wine blend. A celebratory drink served at
weddings and festivals.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign
of King Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple
collaborated on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones
served at festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.A
fruit wine produced in Aicruae alongside traditional grape wine. Part of the
kingdomʼs winemaking tradition, sometimes served as a lighter alternative to red
wine at celebrations.
Flower Chocolates
Flower-moulded chocolates or marchpane (marzipan) filled with thick fruit pastes
in strawberry, lemon, peach, and banana varieties. Often given as gifts during
courtship.One of the dishes and desserts developed during the reign of King
Hailour Layern Patton II and Queen Isalian Liazen. The royal couple collaborated
on recipe creation, and these dishes became cultural touchstones served at
festivals, weddings, and court celebrations throughout the kingdom.

entries.title: Language
entries.text:
Language
Aicruae speaks Ananara. This language sounds friendly and approachable. But
there written language is called Kurti. The written language of Kurti is made up of
26 letters.
Gherci and Coleum speak the language of Speail aka the language of the wales. It
is known for its long drawn-out syllables that are deep and bellowing.
Pireaynea speaks Pocorki, a country-like language with lots of crude and rude
words that creates that country-like flair.
Vikistv speaks 3 major languages all a combination of different languages
because Vikistv is like a city.
The first is Traer a combination of Speail and Pocorki.
The second is Jalʼvae a combination of Speail and Ananara
The third is Dorrena a combination of Kurti and Audru
Equateiy  Speaks two languages Audru, and Lato. Lato is a romantic and fancysounding language. Audru is a rural language that sounds very aggressive.
Numbers in Kurti are created using plug on numbers. For example, if you wanted
to make twenty-five you would have to combine the symbol for the number two
with the symbol number five. If wanted to create a number like one hundred you
would use the symbol for the number one and two symbols of the number zero
and combine them. Kurti is a simple enough language, and an alphabet is provided
that helps translate the symbols into their English counterparts.

Dynastic & Succession Tension
A monarch whose legitimacy is questioned (bastardy rumors, disputed parentage,
foreign bloodline).
A fragile line of succession with too few heirs — or too many claimants.
A powerful noble house insisting their bloodline is the rightful one.
A child heir whose regency council becomes the real battleground.
Marriage as a Weapon
Political marriages used to secure alliances or neutralize rivals.
A spouse chosen for strategy, not affection — creating resentment, affairs, or
factional divides.
A widowed ruler pressured to remarry for “the good of the realm.”
A marriage that unexpectedly strengthens the “wrong” faction.
Court Factions & Whisper Networks
Two or three major blocs constantly shifting alliances (like Greens vs. Blacks).
Courtiers who survive by information trading, rumor ‑ mongering, and subtle
sabotage.
A spymaster who knows everyoneʼs secrets but never reveals their own.
A favorite or advisor whose influence rivals that of the monarch.
The Dangerous Heir Archetypes
The brilliant but unstable heir.
The overlooked second child who becomes the real political mastermind.
The “outsider” heir raised far from court, returning with unexpected loyalties.
The heir who is too kind for the brutality of succession politics.
Religious or Ideological Fracture
A new faith or doctrine challenging the old order.
Nobles using religious alignment as a political identity.
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
4
A monarch torn between personal belief and political necessity.
A heresy scare used as a pretext to purge rivals.
Civil War as a Slow Burn
Border skirmishes and proxy conflicts before open war.
Houses forced to choose sides publicly — or secretly play both.
A single symbolic event (a death, a coronation, a betrayal) that tips the realm into
war.
The war becoming a generational trauma that reshapes the kingdom.
Symbolic Power & Heraldry
House sigils that carry centuries of meaning (dragons, roses, stags, serpents).
Colors and clothing used as political statements (like Green vs. Black gowns).
A houseʼs ancestral weapon, artifact, or creature becoming a rallying symbol.
A crest or motto that becomes tragically ironic over time.
The Brutality of Court Life
Public ceremony masking private cruelty.
A noble executed for treason on flimsy evidence — to send a message.
A queen or consort isolated, watched, or politically caged.
A council chamber where every smile hides a knife.
The Rise of “New Blood”
A lowborn favorite rising too quickly and angering the old nobility.
A merchant family gaining wealth that threatens traditional houses.
A knight or warrior whose popularity becomes politically dangerous.
A scholar, healer, or mystic whose influence shifts the balance of power.
Prophecy, Omens & Political Mythmaking
A prophecy interpreted differently by each faction.
Dreams, visions, or celestial events used to justify political moves.
A ruler obsessed with destiny, ignoring practical governance.
A prophecy that becomes self ‑ fulfilling because people act on it.
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
5
Empresses in the Palace The Legend of Zhen Huan) — The closest match to
Magnificent Century in tone; intense harem politics and imperial power games.
Ruyiʼs Royal Love in the Palace — Slow-burn, elegant, devastating look at imperial
marriage and betrayal.
Story of Yanxi Palace — Fast-paced, clever heroine navigating palace factions.
The Rise of Phoenixes — Court politics, succession, betrayal; visually stunning
and morally complex.
Nirvana in Fire — Political strategy masterpiece; no magic, just brilliant scheming.
Nirvana in Fire II — Same political depth, new cast and storyline.
Royal Nirvana — Crown prince under crushing political pressure; tragic,
atmospheric.
Serenade of Peaceful Joy — Court life + father–daughter dynamics with Princess
Huirou.
The Story of Minglan — Aristocratic family politics, marriage alliances, and social
maneuvering.
The Rebel Princess — A noblewoman and a general navigate power, marriage,
and rebellion.
The Longest Day in Changʼan — Political thriller set in Tang dynasty; grounded.
The Story of Yanxi Palace: Princess Adventures — Continuation with more
palace intrigue.
Court Lady — Tang dynasty romance + political ambition, light but grounded.
The Story of Han Dynasty Han Wu Da Di) — Classic imperial court drama with
real historical figures.
Empress Ki — Korean woman rises in Yuan dynasty court; political, romantic,
sweeping.
Dong Yi — Palace intrigue centered on a low-born woman who becomes a royal
consort.
Jewel in the Palace Dae Jang Geum) — Court life through medicine and cooking;
iconic.
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
6
Queen Seondeok — Power struggles, succession, and female leadership in Silla
dynasty.
Six Flying Dragons — Political rise of Joseon dynasty founders; strategic,
grounded.
The Red Sleeve — Romance + court duty between a king and a court lady;
emotionally rich.
Saimdang: Memoir of Colors — Historical artistry and court pressures (minimal
fantasy elements; grounded overall).
The Kingʼs Woman — Qin dynasty drama about love, ambition, and political
survival.
The Tudors — Henry VIIIʼs reign, marriages, and political upheaval.
The Borgias — Renaissance Italyʼs most infamous power family.
The White Queen — Wars of the Roses from the womenʼs perspective.
The White Princess — Tudor consolidation after the York/Lancaster conflict.
The Spanish Princess — Catherine of Aragonʼs rise and fall.
The Queen Who Crowned — Included as requested; similar royal-womancentered political arc.)
Versailles — Louis XIVʼs court, ambition, and decadence.
Medici: Masters of Florence — Banking dynasty, political strategy, and
Renaissance power.
Catherine the Great — Russian imperial politics and personal rule.
Reign — Loosely historical but still grounded in court politics and alliances.
Magnificent Century: Kösem — Successor series with even more political
maneuvering.
The Last Kingdom — Saxon vs. Dane politics, succession, and war strategy.
Vikings — Political alliances, power struggles, and dynastic ambition.
Vikings: Valhalla — Continuation with more political maneuvering.
Becoming Elizabeth — Young Elizabeth I navigating a deadly court.
Mary Queen of Scots 2018 film, but fits the vibe) — Tudor-era political tension.
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
7
Gunpowder — Conspiracy and political rebellion in Stuart England.
Wolf Hall — Thomas Cromwellʼs rise; extremely political and grounded.
The Pillars of the Earth — Medieval power, church politics, and succession.
World Without End — Follow-up to Pillars; political and social upheaval.
Marco Polo — Mongol court politics, alliances, and betrayals.
The Serpent Queen — Catherine deʼ Mediciʼs rise to power.
Domina — Ancient Rome from the perspective of Livia Drusilla.
Rome — Senate politics, Caesarʼs rise, and shifting power.
Knightfall — Templar politics, royal alliances, and betrayal.
Barbarians
The Advisors Alliance — Sima Yiʼs political rise in the Three Kingdoms era.
The Qin Empire (series trilogy) — Statecraft, war, and political reform.
Joy of Life (minimal fantasy elements; mostly political maneuvering) — Sharp
political strategy and court tension.
The Long River — Governance, reform, and political conflict in Qing dynasty.
The Sleuth of Ming Dynasty — Court politics + investigation (grounded).
The Imperial Doctress — Medical court drama with political pressure.
The Legend of Miyue — A womanʼs rise to power in the Warring States period.
The Legend of Haolan — Political marriages and palace intrigue in Qin dynasty.
The Story of Yanxi Palace: Princess Adventures — More palace politics.
The Story of the Batavia Queen — Court alliances and political marriages.
Queen for Seven Days — A queen caught between rival political factions.
Mr. Sunshine — Not royal, but deeply political and historically grounded.
The Crowned Clown — A political thriller about a kingʼs double (no magic).
My Country: The New Age — Power struggles during the founding of Joseon.
The Kingʼs Affection — Gender disguise but no fantasy; court politics heavy.
The Great Queen Seondeok — Succession battles and political strategy.
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
8
Jang Ok-jung: Living by Love — Court intrigue from a famous concubineʼs POV.
Yi San — Court politics and royal romance with historical grounding.
The Kingʼs Face — Succession conflict and political tension.
Isabel Spain — Queen Isabellaʼs rise and political alliances.
Carlos, Rey Emperador — Charles Vʼs rule and European power politics.
Borgia: Faith and Fear — A European-produced version of The Borgias.
Queen of the South (not historical, but political rise-to-power arc).
The Empress Germany) — Elisabeth of Austriaʼs political and personal struggles.
Marie Antoinette BBC — Court politics and royal pressure.
Dynastic & Succession Tension
A monarch whose legitimacy is questioned (bastardy rumors, disputed parentage,
foreign bloodline).
A fragile line of succession with too few heirs — or too many claimants.
A powerful noble house insisting their bloodline is the rightful one.
A child heir whose regency council becomes the real battleground.
Marriage as a Weapon
Political marriages used to secure alliances or neutralize rivals.
A spouse chosen for strategy, not affection — creating resentment, affairs, or
factional divides.
A widowed ruler pressured to remarry for “the good of the realm.”
A marriage that unexpectedly strengthens the “wrong” faction.
Court Factions & Whisper Networks
Two or three major blocs constantly shifting alliances (like Greens vs. Blacks).
Courtiers who survive by information trading, rumor ‑ mongering, and subtle
sabotage.
A spymaster who knows everyoneʼs secrets but never reveals their own.
A favorite or advisor whose influence rivals that of the monarch.
The Dangerous Heir Archetypes
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
9
The brilliant but unstable heir.
The overlooked second child who becomes the real political mastermind.
The “outsider” heir raised far from court, returning with unexpected loyalties.
The heir who is too kind for the brutality of succession politics.
Religious or Ideological Fracture
A new faith or doctrine challenging the old order.
Nobles using religious alignment as a political identity.
A monarch torn between personal belief and political necessity.
A heresy scare used as a pretext to purge rivals.
Civil War as a Slow Burn
Border skirmishes and proxy conflicts before open war.
Houses forced to choose sides publicly — or secretly play both.
A single symbolic event (a death, a coronation, a betrayal) that tips the realm into
war.
The war becoming a generational trauma that reshapes the kingdom.
Symbolic Power & Heraldry
House sigils that carry centuries of meaning (dragons, roses, stags, serpents).
Colors and clothing used as political statements (like Green vs. Black gowns).
A houseʼs ancestral weapon, artifact, or creature becoming a rallying symbol.
A crest or motto that becomes tragically ironic over time.
The Brutality of Court Life
Public ceremony masking private cruelty.
A noble executed for treason on flimsy evidence — to send a message.
A queen or consort isolated, watched, or politically caged.
A council chamber where every smile hides a knife.
The Rise of “New Blood”
A lowborn favorite rising too quickly and angering the old nobility.
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
10
A merchant family gaining wealth that threatens traditional houses.
A knight or warrior whose popularity becomes politically dangerous.
A scholar, healer, or mystic whose influence shifts the balance of power.
Prophecy, Omens & Political Mythmaking
A prophecy interpreted differently by each faction.
Dreams, visions, or celestial events used to justify political moves.
A ruler obsessed with destiny, ignoring practical governance.
A prophecy that becomes self ‑ fulfilling because people act on it.
Refrence doc to help with world building pull from some of these and tie them into the world
11

CANON AUDIT  — T racking Doc
1
📍  Locations
🔴  Conflicts
Coelum migrates north →  south. Solis's Era = "North-central / north of
Gherci"; Minara's Era places Atriki (formerly Coelum) in the southern row
bordering the Fetora Sea.
Mystic Isles / Thult relocate SW of Aicruae →  "South" →  southeast by Vikitsv
across the eras.
Lajazer is "westernmost" but the capital-move story says Hailour moved it
inland "toward the center" for defense.
Magic timing: magic "introduced formally" under Goteivati III 2550 AR, yet
Grand Sorcerer Sevtor uses battlefield magic at Valea in 7,217 BR 7,000 yrs
earlier).
Henem Bay placement shifts with Coelum's position (north of Coelum vs.
bordering Tarmet/Gherci).
🟠  Errors / cleanup
Eastern Aicruae population = 40,000 yet "largest unhoused/poor population"
of a 120M nation — likely should be 40 million.
Population math doesn't sum to the stated 120M total across regions +
satellites.
