entries.title: Confirmed and Decided Log 2
entries.text:
✅
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
✅This is the decision record for our canon-grounding sessions on World
Without God. Every entry below spells out the question, the actual
options we weighed A / B / C / Layered), the verdict you chose
(verbatim), and the confirmed canon that resulted. Nothing here is
shorthand — if you picked "AB," you'll see exactly what A and B were.
How to read each entry
The why — the canon question we were grounding.
Options weighed — the candidate motives I laid out, lettered A/B/C, plus the
"Layered" blend option.
Your verdict — exactly what you chose (quoted).
Confirmed canon — the locked motive that goes into the bible.
Part A — God-tier divine keystones
The four cosmological load-bearing whys. These set how the gods behave and
why the whole tragedy is possible.
1. Why does Razar break divine restraint to back Solis?
Options weighed
A  The Founding Debt comes due: Razar founded the Patton line on a
prophecy; backing Solis is the prophecy finally paying off. The root cause.
B  The Worship Investment: an empire of Patton worshippers is Razar's
return on investment; he protects the asset.
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
1
C  The Crown Prince's pet war: a status/family split among the gods, Solis
as Razar's favored cause.
Your verdict:"A  B/C layered (founding root, others as secondary motives)."
Confirmed canon: The founding debt A) is the primary engine — Razar is
collecting on the prophecy he staked the dynasty on. The worship return B) and
the divine-family politics C) are real but secondary reinforcing layers.
2. Why does "The Great Usurper" stick to Solis
alongside "revered founder"?
Options weighed
A  He usurped a continent: the sheer scale of what he took earns the title;
usurpation that big becomes legend.
B  The Twins' slur that outlived them: Orcus and Iris's propaganda brand
for him survived their fall.
C  He usurped the gods' prerogative: a theological reading — he took what
belonged to the divine.
Your verdict:"Other: AB."
Confirmed canon: The name sticks because of scale A and because the Twins'
slur outlived them B. We dropped C — the theological "usurped the gods"
reading is not the canon reason.
3. Why does Nellebrie arm Harnua against Razar's
chosen?
Options weighed
A  Cosmic balance: the pantheon correcting Razar's overreach, impersonal.
B  The unloved daughter strikes the golden father through her saint:
Nellebrie's personal wound against Razar, aimed through Harnua.
C  Deniable proxy war: the pantheon checks Razar quietly, plausible
deniability.
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
2
Your verdict:"B  The unloved daughter strikes the golden father through her
saint."
Confirmed canon: It's personal. Nellebrie arms Harnua to wound Razar — the
slighted daughter striking the favored father through his chosen line.
4. Why does Solis turn from avenger into tyrant?
Options weighed
A  The wound that can never close: grief/trauma he can never resolve, so
he never stops.
B  The Valea threshold: he crosses a moral line once, it works, and that
opens the door.
C  He becomes the usurper he hated: power itself demands it; he turns into
the thing he set out to destroy.
Your verdict:"C  He becomes the usurper he hated (power demands it)."
Confirmed canon: Solis becomes the very usurper he rose to overthrow. Power's
own logic transforms the avenger into the tyrant.
Part B — Character & house keystones
5. Why does Esterica marry Solis?
Options weighed
A  A Fallen house's reclamation: marrying the rising king to restore her
broken house's standing.
B  Childhood love, open-eyed: she loves him and chooses him knowingly.
C  The seer who backs the vision: she sees what he'll become and bets on
it.
Your verdict (override):"She places her bets on Solis because Mihel and
Harnua's mom was going to marry her off to the knight/ser she was staying with.
She didn't want to become a 2nd wife."
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
3
Confirmed canon: Esterica's driving reason is escape. She was about to be
married off as a second wife to the household knight/ser she was staying with
(arranged by Mihel and Harnua's mother). Choosing Solis is the way out of that
fate — she bets on him rather than accept a second-wife marriage.
6. Why does Benjamin crown 9-year-old Solis over the
trueborn twins?
Options weighed
A  Break the Vika stranglehold: an heir with no powerful maternal house
keeps the crown free of Vika control.
B  Personal collapse: an appetite-ruled, wounded king's love for Emillea
plus his spite toward his Vika wife.
C  He believed Solis was the truer king: Razar's favor / the "real Patton"
reasoning.
Your verdict:"Layered — A spine (anti-Vika) + B (personal collapse lit the fuse) +
tragic irony."
Confirmed canon: The spine is A — breaking the Vika stranglehold. B (personal
collapse) lit the fuse, and the choice carries tragic irony. C is not the driver.)
7. Why does harmony-seeking Orcus lead a brutal
coup?
Options weighed
A  Protection, not ambition: a passed-over heir either rules or dies; he acts
to survive and shield his own.
B  Iris is the engine, Orcus is the heart: he can't refuse the one person he
can't lose.
C  The rotting-mother wound: vengeance for Mihai and a refusal to share
her fate.
Your verdict:"Layered — C the shared wound →  B Iris drives it →  A Orcus acts to
protect, not to rule."
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
4
Confirmed canon: Layered in sequence — C (the shared mother-wound) is the
soil, B Iris drives it) is the engine, and A Orcus acts to protect, not to rule) is how
he carries it out.
8. Why does Maen become a paranoid, brutal tyrant?
Options weighed
A  The shadow of a god: he can never be Solis, so he seizes the control that
adoration won't give him.
B — "Solis's creation": groomed into a role with no self beneath it; any threat
to control feels like annihilation.
C  Abandoned twice: mother dead at 3, father gone — trust is fatal.
Your verdict:"Other: A  B."
Confirmed canon:A  B — he's the unfillable shadow of a god A) who was built
into a role with no self underneath B. We dropped C (the "abandoned twice"
framing is not the driver).
9. Why does Harnua spend her dying breath raising
Orcus's moon — bigger and faster than Solis's?
Options weighed
A  The last love letter: her final act of devotion to Orcus.
B  The final insult to Solis: outdoing his moon as a parting blow.
C  The saint's apotheosis: her divine signature on the world.
Your verdict:"Layered — A engine + B's spite + C's theology (my rec)."
Confirmed canon: Layered — A (love for Orcus) is the engine, sharpened by B
(spite toward Solis) and elevated by C (the saint's theological capstone).
10. Why does Mihel Kulio swear his bloodline will end
with him?
Options weighed
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
5
A  Penance: the kingmaker sentences himself to erasure for what he set in
motion.
B  Breaking the curse: the Fallen end their own rot by ending the line.
C  Grief: nothing and no one left to build a future for.
Your verdict:"Other: A  C."
Confirmed canon:A  C — penance for his role plus grief with nothing left to
build for. We dropped B (the "breaking the curse" framing is not canon).
11. Why does Emillea Hige become King Benjamin's
concubine?
Options weighed
A  Love: the one real bond in a loveless dynasty.
B  The house's one open door: belated respect/standing for House Hige.
C  Agency: a low-house woman climbs the only ladder available to her.
Your verdict:"Layered — A starts it, B rides on it, C hardens it (my rec)."
Confirmed canon: Layered — A (love) starts it, B (the house's open door) rides on
it, C (agency) hardens it.
12. Why does Mihai self-poison with Nerai and let her
body rot untended?
Options weighed
A  The humiliated queen: her pride annihilated by Emillea's rise.
B  The Vika madness: a sick house claiming its own.
C  The trapped hostage: the only act of will left to a prisoner.
Your verdict:"Other: A  C."
Confirmed canon:A  C — the humiliated queen A) exercising the last will left to
a trapped hostage C. We dropped B — Mihai is not hereditarily/Vika-mad; the
"Vika madness" framing is rejected.
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
6
13. Why does Orcus reject Harnua's proposal?
Options weighed
A  Honesty: he sees a little sister and won't fake a love he doesn't feel.
B  Pride: a crown earned, not borrowed from a saint's god.
C  Protection: he won't doom her by chaining her to his fall.
Your verdict:"Layered — A core + B spoken + C buried (my rec)."
Confirmed canon: Layered — A (honesty) is the core, B (pride) is what he says
aloud, C (protection) is the buried truth.
14. Why does Vandrea choose 10,000 years of
suffering over a clean kill?
Options weighed
A  Proportion ("to suffer as I did"): a clean kill is too merciful; the
punishment must equal her own suffering.
B  Displaced guilt: endless war so she never has to face leaving Enyokia.
C  Renedin's bargain: a god hijacks her grief and stretches it into the long
ruin.
Your verdict:"Layered — A named + B underneath + C the trap (my rec)."
Confirmed canon: Layered — A (proportion) is the reason she'd name, B
(displaced guilt) runs underneath, C Renedin's bargain) is the trap she's caught
in.
15. Why is Iris relentlessly cruel?
Options weighed
A  Terror of powerlessness: never be the rotting, helpless queen.
B  Inherited damage: the Mad House and a childhood of poison.
C  Grief weaponized: avenging her discarded mother.
Your verdict:"Layered — A engine + B soil + C aim (my rec)."
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
7
Confirmed canon: Layered — A (terror of powerlessness) is the engine, B
(inherited damage) is the soil, C (weaponized grief) is the aim.
16. Why does Harnua try to kill her brother Mihel?
Options weighed
A  Love over blood: Orcus above all, even her own brother.
B  Betrayal of god and house: Mihel served the usurper.
C  Strategic decapitation: kill the brain of the enemy to save Orcus.
Your verdict:"Layered — A engine + B permission + C method (my rec)."
Confirmed canon: Layered — A (love over blood) is the engine, B (his betrayal) is
the permission, C (strategic decapitation) is the method.
17. Why does Solis bury the twins honorably?
Options weighed
A  Confession dressed as devotion: the disaster was his too, and the burial
half-admits it.
B  Claiming them permanently: the victor writes the dead into his own story.
C  The brother he never got: love that couldn't be.
Your verdict:"C  The brother he never got: love that couldn't be."
Confirmed canon: Solis honors them out of grief for the brother he never got to
have — a love that was never allowed to exist.
18. Why does Coyre build a museum for the mother
she never knew?
Options weighed
A  To meet the mother she was denied: grief for an absence.
B  To author an identity of her own.
C  To found the dynasty's mother-myth.
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
8
Your verdict:"C  To found the dynasty's mother-myth."
Confirmed canon: The museum is dynastic myth-making — Coyre founds the
official mother-myth of the line.
19. Why does Natav Yailk betray Vikitsv (and die for it
anyway)?
Options weighed
A  The coward's bargain: he sold everything to save his own life.
B  The man promised everything: ambition that wouldn't die even as the
kingdom fell.
C  The believer who stopped believing: a nationalist's apostasy.
Your verdict:"Other: A  B."
Confirmed canon:A  B — a coward's bargain to save his skin A) fused with
ambition that outlived the kingdom B. We dropped C (the apostasy/lost-faith
framing is not canon).
20. Why does Merigen lead the witch's coup against
the Pattons?
Options weighed
A  Blood vengeance: the burned house Orana comes home for revenge.
B  The persecuted's uprising: the hunted seize the throne.
C  The man who became what he hated: the persecutor's mirror.
Your verdict:"B  The persecuted's uprising: the hunted seize the throne."
Confirmed canon: It's a liberation, framed as the persecuted rising up — the
hunted (witches) seizing the throne. Not primarily personal blood-vengeance.)
21. Why does Benjamin preach against the love that
ruins him?
Options weighed
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
9
A  The creed he inherited: Pattons sit above human feeling.
B  The warning of an addict: he knows love's power because it owns him.
C  The cope of a loveless man: dignifying a joyless throne.
Your verdict:"B  The warning of an addict: he knows love's power because it
owns him."
Confirmed canon: Benjamin preaches against love precisely because it owns him
— the addict warning others away from his own ruin.
22. Why does Mihai believe Vika blood built the
throne?
Options weighed
A  Because it's true: the crown carries an unpayable debt to House Vika.
B  Because it's all she was given: reduced to nothing but her house's worth.
C  Because she needed to feel safe: clinging to a security that wasn't really
there.
Your verdict:"Layered — A foundation + B all she had + C fatal turn (my rec)."
Confirmed canon: Layered — A (it really is true) is the foundation, B (it's all she
was given) is why she clings, C (the need for safety) is the fatal turn.
23. Why did Reasaec (Equateiy) and Sevtor
(Valea/Orana) back Orcus?
Options weighed
A  The banker's bet: legitimacy is the safe investment.
B  The blood tie: a personal/family stake dressed as a cause.
C  The fear of Solis: back the heir to stop the usurper.
Your verdict:"Layered — Reasaec=A money, Sevtor=B blood, both on C fear (my
rec)."
Confirmed canon: Split motives on a shared fear. Reasaec backs Orcus for
money A; Sevtor backs him for blood B; both are driven underneath by fear
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
10
of Solis C.
24. Why was Iris betrothed to Cequailian Orana?
Options weighed
A  Magic wins wars: the betrothal buys House Orana's Vikitsv sorcery.
B  Iris was expendable: the spare twin, sold off.
C  A marriage of equals in shame: two second-children of suspect houses
matched together.
Your verdict:"Other: B  Iris's father saw her becoming more like her mother and
more Vika-like as she grew, and he didn't like that."
Confirmed canon:B plus a father-animus override. Iris was the expendable
spare B — but the real driver is Benjamin: as Iris grew, he saw her becoming
more like her mother Mihai, more Vika, and he disliked it. Betrothing her to distant
Vikitsv both bought the Orana sorcery (the official excuse) and removed the
daughter who mirrored the wife he'd discarded (the real want). Iris overheard this
— the second of only two times she is shown crying. Irony: Benjamin's petty act
forged the Orana alliance that later became the Twins' deadliest weapon against
Solis.
Part C — Grounded but NOT locked
Iris & Yera — why she enslaves the girl who resembles
her
I laid out the options below, but you skipped the survey, so this is not locked.
Recorded here so we don't lose the groundwork.
A  The doll she can control: a version of herself she finally gets to
command.
B  Punishing the girl she used to be: hurting the reflection of her own
younger, powerless self.
Confirmed and Decided Log 2
11
C  The only intimacy she can allow: ownership as the sole form of
closeness she permits herself.
Layered: a blend of the above.
Status: Open. Pick a verdict when you want to lock it.
Part D — Open why-candidates (queued,
not yet grounded)
Apharia — why she loves Soli.
Renedin — why his corruption reads as "love" of Vandrea.
Mokar Hige — why he steals from a dead man to buy a title.
Crandona — why she falls for Merigen and then kills him.
Part E — Unresolved canon flags (need
your ruling)
Contradictions surfaced during grounding that are not yet decided:
Esterica/Kulio mothers: Is Mihel & Harnua's relationship to Esterica full
siblings Count Eserindeo Kulio's first wife) — or does the House Kulio page's
"Mihel & Esterica full siblings (mother Mihela)" stand? Conflicting parentage.
Merigen reign-length: 15-year gap — coup lands 0/1 BR, text says "rules
six years," but he's overthrown 14 AR. Numbers don't reconcile.
Nerai contradiction: described as a slow elixir in one place vs. a near-instant
neurotoxin ("the Joyless Death") in another.
Vandrea chronology: born 7,236 BR vs. the "over 10,000 years" of suffering.
Timeline mismatch.
Magic Tower lineage: 23 generations vs. centuries; Sevtor descends from
Verna's eldest son Liaerto I; Ulian →  Kiear / Liaerto III conflict.
Confirmed and Decided Log 2

✅
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
🗂Decision log for the Canon Grounding Pass. This records the questions
we worked through in chat: the question asked, how we reasoned to the
answer, and what we settled on.
The four most recent items (the Harnua / Ilkai / Nellebrie / Moon cluster)
include paste-ready canon text. Two are reproduced verbatim exactly
as written in chat; two are clean canon prose rebuilt faithfully from the
confirmed reasoning. Earlier items record the confirmed reasoning and
conclusion — where fuller paste-ready wording was written in chat, treat
that wording as the source of truth.
This page is a log, not a canon rewrite. Nothing here edits the canon
pages themselves.

Part I — The Divine Machinery (Harnua, Ilkai, Nellebrie,
the Moon)
The most recent cluster, worked in this session. Full canon text included.
1. Why a god-killing herb (Ilkai) even exists
How we got here: Loaded KEY WORDS AND TERMS in full. Cross-checked the
entries for Ilkai, the Pertari Stairs, the Gods Nellebrie), and Iswan / the Oath of
Memiet.
Confirmed reasoning 5 pillars):
Not a weapon — a wound. It grows only on Mount Aicren, where Nellebrie's
domain of disaster and Iswan's craft of alchemy overlap. Where two divine
domains press together, the world scars; the deadliest thing in creation grows
from that scar.
"God-killing" is a side effect. It does not kill the body (a god can mend a body)
— it shatters the soul past the point its pieces can rejoin the Song, sending it

up the Pertari Stairs forever. That is the one death even a god cannot undo.
One of only four ways a soul is lost forever.
Discovered, not invented — by Vekta & Aryanara during their study of the soul
cycle; the knowledge buried at once, guarded by Vikitsv scholars, the Magic
Tower, and House Orana.
Why Ilkai for Solis: the entry states it "bypasses divine protection." Solis
carries Razar's real favor, which turns mortal blades and poisons aside; only a
soul-level death could reach a divinely shielded man.
The seed of the later fear: a god knowingly told a mortal where a god-killer
grows.
📜Why Ilkai Exists(canon text — rebuilt from the confirmed reasoning)
Ilkai is not a weapon. It is a wound in the world.
It grows in only one place — high on Mount Aicren, where Nellebrie's
hand of disaster and Iswan's craft of alchemy press against one another.
Where two divine domains overlap, the world scars, and from that scar
grows the deadliest thing in creation.
What makes it god-killing is not that it kills the body, for a god can mend
a body. Ilkai shatters the soul itself, breaking it past the point where its
pieces can ever rejoin the Song, so that what it takes climbs the Pertari
Stairs and never comes down. That is the one death even a god cannot
undo, for no power has ever called a soul back from those stairs. It is
one of only four ways a soul can be lost forever.
It was not invented but discovered, by Vekta and Aryanara in their long
study of the soul's journey, and the knowing of it was buried at once —
guarded by the scholars of Vikitsv, the masters of the Magic Tower, and
the keepers of House Orana, who understood that to write it plainly was
to hand the world a way to murder gods.
And that is why it, of all poisons, was the one raised against Solis. He
carries a god's true favor, and a god's favor turns mortal blades and
mortal poisons aside. Only a death that reaches past the body to the
soul could touch him. That a god knowingly told a mortal where such a
thing grew is the seed of every fear that came after.
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
3
2. Why Nellebrie would arm a mortal with Ilkai
How we got here: Built on the KEY WORDS Ilkai / Oath of Memiet entries and the
Gods page Nellebrie = goddess of Disasters, daughter of Razar + Paha, creator
of Mount Aicren, who blessed Harnua at age 10.
Confirmed reasoning 5 pillars + thesis):
Only Nellebrie could know the location — she created Mount Aicren, where
Ilkai grows.
She is the goddess of disasters — arming Harnua is her nature, not a scheme.
Harnua is her own blessed saint (blessed at age 10.
The Oath of Memiet may have forced reciprocity: Harnua offered weight
enough, so under the Oath Nellebrie owed her — the fail-safe meant to protect
mortals armed a god-killer.
Nellebrie is Razar's daughter →  arming the assassin of Razar's champion
proves the divine house is split over Solis.
Thesis: not betrayal but three consistent acts — honor her saint, be what she is,
pay what she owes — that sum to a deicide weapon.
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
4
📜Why Nellebrie Gave Harnua the Herb(canon text — rebuilt from the
confirmed reasoning)
Nellebrie did not betray her kind so much as be exactly what she is.
Only she could have known where Ilkai grows, for she made Mount
Aicren with her own hand. She is the goddess of disasters; to arm a
grieving woman with the deadliest thing in the world is not a scheme
against her nature but an expression of it. And Harnua was hers — her
own blessed saint, marked at ten years old.
The Oath of Memiet may have left her no choice at all. The Oath binds a
god to give nothing without taking equal in return, and Harnua came
offering weight enough to move a goddess. The fail-safe meant to
protect mortals from the gods became the very thing that armed one to
kill them.
And Nellebrie is Razar's daughter. That the assassin of Razar's own
champion was armed by Razar's own child is the first proof that the
divine house is split over Solis — that the war fought on the ground had
a mirror in heaven.
It was not one betrayal. It was three honest acts — honor her saint, be
what she is, pay what she owed — that happened to add up to a weapon
meant to end a god.
3. What Harnua traded Nellebrie in return
How we got here: Followed the Oath of Memiet (gods cannot take without giving
equal) into the canon of saint-death (each saint's death creates a calendar month)
and Harnua's death (the second moon + the 40-day month Agarisono; Esterica
drank the cup; Harnua burned 7,214 BR; "second only to Reron in infamy").
Confirmed reasoning: The Oath sets a brutal price floor — the coin must match
the world's heaviest secret. The only thing heavy enough is Harnua's death — the
last saint-death that will ever occur — which she spent deliberately, forging it into
the second moon and the over-long 13th month (the visible "receipt"). The same
dying act honored Orcus and paid Nellebrie at once. A quieter second coin: her
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
5
good name (infamy) and possibly her soul's peace. The bargain balanced on both
sides and still failed — Esterica drank the cup, Solis lived.
GRRMCause — the Oath forbids a free gift. Cost — the last saint-death ever, plus
her name and perhaps her eternity. Want — kill Solis and honor Orcus; the moon
does the latter and pays the god. Why now/why them — only the final saint owns
a death rare enough to be the coin, spendable once.
📜What Harnua PaidVERBATIM from chat)
Nothing is given freely by the gods. The Oath of Memiet binds them to
take only what they repay in kind, and Nellebrie had given the heaviest
thing in the world — the place where the god-killer grows. To balance it,
Harnua needed a coin just as rare, and she owned exactly one.
She was the last saint. Her death would be the last saint's death the
world would ever know, and a saint's death does not pass quietly — it
remakes the calendar itself. That power was hers to spend once, and
she spent it where Nellebrie could collect. Where every saint before her
left behind a single month and nothing more, Harnua's death raised a
second moon into the sky and stretched a thirteenth month to forty days.
The excess was the receipt. She did not let her death scatter into the
year; she forged it into a lasting disturbance in the heavens, which is the
disaster-goddess's own country.
It was the same breath that honored Orcus. The moon she raised for her
lost love was the very thing she owed her god — one act paying a grief
and a debt at once.
And there was a quieter price. She gave up her good name to the ages,
dying second only to Reron in infamy, a saint remembered as a traitor.
Some say she gave up more than that — her clean return to the Song,
her soul's next quiet life. She paid with her death, her name, and
perhaps her eternity.
The cruelest part is that the books balanced and still it bought her
nothing. Esterica drank the cup. The god kept her moon, the world kept
its monster, and Solis lived. That is what it costs to bargain with the
goddess of disasters: the disaster comes whether or not you get what
you asked for.
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
6
4. What the second moon + Agarisono did to the world
How we got here: Consequence-mapping across domains, grounded in the canon
of the second moon (bigger than Solis's moon, spins 3× faster, always overtakes
it; raised in Orcus's honor), the 40-day 13th month Agarisono, and the 13th
Eternal Sign Garisono ("incapable of love").
Confirmed reasoning 5 effects):
The sky reenacts the war — Orcus wins nightly. The greater, faster moon
Orcus's) runs the empire's moon Solis's) down every night. Solis won on the
ground; he loses the sky forever.
Undeniable proof a mortal reached divine power — hung where it can't be
burned. Reason for the gods' fear; a doctrinal crisis for the Circle; a permanent
recruiting banner for the Pure Ones.
The seas changed — two moons tangled the tides; the fishing/maritime coasts
Aicruae, Dajanyi, Baliva, Coelum) paid in wrecks until they relearned the
water. Fitting payment for the disaster-goddess.
Time itself grew by 40 days — a permanent before/after-7,214 fracture; the
year now ends in mourning under Harnua's moon.
The cursed month's children — those born under Garisono branded
"incapable of love," carrying the last saint's shadow forward forever.
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
7
📜The Moon and the Thirteenth MonthVERBATIM from chat)
When Harnua raised her moon, she changed the world below it.
There were two moons now, and hers was the greater — larger than the
old one, and three times as swift, so that every night it ran the empire's
moon down and passed it. The old moon was Solis's, the moon of his
golden reign. Harnua's was Orcus's. The war had ended on the ground
with Solis the victor, but in the sky it was fought again each night, and
each night Orcus won. An emperor may take six kingdoms and never
take the heavens. It was the one defeat he could not bury, lit nightly
above every head in the world.
It was also proof. To move the heavens is the work of a god, and a
mortal saint had done it, and the doing of it would not come down. The
gods saw their own undoing hanging in the dark and went quiet with
fear. The Circle was left to explain why the sky honored a traitor. And the
Pure Ones, who taught that mortals might rise to take the gods' place,
needed no scripture any longer — their proof rose every evening, and no
fire could reach it.
The seas felt it too. Two moons pulled the tides into a tangle no almanac
had charted, and the coasts that lived by fishing and sailing paid in
wrecked hulls and drowned men until they learned the water again. The
goddess of disasters had been paid, and her payment ran all the way
down to the waterline.
And time itself grew longer. Forty days were added to the year in a
thirteenth month, Agarisono, that closed the calendar in cold and
mourning under Harnua's moon. Those born in its span were said to be
born incapable of love, and carried the last saint's shadow into every life
that followed. She died once, and the world has kept her death ever
since — in its sky, its seas, its calendar, and its children.
5. How the empire managed / renamed Orcus's moon — ⚠  IN
PROGRESS (paused here)
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
8
Status: Started but not finished — this is where we paused. No final conclusion
confirmed yet.
How we got here: Ran 6 searches for real-world precedent on managing a symbol
you can't destroy. Named precedents gathered:
Caesar's Comet / Sidus Iulium — Augustus reframed an unexplained celestial
event over Caesar's funeral games as proof of his deified father, turning the
heavens into an endorsement of his legitimacy. The "claim it" move.)
Damnatio memoriae / abolitio nominis — official erasure of names Geta,
Domitian, Nero; Trotsky airbrushed). Frequently backfired.
Sol Invictus →  Christmas — co-opting a rival cult's festival by overwriting it
with state liturgy.
Quintilis → July, Sextilis → August — rulers rename calendar units after
themselves, but such renamings were often "abandoned by their successors."
Fallen-regime monuments — the replace / reinterpret / remove framework;
"lost cause" monuments that redeem a defeat.
The Streisand effect — suppression amplifies the thing suppressed.
Direction being argued (not yet confirmed): "Remove" is impossible (it's a
moon), so the regime is forced into reinterpret + co-opt. Likely arc: Phase 1 —
attempt erasure of the name, which backfires Streisand); Phase 2 — the
Augustus move, claim the moon and rename it (re-attribute to Razar / the new
golden age / possibly Esterica, the empress who actually died); Phase 3 — co-opt
the moon-festival and Agarisono into the state cult Sol Invictus pattern); Phase 4
— the rename only half-sticks: the official name lives in the archive, the folk name
("Orcus's moon") survives in taverns and among Najil "rightful heir" partisans and
the Pure Ones, making it a permanent lost-cause banner.
⏭Pick up here next session: finish the playbook, decide the empire's
official name for the moon (candidate idea worth weighing: reframing it
as Esterica's moon — stealing the assassin's monument for the woman
her poison actually killed), and decide how much the renaming sticks vs.
survives underground.
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
9
Part II — The Civil War & Solis's Rise
Worked earlier in the thread. Conclusions recorded; fuller paste-ready wording,
where written, lives in chat.
6. Why Solis turned on the Cidet
How we got here: The Cidet is the neutral Temple of the Gods — holy city, 9M
pilgrims a year, guarded by the Danepelie. Attacking it is open sacrilege, so the
question was how a divinely favored king could do it and survive. Crossreferenced the war chapter map Yr2 Ch.26; Yr3 Ch.30.
Confirmed (a three-part engine, not one motive):
Strategic necessity — by Yr3 the Cidet had become the enemy's shelter:
Harnua had fled there and Orcus rescued her there Ch.30. Solis could not
leave a hostile stronghold sheltering the assassin and the rebel at his back,
neutral ground or not.
Pretext — the neutrality was already broken — Harnua had first defiled the
Cidet by murdering its officials there Yr2, Ch.26. So Solis could frame his
assault not as breaking the Temple's neutrality but as answering a desecration
the other side had already committed.
Theological cover — Solis carries Razar's real favor, and with the gods silent,
no bolt fell to stop him. Silence read as permission: the favored champion
cannot be committing sacrilege if the gods do not strike him down.
7. Why Gherci doesn't turn its back on Solis after he attacks the
Cidet — ⭐  flagged gap, resolved
How we got here: Gherci's faith = the Teire (the Main Master outranks the king);
Kamerida settlement; Cidet/Circle theology.
Confirmed: Gherci's loyalty isn't to a crown or even to the Cidet — it's to the
Teire. Three legs: 1 Teire-over-crown — religious authority, not the king,
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
10
commands Gherci, and that authority had already thrown in with Solis; 2) the
Kamerida settlement bound Gherci in; 3) a "silence is obedience" theology that
reads non-resistance as divine will. So attacking the Cidet did not break Gherci's
logic for staying.
This is the gap Azora asked to note and keep hunting from — confirmed
resolved.)
8. Why Orcus broke the Treaty of Deouilu
Confirmed: The Treaty of Deouilu = the founding pact of the Aicruae–Gherci
alliance and Cidet neutrality; broken in Ch. 31. The break is established and
motivated; exact terms still TBD.
9. Why the coup took ~20 years (the reign-length discrepancy)
Confirmed: Book 1's "ruled 7 years" is a drafting slip. Reconciled to the 20
year span implied by the dated timeline. Resolved in chat — not yet logged to the
timeline pages; see open items.)
10. Why the church / Circle legitimized Solis
Confirmed: A three-pillar logic (+ GRRM): Solis carries Razar's real divine favor,
which the Circle reads as endorsement; the gods' silence is misread as
ratification; and Solis co-opts rather than destroys the priesthood, making
collaboration safer than resistance.
11. Why the gods chose silence over Solis
Confirmed — keystone reframe:Solis is the cause of the silence, not its victim.
The gods did not abandon a favored son; their withdrawal is a consequence of
what his rise set in motion. This reframe feeds the still-open keystone: Razar's
active favor vs. the wider divine silence.)
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
11
Part III — Faith, Heresy & the Long Past
12. What happens to the Danepelie / Cidet priests afterward
Type: Texture/realism.
Confirmed: Solis co-opts rather than destroys the priesthood and the Danepelie
— he absorbs the machinery of the Cidet rather than razing it.
13. Why the Order of the Pure Ones survives the purge
Type: Texture/realism — grounded in real persecuted-faith precedent Cathars,
Kakure Kirishitan, Marranos, Waldensians).
Confirmed: The Order survives the way real outlawed faiths survive — by going
underground, hiding observance, and persisting in protected pockets (e.g., open
patronage by House Dajanyi).
14. How the Circle of Eternal Light could crown / bless a saintburner
Confirmed 5 pillars): The Circle worships gods, not saints, so saint-veneration is
itself Pure Ones heresy; Harnua was a regicide caught in the act, not a martyr;
saints dying at mortal hands is the norm; a "taboo saint" category already exists
Reron; and the gods' silence was misread as ratification. Irony: burning Harnua
is exactly what canonizes her — the second moon and the 13th month, Agarisono.
15. Why Iswan's secret stayed buried
Type: In-world logic.
The secret: Iswan's "Lie That Saved the World" — she proposed the Saint system
to Vapaz, but secretly intends saints to one day replace the gods.
Confirmed 5 reasons it stays hidden):
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
12
No witness, no document — it is an unspoken intent in Iswan's own mind;
there is nothing to leak.
The knowledge kills its holder — anyone who grasped that saints could
supplant gods becomes the gods' deadliest threat. The Order of the Pure
Ones, who venerate saints, are exactly the ones hunted (the Massacre of
Light). Speaking it gets you erased.
The gods suppress it — it exposes their vulnerability, so the divine
establishment and the Circle smother any doctrine that points toward it.
Secrecy is Iswan's own domain — goddess of alchemy and forbidden
knowledge; concealment is her nature.
The proof comes too late — only Harnua's moon finally shows a saint
reaching divine power, and by then the gods answer with terrified silence
rather than explanation, burying the confirmation under the very fear it
caused.
16. Why House Dajanyi keeps the Pure Ones' faith
Type: In-world logic.
How we got here: Dajanyi = ex-pirates of Coelum, late arrivals (migrated 8,978
BR, recognized 8,804 BR, seat at Port Vento, the most notable open follower of
the outlawed Order of the Pure Ones; motto "Forever Lasting"; house myth the
Mirrors of Nimlye.
Confirmed 5 reasons):
Outsider origin — risen from piracy and recognized late, they were never
woven into the establishment the state cult (the Circle) serves, so they have
little stake in its orthodoxy.
A creed that fits outsiders — the Pure Ones exalt saints, mortals who rose
above their birth; a fitting faith for a house that climbed from nothing.
Maritime distance — a seafaring house at Port Vento sits far from the Cidet's
heartland power and can hold a heterodox faith out of easy reach.
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
13
Faith as identity and defiance — keeping an outlawed religion openly is itself
a statement of independence and endurance, of a piece with "Forever
Lasting."
Survivors by self-image — their founding myth (the Mirrors of Nimlye; Rigu
Dajanyi survived) casts them as those who endure persecution, making a
persecuted faith consistent with who they believe they are.
17. Why Viake ordered the Massacre of Light, and why then
Confirmed: Three forces converged in 8,558 BR: the Pure Ones' doctrine
dissolves divine-right kingship (an existential threat to a Razar-bonded crown); a
weak king Viake, "the Skunk King"); and the Order had swelled to 90,000 —
large enough to read as a standing threat. The brakes came off, and 90,000 were
killed.
18. Who set the suspicious fire that killed Viake and Mari (8,552
BR)
Confirmed (ranked):
A — strongest: an inside job, with heir Sayero implicated. Lajazer's
impregnable cliff means only insiders could reach them; the king was a
radioactive liability after the Massacre; Sayero inherits; Sayero later dies of
Sela Meysei Night Terrors), read as guilt.
B — the Pure Ones' vengeance: the story the realm believed (and the more
useful public myth), whether or not it's true.
C — an omen layer over the top.
Karinoa ruled out.
Part IV — Earlier threads worked in this pass
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
14
Covered earlier in the thread; conclusions recorded in chat. Index kept here so the
log is complete.
📌Razar's favor for Solis is canonically REAL — backed by the Divine
Contract and the blinding of Kisaleli. Not propaganda. Load-bearing
correction; governs the open keystone.)
Razar's motive for backing Solis — worked.
Mihai's madness — motive worked.
Houses Orana & Kivier backing Orcus — foreign/noble backing of
the rebellion worked.
King Benjamin II's favoritism toward Solis — worked.
Benjamin II's death (the poisoning question) — worked.
The Vika prunings — worked.
The Najil betrayal — worked.
Still open (for the next logs)
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
15
🔭THE KEYSTONE  Razar's active favor vs. the gods' silence. Razar
blinds Kisaleli and backs Solis (real Divine Contract), yet the
pantheon goes silent in fear. The Nellebrie answer now feeds this
directly (his daughter armed the assassin; the divine house is split).
Pull this first next session.
Solis: founder AND "Great Usurper" paradox — he founds the
empire yet is later branded the Great Usurper while House Najil
carries a "rightful heir" claim.
Finish #5 — how the empire managed Orcus's moon (the renaming
playbook).
Timeline housekeeping: the twins' 20-year reign fix (resolved in
chat, not yet written to the timeline pages); other dating drifts noted
in the audit.
Confirmed & Decided — Log 1
16

entries.title: Inferred Canon Fixes
entries.text: 🧩 Inferred Canon Fixes 🧩This page collects inferred fixes for canon conflicts, gaps, and logic errors across World Without God — solutions designed to preserve your existing canon wherever possible. It tracks our section-by-section pass. Nothing here is live canon until you approve it; once you do, I'll write the fix into the relevant hub page. Key: ✅ Proposed fix · ❓ Needs your ruling · 🔧 Mechanical date/ordering fix 1 · The Timeline & the 7,000-Year Gap Pairs with: TIMELINE and ERAʼS REFRENCE The core problem Book 1 (A Tale of a Thousand Songs) sits at 7,250 BR; Books 34 run 0 AR → 2,652 AR. That asks your noble houses to survive 7,0009,800 years of continuous history. The Patton dynasty is the extreme case: founded by Haliour Layern Patton I in 8,759 BR, still on the throne Emperor Veo / Crown Prince Elleraian Patton) in 2,652 AR — an unbroken 11,400-year dynasty. No real dynasty lasts more than 300 years. The calendar middle is empty. Between the Early Empire 7,163 BR) and the Dark Ages 0 AR — roughly 7,000 years — almost nothing is recorded. That's the literal "nothing happened for millennia" failure state. You currently have two competing era frameworks: the granular spine on Era's Refrence and the coarse 6-row Era Overview table on Timeline. They don't match, and the Era Overview is still blank. Inferred Canon Fixes 1 ✅ Fix 1 — One canonical era spine Adopt the Era's Refrence chronology as the single source of truth (it's already gap-free). Proposed canonical spine: Era Span Notes Era of the First Song 30,000 BR 8,900 BRDivine age + Age of Saints Warriors' Age 8,900 7,945 BR Kingdoms founded The Classical Kingdoms 7,945 7,400 BR Six-kingdom equilibrium The Pre-Unification Period7,400 7,250 BR Pressure builds toward Solis The Civil War Period 7,250 7,217 BR Solis born → war Book 1 The Great Conquest 7,217 7,163 BR Solis unifies the world The Early Empire 7,163 – 4,000 BR Matsiali imperial order Golden Millennia 4,000 – 500 BR Imperial height The Late Golden Period 500 BR 0 AR Slow rot before the fall Dark Ages 0 – 50 AR Goteivati III Books 3, calendar reset) The Restoration 50 400 AR Recovery from Goteivati The Long Stability 400 1,326 AR "Illusory Peace" begins The Blood Trials 1,326 1,528 AR 1,000,000 killed; not peace The Age of Reforms 1,528 1,852 AR Takar; Astyan II reforms The Post-Reform Period 1,852 2,400 AR The Late Modern Period 2,400 2,632 AR Minara / Crown of Glory Book 4 ✅ Fix 2 — Populate the blank "Era Overview" (macro view) The 6-row Era Overview on Timeline is too coarse to cover 32,000 years and skips whole stretches. Redefine its buckets so they're complete and nonoverlapping: Macro Era Span Era of the First Song 30,000 BR 8,900 BR Warriors' Age 8,900 7,945 BR The Age of Unification & Empire 7,945 BR 0 AR Inferred Canon Fixes 2 Macro Era Span Golden Millennia 4,000 BR 0 AR (height within the above) Dark Ages & Restoration 0 400 AR Illusory Peace 400 2,632 AR ❓ Decision: keep the coarse 6-row macro view in addition to the full spine, or replace it entirely with the spine? My vote: keep the spine as canon and use the macro view only as a reader-facing summary. ✅ Fix 3 — "House Patton" is a throne-name, not an 11,400-year bloodline (the big one) 🔒 LOCKED — your ruling 9 Jun Patton becomes a claimed throne-name carried across numbered dynasties, with real breaks, usurpations, and restorations. Stop treating Patton as one unbroken blood-line. Reframe it the way Rome treated "Caesar" or Egypt treated its numbered dynasties: a dynastic name/claim that multiple bloodlines have held, punctuated by usurpations, cadet-branch restorations, and at least a few interregna. Your canon already supports this: Merigen Bleelack's coup against Emperor Hevet Xacrey Patton 0 AR, with Crandona reclaiming the throne, is a built-in dynastic break. That's precedent, not an exception. Recast the "unbroken Patton dynasty" as imperial propaganda — a continuity myth the empire tells about itself. The reality across 11,000 years includes broken lines, adopted heirs, married-in claimants who took the name, and "Patton Restorations." This adds dynastic blood-sport texture Tudor / Rome) instead of straining belief. ✅ Fix 4 — Make the Golden Millennia earn its 3,500 years A 3,500-year "Golden" age labeled as peace is the single biggest worldbuilding liability — it's the "nothing happened" trap. Seed it with recurring, era-appropriate friction (proposals, to be detailed per-era as we go): Succession disputes & regency wars inside the Patton claim Inferred Canon Fixes 3 Religious schism — the Circle of Eternal Light fracturing into rival rites Provincial secessions / reconquests (especially restless Pireaynea & the poor north) Periodic plagues, famines, and economic shocks tied to the trade map The slow institutional rise of Vikitsv's magic order as a rival power center The drift that left the enlightened Matsiali order brittle enough for Goteivati III to topple it overnight 🔧 Smaller dating / continuity fixes found on the Timeline Saints count 12 vs 13 Timeline calls Reron "the twelfth and final saint" (d. 7,402 BR, while the saints table has Harnua's execution raising a second moon and a 13th month. Fix: 12 honored saints; Harnua is the disgraced/erased 13th. Reron = last of the honored line. Circle of Eternal Light founding 14,271 BR entry is flagged "CHECK: may already exist." Fix: confirm one founding date, delete the duplicate. Battle of Relirian collision: appears here as Saint Reron's last stand 7,402 BR, Aicruae), but Gherci canon uses a "Battle of Relirian" to explain its 78%-female population. 🔒 LOCKED — your ruling 9 Jun one battle. Reron's apocalyptic last stand at Relirian 7,402 BR is the catastrophe that gutted Gherci's fighting-age men, leaving the realm 78% female for generations. Merge the two entries into a single event carrying both consequences (the saint's death and the demographic scar). Battle of Aishae ordering: dated 8,704 BR but listed mid-sequence around the 8,200s entries. Fix: re-sort into chronological order. Infant Laws 8,683 BR listed next to 8,051 BR entries. Fix: re-sort. Material culture is layered per era, so it starts with our first real era section (the Warriors' Age) — there's no single material culture to attach to the structural timeline itself. 2 · The Warriors' Age (8,900 – 7,945 BR) Inferred Canon Fixes 4 Pairs with: TIMELINE, Historical Figures, Noble Houses Patton / Arvento), Aicruae Funeral Traditions, Material Culture 🗺Real-world anchors (approved mapping). This founding era leans almost entirely on Aicruae → Iron Age Celtic Gaul Hallstatt → La Tène cultures, 80050 BCE. The other five are still just founding dates, so their material culture comes online as they enter the story: Coelum → Atlantic Scotland / Pictish + Norse; Equateiy → Villanovan / Etruscan Italy; Gherci → Anatolian highland + Aksumite-Ethiopian; Vikitsv → early Korean confederacy + Tibetan highland; Pireaynea → tribal Samnite / Sicel south Italy. What this era actually is The founding age — six kingdoms hacked out of tribal country. The problem: it's 95% Aicruae. House Patton (founded 8,759 BR, House Arvento 8,746 BR, the class-war chain, the Massacre of Light — all Aicruan. The other five kingdoms are a founding date and nothing else. That's the first thing to fix structurally. 🔴 / 🟠 Canon conflicts & errors landing in this era 🔴 Massacre of Light — who ordered it? Religion names King Viake Recreadion Patton (with Queen Mari); the Timeline carried an open note "fix the queen name." 🔒 LOCKED — your ruling 9 Jun a joint atrocity — King Viake orders it, Queen Mari is the true zealot driving it. Delete the stray note. You get a two-hander instead of a faceless decree, and Mari becomes your first named monster: the queen who believed. 🟠 Battle of Aishae 8,704 BR) is mis-sorted among the 8,200s entries. 🔧 Re-sort into chronological order. 🔴 Patton genealogy is physically impossible (and it's a symptom of the bloodline myth). Queen Cawiloan (b. 8,730 BR "bears" Haliour II 8,672) and Asayera 8,674) at age 5658; King Ilaem Nefest Patton I is dated 8,734 BR but his parents marry 8,732 BR (born two years before the wedding). ✅ Proposed fix: these dissolve once Patton is a throne-name Fix 3 — recast Inferred Canon Fixes 5 the impossible links as adopted heirs / cadet-branch claimants / married-in successors who took the name, then clean the raw date typos. 🟡 "1516 generations" from Haliour I to Solis across 1,540 years is impossible (that's 55 generations), and the family tree has a 1,000-year undocumented hole 8,459 → 7,408 BR. ✅ Proposed fix: the throne-name model turns that hole into several dynasties rather than one improbable line; we backfill it with the macro-texture from Fix 4. 🟠 Aicruan body-paint color clash: the real-world Celtic anchor uses woad blue, but your Aicruae Funeral Traditions centers red mourning paint. 🔒 LOCKED — your ruling 9 Jun split the colors.Blue = war paint (worn into battle — the face an enemy sees), red = mourning/kinship paint (worn for the dead, reading as blood and bloodline). Two ritual colors doing two jobs is richer than either alone, and it keeps your funeral canon load-bearing while honoring the Celtic woad parallel. ✍ Worldbuilding critique (Warriors' Age) What's working — keep it. The Aicruan class-war chain Little Hill 8,264 → Bears 8,262 → Bloody Winter 8,259 → Highwater 7,463) is the best thing in your whole timeline: a multi-century resentment arc with memory, betrayal, and the first successful coup. (c) Succession: his bastard son Hefu Bahsi is installed as Emperor Hefu Patton by his mother Lady Reyqe Bahsi of House Bahsi Goteivati's long-time mistress and bedmate) — and it is Hefu, not Goteivati, who becomes the Sun King and turns the terror-state into a gilded court. (d) The Pataoiut institutionalizes here: decree → permanent law → unquestioned common sense. (e) The Circle of Eternal Light is rebuilt as a crowncontrolled Gallican state church under the emperor (the Order of the Pure Ones absorbed or outlawed). (f) The roughly 350 years are subdivided into a revised five-phase arc (this lock supersedes the older proposed scaffolding further down the section): I · The Tyrant Toppled (roughly 5080 AR — the coalition that ends Goteivati; the terror-state suddenly without its terror, and a scramble to control the machine he built. II · The Bastard Crowned (roughly 80130 AR — Lady Reyqe Bahsi maneuvers her son Hefu onto the throne; he is legitimized as Emperor Hefu Patton; House Bahsi rises from a mistress's house to an imperial dynasty. III · The Sun Court Rises (roughly 130230 AR — Hefu Patton perfects absolutism: the Versailles-analog court, the great houses caged in gold, the Pataoiut hardened from decree into permanent law. IV · The Gilded Settlement (roughly 230330 AR — the Circle rebuilt as a Gallican state church under the emperor; the magic registry institutionalized (the Solisian Academy transformed, not founded); the Pure Ones absorbed or outlawed. V · Into the Long Calm (roughly 330400 AR — the gilded order settles into unquestioned "common sense" and carries the empire into the Long Stability. Inferred Canon Fixes 51 What this era actually is The 350 years after the Damned — and for once the job isn't filling empty centuries, it's showing how an empire lives with what just happened to it. Goteivati doesn't die in his bed — he is overthrown and deposed, the only end the Damned could earn. What comes next is the part that turns terror into a dynasty: his bastard son, Hefu Bahsi, is maneuvered onto the throne as Emperor Hefu Patton by his mother, Lady Reyqe Bahsi of House Bahsi — Goteivati's long-time mistress and bedmate — and it is Hefu, not his father, who becomes the Sun King and makes the new order beautiful. The Restoration is everything Goteivati's terror made possible without him: the Ten Rules outlast their author, the patriarchal Pataoiut hardens from decree into permanent law into unquestioned common sense, the broken Circle of Eternal Light is rebuilt as a crown-controlled Gallican state church under the emperor, the provinces he renamed stay renamed, and the magic registry he built Article VII) grows — across these centuries — into the empire's formal magical-education system, the Solisian Academy. This is the era that decides whether the Dark Ages were a wound the empire healed or a cage it learned to decorate. Your canon says the cage: the Pataoiut persists for 1,800 years, all the way to Astyan II's reforms 1,852 AR. The Restoration is where a tyrant's decree quietly becomes the way things have always been. 🔴 / 🟠 Canon conflicts & errors landing in this era 🟠 Goteivati's death is unrecorded — the era's first real gap. Canon tracks him to the Ten Rules and the Pataoiut, then goes quiet: no death date, no cause, no named successor. After Section 10's lock that matters double — his body carries Reio's corrupted soul, so his death is also the death of the single most dangerous magical being in the empire. That should cost something. ✅ Options for your ruling (below): he dies early 50 AR, the dark soul burning the body out young), he's overthrown once the empress-mother's restraint is decades gone, or the Damned rules long and the terror only ends when he does. Each reshapes how much of the Restoration is his and how much is the recovery from him. 🟢 The Solisian Academy is transformed here, not founded here. Timing flag — per your standing rule.) Your own map page is explicit: “During the reign of Emperor Goteivati Zivc Patton III, it was chiefly a school for adolescent nobility; it later transformed into the empire's formal magical-education Inferred Canon Fixes 52 infrastructure.” So the Academy is old — a noble finishing school that predates Goteivati. What belongs to this era is its conversion: Article VII's registry of conscripted mages needs somewhere to put them, and across the Restoration that somewhere becomes the Academy. Don't write “the Academy is founded” in the Restoration — write that the Restoration repurposes an existing noble school into the empire's magic institution. Exactly the Barqeten trap: the thing already exists; only its new function is new.) 🟢 The imperial renamings are Crandona's-era work — anchor them, don't restate them as Restoration-new. Canon: Vikitsv “became Theolisseia during Crandona's Era,” and the old Aicruan royal dynasty was “reorganized into the Tanan Grand Duchy after the empire's formation during Crandona's Era.” So the map's redrawing belongs to the reset itself (late Dark Ages / the dawn of the Restoration), not a fresh Restoration project. ✅ Anchor the renames to the Reconstruction's administrative settlement so they stop floating between eras. 🟠 How does a tyrant's decree outlive the tyrant by 1,800 years? It can't — unless the Restoration institutionalizes it. This is the era's central task: show the Pataoiut converting from terror (enforced by Goteivati's informants, Article VIII) into law, then custom, then plain common sense (enforced by nobody, because everyone now believes it). The Louis XIV settlement is precisely that machinery — the generation that grows up here never knew the Matsiali, so to them the inversion simply is the world. 🟢 Religion needs rebuilding — Article II gutted it. Goteivati crushed the Circle and seized its temples Section 10. The Restoration has to fill that hole. ✅ A reading that pays off your canon: a crown-controlled state Circle — a Gallican-style church that answers to the emperor, not to itself — with the breakaway Order of the Pure Ones either absorbed into it or outlawed outright under a Revocation-of-Nantes–style demand for one faith. Flag for your call. ✍ Worldbuilding critique (Restoration) Blunt: the trap here is the opposite of the empty eras and the opposite of the Dark Ages too. The danger isn't a blank, and it isn't a cartoon villain — it's writing this era as relief. “And then things got better.” They didn't get better; they got permanent. That's the horror you're actually sitting on, so play it. Inferred Canon Fixes 53 Make it a settlement, not a recovery. The cruelty of the Pataoiut isn't the terror that imposed it — it's the 1,800 years it lasted after the terror stopped, once nobody had to be forced anymore. Show the first generation raised entirely inside it, to whom a woman holding office is an absurd old story. That's how an atrocity becomes a tradition. The Sun King needs a face. Give me the emperor who turns Goteivati's terrorstate into a court — the one who works out that you can cage a duke more cheaply with an invitation than an axe. He isn't a monster like his predecessor; he's subtler, and arguably more durable. The most dangerous man in the era is the one who made tyranny comfortable. That's your Versailles / Catherine the Great figure. The Academy is your bridge to Book 4 — build it on-page. The registry becoming the Solisian Academy is the throughline that pays off in A Crown of Glory Minara, the Catern bride, the Gnati division). Show the ugly seam: an institution born as a leash (register and conscript every mage, Article VII) slowly rebranding itself as a school. The Academy's polite motto and the registry's iron purpose are the same document — and that tension is a gift for the later book. Where do the women go? Three thousand years of matriarchy don't evaporate because a law says so. The Restoration is where the resistance goes underground and clever — dowager duchesses running houses through male figureheads, the old Matsiali rites kept alive as harmless “family tradition,” marriages still brokered by women who legally can't own the deal. Plant the long fuse here for whatever finally reverses the Pataoiut Astyan II, 1,852 AR. The inversion should never once sit easy. 🏺 Material culture — Louis XIV's France (~1643–1715) Grounded in cited Sun-King practice Versailles court society, Colbert's mercantilism, the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes), then adapted — carrying the matriarchy → patriarchy inversion from Sections 710 into its settled, gilded form. Redirect any anchor that doesn't fit. Clothing & fashion. Real Sun-King court: the king was fashion — courtiers bankrupted themselves on silk, lace, and heels (the red heel marked the privileged few admitted near the king), and rank was measured by who Inferred Canon Fixes 54 attended the royal lever (the ceremonial rising and dressing). Adapt: after the Pataoiut inversion Section 10, male court dress reaches its gaudy peak — the men who seized the purple and rank-dyes of the old matriarchy now perform power in them; access to the emperor's morning rising becomes the era's true currency of status, and what a woman may wear is the Pataoiut written in cloth. Food & cuisine. Real: the grand couvert — the king dined in public as theatre, while haute cuisine, table etiquette, and sugar-sculpture spectacle were born at court. Adapt: imperial dining becomes a daily ceremony of the restored order; the new Pataoiut nobility eat the Reconstruction's seized wealth in full view while etiquette polices every gesture — the table as a stage for belonging. Architecture. Real: Versailles — a palace built on purpose to centralize power and trap the aristocracy in supervised splendor; baroque scale, halls of mirrors, gardens forcing geometry onto nature. Adapt: the emperor raises a vast new sun-palace to Razar and moves the great houses into it — Goteivati emptied the temples, his heirs build a palace-temple to themselves; the literal Sun King inside a sun-god's empire. The gutted Razar temples Section 10) are either rebuilt under crown control or left standing as monuments to Year Zero. Weapons & military tactics. Real: Louis's standing professional royal army Louvois' reforms made it Europe's largest), Vauban's star-fortresses, and wars of prestige and expansion. Adapt: Goteivati's personal-loyalty gunpowder force Section 10) is professionalized into a standing imperial army answerable to the throne alone; the registered “gifted” Article VII) become a formal magical corps within it — the leash turned into a permanent state weapon, magic now openly deployed rather than merely feared. Legal systems. Real: absolutism codified — the Grande Ordonnance / Code Louis, intendants governing provinces for the crown, lits de justice, and the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes enforcing one faith. Adapt: the Ten Rules stop being one man's decree and become a permanent legal code; intendantstyle crown agents replace the informant-terror of Article VIII — control by bureaucracy, not denunciation; Article IX's forced unity matures into a Revocation-style religious settlement. Inferred Canon Fixes 55 Trade goods & economy. Real: mercantilism under Colbert — state manufactures, royal monopolies, a stabilized currency, and wealth marshaled to the crown. Adapt: the Rern, reset to Year Zero in the Dark Ages Section 10, is rebuilt into a mercantilist standard; the temple wealth Goteivati seized Article II) bankrolls royal manufactures and the new Pataoiut gentry who owe everything to the Reconstruction and will defend it to the death. Funeral & death customs. Real: royal funerals at Saint-Denis and “Le roi est mort, vive le roi” — the cult of unbroken succession, staged in elaborate state mourning. Adapt: the dynasty performs continuity hard precisely because the Damned broke it — but Goteivati's own burial is the open question: does the empire entomb the Damned with honors it doesn't feel, or bury him quietly and let the propaganda finish the story? Ties straight to the death-gap above.) Daily life. Real: court society — the nobility domesticated into courtiers whose whole existence is the contest for the king's notice, the provinces run by bureaucrats, the performance of loyalty made a way of life. Adapt: the great houses that survived the terror are pulled into a gilded court where status is nearness to the emperor — Goteivati ruled by fear, his heirs rule by seduction. The Dark Ages' “public conformity, private grief” becomes “public splendor, private accounting”; and the women the Pataoiut stripped of office run real power from behind the court's curtains — the whisper-network the system insists doesn't exist. ✅ Fix — subdivide the ~350 years into named phases The recovery-into-absolutism arc: the terror outliving its author, a Sun King taming the houses, the gilded high court, the calcification, and the drift into the Long Stability. Scaffolding to fill with named emperors and crises as we build, spending Fix 4's friction list. Phase (proposed) Span (approx.) What defines it I · The Throne Without Its Tyrant 50 – 120 AR Goteivati is gone; the Ten Rules and the Pataoiut run on fear and inertia. Regents and uncertain heirs hold a machine no one dares dismantle — the terror's apparatus outliving the man who built it. II · The Gathering of the Crown 120 – 210 AR A strong absolutist emperor centralizes — the Sun King. The great houses, exhausted by the Dark Inferred Canon Fixes 56 Phase (proposed) Span (approx.) What defines it Ages, are drawn toward the throne; the Pataoiut hardens from a tyrant's decree into settled, permanent law. III · The Sun Court 210 – 300 AR High absolutism: a Versailles-analog palace cages the nobility in gold, etiquette replaces the executioner, and the magic registry Article VII) is repurposed into the Solisian Academy — the empire's formal magical-education system. Marriage to the Sun-Forged becomes ordinary. IV · The Gilded Settlement 300 – 360 AR The order calcifies into routine; the Circle is rebuilt as a crown-controlled church and dissent is purged by law rather than terror (a Revocation-of-Nantes religious uniformity). Beauty over fear — and resentment under the gilt. V · Into the Long Calm 360 400 AR Absolutism settles into bureaucracy; the empire mistakes its gilded stillness for peace. The drift into the “Illusory Peace” of the Long Stability. Handoff to Section 12. ❓Section 11 — open rulings before I lock it. (a) Adopt Louis XIV's France Sun King absolutism) as the era's anchor? (b) When/how does Goteivati die — early 50 AR, Reio's soul burning the body out young), overthrown once Crandona's restraint is long gone, or does the Damned rule long? (c) Who succeeds him — does his cursed bloodline continue, or does a new Patton branch take the throne? (d) Confirm the Pataoiut institutionalizes here — decree → permanent law → common sense? (e) Religion: rebuild the Circle as a crown-controlled state church, with the Pure Ones absorbed or outlawed? (f) Subdivide the 350 years into the five-phase arc above, or keep it as prose? Inferred Canon Fixes 57

entries.text:
🧩
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
🧩Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2. Continuation of 🧩Inferred Canon Fixes
— Sections 110 live there. This page carries Section 11 onward so the
doc stays loadable as it grows. Same rules: nothing here is live canon
until you approve it; once you do, I'll write the fix into the relevant hub
page.
Key: ✅  Proposed fix · ❓  Needs your ruling · 🔧  Mechanical date/ordering fix
11 · The Restoration (~50 – 400 AR)
Pairs with: TIMELINE, ERAʼS REFRENCE , House Patton, , The Solisian Academy,
KEY WORDS AND TERMS, Name Evolution Across Eras, Magic System
🗺Real-world anchors (this era). Per your era → period map, the recovery
from Goteivati is Louis XIV's France 16431715 — and the Sun King
fit is almost too good for a world that worships a sun god. Where
Goteivati ruled by terror (the Tudor Reformation, Section 10, the dynasty
that buries him rules by spectacle: absolute monarchy perfected, the
great houses tamed not on the scaffold but at court, etiquette and
nearness to the throne standing in for the executioner. Louis hands you
the whole kit — a Versailles built to cage the nobility in gold, “l'état,
c'est moi” absolutism, a professional royal army, mercantilist state
wealth, the revocation of the Edict of Nantes (one faith by royal will),
and a court where a duke spends his whole life competing to hand the
king his shirt. The Restoration is where Goteivati's blood-soaked Year
Zero hardens into a permanent, gilded order — the Pataoiut made
forever, and made beautiful.
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
1
What this era actually is
The empire comes out of the Dark Ages the way France came out of its wars of
religion — not by undoing the strongman's work, but by making it permanent and
beautiful. Goteivati is overthrown and deposed. The terror doesn't fade on its
own and it doesn't end with a deathbed; it is ended by force, and the man who
called himself the Reconstruction's deliverer is pulled down. But what follows is
not a return to the matriarchal world he erased.
His bastard son, Hefu Bahsi — born to Lady Reyqe Bahsi of House Bahsi, the
house-bred mistress who shared Goteivati's bed for decades — is lifted onto the
throne by his mother's maneuvering and crowned Emperor Hefu Patton. It is
Hefu, not Goteivati, who becomes the Sun King: he takes his father's Year Zero
and turns it into a gilded, permanent order. The Ten Rules outlast their author. The
patriarchal Pataoiut hardens from one tyrant's decree into permanent law — and
then into something heavier than law: common sense, the way things have simply
always been. The shattered Circle of Eternal Light is rebuilt, but as a crowncontrolled state church answerable to the emperor rather than the gods. And the
magic registry Goteivati built out of fear Article VII) is turned into permanent
institution — the moment the Solisian Academy is transformed into the empire's
formal magical-education machinery. The terror becomes a civilization.
🔴  / 🟠  Canon conflicts & errors landing in this era
🟢  Goteivati is overthrown — and a bastard's line takes the throne (the era's
spine; locked). Your ruling settles the open death-gap from Section 10: the
Damned does not die quietly or rule into old age — he is deposed by force.
Power passes to his bastard son Hefu Bahsi, crowned Emperor Hefu Patton,
installed by his mother Lady Reyqe Bahsi of House Bahsi Goteivati's longtime mistress). The Sun King is Hefu, not his father. This is the hinge the whole
era turns on, and it's new canon — House Bahsi rises from a mistress's house
into an imperial dynasty.
🟢  The Pataoiut institutionalizes here — decree →  permanent law →
common sense (locked). Goteivati declared the patriarchal Pataoiut 36 AR,
Section 10; the Restoration is where it sets like concrete. Hefu's reign is
where a violent reversal stops being one man's edict and becomes the
empire's permanent legal order — and then, across generations, the thing
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
2
nobody questions. By the end of the era a person can be born, live, and die
without ever knowing the world was once matriarchal. That's a darker victory
than the terror itself.
🟢  The Circle is rebuilt as a crown-controlled state church — a Gallican
settlement (locked). Goteivati crushed the Circle of Eternal Light Section 10,
Article II. The Restoration doesn't restore its independence — it rebuilds the
faith as an arm of the throne, a state church under the emperor (the Gallican /
Louis-XIV model, where the crown controls the clergy and one faith is imposed
by royal will, like the revocation of the Edict of Nantes). The breakaway Order
of the Pure Ones is absorbed into the new orthodoxy or outlawed as a rival.
Religion comes back, but on the emperor's leash.
🟢  The Solisian Academy is transformed here, not founded (timing fix;
locked). Canon describes the Academy as having begun "chiefly a school for
adolescent nobility" that "later transformed into the empire's formal magicaleducation infrastructure." That transformation belongs here — the Restoration
is when Goteivati's fearful magic registry Article VII) is rebuilt into a
permanent institution. Do not write the Academy as newly founded in this era;
it already existed and is being repurposed.
🟠  Two renamings belong to Crandona's Era, not the Restoration (don't
double-count). Search confirms Vikitsv →  Theolisseia and the old Aicruan
dynasty →  Tanan Grand Duchy are dated to Crandona's Era. Anchor those
renamings there; the Restoration's job is institutional hardening (law, church,
academy), not the map-renaming, which has its own home.
✍  Worldbuilding critique (Restoration)
Don't let the overthrow happen offstage. "Goteivati is deposed" is a
sentence; the toppling of a god-emperor is a decade. Who moves against him
— the old matriarchal houses he gutted, a faction of his own conscripted
mages, the army? A tyrant that total doesn't fall to a palace knife; he falls to a
coalition that has finally decided the cost of obedience is higher than the cost
of revolt. Dramatize the math.
Reyqe Bahsi is your engine — play her like Maintenon / Kösem. A mistress
who outlasts the tyrant and then puts her own bastard on the throne is one of
the best pieces of court drama in the whole project. She's not a footnote to
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
3
Hefu; she's the architect of him. Give her the regency-mother arc — the
woman who survived sharing a monster's bed, kept her son alive through the
overthrow, and out-maneuvered every trueborn claimant to crown a bastard.
House Bahsi rising from "the mistress's house" to the imperial dynasty is a
Magnificent Century spine.
The Sun Court has to cage, not just glitter. Versailles wasn't pretty for its own
sake — it was a trap that turned dangerous warlords into courtiers fighting
over who hands the emperor his shirt. Show the old houses losing their teeth
at court: a duke who once held an army now holds a ceremonial title and a
room near the throne. And remember your own rule — peace still has
skirmishes: faction wars, proxy intrigues, mistresses and ministers knifing
each other for the Sun King's ear.
The quiet horror is the generation that forgets. The most chilling beat of this
era isn't a purge — it's a young noblewoman in 350 AR who has never heard
that women once ruled, who thinks the Pataoiut is simply nature. Goteivati
made the terror; Hefu's Restoration makes it normal. Land that and the era
earns its place.
🏺  Material culture — Louis XIV's France (~1643–1715)
Grounded in cited Sun-King practice Versailles, Colbert's mercantilism, the Code
Louis, the revocation of the Edict of Nantes), then adapted — carrying the
matriarchy → patriarchy inversion Section 10) into its permanent, gilded form.
Redirect any anchor that doesn't fit.
Clothing & fashion. Real France: the king set fashion for a continent — the
justaucorps, towering perruque wigs, and red heels reserved by royal favor
(you literally could not wear them without the king's blessing). Dress was a
map of nearness to the throne. Adapt: the Sun Court turns clothing into a
favor-economy — the rank-dyes and insignia that ran through the female line
under Matsiali Section 8) are now permanently reassigned to men under the
Pataoiut, and a courtier's wardrobe broadcasts exactly how close they sit to
Emperor Hefu.
Food & cuisine. Real France: the grand couvert — the king dining in public as
theater, watched by a ranked audience — and the birth of haute cuisine as
court spectacle. Adapt: imperial public dining becomes a ceremony of rank;
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
4
who is permitted to watch the emperor eat, and from how near, is a
measurable unit of standing — the Sun Court's pecking order made edible.
Architecture. Real France: Versailles — a palace built less to live in than to
cage the nobility in gold, with Le Nôtre's controlled gardens and the Hall of
Mirrors as propaganda. Adapt: Hefu raises a new sun-palace on land Goteivati
seized from the temples Section 10 — the Razar sun-imagery, once the
Circle's, now glorifying the Sun King himself; the great houses are summoned
to live inside it, where the throne can watch them.
Weapons & military tactics. Real France: Louvois's professional standing
army (the largest in Europe), Vauban's star-fortresses and scientific siegecraft, war run as a state enterprise. Adapt: the standing imperial army settles
into a permanent, emperor-loyal force; Goteivati's registered "gifted" Article
VII) are institutionalized into a state magical corps — the Solisian Academy
transformed into the pipeline that trains and assigns them; war becomes
managed and bureaucratic, fought at fortified frontiers rather than in the
heartland.
Legal systems. Real France: "l'état, c'est moi" absolutism, the codifying
Grand Ordonnances (the Code Louis, 16671670, and intendants enforcing
royal law in every province over local lords. Adapt: this is where the Pataoiut is
codified — the gender inversion written permanently into civil law (marriage,
inheritance, property, office), and intendant-style royal agents replace
whatever local matriarchal authority survived. Law is how the terror becomes
irreversible.
Trade goods & economy. Real France: Colbert's mercantilism — state
manufactures, luxury exports (silk, glass, mirrors), tax farming, roads and
canals built to enrich the crown. Adapt: imperial mercantilism funds the Sun
Court's gold; the Rern, reset after the Dark Ages, is restabilized into a hard
currency again; the once-suppressed magic trade is brought fully under state
license — taxed, monopolized, and profitable.
Funeral & death customs. Real France: royal burial at Saint-Denis, the cry "le
roi est mort, vive le roi" (the throne never dies), and the doctrine of the king's
two bodies. Adapt: a new imperial necropolis for the Patton-Bahsi line, and a
continuity doctrine that papers over the bastard origin — official rites insisting
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
5
Hefu's crown is unbroken and god-given, so the throne can never be seen to
have passed through a mistress's son.
Daily life. Real France: the levée (nobles competing for the honor of attending
the king's morning rising), etiquette as the instrument of control, and royal
mistresses as real power-brokers Montespan, then Maintenon). Adapt: the
Sun Court's suffocating etiquette is the cage; Lady Reyqe Bahsi is your
Maintenon — the mistress who became the power behind the throne;
nearness to Emperor Hefu is the only currency that matters; and the
matriarchy is now something the old families remember in private and deny in
public.
✅  Fix — subdivide the ~350 years into a five-phase arc
The recovery from Goteivati, walked from the overthrow to the threshold of the
Long Stability. Scaffolding to fill with named reigns and crises as we build,
spending Fix 4's friction list.
Phase Span (approx.) What defines it
I · The Tyrant
Toppled 50  80 AR
The coalition that finally ends Goteivati — old
matriarchal houses, disaffected mages, and the army
deciding obedience costs more than revolt. The
Damned is overthrown and deposed by force; the
empire is left victorious but leaderless.
II · The Bastard
Crowned 80  130 AR
Lady Reyqe Bahsi maneuvers her son Hefu Bahsi
past every trueborn claimant and onto the throne as
Emperor Hefu Patton. A legitimacy war over a
bastard's right to rule; House Bahsi rises from the
mistress's house into an imperial dynasty.
III · The Sun
Court Rises 130  230 AR
Absolutism perfected. Hefu becomes the Sun King; a
Versailles-analog sun-palace cages the great houses;
the Pataoiut is codified into permanent law. The
warlords become courtiers fighting over ceremony.
IV · The Gilded
Settlement
230  330 AR The institutions set. The Circle is rebuilt as a crowncontrolled state church Gallican settlement); the
Order of the Pure Ones is absorbed or outlawed; the
magic registry is institutionalized — the Solisian

Phase Span (approx.) What defines it
Academy *transformed • into the empire's formal
magical-education corps.
V · Into the Long
Calm 330  400 AR
The gilded order stops being policy and becomes
common sense — a generation that no longer
remembers the matriarchy. The Pataoiut is simply
"how things are." The settled, ossifying peace carries
straight into the Long Stability.
🔒LOCKED  Section 11 The Restoration, 50400 AR. (a) Anchor:
Louis XIV's France / the Sun King. (b) Goteivati "the Damned" is
overthrown and deposed — the terror ends by force, not by a natural
death. (c) Succession: his bastard son Hefu Bahsi is crowned Emperor
Hefu Patton, installed by his mother Lady Reyqe Bahsi of House Bahsi
Goteivati's long-time mistress) — and it is Hefu, not Goteivati, who is
the Sun King. (d) The Pataoiut institutionalizes here: decree →
permanent law →  common sense. (e) The shattered Circle of Eternal
Light is rebuilt as a crown-controlled state church under the emperor
Gallican settlement); the Order of the Pure Ones is absorbed or
outlawed. (f) Timing flags: the Solisian Academy is transformed, not
founded here; the renamings Vikitsv →  Theolisseia and Aicruan
dynasty →  Tanan Grand Duchy belong to Crandona's Era. (g) The 350
years are subdivided into the five-phase arc above.
12 · The Long Stability (~400 – 1,326 AR)
Pairs with: TIMELINE, ERAʼS REFRENCE , House Patton, The Solisian Academy,
Magic System, Religion , KEY WORDS AND TERMS
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
7
🗺Real-world anchors (this era). The 926 years of the Long Stability map
cleanly onto Song Dynasty China 9601279 CE — the empire at its
most prosperous, most bureaucratic, and most quietly brittle. Song
China gives you the whole kit: a civil examination system that makes
merit (on paper) the path to power, printing and encyclopaedias,
explosive growth in trade, porcelain, and silk, Neo-Confucian
philosophy that hardens patriarchal family hierarchy into cosmic law,
and — crucially — the era when footbinding becomes normalized
among the elite, a physical enforcement of female immobility that maps
directly onto your Pataoiut. Song China looks like a golden age in every
chronicle and feels like a cage from inside. The Long Stability is where

Sisters text and Religion  say Soli is two souls in one body Paxtino,
