guise); the Quote Bank flips it to "two twin gods, one soul." Lock the twoInferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
49
souls-one-body version: it is the one the pantheon structure depends on (two
distinct gods, one shared vessel) and the one that makes the Soli-as-mortal
arc legible. Fix the Quote Bank line.
🔧  The War of Gods is two wars — the TIMELINE only records one. In-Story,
KEY WORDS, Religion , and A CROWN OF GLORY BOOK INFO all confirm a
War of Gods II (triggered by the union of Soli and Apharia, 7,2007,100 BR;
the TIMELINE lists only War of Gods I 30,000 BR, Renedin's murder of
Gaialana). This is a straight omission, not a conflict — add War of Gods II to
the TIMELINE at its 7,2007,100 BR slot so all sources agree.
✅  Renedin: one god, two myths — reconcile as "hidden architect." Canon
carries two competing War-of-Gods stories: Renedin as "one of four brothers"
(the four Old Gods crystallized from Noirta) versus Renedin as the "mastervillain" behind everything. Both are true at different depths — he is one of the
four Old Gods (the cosmological fact) and the hidden architect of the divine
catastrophes (the murder of Gaialana, the secret fatherhood, the engine of
Book 4. The "one of four" version is what the Brotherhood of Westwinds
preaches; the "master-villain" version is the truth the books reveal. Same god,
two registers — same move as the twins' paternity.
✅  Two Religion hubs — keep both (your ruling). The cosmology lives in two
places: the main Religion  bible and a secondary "Gods and Saints" hub. Your
ruling: keep both — the main bible is the canonical source of record, and the
secondary hub stays as a quick-reference index. Where they diverge (the
twins' father, the saint count), the bible wins and the hub is corrected to match
it, so the index never contradicts the source.
B · The saints — count, names, and dates
✅  Twelve honored saints, plus a disgraced thirteenth. The TIMELINE and
the secondary hub call Reron the 12th and final saint; KEY WORDS AND
TERMS and the main Religion  page call Harnua the 13th and final. Both are
right once you split "final" from "honored": twelve canonized, venerated
saints (ending with Reron), then Harnua Kulio as the disgraced, uncanonized thirteenth — the Infamous Thirteenth, blessed by Nellebrie but
burned by Solis, remembered as tragedy and warning rather than honored.
"Twelve saints" is the count the faithful recite; "thirteen" is the true total
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
50
including the one the Circle would rather forget. Fix the TIMELINE and the
secondary hub to name Harnua as the thirteenth-but-disgraced, not erase her.
🔧  Harnua's death date and epithet — pick one of each. Harnua carries two
death dates (an unspecified execution vs 7,214 BR) and two epithets ("the
Infamous Thirteenth" vs "The Great Tragedy"). Lock 7,214 BR as the death
date; keep both epithets as what two traditions call her — the Circle's
dismissive "Infamous Thirteenth" and the folk / Orcus-cult's mournful "Great
Tragedy." Reconcile the wording wherever only one currently appears.
🔧  Saint Duri founded Gherci sixteen years before he was born — fix the
date.Religion  has Saint Duri Mother of Gherci) born 8,747 BR but
"incorporating lands into Gherci" in 8,763 BR — sixteen years before birth.
One number is transposed. Cleanest fix: the founding date is wrong, not the
birth — move the incorporation to after 8,747 BR (e.g. 8,720 BR, in Duri's
adult life). Confirm against the longevity note Duri longest-lived, 8,7478,670
BR.
🔧  The "saints end" rule needs one statement. Canon says the gods stop
raising saints ~7,163 BR, yet the disgraced final saint Harnua dies 7,214 BR and
the last honored saint Reron dies at the Battle of Relirian 7,402 BR. Lock a
single rule — "Harnua (d. 7,214 BR) is the last figure any god ever touched;
no saint was raised after her" — and drop or restate the 7,163 cutoff so it
doesn't read as a second, conflicting end date.
C · Geography and names
✅  The Lajazer / Vellin tangle — Lajazer is the kingdom, Vellin is the capital
(your ruling). The messiest geographic knot in the canon, now settled. Per
Name Evolution Across Eras — Aicruae →  Kingdom of Lajazer, capital Vellin
— that is the locked form. The conflicting line in A CROWN OF GLORY BOOK
INFO that reads "Lajazer, capital of the Kingdom of Vellin" has kingdom and
capital swapped and is the error to fix: rewrite it to Vellin, capital of the
Kingdom of Lajazer. Root cause confirmed: the Six Kingdoms map filled
Minara-era kingdom names into the capital field, scrambling country and city.
All pages normalize to kingdom = Lajazer, capital = Vellin.
✅  Coelum — northern "Forsaken Land," capital Atriki (your ruling,
confirmed against the master map). Coelum is the northern / north-central
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
51
kingdom, not a southern Fetora-Sea one. The Civil War-era master continental
map (<mention-page
url="https://app.notion.com/p/378a374231bc80349db8eac2d9e31ec5"Map
of the world during the 7,250 BR ────  The Civil War Period ────  7,217 BR
</mention-page>) settles it: capital Atriki sits beside Lake Trang, fanning north to
the Henem Bay ports, bordered to the south by Gherci. Elgan, the southern
reference city near Minara's birth village, is in the region's orbit but is not the
capital — Atriki is.) Coelum keeps its flag as "The Forsaken Land," canon's only
atheistic society. Mechanical cleanup: the Pireaynea map sheet mislabels it
"Coelys" — normalize to Coelum everywhere.
✅  Spelling — locked one form per name (your ruling). Systemic drift to clean
up by find-and-replace: Vikitsv vs Vikistv (the big one — both appear across
pages), plus Mikani/Mikiani, Nimlye/Nimyle, Vesmen/Vesme,
Chairameron/Chairamero. Locked canonical forms: Vikitsv, Mikani, Nimlye,
Vesmen, Chairameron — note Vesmen is correct (per  and the Karniode
Vesmen surname), overriding the earlier "Vesme" proposal. I'll normalize every
page to these.
D · Dates, epochs, and mechanics
🔧  The Civil War has three date ranges — pick one. Three values are live:
7,2227,217 BR Maps, 7,2217,217 BR Historical Figures), 7,2507,217 BR (a
map subpage title). The end (7,217 BR) is stable everywhere; only the start
drifts. Proposed lock: 7,2227,217 BR (the Maps value, the tightest plausible
window); the 7,250 subpage title is almost certainly a typo. Confirm and I'll
align all three.
✅  The post-Goteivati epoch name — "Restoration" wins, "Reconstruction"
is the regime's own propaganda term. Goteivati's regime Emperor Goteivati's
Ten Rules) calls the era the "Reconstruction"; the ERAʼS REFRENCE  spine
calls the recovery the Dark Ages →  Restoration. Resolve by register:
"Reconstruction" is what Goteivati's regime called its own Year Zero (the
tyrant's self-justifying label, §10, and "Restoration" is the historians' name
for the recovery that buries him (§11). Both stay — they name different things
from different sides. No date change.
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
52
✅  Magic's arrival — "integrated by intermarriage," not "introduced by
decree." One line has magic "introduced under Goteivati III"; the Magic
System page resolves it as magic integrated into the bloodlines via
intermarriage over generations (the Iswan/Verna bargain as origin, then
spread by marriage). Lock the Magic System version and reword the Locations
line so magic is integrated, not invented, under Goteivati III.
E · The open prophecy
✅  The False Star = Vandrea / Empress Macenja (your ruling). The central
prophecy — "when the Eclipsing Sun and the False Star meet, the old god
shall shatter the world" — now has all three terms. The old god = Renedin; the
Eclipsing Sun is the Patton heir (the reigning emperor's firstborn, the dynastic
title); and the False Star = Vandrea, the false empress wearing Empress
Macenja. This is the engine: Renedin maneuvers Vandrea / Empress Macenja
into bearing a Patton heir because she is the False Star — drawing the
prophecy's two halves together under one roof so the old god can shatter the
world. The dark irony is a misreading of the prophecy's own words: because it
says Eclipsing Son, both Vandrea and Renedin assume the heir must be a boy
— so when Vandrea bears a daughter, Minara, she sends the child off to die.
The prophecy turns self-fulfilling through the very act meant to defeat it:
Minara is the true Eclipsing Sun, and Vandrea's attempt to discard her is what
sets the meeting in motion.
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
53
🔒LOCKED  Section 17 Cross-Era Canon Audit). All five judgment calls
are now ruled, and every ✅ / 🔧  fix above is ready to write into the live
hub pages. (a) Lajazer/Vellin: Lajazer is the kingdom, Vellin the capital
— the Crown of Glory Book Info line is the error to flip. (b) Coelum: the
northern "Forsaken Land," capital Atriki Lake Trang, Henem Bay) —
normalize the "Coelys" map-sheet spelling. (c) Religion hubs:keep both
— main bible is canon, secondary hub is a quick index corrected to
match it. (d) Spellings: locked to Vikitsv, Mikani, Nimlye, Vesmen,
Chairameron Vesmen, not Vesme). (e) False Star = Vandrea / Empress
Macenja — the Eclipsing Sun is the Patton heir; Renedin breeds the
False Star into the dynasty, and the "Eclipsing Sun" misreading drives
Vandrea to cast out the daughter Minara who is the true Eclipsing Sun.
Per your ruling, every error and flag stays documented here on this
page — the live hub pages TIMELINE, Religion, the second hub, Quote
Bank, Name Evolution, Historical Figures, the maps) are left untouched.
This audit is the single consolidated record; nothing is propagated out
into live canon.
Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2
54

stages a populated TIMELINE against the locked era spine from 🧩Inferred Canon
Fixes and 🧩Inferred Canon Fixes — Part 2. Nothing here is written into the live hub
until you approve it. First deliverable: the ERA OVERVIEW backbone — the skeleton
every later entry (era events, ruler succession, lifespans) hangs off.

The Early Empire · 7,163 – ~4,000 BR
Per your locked ruling Inferred Canon Fixes §7, this 3,000-year span is no longer one
undifferentiated block — it is five named imperial phases, and its first succession is a
matrilineal pass that keeps Solis's blood on the throne through a daughter (not a throne-name
break).
7,163 BR  Emperor Solis dies (age 87); his son Maen inherits at 54 and renames the realm
the Solisian Empire.
7,140 BR  Emperor Maen dies childless at 77 (three wives, no surviving issue); the throne
passes to his sister Coyre's eldest son.
7,140 – 7,092 BR  Emperor Elleinaj Patton I Solis's grandson via the female line)
inherits at 55, rules 48 years, and stabilizes the empire after Maen's barren reign; later
weds his daughter Cenainaya to Snieoa's grandson Eavanileto Yurea, reuniting the two
branches of Solis's descendants.
Phase I · The Founding & the Matrilineal Settlement 7,163 – 7,000 BR the female-line
succession sets precedent; conquered kingdoms are renamed Pireaynea →  Lingia,
Coelum →  Hikai); House Leva's pre-imperial Divine Matriarch Brimena Leva, 8,902 BR)
is scaled up into the imperial Matsiali state ideology.
Phase II · The High Matsiali / First Golden Age 7,000 – 6,200 BR the matriarchal order
at its confident height; Roman-style codified law, roads, aqueducts, and citizenship-asintegration; the conquered patriarchies simmer beneath.
